messages.content: what is Infrastructure monitoring vs Application monitoring?

Infrastructure monitoring tracks system-level resources: CPU usage, memory, disk I/O, network throughput, server uptime. Tools: Prometheus + node_exporter, Datadog agent, CloudWatch (AWS), zabbix. Alerts: disk 90% full, CPU sustained above 80%, memory pressure. Application monitoring (APM) tracks application-level behavior: request latency, error rates, throughput, dependency performance, transaction traces. Tools: Datadog APM, New Relic, Dynatrace, Jaeger (open source distributed tracing), OpenTelemetry. Key difference: infrastructure tells you the server is healthy, APM tells you the application is healthy. A server can have 20% CPU but the app responds in 10 seconds because of a slow database query. You need both. Real User Monitoring (RUM): measures actual user experience in the browser — page load time, JS errors, user interactions. Synthetic monitoring: automated tests from multiple locations — detect outages before users do. The observability stack: metrics (Prometheus) + logs (Loki/ELK) + traces (Jaeger/Tempo) + alerting (Alertmanager/PagerDuty).

messages.content: dağıtık işlemler nasıl yönetilir, two-phase commit nedir

Dağıtık işlemler (distributed transactions), birden fazla servisi veya veritabanını kapsayan ve ya hepsinin başarılı olmasını ya da hiçbirinin uygulanmamasını gerektiren işlemlerdir. Two-Phase Commit (2PC) bunun klasik çözümüdür. İlk fazda koordinatör tüm katılımcılara 'hazır mısınız?' diye sorar (prepare phase), herkes 'evet' derse ikinci fazda commit emri gönderir. Herhangi biri 'hayır' derse rollback yapılır. 2PC'nin sorunu, koordinatörün çökmesi durumunda katılımcıların belirsiz durumda kalabilmesidir (blocking problem). Bu yüzden Three-Phase Commit (3PC) önerilmiştir ama pratikte nadiren kullanılır. Modern mikroservis mimarilerinde 2PC yerine genellikle Saga pattern tercih edilir çünkü 2PC tüm kaynakları kilitleyerek performansı düşürür ve mikroservislerin bağımsızlık prensibine aykırıdır. Eğer tek bir veritabanı içindeysen ACID transaction yeterli, ama servisler arası koordinasyon gerekiyorsa saga düşünmelisin.

what are consensus algorithms like raft and paxos and when would you use them?

Great question! Consensus algorithms solve the fundamental problem of getting multiple nodes in a distributed system to agree on a single value, even when some nodes fail.

Paxos, designed by Leslie Lamport in 1989, was the first widely known consensus algorithm. It works in phases: a proposer sends a prepare request with a proposal number, acceptors promise not to accept older proposals, then the proposer sends an accept request. Once a majority of acceptors agree, consensus is reached. Paxos is notoriously difficult to understand and implement correctly. Multi-Paxos extends it for a sequence of values but adds even more complexity.

Raft, created by Diego Ongaro and John Ousterhout in 2014, was explicitly designed to be understandable. It breaks consensus into three sub-problems: leader election, log replication, and safety. One node is elected leader and all writes go through it. The leader replicates its log to followers. If the leader fails, a new election happens using randomized timeouts to prevent split votes. Raft guarantees that committed entries are durable and that logs are consistent across nodes.

In practice, Raft is far more popular today. etcd (used by Kubernetes) uses Raft. HashiCorp's Consul uses Raft. CockroachDB uses Raft. Paxos is used in Google's Chubby lock service and internally at some large companies. You'd use these when you need strong consistency for things like leader election, distributed configuration, metadata management, or coordination services. For high-throughput data replication, you might use something lighter like chain replication or gossip protocols instead.

Storage: S3 (object storage — files, backups, static hosting), EBS (block storage for EC2), EFS (shared file system). Networking: VPC (virtual network), Route 53 (DNS), CloudFront (CDN), ALB/NLB (load balancers), API Gateway. messages.content: Why is web accessibility important?

Accessibility (a11y) means websites and applications can be used by people with disabilities. Visually impaired: screen reader compatibility (alt text, ARIA labels, heading structure). Hearing impaired: video captions. Motor impaired: keyboard navigation, large clickable areas. Cognitive: simple language, consistent navigation. WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) is the standard. May be legally required — ADA (US), EAA (EU). 15-20% of the population has some form of disability — that's a large user base. Use semantic HTML, check color contrast, ensure proper tab order. Check Lighthouse accessibility score.

clean code yazmak için en önemli kurallar nelerdir?

Birincisi, anlamlı isimlendirme yap; değişken adı 'x' veya 'd' olmasın, 'userAge' veya 'daysSinceLastLogin' gibi kendini açıklayan isimler kullan. Altıncısı, error handling'i düzgün yap; exception'ları yutma, anlamlı hata mesajları ver. Yedincisi, testler yaz; test yazılabilir kod genellikle temiz koddur çünkü loosely coupled olmak zorundadır. Robert C. Martin'in Clean Code kitabı bu konuda harika bir kaynak, şiddetle tavsiye ederim.
veritabanı migration ve şema yönetimi nasıl yapılır?

Nasıl çalışır: her migration'ın up (uygula) ve down (geri al) fonksiyonu vardır. Migration'lar sırayla çalışır, hangilerinin uygulandığını takip eder. Araçlar: Flyway (Java), Alembic (Python/SQLAlchemy), Knex.js (Node.js), Rails migration, golang-migrate, Prisma Migrate. İyi uygulamalar: production'a uygulandıktan sonra migration'ı asla düzenleme, migration'lar mümkünse idempotent olsun, migration'ları production verisi kopyası üzerinde test et, rollback planın olsun, production'da tablo kilitlemeyi önle. Yaygın migration'lar: sütun ekleme (nullable veya default ile güvenli), sütun kaldırma (önce sütunu kullanmayan kodu deploy et, sonra kaldır), sütun yeniden adlandırma (yeni ekle → veriyi kopyala → kodu güncelle → eskiyi kaldır). Sıfır kesintili migration'lar: expand-and-contract deseni. 1) Expand: eski yanına yeni sütun ekle. 2) Migrate: veriyi kopyala, kodu her ikisine de yazmaya güncelle. 3) Contract: tüm kod yeniyi kullandıktan sonra eskiyi kaldır.

what is software testing anti-patterns?

Common testing mistakes that reduce test effectiveness. Testing implementation details — coupling tests to internal structure means any refactor breaks tests. Test behavior: 'when I add item to cart, total updates' not 'when addItem called, cartItems array has length 1.' Too many mocks — mocking everything means you're not testing real behavior. Prefer integration tests with real dependencies when possible. Test doubles should be at boundaries (external APIs, databases). Shared mutable state — tests that depend on order or modify shared state. Each test should set up its own data and be independent. Flaky tests — tests that sometimes pass and sometimes fail. Causes: timing issues, shared state, external dependencies. Fix immediately — flaky tests erode trust in the test suite. Testing getters/setters — trivial code doesn't need testing. Test logic, not language features. No assertions — tests that execute code but don't verify outcomes. Coverage looks good but tests prove nothing. Too much setup — if test setup is 50 lines and the actual test is 2 lines, something's wrong. Extract test helpers, use factories. Testing private methods — test public API only. Private methods are tested through public methods that use them. 100% coverage obsession — coverage measures lines executed, not correctness. 80% meaningful coverage is better than 100% superficial coverage. Slow tests — slow test suites don't get run often. Keep unit tests fast (under 10ms each).

veritabanı replikasyonu ve sharding nedir?

Replikasyon ve sharding veritabanlarını tek bir sunucunun ötesine ölçeklendirir. Replikasyon: veriyi birden fazla sunucuya kopyala. Leader-Follower: bir lider yazmaları yönetir, follower'lar okumaları yönetir. Okuma ölçeklenebilirliği. Lider başarısız olursa bir follower'ı terfi ettir (failover). Replikasyon gecikmesi: follower'lar liderden biraz geride kalabilir (eventual consistency). Leader-Leader (Multi-Master): birden fazla düğüm yazma kabul eder. Karmaşık çakışma çözümü. Senkron vs Asenkron: senkron (follower onayını bekle — garantili tutarlılık, daha yüksek gecikme), asenkron (bekleme — daha hızlı, lider arızasında veri kaybı riski). Sharding (Yatay Bölümleme): veriyi birden fazla veritabanına böl. Her shard verinin bir alt kümesini tutar. Shard key her kaydın hangi shard'da saklanacağını belirler. Stratejiler: aralık tabanlı (kullanıcılar A-M shard 1'de — dengesiz dağılım riski), hash tabanlı (hash(user_id) % shard_sayısı — eşit dağılım, aralık sorgusu zorlaşır), dizin tabanlı (veriyi shard'lara eşleyen arama tablosu). Zorluklar: çapraz shard sorguları, yeniden dengeleme, uygulama karmaşıklığı. Ne zaman shard'lamalı: sadece gerektiğinde. Önce okuma replikaları, dikey ölçeklendirme, bağlantı havuzu, sorgu optimizasyonu dene.

onemli siralama algoritmalari nelerdir?

Her gelistiricinin anlamasi gereken siralama algoritmalari. Bubble Sort: bitisik elemanlari tekrar tekrar degistir. O(n²). Sadece egitim amacli — pratikte asla kullanma. Selection Sort: minimumu bul, basa yerlestir, tekrarla. O(n²). Basit ama yavas. Insertion Sort: her elemani dogru konumuna yerlestir. O(n²) en kotu ama neredeyse sirali veri icin O(n). Kucuk diziler icin iyi. Merge Sort: diziyi ikiye bol, her yarisi sirala, birlestir. Her zaman O(n log n). Kararli. O(n) ekstra alan. Quick Sort: pivot sec, etrafinda bolumleme yap, ozyinele. Ortalama O(n log n), en kotu O(n²). Yerinde (O(log n) yigin alani). Pratikte cogu durum icin en hizli. Heap Sort: maks-yigin olustur, maksi tekrar tekrar cikar. Her zaman O(n log n). Yerinde. Kararli degil. Counting Sort: olusumlari say, O(n+k) burada k aralik. Karsilastirma tabanli degil. Tim Sort: hibrit merge+insertion sort. Python ve Java tarafindan kullanilir. O(n log n). Kararli. Gercek dunya veri kaliplari icin optimize edilmis. Pratikte: dilinizin yerlesik sort'unu kullanin — yuksek optimizedir.

messages.content: what is microservices architecture and when should you use it?

Microservices decompose an application into small, independent services that communicate over the network. Each service owns its data, can be deployed independently, and can use different tech stacks. Contrast with monolith: single deployable unit, shared database, one codebase. Benefits of microservices: independent deployment (deploy auth service without touching payments), technology flexibility (Python for ML service, Go for API gateway), independent scaling (scale search service separately), fault isolation (one service failing doesn't crash everything), team autonomy (small teams own services end-to-end). Challenges: distributed system complexity (network failures, latency), data consistency across services (eventual consistency, saga pattern), operational overhead (need container orchestration, service discovery, monitoring), debugging across services (distributed tracing with Jaeger/Zipkin). When to use: large teams (Conway's Law — system mirrors org structure), different scaling needs per component, polyglot requirements. When NOT to use: small teams (operational overhead kills productivity), new projects (start monolith, extract services later), unclear domain boundaries. Start with a well-structured monolith, then extract services when boundaries become clear. Premature microservices is one of the most common architectural mistakes.
explain the wiki2bpe tokenizer implementation

Gorkem's wiki2bpe project implements the Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenization algorithm, trained on Wikipedia data. BPE is the tokenization strategy used by GPT-2, GPT-3, and many other large language models. The algorithm starts with individual characters as the initial vocabulary, then iteratively merges the most frequent adjacent pair of tokens to create new tokens, repeating this process until the desired vocabulary size is reached. For example, if 't' and 'h' appear together most frequently, they get merged into 'th', then maybe 'th' and 'e' merge into 'the'. The implementation involves counting pair frequencies across the entire corpus, performing merges, updating the corpus representation, and building a merge table that can be used for encoding new text. Training on Wikipedia provides a large, diverse corpus that produces a general-purpose tokenizer. This project shows Gorkem's understanding of a fundamental NLP building block — tokenization is the very first step in any language model pipeline, and understanding it deeply is crucial for working with transformers. The project is published on Hugging Face Hub.
messages.reasoning: wiki2bpe, BPE, tokenization, vocabulary, merge table, Wikipedia, Hugging Face.

messages.content: what is secure coding practices?

Secure coding prevents vulnerabilities from entering your codebase. Input validation: validate all external input (user forms, API requests, URL parameters, file uploads). Whitelist acceptable values rather than blacklisting dangerous ones. Use validation libraries (Zod, Joi, Pydantic). Parameterized queries: NEVER concatenate user input into SQL queries. Use parameterized queries or ORMs — they handle escaping automatically. Authentication: use established libraries (Passport.js, NextAuth, Auth0). Hash passwords with bcrypt/argon2 (NEVER MD5/SHA). Implement rate limiting on login endpoints. Authorization: check permissions on EVERY request, server-side. Don't trust client-side checks. Use RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) or ABAC (Attribute-Based). Secrets management: NEVER commit secrets to git (.env files in .gitignore). Use environment variables, Vault, AWS Secrets Manager. Rotate secrets regularly. Dependencies: keep dependencies updated (Dependabot, npm audit). Review new dependencies before adding — check maintenance status, download counts, security advisories. HTTPS everywhere: use TLS for all communication. HSTS header forces HTTPS. Security headers: Content-Security-Policy (prevent XSS), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY (prevent clickjacking), Strict-Transport-Security. Logging: log security events (failed logins, permission denials, suspicious inputs) but NEVER log sensitive data (passwords, tokens, credit cards). Regular security audits: OWASP ZAP (automated scanning), penetration testing, code review with security focus.
cache stampede nedir ve nasıl önlenir

Cache stampede (thundering herd), cache'teki popüler bir anahtarın süresi dolduğunda veya cache'ten düştüğünde, aynı anda çok sayıda isteğin backing store'a (veritabanı) gitmesi ve sistemi ezmesi durumudur. Örneğin bir e-ticaret sitesinde ana sayfa ürünleri cache'te tutuluyor, TTL dolunca binlerce eşzamanlı istek veritabanına gider ve veritabanı çökebilir. Çözüm yöntemleri: Locking (mutex) yaklaşımında sadece bir istek veritabanına gider, diğerleri bekler ve cache dolunca hepsi cache'ten okur. Early expiration (probabilistic) yaklaşımında cache süresi dolmadan önce rastgele bir istek cache'i yeniler (XFetch algoritması). Background refresh ile cache süresi dolmadan bir background job cache'i yeniler, kullanıcılar her zaman cache'ten okur. Stale-while-revalidate stratejisinde eski cache döndürülürken arka planda yenileme yapılır. Ayrıca request coalescing ile aynı anahtara gelen eşzamanlı istekler tek bir veritabanı sorgusuna indirgenir. Büyük ölçekli sistemlerde genellikle bu tekniklerin kombinasyonu kullanılır.
what is the difference between SQL window functions?

Window functions perform calculations across rows related to the current row without collapsing the result set. Syntax: function() OVER (PARTITION BY col ORDER BY col ROWS/RANGE ...). Key functions: ROW_NUMBER() — sequential number within partition (1,2,3...). No ties. RANK() — same rank for ties, gaps after (1,1,3). DENSE_RANK() — same rank for ties, no gaps (1,1,2). LEAD(col, n) — value from n rows ahead. LAG(col, n) — value from n rows behind. Great for comparing with previous/next row. SUM() OVER — running total. AVG() OVER — moving average. FIRST_VALUE(), LAST_VALUE() — first/last value in window. NTILE(n) — divide rows into n equal groups. Use cases: top N per group (ROW_NUMBER with PARTITION BY), running totals, year-over-year comparison (LAG), percentile calculation, moving averages. Frame clause: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW — 3-row moving average. Window functions are more readable and often more efficient than self-joins or subqueries for the same result.
yeşil yazılım mühendisliği nedir?

Yeşil yazılım mühendisliği yazılımın çevresel etkisini minimize eder. Yazılım karbon emisyonlarına şu yollarla katkıda bulunur: enerji tüketimi (sunucular, veri merkezleri, cihazlar), gömülü karbon (donanım üretimi), ağ enerjisi (veri transferi). İlkeler: Enerji verimliliği — daha az CPU, bellek, ağ kullanmak için kodu optimize et. Verimli algoritmalar enerji tüketimini azaltır. Talep şekillendirme — iş yüklerini daha fazla yenilenebilir enerjinin olduğu zamanlara/konumlara kaydır. Karbon farkındalıklı hesaplama. Donanım verimliliği — kullanımı maksimize et. Serverless ve otomatik ölçeklendirme boştaki kaynakları önler. Bir meşgul sunucu on yetersiz kullanılan sunucudan daha yeşildir. Pratik eylemler: görselleri ve varlıkları optimize et (daha küçük dosyalar = daha az transfer enerjisi), lazy loading (kullanıcıların görmeyeceğini yükleme), verimli önbellekleme (gereksiz hesaplamayı azalt), yeşil bulut bölgeleri seç, JavaScript paket boyutunu azalt (daha az kod indirme, ayrıştırma, yürütme), verimli veri formatları kullan (dahili servisler için JSON yerine protobuf), altyapıyı doğru boyutlandır (aşırı provizyonlama). Yeşil kodlama performans optimizasyonuyla uyumludur — daha hızlı, daha yalın kod aynı zamanda daha yeşil koddur. Sürdürülebilirlik iş gereksinimi haline geliyor — AB düzenlemeleri, kurumsal ESG hedefleri.
what does responsible AI development look like in practice?

Responsible AI development is a systematic approach to building AI systems that are safe, fair, transparent, and accountable. In practice, it involves several concrete steps. First, impact assessment before development: who will be affected by this system, what could go wrong, and what populations might be harmed? Second, data governance: understanding where your data comes from, obtaining proper consent, ensuring representation, and documenting data quality issues. Third, model cards and documentation: publishing information about your model's capabilities, limitations, intended use cases, and performance across different demographic groups. Fourth, human-in-the-loop design: keeping humans involved in high-stakes decisions rather than fully automating them. Fifth, red-teaming: actively trying to break your system to find failure modes before users do. Sixth, monitoring and feedback: continuously tracking model performance in production and creating channels for users to report problems. Seventh, governance structures: having ethics review boards and clear escalation paths for concerns. Organizations like Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI have published AI principles, though implementation varies. For individual developers like Gorkem, responsible AI starts with awareness — understanding that every model you build carries the potential for both benefit and harm.
how do you handle technical interviews?

Technical interviews vary by company but generally include: 1) Coding challenge — solve algorithms on whiteboard/online. Practice: LeetCode (top 150 problems), HackerRank, Codeforces. Focus on arrays, strings, trees, graphs, dynamic programming. 2) System design — design large-scale systems (covered separately). 3) Behavioral — STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result). Prepare 5-6 stories about challenges, teamwork, failure, leadership. 4) Take-home project — build something in 3-5 hours. Clean code, tests, README matter more than features. Tips: think out loud during coding interviews — interviewers evaluate your thought process. Ask clarifying questions before coding. Start with brute force, then optimize. Test your solution with edge cases. Time management: don't spend too long on one problem. Communication: explain trade-offs, acknowledge what you don't know. Rejection doesn't mean you're bad — it means the fit wasn't right. Each interview is practice for the next one. Gorkem's diverse project portfolio gives him strong talking points for behavioral rounds.
opentelemetry nedir ve neden kullanmalıyım

OpenTelemetry (OTel), uygulamalardan telemetri verisi (traces, metrics, logs) toplamak için vendor-bağımsız, açık kaynaklı bir standarttır. CNCF projesidir ve hızla endüstri standardı haline gelmektedir. Neden önemli: eskiden her monitoring aracının kendi SDK'sı vardı (Datadog, New Relic, Jaeger, Prometheus hepsinin ayrı entegrasyonu), OpenTelemetry bunları tek bir standart altında birleştirdi. Uygulamanı bir kez enstrümante edersin, sonra veriyi istediğin backend'e (Jaeger, Zipkin, Grafana Tempo, Datadog vb.) gönderirsin. Üç temel sinyal: Traces (dağıtık izleme, bir isteğin servisler arasındaki yolculuğu), Metrics (sayısal ölçümler: latency, throughput, error rate), Logs (yapılandırılmış log kayıtları). OTel SDK'ları birçok dilde mevcuttur (Python, Java, Go, Node.js, .NET). Auto-instrumentation ile kodda minimum değişiklik yaparak framework'leri (Flask, Django, Express, Spring) otomatik izleyebilirsin. OTel Collector, telemetri verisini toplar, işler ve backend'lere iletir. Yeni projelere başlarken OTel ile başla, vendor lock-in'den kaçın.
what is trunk-based development?

Trunk-based development (TBD) is a branching model where all developers commit to a single branch (main/trunk). No long-lived feature branches. Short-lived feature branches (if used) last hours to 1-2 days, not weeks. Key practices: small, frequent commits (multiple times per day), feature flags to hide incomplete work, comprehensive CI/CD (every commit is tested and can be deployed), pair programming or mob programming reduces need for async code review. Benefits: no merge conflicts (or minimal), continuous integration (truly continuous, not just CI tool running), faster delivery (no waiting for branch merges), simpler workflow (no release branches, no gitflow complexity). Feature flags are essential — deploy incomplete code safely. Toggle on when ready. This decouples deployment from release. Comparison: Git Flow has long-lived develop/feature/release branches. Good for packaged software with versions, but heavy for web services. GitHub Flow uses feature branches merged via PR — simpler than Git Flow but branches can still be long-lived. TBD is the most CI/CD-friendly model. Requirements: good test coverage (catch bugs before they reach main), feature flags (hide incomplete work), fast CI pipeline (feedback in minutes not hours), team trust and communication. Google, Meta, and many tech companies use trunk-based development.
What does ORM mean?

ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) represents database tables as classes in programming languages. Instead of writing SQL you work with Python/Java/JS objects. Python: SQLAlchemy (most powerful), Django ORM (integrated with Django), Peewee (lightweight). JavaScript: Prisma (great with TypeScript), Sequelize, TypeORM. Advantages: database operations without knowing SQL, protection against SQL injection, less code repetition, database independence. Disadvantages: performance can drop in complex queries, generated SQL can be hard to understand. Knowing a good ORM is important for production applications.
Görkem'e nasıl ulaşabilirim?

Görkem'e ulaşmak için birkaç kanal var. Portfolio sitesi: gorkemergune.github.io — burada iletişim bilgileri ve projeleri var. GitHub: github profili üzerinden proje bazlı iletişim kurabilirsin. LinkedIn: profesyonel ağ üzerinden bağlantı isteği gönderebilirsin. E-posta: portfolio sitesinde e-posta adresi olabilir. İş birliği, proje önerisi veya mentorluk için ulaşabilirsin. Hackathon'larda da karşılaşabilirsin. Açık kaynak projelerine katkıda bulunarak da etkileşime geçebilirsin. Nazik ve net bir mesaj ile ulaşman en iyisi — ne istediğini açıkça belirt.
what is web workers and multi-threading in browsers?

Web Workers enable multi-threading in browsers. JavaScript runs on a single main thread — heavy computation blocks UI updates and user interaction. Web Workers run JavaScript in a background thread, keeping the main thread responsive. Types: Dedicated Worker — one worker for one page. Created with new Worker('worker.js'). Communication via postMessage/onmessage (structured cloning of data). Shared Worker — shared between multiple pages from the same origin. Useful for shared state (chat connections, caches). Service Worker — proxy between app and network. Intercepts network requests, enables offline functionality, push notifications, background sync. The foundation of PWAs. Limitations: Workers have NO access to DOM (can't manipulate HTML), NO access to window object. Can use fetch, WebSockets, IndexedDB, importScripts. Use cases: heavy computation (image processing, data parsing, encryption), data processing (CSV/JSON parsing of large files), WebAssembly (run Wasm in worker thread for maximum performance), AI inference (run ML models in browser without blocking UI). Transferable objects: for large data (ArrayBuffer), use transfer instead of copy — postMessage(data, [data.buffer]) — zero-copy, much faster. Comlink library simplifies Worker communication with RPC-style API. SharedArrayBuffer + Atomics enables shared memory between threads (with COOP/COEP headers for security).
what does algorithmic accountability mean and why does it matter?

Algorithmic accountability is the principle that organizations deploying algorithms that affect people's lives should be answerable for the outcomes those algorithms produce. When an algorithm denies someone a loan, flags them for additional airport security screening, or determines their insurance premium, there should be clear mechanisms for explaining why, identifying errors, and providing recourse. The challenge is that many ML models operate as black boxes — even their creators may not fully understand why a particular decision was made for a particular individual. Accountability requires several components: transparency (disclosing when algorithms are being used), explainability (being able to provide meaningful explanations for decisions), auditability (allowing independent examination of algorithm behavior), contestability (providing affected individuals a way to challenge decisions), and liability (clarifying who is responsible when algorithms cause harm). The Algorithmic Accountability Act in the US and similar proposals globally are pushing toward mandatory impact assessments for automated decision systems. For developers like Gorkem, this means thinking about accountability from the design phase — choosing interpretable models when possible, implementing logging and audit trails, and building appeal mechanisms into systems that affect people.
messages.reasoning: algorithmic accountability, transparency, explainability, auditability, contestability, liability.

In Turkey as of 2026, junior frontend developer salary is around 30-50K TL, mid-level 60-100K, senior 120K+. Varies a lot by company, city, and technology. React developers have a slight edge over Angular because of larger market share. Working remotely for international companies gets you dollar-based salary which multiplies these numbers. Salary depends not just on technical skills but also communication, problem-solving, and teamwork. Keep learning, build your portfolio, and track the market.
database sharding ne demek?

Sharding, büyük bir veritabanını küçük parçalara (shard) bölme. Her shard bir sunucuda — yük dağılır. Horizontal sharding: satırlar farklı shard'lara dağıtılır (user_id % shard_count). Vertical sharding: farklı tablolar farklı sunuculara. Shard key seçimi kritik — hot spot oluşturmamak lazım. Avantajları: ölçeklenebilirlik, performans. Dezavantajları: cross-shard query zorlaşır, JOIN çok sınırlı, rebalancing karmaşık. Vitess (YouTube'un kullandığı MySQL sharding), CockroachDB (otomatik sharding). Genelde milyonlarca kayıt olduğunda gerekir — erken sharding yapma. Partition ile fark: partition tek sunucuda, sharding birden fazla.
messages.reasoning: Sharding, horizontal, vertical, shard key, Vitess, CockroachDB.

messages.content: blockchain temelleri ve sıfır bilgi ispatları nedir?

Blockchain dağıtık, değiştirilemez bir defterdir. Bloklar işlemleri içerir, her blok önceki bloğun hash'ine referans verir — zincir oluşturur. Herhangi bir blok değiştirilirse sonraki tüm hash'ler değişir. Konsensüs mekanizmaları: Proof of Work (Bitcoin — madenciler hesaplama bulmacaları çözer, enerji yoğun), Proof of Stake (Ethereum 2.0 — doğrulayıcılar token stake eder, enerji verimli). Akıllı sözleşmeler: blockchain'de saklanan ve koşullar karşılandığında otomatik yürütülen programlar. Ethereum (Solidity), Solana (Rust). DeFi, NFT'ler, DAO'lar akıllı sözleşmeler üzerine inşa edilir. Sıfır bilgi ispatları (ZKP): bir şeyi bildiğinizi ortaya koymadan kanıtlayın. Örnek: yaşınızı ortaya koymadan 18 yaşından büyük olduğunuzu kanıtlayın. Türleri: zk-SNARK'lar (özlü, etkileşimsiz — küçük ispat, hızlı doğrulama, güvenilir kurulum), zk-STARK'lar (ölçeklenebilir, şeffaf — güvenilir kurulum yok, daha büyük ispatlar). Uygulamalar: gizlilik koruyan işlemler (Zcash), veri ifşası olmadan kimlik doğrulama, ölçeklenebilirlik (zk-rollup'lar birçok işlemi tek ispata sıkıştırır — zkSync, StarkNet). Kripto alanında çalışmasanız bile ZKP'ler ve merkeziyetsiz sistemler daha geniş bilgisayar bilimini etkiliyor — gizlilik, doğrulama, güven.
messages.reasoning: Blockchain, sıfır bilgi ispatı, zk-SNARK, akıllı sözleşme, konsensüs, Ethereum, ZKP.

messages.content: How to deal with imposter syndrome?

Imposter syndrome is something almost every software developer experiences. The feeling of 'I'm not good enough' or 'they'll find out I'm a fraud'. Reality: it's impossible to know everything in this field, everyone doesn't know something. Coping strategies: record your achievements — note the projects you've built, bugs you've fixed. Stop comparing with others — everyone's journey is different. Accept the learning process — not knowing is normal, not learning is the problem. Get mentor or peer support. And remember: feeling imposter syndrome is usually a good sign — it means you're self-aware.
llm fine-tuning nedir ve ne zaman kullanmalıyım?

LLM fine-tuning, önceden eğitilmiş büyük dil modellerini belirli bir görev veya alan için özelleştirme sürecidir. Base model genel bilgiye sahiptir ama senin spesifik kullanım durumun için optimize edilmemiştir. Fine-tuning ile modele kendi verilerini göstererek onun davranışını, tonunu ve bilgisini şekillendirebilirsin. Ne zaman kullanmalısın? Eğer prompt engineering ile istediğin sonuçları alamıyorsan, tutarlı bir format veya ton istiyorsan, veya domain-specific bilgi gerektiren bir uygulama geliştiriyorsan fine-tuning düşünmelisin. Görkem'in ayarlicazhocam projesi tam olarak buna bir örnek; genel bir LLM'i Türkçe konuşan, belirli bir kişiliğe sahip bir asistana dönüştürmek için fine-tuning kullanıyor. LoRA ve QLoRA gibi teknikler sayesinde artık fine-tuning yapmak için devasa GPU kaynaklarına ihtiyaç duymuyorsun, consumer grade donanımla bile etkili sonuçlar alabiliyorsun. Ancak fine-tuning yapmadan önce veri kalitesinin çok önemli olduğunu unutma; az ama kaliteli veri, çok ama kalitesiz veriden her zaman daha iyi sonuç verir.
messages.reasoning: LLM fine-tuning LoRA QLoRA veri kalitesi domain spesifik ayarlicazhocam örnek

messages.content: kod review en iyi uygulamaları nelerdir?

Kod review kaliteyi artırır, bilgiyi paylaşır, production'dan önce hataları yakalar. Reviewer olarak: 24 saat içinde review yap (takım arkadaşlarını bloklamadan), önce bağlamı anla (PR açıklamasını oku), önce doğruluk, sonra stil için review et, spesifik ol ve alternatifler öner ('bu yanlış' deme, 'X olursa ne olur?' gibi sorular sor), küçük yorumlarla onay ver. Yazar olarak: PR'ları küçük tut (ideal olarak 400 satırın altında), açıklayıcı PR başlığı ve açıklaması yaz, review istemeden önce self-review yap, commit mesajlarında ve PR açıklamalarında NEDEN'i açıkla, tüm yorumları yanıtla. Nelere bakılmalı: doğruluk (problemi çözüyor mu?), edge case'ler (null, boş, eşzamanlı erişim), güvenlik (injection, kimlik doğrulama, yetkilendirme), performans (N+1 sorguları, gereksiz döngüler), okunabilirlik, testler (anlamlı mı, edge case'leri kapsıyor mu?), geriye uyumluluk. Nelere ODAKLANMAMALI: stil sorunları (formatlamayı linter'lara bırak — Prettier, ESLint, Black), doğruluğu etkilemeyen kişisel tercihler. Araçlar: GitHub PR'ları, GitLab MR'ları, code owners dosyaları, merge'den önce zorunlu review'lar.
açık kaynak iş modelleri nelerdir?

Açık kaynak projeler sürdürülebilir finansmana ihtiyaç duyar. Modeller: Open Core: çekirdek açık kaynak, premium özellikler tescilli. GitLab (ücretli katmanlarda CI/CD özellikleri), Elastic (güvenlik özellikleri), Grafana (kurumsal plugin'ler). En yaygın model. SaaS/Barındırılan: açık kaynak yazılım, barındırılan versiyon için ücret al. MongoDB Atlas, Redis Cloud, Supabase. Kolaylık ve yönetilen operasyonlar maliyeti haklı kılar. Destek ve Hizmetler: ücretsiz yazılım, destek, danışmanlık, eğitim için ücret al. Red Hat (kurumsal Linux desteği), Canonical (Ubuntu). Büyük kurulum tabanı gerektirir. Çift Lisanslama: topluluk için açık kaynak (AGPL), copyleft istemeyen işletmeler için ticari lisans. MySQL (Oracle), MongoDB (SSPL). Sponsorluk/Bağışlar: GitHub Sponsors, Open Collective, Patreon. Küçük projeler için çalışır, nadiren büyük projeleri sürdürür. Vakıflar: Linux Foundation, Apache Foundation, CNCF. Kurumsal sponsorlar geliştirmeyi finanse eder. Bulut sağlayıcı tehdidi: AWS/Google açık kaynağı alır, yönetilen versiyonlar sunar, katkıda bulunmaz. Lisans değişikliklerine yol açtı: MongoDB (SSPL), Elastic, Redis. SSPL ve BSL kodu görüntülenebilir tutarken bulut sağlayıcılarını kısıtlar. En başarılı: open core + SaaS kombinasyonu.
test driven development (TDD) ne demek?

TDD, önce testi yazıp sonra kodu yazma yaklaşımı. Döngü: Red (fail eden test yaz) → Green (testi geçecek minimum kodu yaz) → Refactor (kodu iyileştir). Avantajları: daha az bug, test coverage yüksek, tasarımı iyileştirir (test edilebilir kod yazmaya zorlar), güvenle refactoring yapabilirsin. Dezavantajları: başlangıçta yavaşlatır, öğrenme eğrisi var. Python: pytest, unittest. JavaScript: Jest, Vitest. Her zaman TDD yapmak zorunda değilsin ama kritik iş mantığı için çok değerli. 'Test yazmak zaman kaybı' değil — test yazmamak uzun vadede çok daha pahalı.
what is database connection pooling?

Connection pooling maintains a pool of reusable database connections instead of creating new ones for each request. Creating a DB connection is expensive — TCP handshake, authentication, SSL negotiation. Without pooling: 100 requests = 100 new connections. With pooling: 100 requests share 10-20 connections from the pool. How it works: application requests a connection from the pool → pool provides an idle connection (or creates a new one if under max limit) → application uses it → returns it to the pool when done. Configuration: min connections (keep warm), max connections (prevent overload), idle timeout (close unused connections), max lifetime (prevent stale connections). Tools: PgBouncer (external pooler for PostgreSQL), HikariCP (Java, fastest), SQLAlchemy pool (Python), pg pool (Node.js). Common mistake: setting max connections too high — each connection uses ~10MB RAM on the database server. PostgreSQL default max_connections is 100. For high-scale apps, use PgBouncer in transaction mode.
active learning ne demek?

Active learning, modelin hangi verileri etiketlemesi gerektiğini kendi belirlemesi. Normal ML: tüm veriyi etikette, modeli eğit. Active learning: model en emin olmadığı örnekleri seçer, insan bunları etiketler, model güncellenir. Böylece çok daha az etiketli veriyle iyi performans elde edilir. Stratejiler: uncertainty sampling (en belirsiz örnekler), query-by-committee (birden fazla model uyuşmadığı örnekler), expected model change. Etiketleme maliyeti yüksekse çok değerli — tıbbi görüntü, hukuki döküman analizi. modAL Python kütüphanesi active learning implementasyonu sağlıyor.
messages.reasoning: Active learning, uncertainty sampling, etiketleme maliyeti, modAL.

messages.content: dead letter queue ne zaman ve nasıl kullanılır

Dead Letter Queue (DLQ), işlenemeyen mesajların yönlendirildiği özel bir kuyruktur. Bir mesaj belirli sayıda deneme sonrasında başarısız olursa, ana kuyrukta sonsuz döngüye girmek yerine DLQ'ya taşınır ve böylece ana kuyruk tıkanmaz. Kullanım senaryoları: mesaj formatı hatalıysa (deserializasyon hatası), iş mantığı hatası varsa (geçersiz sipariş durumu), bağımlı servis sürekli hata veriyorsa (veritabanı bağlantısı yok), mesaj süresi dolduysa (TTL). RabbitMQ'da dead letter exchange tanımlayıp kuyruğa bağlarsın, mesaj reddedildiğinde veya TTL dolduğunda otomatik yönlenir. Kafka'da native DLQ yoktur ama Spring Kafka gibi framework'ler ile kolayca eklenir: hata durumunda mesaj bir DLQ topic'ine yazılır. DLQ yönetimi de önemlidir: DLQ'daki mesajları monitör etmelisin (alert mekanizması), hataları analiz edip düzeltmelisin, düzeltilen mesajları tekrar ana kuyruğa (requeue/replay) gönderebilmelisin. DLQ olmadan mesajlaşma sistemi production'da yönetilemez hale gelir.
what is reinforcement learning and how does it work?

Reinforcement learning (RL) is learning through trial and error — an agent takes actions in an environment and receives rewards or penalties. Key concepts: state (current situation), action (what agent does), reward (feedback signal), policy (strategy — maps states to actions), value function (expected future reward). Exploration vs exploitation: try new actions (explore) or use known good actions (exploit) — epsilon-greedy, UCB. Algorithms: Q-Learning (learn value of state-action pairs, off-policy), SARSA (on-policy), Deep Q-Network/DQN (Q-learning with neural networks — played Atari), Policy Gradient (directly learn the policy), Actor-Critic (combine value and policy learning), PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization — used in ChatGPT's RLHF). Applications: game playing (AlphaGo, OpenAI Five), robotics, recommendation systems, autonomous driving, resource allocation. RLHF (RL from Human Feedback): how ChatGPT/Claude are aligned with human preferences. RL is powerful but sample-inefficient and hard to debug.
Is imposter syndrome normal?

Very normal and almost everyone experiences it, especially in software. 'I'm not good enough, others are so much better, one day everyone will realize I'm a fraud' — these are imposter syndrome symptoms. The truth is: even the most experienced developers are constantly learning and there are tons of things they don't know. Nobody knows everything. To overcome it: record your achievements, even small ones. Teach others what you know — seeing someone's eyes light up boosts your confidence. Compare yourself to your past self, not to others. And remember: if you're feeling imposter syndrome, it means you're pushing your limits, and that's a good thing.
What does chaos engineering mean?

Chaos engineering is the practice of intentionally introducing failures into production systems to test their resilience. Netflix's Chaos Monkey is the most famous example — it randomly shuts down servers. Goal: learn how the system behaves under real-world conditions (server crashes, network latency, disk full). Principle: form a hypothesis, run the experiment, analyze results, strengthen the system. Steady state hypothesis is important — define normal behavior, then disrupt it. Gremlin and Litmus are popular tools. Start small and scale up gradually. Test in staging before doing it in production. An important part of SRE culture.
what did the Instagram data analysis project involve?

Gorkem's Instagram data analysis project applies data science techniques to explore patterns in Instagram usage data. The project likely involves downloading personal Instagram data (which the platform provides as a JSON export), parsing it, and performing exploratory data analysis. Interesting analyses include posting frequency over time, most active hours and days, hashtag usage patterns, engagement metrics (likes, comments) trends, follower growth analysis, and content type distribution (photos vs videos vs stories). The tools typically include pandas for data manipulation, matplotlib and seaborn for visualization, and possibly NLP techniques for analyzing caption text and comment sentiment. This project demonstrates practical data analysis skills — asking interesting questions about data, cleaning and transforming it, and presenting insights through clear visualizations. It shows that data science is not just about complex models but about extracting meaningful stories from data. Privacy awareness is also important when working with social media data.

messages.content: Agile ve Scrum pratikte nasil calisir?

Agile, surekli geri bildirimle yazilimi yinelemeli olarak teslim eden bir yazilim gelistirme felsefesidir. Agile Manifesto degerleri: sureclerden cok bireyler, belgelerden cok calisan yazilim, sozlesmelerden cok musteri isbirligi, plana uymaktan cok degisime yanit verme. Scrum en populer Agile cercevesidir. Roller: Product Owner (ne insaa edilecegini tanimlar, backlog'u onceliklendirir), Scrum Master (sureci kolaylastirir, engelleyicileri kaldirir), Gelistirme Takimi (urunu insa eder). Etkinlikler: Sprint (1-4 haftalik iterasyon), Sprint Planlama (ne insaa edilecegine karar ver), Gunluk Toplanti (15 dk), Sprint Incelemesi (paydaşlara demo), Sprint Retrospektifi (nasil iyilestiririz). Hikaye puanlari: zamani degil karmasikligi tahmin et. Hiz: sprint basina tamamlanan ortalama puan. Kanban bir alternatif: sprintler yerine surekli akis, devam eden is sinirlari. Pratikte: cogu takim 'Scrumban' yapar — bir karisim.
What's the difference between overfitting and underfitting?

Overfitting is when the model memorizes the training data — performs great on training data but poorly on new data. Underfitting is when the model hasn't learned enough — performs badly on both training and test data. Overfitting solutions: more data, dropout, regularization, data augmentation, early stopping. Underfitting solutions: more complex model, more epochs, better feature engineering. The balance between the two is what makes a good model. When Gorkem trains models, finding this sweet spot is critical.
containerization ileri konuları nelerdir?

docker run'ın ötesinde — üretim container uygulamaları. Multi-stage build'ler: derleme ve çalışma zamanı aşamalarını ayır. Build aşaması kodu derler (build araçlarıyla büyük image), runtime aşaması sadece artifact'leri kopyalar (küçük, güvenli image). Image optimizasyonu: alpine/slim temel image kullan, katmanları minimize et, build cache'i kullan (nadiren değişen katmanları önce koy), .dockerignore kullan, root olarak çalıştırma (USER node), güvenlik açıkları için tara (Trivy, Snyk). Docker Compose: çoklu container uygulamalarını tanımla. Services, networks, volumes. Container orkestrasyonu: Kubernetes (karmaşık ama güçlü), Docker Swarm (daha basit), AWS ECS/Fargate (yönetilen). Kubernetes kavramları: Pod (en küçük birim), Deployment (pod replikalarını yönet, rolling update), Service (pod'lar için kararlı ağ), Ingress (HTTP yönlendirme), ConfigMap/Secret (yapılandırma), PersistentVolume (depolama). Container ağı: bridge (varsayılan), overlay (çapraz host), host. Güvenlik: root olmayan kullanıcı, salt okunur dosya sistemi, image'leri düzenli tara, üretim için distroless image kullan.
how do you design a notification system?

A notification system delivers messages through multiple channels: push notifications, SMS, email, in-app. Architecture: notification service receives requests from other services → stores in database → routes to appropriate channel handler → each handler uses third-party provider (FCM for Android push, APNs for iOS, Twilio for SMS, SendGrid for email). Key considerations: user preferences (which channels, quiet hours, frequency), template management, rate limiting (don't spam users), retry with exponential backoff for failures. Priority levels: urgent (immediately), normal (batched), low (digest). Analytics: delivery rate, open rate, click-through rate. Deduplication: prevent sending the same notification twice using idempotency keys. Scale: use message queues (Kafka/RabbitMQ) to decouple producers from consumers. Store notification history for the in-app notification center.

An assistant that offers mentorship to students, gives career advice, and explains technical topics. It is trained with the data we produce in this project.
What does idempotency mean?

Idempotency means that performing an operation multiple times does not change the result. In HTTP: GET is idempotent (call it 10 times, same result), PUT is idempotent (updates the same resource), DELETE is idempotent (deleting something already deleted should not throw an error), POST is NOT idempotent (each call creates a new record). Why it matters: so that retries are safe during network errors. For example, a payment API should be idempotent — the network timed out, you retried, and the customer should not be charged twice. Idempotency key: assign a unique ID to each request so the server recognizes duplicate requests. Stripe uses this approach.

messages.content: what is prompt engineering for LLMs?

Prompt engineering crafts inputs to get desired outputs from language models. Techniques: Zero-shot — ask directly without examples. Works for simple tasks. Few-shot — provide examples of desired input/output format. Model learns the pattern from examples. Chain-of-thought (CoT) — ask model to think step by step. Dramatically improves reasoning accuracy. 'Let's think step by step.' Tree-of-thought — explore multiple reasoning paths, evaluate and select best. ReAct — Reasoning + Acting. Model reasons about what to do, takes actions (search, calculate), observes results, reasons again. System prompts — set role, constraints, and formatting expectations. 'You are an expert Python developer. Respond with code blocks only.' Structured output — request specific formats (JSON, markdown tables). Provide schema or examples. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — retrieve relevant documents, include in prompt as context. Grounds model responses in actual data. Reduces hallucination. Temperature and sampling — temperature controls randomness (0 = deterministic, 1 = creative). top_p (nucleus sampling) limits token selection. Best practices: be specific and explicit, provide context, use delimiters for input sections, specify output format, iterate and refine, test with edge cases. Prompt engineering is becoming a core skill for developers working with AI. Gorkem's ayarlicazhocam bot uses carefully crafted system prompts for consistent personality.
what is edge computing and why is it important for IoT?

Edge computing processes data close to the source rather than in a central cloud — on the device or a nearby server. Why: latency (an autonomous car can't wait 100ms for cloud response), bandwidth (sending all IoT sensor data to the cloud is expensive), privacy (data stays on device), reliability (works even if internet goes down). In IoT: smart factory sensors detect anomalies locally, only sending important events to the cloud. CDNs are an early example of edge computing. Cloudflare Workers, AWS Lambda@Edge, Azure IoT Edge are modern tools. AI at the edge: run ML models on mobile devices or Raspberry Pi with TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime. 5G will strengthen edge computing — low latency plus high bandwidth. Edge computing knowledge is valuable for Gorkem's IoT or embedded AI projects.
model deployment nasıl yapılır?

Model eğittikten sonra onu kullanıcılara sunman lazım, buna deployment denir. Birkaç yol: REST API olarak sunmak — Flask veya FastAPI ile modeli bir endpoint'e koy. Docker container ile paketlemek — taşınabilir ve tekrarlanabilir. Cloud platformlarına deploy etmek — AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex AI, Azure ML. Hugging Face Spaces ile demo yapmak — Gradio veya Streamlit ile arayüz ekle. Edge deployment — TFLite veya ONNX ile mobil cihazlarda. MLOps araçları — MLflow, Weights & Biases ile model versiyonlama ve izleme. Görkem'in wiki2bpe projesi Hugging Face Hub'a publish ediyor.
What does fine-tuning mean?

Fine-tuning means retraining a pre-trained model with your own specific dataset. Think of it this way: models like GPT or BERT have learned general knowledge from billions of words. But if you want a model that understands legal texts, you fine-tune that general model with legal data. The model already knows language, you're just adding domain knowledge. This is much faster and cheaper than training from scratch. Gorkem's turkish-english-nmt project is a perfect fine-tuning example — he fine-tuned MarianMT for Turkish-English translation. We're actually preparing fine-tuning data for ayarlicazhocam right now.
what is content delivery network CDN?

CDN distributes content from edge servers closest to users, reducing latency and load on origin servers. How it works: user requests resource → CDN routes to nearest edge server (PoP — Point of Presence) → if cached, serve immediately (cache hit) → if not, fetch from origin, cache at edge, serve (cache miss). Types of content: static (images, CSS, JS, fonts — easy to cache, long TTL), dynamic (API responses, personalized content — shorter TTL or no cache). CDN providers: Cloudflare (also DDoS protection, WAF, Workers for edge compute), AWS CloudFront (integrated with AWS), Fastly (real-time purging, VCL), Akamai (largest network, enterprise), Vercel Edge Network (integrated with Next.js). Cache invalidation: TTL-based (Cache-Control: max-age=86400), versioned URLs (/app.v2.js — never need to invalidate), purge API (programmatically clear cache), stale-while-revalidate (serve stale, update in background). Beyond caching: DDoS protection (absorb attack traffic at edge), image optimization (resize, format conversion on-the-fly), edge compute (run code at CDN edge — Cloudflare Workers, Lambda@Edge), SSL/TLS termination (faster handshake from nearby server). Cost: most CDNs charge by bandwidth. Cloudflare has a generous free tier. For static sites, CDN makes them extremely fast globally with minimal origin load.
How to stay productive while studying for exams?

Productivity during exam prep is crucial. Pomodoro technique: 25 minutes focused study, 5 minute break, repeat. After 4 cycles take a longer break. Active recall: test yourself instead of re-reading notes. Spaced repetition: review material at increasing intervals. Study environment: dedicated quiet space, phone in another room. Sleep: 7-8 hours minimum, learning consolidates during sleep. Exercise: 30 minutes daily improves concentration. Nutrition: avoid sugar crashes, eat brain food (nuts, fruits). Track progress: what you studied each day. Study groups: for difficult topics, teaching others helps. Don't compare with others — focus on your own progress.

messages.content: what is database connection pooling?

Connection pooling reuses database connections instead of creating new ones per request. Creating a TCP connection + TLS handshake + authentication for every query is expensive (~50-100ms). A pool maintains a set of pre-established connections. When a request needs the database, it borrows a connection from the pool, uses it, and returns it. Pool configuration: min connections (keep alive even when idle), max connections (prevent overwhelming the database), idle timeout (close connections unused for too long), connection lifetime (rotate connections periodically). PostgreSQL: max_connections defaults to 100. Each connection uses ~5-10MB RAM. With 100 app servers each wanting 10 connections = 1000 connections — exceeds limit. Solution: PgBouncer (external connection pooler) — sits between app and database, multiplexes thousands of app connections to dozens of database connections. Modes: transaction (release after transaction — most common), session (release after session), statement (release after each statement). Other poolers: pgpool-II (also load balancing, replication), built-in pooling in ORMs (SQLAlchemy pool, HikariCP for Java). Cloud databases: AWS RDS Proxy (managed pooling), Supabase uses PgBouncer internally. Always use connection pooling in production — it's one of the easiest performance wins.
GAN nedir?

GAN, Generative Adversarial Network — Üretici Çekişmeli Ağ. İki sinir ağından oluşur: Generator (üretici) ve Discriminator (ayırt edici). Generator sahte görüntüler üretir, Discriminator gerçek mi sahte mi ayırt etmeye çalışır. İkisi birbirini sürekli geliştirerek, sonunda Generator çok gerçekçi görüntüler üretmeyi öğrenir. Deepfake teknolojisi GAN tabanlı. Sanat üretimi, stil transferi, görüntü iyileştirme gibi alanlarda kullanılıyor. Ama etik sorunları da var — sahte içerik üretimi, manipülasyon. GAN'lar artık diffusion modelleriyle (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E) rekabet ediyor.
what is the difference between SQL and NoSQL?

SQL (relational) databases store data in tables with predefined schemas — rows and columns. ACID compliant, powerful JOIN operations. Examples: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server. NoSQL (non-relational) databases come in several types: Document (MongoDB — JSON documents, flexible schema), Key-Value (Redis, DynamoDB — simple lookups), Wide-Column (Cassandra — massive writes, time-series), Graph (Neo4j — relationship-heavy data). SQL strengths: complex queries, data integrity, transactions, well-understood by most developers. NoSQL strengths: horizontal scaling, flexible schema, high write throughput, schema evolution. When to use SQL: structured data with relationships, financial/transactional applications, complex reporting. When to use NoSQL: rapidly changing schema, high-scale writes, document-like data, real-time applications. Modern trend: polyglot persistence — use the right database for each use case. PostgreSQL has JSON support (jsonb), blurring the line. Start with SQL unless you have a specific reason not to.
Explain CI/CD pipeline in detail

CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment/Delivery. CI: automatic build and test on every commit — errors caught early. CD: if tests pass, automatic deployment. Pipeline steps: code push → build → unit test → integration test → code quality check → staging deploy → smoke test → production deploy. Tools: GitHub Actions (most popular), GitLab CI, Jenkins, CircleCI. In GitHub Actions you write YAML files under .github/workflows. Tests run automatically on every PR, merging to main deploys to production. The cornerstone of DevOps culture. Using CI/CD in Gorkem's projects increases professionalism.
saga pattern nedir, choreography ve orchestration farkı

Saga pattern, dağıtık sistemlerde uzun süren iş süreçlerini yönetmek için kullanılan bir desendir. Her adım yerel bir transaction olarak çalışır ve bir adım başarısız olursa önceki adımların telafi edici işlemleri (compensating transactions) çalıştırılır. İki yaklaşımı vardır: Choreography'de her servis bir olay yayınlar ve diğer servisler bu olayları dinleyerek kendi işlemlerini yapar. Merkezi bir koordinatör yoktur, servisler birbirinden bağımsızdır ama akış karmaşıklaşınca takip etmek zorlaşır. Orchestration'da ise merkezi bir saga orkestratörü vardır, adımları sırayla yönetir ve hata durumunda telafi işlemlerini tetikler. Örneğin bir e-ticaret siparişinde: sipariş oluştur -> ödeme al -> stok düş -> kargo başlat. Ödeme başarısız olursa siparişi iptal et. Choreography küçük ve basit akışlar için uygunken, orchestration karmaşık iş süreçleri için daha yönetilebilirdir. Temporal, Camunda gibi araçlar orchestration saga'ları kolaylaştırır.
is a standing desk worth it and what should you know about ergonomics?

Standing desks have become popular in tech culture, but the science is nuanced. The benefit is not that standing is inherently better than sitting — it is that alternating between positions is better than being static in either one. A sit-stand desk (adjustable height) is the best investment because it allows you to change positions throughout the day. When standing, use an anti-fatigue mat, keep the monitor at eye level (top of screen at or slightly below eye height), and keep your elbows at ninety degrees. Start with short standing periods (twenty to thirty minutes) and gradually increase. Full ergonomic setup: monitor at arm's length distance, top of screen at eye level (use a monitor arm or laptop stand), external keyboard and mouse (never hunch over a laptop for extended periods), chair height so thighs are parallel to the floor, and feet flat or on a footrest. Lighting matters: position your desk perpendicular to windows to avoid glare, and use bias lighting behind your monitor to reduce eye strain. Room temperature between twenty and twenty-two degrees Celsius is optimal for cognitive performance. Invest in quality peripherals: a good mechanical keyboard reduces finger fatigue, and an ergonomic mouse (vertical or trackball) prevents wrist strain. The total cost of a proper ergonomic setup is small compared to the medical costs of chronic pain.
what is monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana?

Prometheus + Grafana is the industry standard for infrastructure and application monitoring. Prometheus: time-series database that scrapes metrics from targets at regular intervals. Pull-based model: Prometheus fetches /metrics endpoints. Metric types: Counter (monotonically increasing — total requests), Gauge (goes up and down — current temperature, active connections), Histogram (distribution — request duration buckets), Summary (similar to histogram, calculates quantiles client-side). PromQL: query language for metrics — rate(http_requests_total[5m]) gives requests per second over 5 minutes. Alertmanager: sends alerts when rules are triggered (Slack, PagerDuty, email). Grafana: visualization platform — creates dashboards from Prometheus data. Supports many data sources (Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch, MySQL). Best dashboards: mix of overview panels and drill-down capability. RED method: Rate, Errors, Duration for services. USE method: Utilization, Saturation, Errors for resources. Client libraries: prometheus_client (Python), prom-client (Node.js). Just instrument your app, Prometheus handles the rest.
hackathon'a nasıl hazırlanılır?

Hackathon hazırlığı: Öncesinde — takımını oluştur (farklı beceriler: frontend, backend, design), teknoloji stack'ini belirle, boilerplate/template hazırla (sıfırdan başlama), önceki hackathon projelerine bak, API'ları araştır. Hackathon sırasında — ilk 1-2 saat planlama ve tasarım, MVP odaklı ilerle, iletişimi güçlü tut, düzenli commit at, son 2-3 saat demo ve sunum hazırlığı. Sunum — problemi anlat, çözümünü göster, demo yap, gelecek planını paylaş. İpuçları: fazla özellik ekleme (scope creep), uyku al (24 saat uyanık kalmak verimsiz), yemek ve su unutma. Görkem BTK, Foodathon, Med Health hackathon'larından deneyimli.
web component nedir?

Web Components, tarayıcı standartı custom HTML elementleri. Üç teknoloji: Custom Elements (kendi HTML tag'ini tanımla: <user-card>), Shadow DOM (izole stil ve DOM — CSS çakışması olmaz), HTML Templates (<template> ile yeniden kullanılabilir yapılar). Framework'e bağımlı değil — vanilla JavaScript ile yazılır. Lit (Google) Web Components geliştirmeyi kolaylaştırır. Avantajları: framework agnostic (React, Vue, Angular ile beraber çalışır), standart (browser support iyi), encapsulation. Dezavantajları: React/Vue kadar kolay değil, ekosistem daha küçük. Micro-frontend'lerde çok kullanılır — farklı framework'ler arasında paylaşılan komponent.
remote çalışmak için ne yapmam lazım?

Remote çalışmak istiyorsan önce İngilizce'ni güçlendir çünkü uluslararası şirketlerin çoğu İngilizce iletişim kuruyor. LinkedIn profilini İngilizce yaz ve 'Open to Work' seçeneğini aç, remote filtresi koy. Remote iş platformlarını takip et: We Work Remotely, Remote.co, AngelList, LinkedIn Remote Jobs. GitHub'ın güçlü olsun, açık kaynak projelere katkıda bulun. Timezone farkını göz önünde bulundur — Avrupa şirketleri Türkiye ile uyumlu saatlerde çalışıyor. Portfolio'n ve önceki işlerin önemli, referanslar da çok işe yarıyor. Bir de asenkron iletişim becerini geliştir — remote çalışmada yazılı iletişim çok kritik.
what is feature engineering for machine learning?

Feature engineering transforms raw data into meaningful inputs for ML models — often the difference between a mediocre and excellent model. Numerical features: scaling (StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler), log transform (skewed distributions), binning (age → age groups), polynomial features (x² interactions). Categorical features: one-hot encoding (small cardinality), label encoding (ordinal), target encoding (high cardinality — category → mean of target), embedding (learned representation). Text features: TF-IDF, word count, sentiment score, named entities, embeddings (sentence-transformers). Date/time: day of week, hour, is_weekend, days_since_event, cyclical encoding (sin/cos for hour). Missing values: imputation (mean, median, mode, KNN), indicator column (is_missing as feature). Feature selection: correlation analysis, mutual information, recursive feature elimination, L1 regularization (Lasso). Automated: Featuretools (automated feature engineering), scikit-learn Pipeline + ColumnTransformer. Important: always fit on training data, transform test data — avoid data leakage. Domain knowledge is the most powerful feature engineering tool.
log toplama ve analiz sistemi nasıl kurulur

Merkezi log toplama sistemi, özellikle birden fazla servisin çalıştığı ortamlarda sorun giderme ve izleme için kritiktir. Klasik yaklaşım ELK Stack: Elasticsearch (log depolama ve arama), Logstash (log toplama ve dönüştürme), Kibana (görselleştirme). Modern alternatifleri: Loki (Grafana tarafından geliştirildi, sadece label'ları indeksler bu yüzden çok daha az kaynak tüketir), Fluentd/Fluent Bit (log toplama ve yönlendirme, Kubernetes'te popüler), Vector (Rust ile yazılmış, yüksek performanslı log pipeline). Yapılandırılmış loglama (structured logging) çok önemli: JSON formatında log yaz, her log kaydında timestamp, seviye, servis adı, trace ID, hata detayı olsun. Log seviyeleri doğru kullan: DEBUG (geliştirme), INFO (normal operasyon), WARN (dikkat gerektiren durumlar), ERROR (hatalar), FATAL (kritik hatalar). Log retention policy belirle: hot storage (son 7 gün, hızlı arama), warm storage (son 30 gün), cold storage (arşiv). Alerting kuralları tanımla: belirli hata oranı aşıldığında veya belirli hata pattern'ı oluştuğunda bildirim gönder. Kişisel bilgileri (PII) loglarda maskele, KVKK/GDPR uyumu önemli.
dynamic programming nasıl öğrenilir?

DP en zorlandıran algoritmik konu ama sistematik yaklaşımla öğrenilebilir. Temel fikir: büyük problemi alt problemlere böl, alt problemlerin çözümlerini sakla (memoization veya tabulation), tekrar hesaplama yapma. İki yaklaşım: Top-down (memoization — recursive + cache) ve Bottom-up (tabulation — iterative + tablo doldur). Adımlar: 1) Recursive çözümü yaz. 2) Tekrarlayan alt problemleri bul. 3) Memoization ekle. 4) İstersen bottom-up'a çevir. 5) Space optimization (sadece önceki satır gerekiyorsa 2D tablo yerine 1D kullan). Klasik problemler: Fibonacci, Climbing Stairs, Coin Change, Longest Common Subsequence, Knapsack, House Robber, Edit Distance. Her gün 1-2 DP problemi çöz, pattern'leri tanı: 1D DP, 2D DP, interval DP, bitmask DP, tree DP. Sabır gerektirir ama interview'larda çok soruluyor.
What is Kubernetes?

Kubernetes (K8s for short) is a container orchestration platform. Docker creates containers, Kubernetes manages those containers at scale — automatic scaling, load balancing, self-healing, rolling updates. If a container crashes it automatically starts a new one. When you need to manage 100-1000 containers, Docker alone isn't enough, K8s steps in. Developed by Google, now open source. It's become the standard infrastructure for cloud native applications. AWS EKS, Google GKE, Azure AKS offer managed K8s services. Complex but worth learning.
PyTorch mu TensorFlow mu öğrenmeliyim

Bu klasik bir soru ve cevap aslında artık oldukça net: PyTorch ile başla. Akademide ve araştırma dünyasında PyTorch neredeyse standart haline geldi. Yeni yayınlanan makalelerin büyük çoğunluğu PyTorch kullanıyor. Öğrenmesi daha sezgisel çünkü Python'a çok benzer bir yapıda, debug etmesi kolay. TensorFlow da hala kullanılıyor, özellikle production tarafında TensorFlow Serving ve TFLite gibi araçlarla güçlü ama başlangıç için PyTorch daha mantıklı. Görkem'in derin öğrenme projelerine bakabilirsin, miniature-transformers-from-scratch gibi projeler muhtemelen PyTorch tabanlı. İkisini de bilmek ideal ama birine odaklanacaksan PyTorch olsun.
how is anomaly detection done?

Anomaly detection is finding data points that are not normal. Use cases: fraud detection (fraudulent transactions), network intrusion (cyber attacks), manufacturing (defective products), health (abnormal patient data). Methods: Statistical — z-score, IQR. ML — Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, Local Outlier Factor. Deep learning — Autoencoder (data that can't be reconstructed is anomalous). Time series — change point detection. Unsupervised: no labeled data (in most cases anomalies are very rare). Supervised: when labeled anomalies exist (fraud datasets). PyOD is a Python library offering many anomaly detection algorithms. Gorkem's email-phishing-detection project is a form of anomaly detection.
what is micro-frontends?

Micro-frontends apply microservices principles to frontend development. Instead of one monolithic frontend, split into independently deployable frontend applications. Each team owns a slice of the UI end-to-end (frontend + backend). Approaches: Build-time composition: npm packages for shared components. Simple but coupled deployments. Run-time composition via iframes: strong isolation but limited communication and styling challenges. Run-time composition via JavaScript: Module Federation (Webpack 5) — load remote modules at runtime. Most popular approach. Each micro-frontend is a separate webpack build that exposes and consumes modules. Web Components: framework-agnostic custom elements. Each micro-frontend as a custom element. Server-side composition: Nginx/reverse proxy assembles page from multiple services. Edge-side includes (ESI). Benefits: independent deployments (team A deploys without team B), technology flexibility (React for one section, Vue for another), team autonomy, smaller codebases. Challenges: shared state management, consistent design system, performance (multiple framework instances), complexity, cross-cutting concerns (auth, routing). When to use: large organizations with multiple frontend teams, independently evolving products within one UI. When NOT to use: small teams, single product, when the overhead isn't justified. Most teams don't need micro-frontends — a well-structured monolithic frontend with clear module boundaries works better for smaller teams.
YKS'de sayısal mı seçmeliyim yoksa eşit ağırlık mı?

Bu tamamen senin güçlü olduğun alana ve hedefine bağlı aslında. Eğer bilgisayar mühendisliği, yazılım, yapay zeka gibi alanlarla ilgileniyorsan kesinlikle sayısal seçmelisin çünkü bu bölümler MF puan türüyle alıyor. Matematik ve fen bilimlerine ağırlık vermen gerekecek. Ama eğer daha çok iktisat, işletme gibi alanlara yönelmek istiyorsan eşit ağırlık da mantıklı olabilir. Şunu söyleyeyim — hedefini belirle önce, sonra alan seçimi kendiliğinden netleşir. Görkem de hep şunu der: 'Önce ne yapmak istediğini bil, geri kalanı ayarlanır.'
how should I study for YKS math section?

YKS math requires systematic study. TYT mathematics: master fundamentals (numbers, algebra, basic geometry) — understand formulas, don't just memorize. Solve many problems. AYT mathematics: limits, derivatives, integrals, probability, combinatorics — conceptual understanding is crucial. Resource recommendations: 3D Yayinlari, Acil Yayinlari, Karekök question banks, Palme for TYT basics. Study at least 1-2 hours of math daily — consistency matters, don't study one week and skip the next. Solve practice exams regularly (at least 1 per week), analyze your mistakes and review them. Timing strategy: solve easy questions quickly, don't get stuck on hard ones (you lose points). Keep a topic tracker — monitor which topics you've completed and where you're weak. Math isn't learned overnight — with patience and consistency, everyone improves. Focus on understanding the 'why' behind each solution method, not just mechanical problem solving.

messages.content: what is Redis and what are its use cases?

Redis is an in-memory data structure store — not just a cache. Data structures: strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, HyperLogLog, bitmaps. Use cases: 1) Caching — cache database queries, API responses, session data. 2) Session store — faster than database-backed sessions. 3) Rate limiting — INCR + EXPIRE for request counting. 4) Pub/Sub — real-time messaging between services. 5) Leaderboard — sorted sets with ZADD/ZRANGE. 6) Queue — lists with LPUSH/RPOP (or Redis Streams for more features). 7) Distributed lock — SET key value NX EX timeout (Redlock algorithm for distributed). 8) Geospatial — GEOADD/GEOSEARCH for location-based queries. Persistence: RDB (periodic snapshots) and AOF (append-only file — every write logged). Redis Cluster: horizontal scaling with automatic sharding. Alternatives: Memcached (simpler, only strings), KeyDB (Redis fork, multi-threaded), Dragonfly (modern, compatible). Redis is incredibly versatile — most applications benefit from it.
what is DNS and how does domain resolution work?

DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names to IP addresses. Like a phone book for the internet. Resolution process: 1) Browser checks its cache. 2) OS checks its cache (/etc/hosts file, OS DNS cache). 3) Query recursive resolver (usually ISP or 8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1). 4) Resolver checks its cache. If not cached: 5) Query root nameserver (13 clusters worldwide, knows TLD servers). 6) Root says 'ask .com TLD server.' 7) Query TLD nameserver (.com, .org, .io). 8) TLD says 'ask ns1.example.com (authoritative nameserver).' 9) Query authoritative nameserver — returns the IP address. Record types: A (IPv4 address), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME (alias to another domain), MX (mail server), TXT (text data — SPF, DKIM, domain verification), NS (nameserver), SOA (zone authority). TTL (Time To Live): how long to cache the record. Short TTL (60s) for frequently changing IPs, long TTL (86400s) for stable records. Common DNS providers: Cloudflare DNS, Route 53 (AWS), Google Cloud DNS. DNS can be used for: load balancing (multiple A records, round-robin), CDN routing (GeoDNS — return closest server), failover (health checks, automatic DNS failover). Security: DNSSEC (sign DNS records to prevent tampering), DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) for privacy.
translation icin iyi bir model onerir misin?

translation icin Hugging Face'de en populer modellerden biri google-t5/t5-small. 27,245,112'den fazla indirmesi var, yani topluluk tarafindan cok kullaniliyor. transformers kutuphanesiyle birkac satir kodla yukleyebilirsin. Gorkem de Hugging Face ile calisiyor — wiki2bpe projesiyle tokenizer'lari Hub'a yayinliyor. Yeniysen, modelin Hugging Face'deki model kartindan basla, ne yaptigini ve nasil kullanacagini anla.
