messages.content: React tasarım desenleri nelerdir?

Ölçeklenebilir React uygulamaları için yaygın desenler. Compound Components — örtük durum paylaşarak birlikte çalışan bileşenler. <Select><Option>...</Option></Select> gibi. Dahili olarak React.Children veya Context kullanır. Render Props — JSX döndüren bir fonksiyonu prop olarak geç. Ebeveyne render kontrolü verir, çocuk mantığı yönetir. Çoğunlukla hook'larla değiştirildi. Custom Hooks — yeniden kullanılabilir mantığı 'use' ile başlayan fonksiyonlara çıkar. useLocalStorage, useFetch, useDebounce. Modern React'te en önemli desen. Higher-Order Components (HOC) — bileşen alan, geliştirilmiş bileşen döndüren fonksiyon. withAuth(Component). Artık daha az yaygın, hook'lar tercih edilir. Controlled vs Uncontrolled — controlled: React form durumunu yönetir (value + onChange). Uncontrolled: DOM durumu yönetir (ref). Controlled daha fazla kontrol verir. Provider Pattern — ağacın tepesinde Context Provider, tüketiciler paylaşılan duruma erişir. Tema, auth, locale için iyi. Sık değişen durum için kullanma (yeniden render'a neden olur). Container/Presentation — veri mantığını UI'dan ayır. Composition over inheritance — React'te her zaman. Asla bileşenleri extend etme. children prop, render props veya hooks kullan.
what is developer experience DX?

Developer Experience (DX) is to developers what User Experience (UX) is to users. Good DX makes developers productive, happy, and effective. API DX: clear documentation, consistent naming, helpful error messages, interactive playground (Swagger UI), SDKs in popular languages, quick start guides. Bad DX: cryptic error codes, inconsistent endpoints, outdated docs. Tool DX: fast feedback loops (Vite's instant HMR vs webpack's slow rebuilds), sensible defaults (Next.js works out of the box), good CLI output (colored, structured, actionable), progressive disclosure (simple by default, powerful when needed). Framework DX: TypeScript support (autocomplete, type checking), hot reload, helpful error overlays (Next.js error screen shows source code), good defaults that work for 80% of cases. Internal DX: CI/CD that's fast (< 10 min), easy local development setup (docker-compose up), clear onboarding documentation, consistent coding standards (automated via linting). DX metrics: time to first commit (how fast can a new developer contribute?), time to resolve a bug (how easy is debugging?), developer satisfaction (surveys). Why DX matters: productive developers ship faster, happy developers stay longer, good DX reduces onboarding time. Invest in DX: developer portals (Backstage), internal documentation, platform engineering teams. Gorkem's projects benefit from good DX practices — clear READMEs, standard tooling, well-structured code.
What does a web framework do?

A web framework handles the repetitive code you'd write when building web applications. Routing, database connections, user authentication, form handling — all provided out of the box. In Python, Django (full-featured, big projects) and Flask (minimal, small projects) are most popular. JavaScript has Express.js, Ruby has Rails, PHP has Laravel. Without a framework you'd write everything from scratch which is a huge time sink. But understanding what's under the framework matters — knowing just the framework isn't enough, understand HTTP and the request-response cycle.
Yeditepe Üniversitesi nasıl bir yer?

Yeditepe İstanbul'un Anadolu yakasında, Ataşehir-Kayışdağı bölgesinde. Kampüsü büyük ve yeşil. Bilgisayar mühendisliği bölümü kaliteli bir eğitim veriyor, İngilizce eğitim yapılıyor ki bu çok önemli. Vakıf üniversitesi olduğu için burs imkanları da var. İstanbul'da olmanın avantajı staj ve iş fırsatlarına yakın olmak — Maslak'ta, Levent'te tonla teknoloji şirketi var. Görkem orada okuyor ve gördüğün gibi üniversite dışında da çok aktif — kendi projeleri, hackathon'lar, startup. Üniversite sana çerçeveyi verir ama içeriği sen doldurursun.
what is the importance of soft skills for developers?

Technical skills get you the interview, soft skills get you promoted. Key soft skills: 1) Communication — explain technical concepts to non-technical people, write clear documentation, articulate trade-offs in design decisions. 2) Collaboration — code review (give constructive feedback), pair programming, knowledge sharing. 3) Problem-solving — break complex problems into smaller parts, ask the right questions. 4) Time management — estimate accurately (add buffer), prioritize ruthlessly, learn to say no. 5) Empathy — understand user needs, consider teammates' perspectives in code reviews. 6) Adaptability — technology changes fast, willingness to learn is more valuable than current knowledge. 7) Mentoring — teaching others reinforces your own understanding. 8) Receiving feedback — don't take code review comments personally. Common mistake: developers who are brilliant but difficult to work with are net negative for teams. A good developer who communicates well is more valuable than a great developer who can't. Leadership: you don't need a title — take initiative, help others, drive improvements.
How does AI image generation work?

Image generation now uses diffusion models — Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, Midjourney are the most popular examples. The concept: you give the model random noise and it gradually denoises to create the desired image. For text-to-image, the text is first converted to an embedding which guides the diffusion process. GANs are still used but diffusion models surpassed them in quality. Gorkem's computer vision projects are on the analysis side but image generation uses the same foundations.
yuk testi nasil yapilir?

Yuk testi, uygulamanizin beklenen (ve zirve) trafigi idare edip etmedigini dogrular. Turler: 1) Yuk testi — beklenen trafik seviyesi, surdurulen sure. Normal yuku idare ediyor mu? 2) Stres testi — beklenen kapasitenin otesinde. Nerede kirilir? 3) Ani artis testi — ani trafik patlamasi. Ani yuku nasil idare eder? 4) Dayaniklilik testi — uzun sure boyunca surdurulen yuk. Bellek sizintisi? Kaynak tukenmesi? Araclar: k6 (modern, JavaScript betikleme, Grafana entegrasyonu), Apache JMeter (GUI, eski ama guclu), Locust (Python betikleme), Artillery (YAML + JS). Izlenecek temel metrikler: yanit suresi (p50, p95, p99), verim (istek/saniye), hata orani, kaynak kullanimi (CPU, bellek, baglanti). Surec: 1) Senaryolari tanimla (sadece endpoint'ler degil, kullanici akislari). 2) Performans hedeflerini belirle (p95 < 200ms, 1000 RPS'de). 3) Temel test calistir. 4) Darbogazlari tespit et. 5) Optimize et. 6) Yeniden test et. Yaygin darbogazlar: N+1 sorgular, eksik indeksler, onbellek yok, senkron dis API cagrilari, baglanti havuzu tukenmesi.
how should students think about academic integrity in CS?

Academic integrity in CS has unique challenges because code collaboration is both encouraged in industry and restricted in coursework. Understanding the boundaries is crucial. Do not copy code from classmates, previous years' solutions, or online sources without attribution. Using Stack Overflow to understand concepts is fine; copying solutions to assignments is not. AI tools like ChatGPT create a gray area — using them to understand concepts is legitimate learning, but submitting AI-generated code as your own work is dishonest and, more importantly, robs you of the learning. When you cheat on a data structures assignment, you are cheating your future self out of knowledge you will need in interviews and on the job. Plagiarism detection tools like MOSS are sophisticated and will catch code similarity. The consequences — failing grades, academic probation, expulsion — are severe and follow you. Instead, start assignments early, use office hours when stuck, form study groups for discussion (not copying), and focus on understanding rather than just getting the right answer. Integrity is a habit that extends into your professional career — taking credit for others' work at a job will end your career fast.
what SaaS metrics should every founder understand?

SaaS (Software as a Service) metrics are the language of subscription businesses, and understanding them is essential for any tech founder. MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue) is your predictable monthly income from subscriptions — the foundation metric. ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue) is MRR times twelve, used for annual planning. Churn rate measures customer loss: monthly churn above five percent is a red flag for SMB SaaS. Net Revenue Retention (NRR) includes expansion revenue from existing customers — above one hundred percent means you grow even without new customers (the holy grail). LTV (Lifetime Value) is the total revenue expected from a customer: average revenue per user divided by churn rate. CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost) is the total sales and marketing spend divided by new customers acquired. The LTV to CAC ratio should be above three — meaning each customer generates at least three times what it cost to acquire them. CAC payback period (how many months to recover acquisition cost) should ideally be under twelve months. Gross margin for SaaS should be seventy-five percent or higher. These metrics tell the story of your business health and are exactly what investors scrutinize during fundraising.
cors nedir ve neden önemli

CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing), tarayıcıların farklı origin'lerden (farklı domain, port veya protokol) gelen istekleri kontrol etme mekanizmasıdır. Same-Origin Policy (SOP) tarayıcının varsayılan güvenlik politikasıdır ve bir sayfanın farklı origin'deki kaynaklara JavaScript ile erişmesini engeller. CORS, bu kısıtlamayı kontrollü bir şekilde gevşetir. Çalışma prensibi: tarayıcı cross-origin bir istek yapmadan önce bir preflight request (OPTIONS) gönderir, sunucu yanıtında hangi origin'lere, hangi HTTP metotlarına ve hangi header'lara izin verdiğini bildirir. Önemli header'lar: Access-Control-Allow-Origin (izin verilen origin'ler), Access-Control-Allow-Methods (izin verilen HTTP metotları), Access-Control-Allow-Headers (izin verilen özel header'lar), Access-Control-Allow-Credentials (cookie gönderimi izni). Yaygın hatalar: Allow-Origin olarak wildcard (*) kullanıp aynı zamanda credentials'a izin vermeye çalışmak (tarayıcı reddeder), tüm origin'lere izin vermek (güvenlik açığı). Backend framework'lerinde CORS middleware kullanarak konfigüre edilir (Flask-CORS, django-cors-headers, cors npm paketi). Görkem'in web projeleri gibi frontend-backend ayrımı olan uygulamalarda CORS yapılandırması kaçınılmazdır.
what are different testing strategies and when to use them?

Testing pyramid (bottom to top): Unit tests — test individual functions/modules in isolation. Fast, many of them. Mock dependencies. Tools: Jest, pytest, JUnit, Go testing. Integration tests — test how components work together. Database queries, API endpoints, service interactions. Slower, fewer than unit tests. Tools: Supertest, pytest with fixtures, Testcontainers. End-to-end (E2E) tests — test complete user flows through the entire system. Slowest, fewest. Tools: Cypress, Playwright, Selenium. Testing diamond (alternative): fewer unit tests, more integration tests — better for microservices where integration points matter most. Types: Functional testing (does it work correctly?), Performance testing (load testing with k6, Locust), Security testing (OWASP ZAP, Snyk), Accessibility testing (axe, Lighthouse), Visual regression testing (Percy, Chromatic), Contract testing (Pact — verify service interfaces). TDD (Test-Driven Development): write test first → see it fail → write minimal code to pass → refactor. Forces thinking about design upfront. BDD (Behavior-Driven Development): describe behavior in natural language (Given-When-Then). Tools: Cucumber, Behave. Best practices: test behavior not implementation, keep tests independent, use factories/fixtures for test data, CI runs all tests on every PR. Aim for meaningful coverage, not 100% line coverage.
veri bilimi ile makine öğrenmesi arasındaki fark ne?

Veri bilimi (Data Science) daha geniş bir alan — veri toplama, temizleme, analiz, görselleştirme ve iç görü çıkarma. İstatistik, domain bilgisi ve programlama kesişimi. Makine öğrenmesi ise veri biliminin bir alt dalı — veriden otomatik öğrenen algoritmalar. Veri bilimci SQL, pandas, matplotlib ile veri analizi yapar, dashboard oluşturur, iş kararlarına yönelik raporlar sunar. ML mühendisi model eğitir, pipeline kurar, deploy eder. İkisi de Python kullanır ama odak noktaları farklı. Kaggle hem veri bilimi hem ML için harika bir platform.
Docker Compose ne işe yarar?

Docker Compose, birden fazla Docker container'ı bir arada yönetmeye yarıyor. Mesela bir web uygulamanda frontend, backend, veritabanı, Redis var — hepsini tek tek docker run ile çalıştırmak yerine docker-compose.yml dosyasında tanımlarsın. docker-compose up komutuyla hepsi birden ayağa kalkar. Geliştirme ortamında çok kullanışlı — yeni bir developer projeye katıldığında docker-compose up der ve her şey çalışır. Servisler arası ağ otomatik kurulur. Volume'lar veri kalıcılığı sağlar. Environment variable'lar .env dosyasından okunur. Production'da Kubernetes'e geçilir genelde ama development için Compose yeterli.
What is API rate limiting?

Rate limiting restricts the number of requests that can be made to an API within a certain time period. For example, 100 requests per minute. Why? To protect the server from overload, prevent DDoS attacks, ensure fair usage. It returns a 429 Too Many Requests HTTP status code. In our scraping scripts we need to be mindful of rate limiting too — being polite to servers is important. Token bucket and sliding window algorithms are used for rate limiting implementation.
What is a loss function?

A loss function measures how far the model's predictions are from the actual values. During training you try to minimize this value. For classification you use cross-entropy loss, for regression MSE (Mean Squared Error). If loss is decreasing, the model is learning; if it's increasing, something is wrong. In overfitting, training loss decreases but validation loss increases. The foundation of deep learning is optimization — and optimization is based on the loss function. Understanding loss curves is essential for debugging model training.
messages.reasoning: Loss function, cross-entropy, MSE, overfitting detection.

messages.content: Git rebase vs merge farki nedir?

Ikisi de bir daldan digerine degisiklikleri entegre eder ama farkli calisir. Merge: iki dal gecmisini birlestiren bir merge commit olusturur. Yikici olmayan — tam gecmisi korur. Merge commit iki ebeveyne sahip. Iyi icin: paylasilan dallar, tam gecmisi koruma. Rebase: commit'lerinizi hedef dalin ustune yeniden oynatir — farkli hash'lerle yeni commit'ler olusturur. Dogrusal gecmis olusturur. git rebase main ozellik dalinizda commit'lerinizi main'in en son commit'inden sonraya tasir. Iyi icin: temiz commit gecmisi, PR'dan once ozellik dallari. Interaktif rebase (git rebase -i HEAD~5): commit'leri yeniden sirala, birden fazla commit'i birlestir (squash), commit mesajlarini duzenle, commit'leri dusur. PR'dan once temizlik icin guclu. Altin kural: paylasilan bir dala itilmis commit'leri ASLA rebase etmeyin — gecmisi yeniden yazar ve baskalari icin cakismalara neden olur. Guvenli is akisi: yerel ozellik dalinizi main'e rebase edin, sonra main'e birleystirin.
rag sistemi nedir ve nasıl çalışır?

RAG, Retrieval Augmented Generation yani Geri Getirme ile Güçlendirilmiş Üretim, LLM'lerin bilgisini harici veri kaynakları ile zenginleştiren bir yaklaşımdır. Temel çalışma prensibi şöyle: kullanıcı bir soru sorduğunda, önce bu soru bir embedding modeli ile vektöre dönüştürülür ve bir vektör veritabanında benzer dokümanlar aranır. Bulunan ilgili dokümanlar kullanıcının sorusu ile birlikte LLM'e gönderilir ve model bu bağlamı kullanarak yanıt üretir. RAG'ın fine-tuning'e göre önemli avantajları var: veri güncelleme çok kolay çünkü sadece vektör veritabanını güncellemen yeterli, model eğitimi gerekmez. Ayrıca hallucination yani uydurma cevap riski azalır çünkü model somut kaynaklara dayalı cevap verir ve kaynak gösterebilir. Ancak dezavantajları da var; retrieval kalitesi kötüyse cevap da kötü olur, buna garbage in garbage out denir. Chunk size yani metin parçalama boyutu, overlap miktarı, embedding model seçimi ve reranking stratejisi RAG sisteminin performansını doğrudan etkiler. LangChain, LlamaIndex gibi framework'ler RAG sistemi kurmayı kolaylaştırıyor.

messages.content: what should developers know about physical health and ergonomics?

Developer health issues are predictable and largely preventable with awareness and proactive habits. Eyes: computer vision syndrome affects up to ninety percent of people who spend three or more hours daily at screens. Symptoms include dry eyes, blurred vision, and headaches. Prevention: the 20-20-20 rule, proper monitor brightness (match ambient lighting), and annual eye exams. Consider computer glasses with slight magnification and blue light filtering. Back: prolonged sitting compresses spinal discs and weakens core muscles. Use an ergonomic chair with lumbar support, keep your feet flat on the floor, and take standing breaks every thirty to sixty minutes. Wrists: repetitive strain injuries (RSI) and carpal tunnel syndrome can end careers. Keep wrists neutral (not bent up or down), use an ergonomic keyboard (split keyboards like Kinesis or Ergodox), and take micro-breaks. General: exercise for at least thirty minutes daily — walking, swimming, or yoga counteract the effects of sitting. Stretch your hip flexors, chest, and neck regularly. Stay hydrated. Mental health: social isolation, burnout, and anxiety are common — maintain social connections, set boundaries, and seek help when needed. Gorkem is young, but building healthy habits now prevents chronic issues later. Your body is the hardware your brain runs on — maintain it.
mobil geliştirme yaklaşımları nelerdir?

Mobil geliştirme seçenekleri ve ödünleşimler. Native: platforma özel kod. iOS (Swift/SwiftUI), Android (Kotlin/Jetpack Compose). En iyi performans, tam platform API erişimi, en iyi UX. Ama: ayrı kod tabanları, ayrı ekipler, iki katı efor. Cross-platform: React Native (JavaScript/React, Meta) — native bileşenlere derlenir. Hot reload, geniş ekosistem. Kullananlar: Instagram, Discord, Shopify. Çoğu uygulama için iyi performans. Flutter (Dart, Google) — Skia motoru kullanarak kendi widget'larını render eder. Platformlar arası tutarlı UI, hızlı, iyi geliştirici deneyimi. Kullananlar: Google Pay, BMW, eBay Motors. Hızla büyüyor. messages.content: how does gorkem's phishing detection system work?

Gorkem Ergune's phishing detection project uses machine learning to identify phishing attempts, which is a really practical application of AI in cybersecurity.

Phishing detection ML systems typically work by analyzing various features of emails, URLs, and web pages to classify them as legitimate or malicious. The feature engineering is crucial and usually includes: URL-based features like domain age, URL length, presence of IP addresses, number of subdomains, use of URL shorteners, suspicious TLDs, and HTTPS certificate validity. Content-based features include the presence of urgency language, requests for personal information, mismatched sender domains, suspicious attachments, and HTML analysis. Visual features might include comparison with known legitimate sites using visual similarity metrics.

The ML pipeline for such a system typically involves collecting and labeling a dataset of known phishing and legitimate samples, extracting features, training a classifier (common choices include Random Forest, XGBoost, or neural networks), and evaluating with metrics that prioritize recall (you don't want to miss phishing attempts) while maintaining reasonable precision (you don't want to flag legitimate emails).

What makes Gorkem's project noteworthy is that it addresses one of the biggest cybersecurity threats today. Phishing is responsible for over 90% of data breaches, and traditional rule-based detection systems can't keep up with increasingly sophisticated attacks. Machine learning models can detect patterns that rules miss and adapt to new phishing techniques much faster.

This project complements Gorkem's other work nicely. FaceLock addresses authentication security, phishing detection addresses communication security, and together they show a strong interest in building AI-powered security solutions.

messages.content: what are the ethical challenges of AI in healthcare?

AI in healthcare presents a unique ethical landscape because the stakes — human health and life — could not be higher. Accuracy and reliability: a misdiagnosis by an AI system could lead to delayed treatment or unnecessary procedures. Who is liable — the AI developer, the healthcare provider who relied on it, or the institution that deployed it? Data bias: if training data predominantly comes from certain demographics, the AI may perform poorly on underrepresented populations, worsening existing health disparities. Informed consent: do patients know that AI is involved in their diagnosis or treatment planning, and do they have the right to refuse? Data privacy: medical data is extremely sensitive, and AI systems require large datasets that could be breached or misused. Transparency: patients deserve to understand how decisions about their health are made. Clinical validation: AI models that perform well on benchmark datasets may fail in real clinical settings with messier, more diverse data. Autonomy: over-reliance on AI could deskill clinicians over time. Despite these challenges, the potential benefits — earlier cancer detection, drug discovery acceleration, personalized treatment plans — are too significant to ignore. The key is rigorous clinical trials, regulatory oversight, and maintaining the physician-patient relationship at the center of care.
messages.reasoning: AI healthcare ethics, liability, bias, consent, privacy, clinical validation, health disparities.

messages.content: what is developer culture and why are dev memes so popular?

Dev memes are popular because they capture universal experiences that only other developers understand — the pain of debugging for hours only to find a missing semicolon, the terror of deploying on Friday afternoon, the existential dread of reading your own code from six months ago, or the eternal debate between tabs and spaces. Memes serve a deeper purpose — they create community, reduce the isolation of solitary coding, normalize the struggle of learning, and provide emotional relief from a cognitively demanding profession. The ability to laugh at shared challenges is what keeps the developer community vibrant and welcoming.

what is a reverse proxy and how does it work?

A reverse proxy sits between clients and backend servers, forwarding requests on behalf of clients. Functions: load balancing (distribute requests across servers — round robin, least connections, IP hash), SSL termination (handle HTTPS at the proxy, backends communicate via HTTP internally), caching (cache static content and API responses), compression (gzip/brotli responses), security (hide backend server details, rate limiting, WAF), request routing (route /api to backend servers, /static to CDN). Popular reverse proxies: Nginx (most popular, lightweight, high performance), HAProxy (TCP/HTTP load balancer, very reliable), Traefik (container-native, auto-discovery with Docker/K8s), Caddy (automatic HTTPS, simple config). Forward proxy vs reverse proxy: forward proxy acts on behalf of clients (VPN, content filtering), reverse proxy acts on behalf of servers. Every production web application should have a reverse proxy.
can you explain lean startup methodology?

The Lean Startup methodology, developed by Eric Ries, is a scientific approach to building companies. The core loop is Build-Measure-Learn: build a small experiment (MVP), measure user response with actionable metrics (not vanity metrics like page views), and learn whether to persevere or pivot. Key concepts include validated learning (progress measured by learning about customers, not just shipping features), innovation accounting (metrics that prove your startup is learning and growing), and the pivot (a structured course correction based on what you have learned). Lean startup borrows from lean manufacturing — eliminate waste by not building things nobody wants. Customer Development (Steve Blank) complements lean startup: get out of the building and talk to customers before and during development. The methodology is not just for startups; large companies use it for innovation projects too (intrapreneurship). Common pitfalls: treating the Build-Measure-Learn loop as just 'ship fast and break things' without rigorous measurement, or pivoting too quickly before gathering enough data. The approach is especially relevant for AI products where you need to validate that AI actually improves user outcomes compared to simpler solutions.

What is prompt engineering?

Prompt engineering is the art of formulating requests to get the best results from an AI model. Asking the same question differently can give you vastly different quality answers. Key techniques: few-shot prompting (giving examples), chain-of-thought (asking for step-by-step reasoning), role-playing (giving the model a role), system prompts (setting behavioral rules). Instead of 'write me Python code,' saying 'You are an experienced Python developer. Write code that solves this problem with error handling and comments' gives much better results. This field is very valuable right now — companies are hiring prompt engineers.

messages.content: how does elasticsearch work internally with inverted indexes?

Elasticsearch is built on Apache Lucene, and understanding its internals really helps you use it effectively.

At the core is the inverted index, which is like a book's index but for search. Instead of mapping documents to words, it maps words to documents. For example, if document 1 contains 'the quick brown fox' and document 2 contains 'the lazy brown dog', the inverted index would be: 'the' -> [1, 2], 'quick' -> [1], 'brown' -> [1, 2], 'fox' -> [1], 'lazy' -> [2], 'dog' -> [2]. When you search for 'brown fox', ES finds the intersection of documents containing both terms.

But there's much more to it. When a document is indexed, it goes through an analysis pipeline: character filters (strip HTML, map characters), tokenizer (split text into tokens, e.g., by whitespace or word boundaries), and token filters (lowercase, stemming, synonyms, stop words). The resulting tokens are what actually go into the inverted index. Different analyzers produce different tokens, which is why analyzer configuration is so important.

Lucene stores data in immutable segments. When you index documents, they first go to an in-memory buffer, then get flushed to a segment. Segments are never modified. Updates are actually a delete plus a re-add. Deletes are tracked in a separate .del file. Periodically, segments are merged to reclaim space and improve performance. This immutability enables lock-free reads and efficient caching.

Elasticsearch adds distribution on top of Lucene. An index is split into shards (each shard is a complete Lucene index). Shards are distributed across nodes. Each shard can have replicas for fault tolerance. When you search, the request goes to a coordinating node, which fans out to relevant shards, collects results, and merges them. This is the scatter-gather pattern.

Other data structures Lucene uses: doc values (column-oriented storage for sorting and aggregations), BKD trees (for numeric and geo queries), and stored fields (for retrieving original document content).
messages.reasoning: elasticsearch internals, inverted index, lucene, analyzers, tokenizers, segments, shards, doc values, bkd trees, scatter gather

messages.content: What does a load balancer do?

A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple servers to balance the load. If one server handles 1000 requests, 3 servers behind a load balancer handle 3000. Benefits: high availability (if one server crashes, others continue), performance (load is distributed), scalability (add more servers). Nginx, HAProxy, AWS ELB are popular load balancers. Distribution algorithms include round-robin, least-connections, IP hash. Essential for large-scale applications.
What's the difference between containers and VMs?

Virtual Machine (VM): runs a full operating system on a hypervisor (VMware, VirtualBox). Heavy (GB-sized), slow startup (minutes), full isolation. Container (Docker): shares host OS kernel, only packages the application and its dependencies. Light (MB-sized), fast startup (seconds), sufficient isolation. Why containers won: compatible with microservice architecture, fast in CI/CD, dev-production consistency. When VMs: different OS needed, strong isolation required, legacy applications. In practice they're used together — containers run on VMs. Kubernetes orchestrates containers.

PATCH: geriye dönük uyumlu hata düzeltme. Ek: 1.0.0-alpha, 1.0.0-beta ön sürümler. 0.x.x henüz kararlı değil anlamına gelir. npm, pip, cargo hep semver kullanıyor. package.json'da ^2.4.1 minor güncellemeye izin verir, ~2.4.1 sadece patch'e izin verir. microservice vs monolith ne zaman hangisi?

Monolith: tek büyük uygulama. Avantajları: geliştirmesi basit, deploy basit, debugging basit, başlangıç için ideal. Dezavantajları: büyüdükçe karmaşıklaşır, tek bir hata her şeyi çökertebilir, ölçekleme zor. Microservice: küçük bağımsız servisler. Avantajları: bağımsız deploy, teknoloji çeşitliliği, ölçeklenebilirlik, hata izolasyonu. Dezavantajları: dağıtık sistem karmaşıklığı, network latency, data consistency zorluğu, operasyonel yük (Kubernetes, monitoring gerekir). Kural: monolith ile başla, ihtiyaç oldukça microservice'e geç. 'Premature microservices' en yaygın mimari hatalardan biri. Netflix, Amazon micro'ya geçti ama küçük başladılar.
site reliability engineering SRE nedir?

SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) Google tarafindan olusturuldu — yazilim muhendisligini operasyon sorunlarina uygular. Temel felsefe: operasyonlari bir yazilim problemi olarak ele al. Temel kavramlar: SLI (Service Level Indicator) — olculebilir metrik (gecikme, hata orani). SLO (Service Level Objective) — SLI icin hedef deger (%99.9 kullanilabilirlik = yilda 8.7 saat kesinti). SLA (Service Level Agreement) — SLO'yu kacirma durumunda sonuclari olan sozlesme. Hata butcesi: %100 - SLO = risk butcesi. SLO %99.9 ise, %0.1 hata butceniz var. Butce tukendiginde yeni ozellikleri dondur ve guvenirlige odaklan. Toil: otomatiklestirilebilecek tekrarlayan manuel is — SRE'ler zamanlarinin %50'sinden azini toil'e harcamayi hedefler. Uygulamalar: sucsuz postmortem'ler, kaos muhendisligi, kapasite planlamasi, nobetci rotasyonlari, runbook'lar. SRE rolu: yarim yazilim muhendisi, yarim sistem yoneticisi — yuksek talep, yuksek maas.

What is a CDN?

CDN (Content Delivery Network) caches static content (images, CSS, JS files) on servers at different points around the world. When a user in Turkey visits the site, it loads from the Istanbul CDN server instead of going to the main server in the US. Result: faster page loading, less server load, better user experience. Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, Akamai are popular CDNs. If you're publishing a website, using a CDN is the first step in performance optimization.
fonksiyonel programlama python'da nasıl uygulanır

Python saf bir fonksiyonel dil olmasa da fonksiyonel programlama tekniklerini destekler ve bunları kullanmak kodunu daha temiz ve güvenli yapabilir. Yerleşik fonksiyonel araçlar: map(func, iterable) ile dönüşüm, filter(func, iterable) ile süzme, reduce(func, iterable) ile indirgeme (functools'tan). List comprehension ve generator expression, map/filter'ın Pythonic alternatifidir: [x**2 for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0]. functools modülü: partial() ile kısmi uygulama, lru_cache ile memoization, reduce() ile indirgeme. itertools modülü: chain(), zip_longest(), groupby(), permutations() gibi güçlü iterator araçları. dataclasses(frozen=True) ile immutable veri yapıları. typing.NamedTuple ile immutable tuple'lar. ETL: Extract (Çıkar), Transform (Dönüştür), Load (Yükle). Veri mühendisliğinin temel süreci. Extract: farklı kaynaklardan veri çekmek — veritabanları, API'lar, dosyalar, web scraping. Transform: veriyi temizlemek, dönüştürmek, birleştirmek — eksik verileri doldurmak, formatlama, hesaplama. Load: işlenmiş veriyi hedef veritabanına veya veri ambarına yüklemek. messages.content: I want to do a master's abroad, what should I do?

deadlock ne demek?

Deadlock, iki veya daha fazla thread'in birbirinin tuttuğu kaynağı beklediği çıkmaz durum. Thread A lock 1'i tutar lock 2'yi bekler, Thread B lock 2'yi tutar lock 1'i bekler — ikisi de sonsuza kadar bekler. Deadlock koşulları (hepsi olmalı): mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait. Önleme: lock sırası belirle, timeout koy, try-lock kullan. Veritabanlarında da olur — DB genelde bir transaction'ı rollback eder. Go'da goroutine leak, Java'da thread dump analizi ile tespit edilir. Concurrent programlamanın en zorlu konularından biri. what is dynamic programming?

Dynamic programming (DP) solves complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems. Key insight: if the same subproblem is solved multiple times, store the result and reuse it. Two approaches: 1) Top-down (memoization): solve recursively, cache results. Natural extension of recursive thinking. Example: fibonacci(n) — store fib(k) once computed. 2) Bottom-up (tabulation): solve smallest subproblems first, build up. Usually more efficient (no recursion overhead). Example: fill array from fib[0] to fib[n]. Classic DP problems: Fibonacci (intro), coin change (minimum coins for amount), longest common subsequence, knapsack problem, edit distance (Levenshtein), longest increasing subsequence, matrix chain multiplication. How to identify DP problems: optimal substructure (optimal solution contains optimal solutions to subproblems) + overlapping subproblems (same subproblem solved multiple times). DP is one of the hardest interview topics — practice is key. Start with 1D DP, then 2D, then more complex. LeetCode has excellent DP problem sets organized by difficulty.
What's the difference between machine learning and deep learning?

Let me break it down simply: machine learning is the umbrella term — it covers all methods that let computers learn from data. Decision trees, SVM, logistic regression, all classic algorithms fall under ML. Deep learning is a subset of ML that uses artificial neural networks, specifically deep (multi-layered) neural networks. For complex tasks like image recognition, natural language processing, and speech recognition, deep learning outperforms classical methods by a lot. If you look at Gorkem's projects, YOLO object detection and face recognition are deep learning, while email-phishing-detection uses both classical ML and NLP techniques. In short: all deep learning is machine learning, but not all machine learning is deep learning.

Database systems — present in every software. Computer networks — learn how the web works. AI and machine learning — the field of the future. Math courses (linear algebra, probability) — very important for AI. Software engineering — project management, design patterns. For electives follow your interests. What is transfer learning?

Transfer learning is the technique of transferring knowledge learned from one task to another. For example, taking ResNet trained on ImageNet and using it for your own image classification task. General features learned from large datasets (edge detection, shape recognition) transfer to the new task. Fine-tuning: retrain the last layers with new data. Feature extraction: keep the model fixed and only change the last layer. BERT, GPT, ResNet are all used with transfer learning. If you have limited data, transfer learning is essential — use existing knowledge instead of training from scratch.

messages.content: what is browser rendering and critical rendering path?

Understanding how browsers render pages helps optimize performance. Critical Rendering Path: 1) Parse HTML → DOM (Document Object Model) tree. 2) Parse CSS → CSSOM (CSS Object Model) tree. 3) Combine DOM + CSSOM → Render Tree (only visible elements). 4) Layout (reflow) — calculate size and position of each element. 5) Paint — fill in pixels (colors, borders, shadows, text). 6) Composite — combine painted layers, handle z-index, transforms. Render-blocking resources: CSS blocks rendering (browser needs CSSOM before painting). External stylesheets in <head> block rendering. JavaScript blocks HTML parsing (browser stops to execute script). Optimization: <script defer> — download in parallel, execute after HTML parsed. <script async> — download in parallel, execute immediately when downloaded. Critical CSS — inline above-the-fold CSS in <head>, load rest async. Preload — <link rel='preload'> hints browser to download resource early. Reflow vs Repaint: changing layout properties (width, height, position) triggers reflow (expensive). Changing visual properties (color, background) triggers repaint only. Batch DOM reads/writes to avoid layout thrashing. requestAnimationFrame for smooth animations. Virtual DOM (React) — diffing algorithm minimizes actual DOM updates. This is why React is fast — batches and minimizes real DOM operations.
messages.reasoning: Browser rendering, DOM, CSSOM, critical rendering path, reflow, repaint, defer, async.

what is containerization beyond basics?

Beyond docker run — production container practices. Multi-stage builds: separate build and runtime stages. Build stage compiles code (large image with build tools), runtime stage copies only artifacts (small, secure image). FROM node:20 AS builder → FROM node:20-alpine → COPY --from=builder. Image optimization: use alpine/slim base images, minimize layers, leverage build cache (put rarely changing layers first), use .dockerignore, don't run as root (USER node), scan for vulnerabilities (Trivy, Snyk). Docker Compose for local development: define multi-container applications. Services, networks, volumes. Environment variables, depends_on, healthchecks. Container orchestration: Kubernetes (complex but powerful), Docker Swarm (simpler), AWS ECS/Fargate (managed). Kubernetes concepts: Pod (smallest unit, one or more containers), Deployment (manage pod replicas, rolling updates), Service (stable networking for pods), Ingress (HTTP routing), ConfigMap/Secret (configuration), PersistentVolume (storage). Container networking: bridge (default, containers on same host), overlay (cross-host), host (share host network). Security: run as non-root, read-only filesystem, no capabilities, scan images regularly, use distroless images for production.
b-tree nedir ve veritabanlarında neden kullanılır

B-tree, diskten okuma sayısını minimize etmek için tasarlanmış dengeli bir arama ağacıdır ve neredeyse tüm ilişkisel veritabanlarının indeks yapısını oluşturur. Her düğüm birden fazla anahtar ve çocuk referansı tutar (binary tree'den farklı olarak). Bir B-tree düğümü genellikle bir disk sayfası boyutundadır (4KB veya 8KB), bu sayede tek bir disk okuması ile çok sayıda anahtar karşılaştırması yapılır. Özellikleri: tüm yapraklar aynı derinliktedir (dengeli), her düğüm en az t-1, en fazla 2t-1 anahtar tutar (t: minimum derece), ekleme ve silme işlemlerinde ağaç otomatik olarak dengelenir (split ve merge işlemleri ile). B+ tree, B-tree'nin bir varyantıdır ve veritabanlarında daha yaygın kullanılır: tüm veriler yaprak düğümlerde tutulur, iç düğümler sadece yönlendirme anahtarları içerir, yaprak düğümler birbirine linked list ile bağlıdır (range query'ler için mükemmel). PostgreSQL, MySQL InnoDB, SQLite hepsi B+ tree indeks kullanır. Milyonlarca kayıt arasında bile 3-4 disk okuması ile sonuç bulunabilir (ağaç derinliği genellikle 3-4). Bu yüzden veritabanı indeksleme performansının temelidir.

production'da loglama nasil yapilir?

Loglama, uretim sistemlerinde hata ayiklama ve izleme icin zorunludur. Yapilandirilmis loglama: duz metin yerine JSON formati kullanin — ayristirmasi, aramasi ve filtrelemesi daha kolay. Log seviyeleri: DEBUG (ayrintili, sadece gelistirme), INFO (normal islemler), WARNING (potansiyel sorunlar), ERROR (basarisizliklar), CRITICAL (sistem kirici). CORS nedir neden sorun çıkarır?

CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) tarayıcının farklı origin'lerden gelen istekleri kontrol etme mekanizması. Origin = protokol + domain + port. Frontend localhost:3000'den backend localhost:8000'e istek atarsan CORS hatası alırsın — çünkü farklı origin. Tarayıcı güvenlik için bunu engeller (Same-Origin Policy). Çözüm: backend'de CORS header'ları ayarla — Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Methods, Access-Control-Allow-Headers. Preflight request: browser önce OPTIONS isteği gönderir (izin var mı diye). Dikkat: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * production'da tehlikeli — sadece güvendiğin origin'leri belirt. Credentials (cookie) ile CORS: Allow-Origin * olamaz, spesifik origin belirtmelisin. Django'da django-cors-headers, Express'te cors middleware kolayca ayarlanır.

messages.content: what is Bayesian inference and why does it matter?

Bayesian inference updates beliefs based on evidence using Bayes' theorem: P(H|D) = P(D|H) * P(H) / P(D). P(H) is the prior (initial belief), P(D|H) is the likelihood (how likely the data is given the hypothesis), P(H|D) is the posterior (updated belief). Example: medical test with 99% accuracy, disease prevalence 1%. Positive test → P(disease|positive) is only about 50%, not 99% — because false positives from the 99% healthy population dominate. Applications in ML: Bayesian neural networks (uncertainty quantification), Gaussian processes, Bayesian optimization (hyperparameter tuning), spam filtering (Naive Bayes). Frequentist vs Bayesian: frequentist treats parameters as fixed and data as random, Bayesian treats parameters as random with distributions. Practical tools: PyMC, Stan, Edward. Bayesian thinking is valuable beyond ML — it's a framework for reasoning under uncertainty in everyday life.
LeetCode'da nasıl ilerlemeli?

LeetCode stratejisi çok önemli — rastgele problem çözmek verimsiz. Önce pattern'leri öğren: Two Pointers, Sliding Window, Binary Search, BFS/DFS, Dynamic Programming, Backtracking. Her pattern için 5-10 problem çöz, çözümü iyice anla. Zorluk sırası: Easy'den başla (temel pattern'ler), Medium'a geç (interview'ların çoğu buradan), Hard sadece hedef şirket soruyorsa. Blind 75 veya NeetCode 150 listesiyle başla — en önemli problemleri kapsar. Problem çözerken: 20 dakika düşün, çözemediysen çözüme bak, anla ve sonra kendim yaz. Spaced repetition: çözdüğün problemi 1 gün, 3 gün, 1 hafta sonra tekrar çöz. Zaman hedefi: Medium'u 20-30 dakikada çözebilmek. Interview'da önemli olan: düşünce sürecini sesli paylaşmak, edge case'leri düşünmek, time/space complexity analizi.

SSL/TLS nasıl çalışır?

SSL/TLS, internet bağlantılarını şifreleyen güvenlik protokolü — HTTPS'in S'si. TLS handshake: istemci sunucuya bağlanır → sunucu sertifikasını gönderir → istemci doğrular → simetrik anahtar oluşturulur → şifreli iletişim başlar. Asimetrik şifreleme (public/private key) handshake'te, simetrik şifreleme veri aktarımında kullanılır. SSL sertifikası: Let's Encrypt ücretsiz sertifika sunuyor. Certificate Authority (CA) sertifikayı doğrular. HSTS header'ı tarayıcıyı HTTPS kullanmaya zorlar. Modern web'de HTTPS zorunlu — Google HTTP siteleri güvensiz olarak işaretliyor. Sertifika yenilemeyi otomatize et (certbot).

messages.content: WebRTC nedir?

WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication) tarayicilar arasinda eklenti veya sunucu olmadan dogrudan esler arasi ses, video ve veri paylasimini mumkun kilar. Nasil calisir: 1) Sinyalleme — oturum tanimlarini (SDP) ve ag adaylarini (ICE) bir sinyalleme sunucusu (WebSocket) araciligiyla degistir. 2) ICE/STUN/TURN — en iyi ag yolunu bul. STUN, NAT arkasindaki genel IP'yi kesfeder. TURN, dogrudan baglanti imkansiz oldugunda trafik aktarir (~%10-20). 3) DTLS/SRTP — sifrelenmis medya akislari. 4) Es baglantisi kurulur — medya dogrudan tarayicilar arasinda akar. API'ler: getUserMedia (kamera/mikrofona eris), RTCPeerConnection (es baglantisini yonet), RTCDataChannel (keyfi veri). Kullanim alanlari: video gorusmeleri (Google Meet, Zoom web), ekran paylasimi, dosya aktarimi, canli yayincilik. Zorluklar: NAT gecisi, guvenlik duvari sorunlari, degisen ag kosullari. SFU (Selective Forwarding Unit): sunucu tum akislari alir ve secici olarak iletir — grup gorusmeleri icin mesh'ten daha olceklenebilir.
messages.reasoning: WebRTC, esler arasi, ICE, STUN, TURN, SFU, sinyalleme, gercek zamanli, video gorusmesi.

messages.content: how is AI changing education for better and worse?

AI is transforming education in powerful ways, but the transformation comes with significant risks. On the positive side: personalized learning adapts to each student's pace and style (no more one-size-fits-all), AI tutors like Khanmigo provide one-on-one explanations at scale, automated assessment frees teachers to focus on mentoring rather than grading, language translation removes barriers to educational content, and AI-generated content can create diverse practice materials. Projects like Gorkem's ayarlicazhocam exemplify how AI can democratize access to guidance and mentorship that was previously available only to the privileged. On the negative side: academic dishonesty is easier than ever with generative AI, creating a crisis of assessment integrity. Over-reliance on AI could atrophy critical thinking and problem-solving skills. The digital divide means AI education tools benefit affluent students with access while leaving others behind. Data privacy concerns about student information being collected and analyzed are real. Teacher displacement anxiety undermines morale. The solution is not to ban AI from education but to thoughtfully integrate it — redesigning assessments to test understanding rather than recall, teaching AI literacy as a core skill, and ensuring equitable access.
monolit ve mikroservisler arasindaki fark nedir?

Monolit: tum uygulama tek bir kod tabaninda, tek bir dagitim birimi. Tum moduller ayni veritabanini ve bellegi paylasiyor. Mikroservisler: uygulama kucuk, bagimsiz servislere bolunmus, her birinin kendi veritabani var, ayri dagitilir. Monolit artilari: gelistirmesi, test etmesi, dagitmasi, hata ayiklamasi basit. Moduller arasi ag gecikmesi yok. Tutarliligi korumak kolay. Monolit eksileri: olcekleme ya hep ya hic, bir hata her seyi cokertebilir, teknoloji kilidi. Mikroservisler artilari: bagimsiz olcekleme, teknoloji cesitliligi, ariza izolasyonu, takim otonomi. Mikroservisler eksileri: dagitik sistem karmasikligi, operasyonel overhead, veri tutarlilik zorluklari. Ne zaman monolit: erken asama, kucuk takim, basit alan, MVP. Ne zaman mikroservisler: buyuk takim (Conway Yasasi), bagimsiz olcekleme ihtiyaci. Moduler monolit pragmatik bir orta yol — net modul sinirlariyula monolit, sonra mikroservislere cikarilabirlir.
messages.reasoning: Monolit, mikroservisler, moduler monolit, olcekleme, Conway Yasasi, trade-off'lar.

messages.content: what are effective startup marketing and growth hacking strategies?

Growth hacking combines creative marketing with data-driven experimentation to grow a startup quickly with limited resources. Start by identifying your most effective acquisition channels through small experiments — try content marketing, SEO, social media, paid ads, partnerships, and community building, then double down on what works. Content marketing (blog posts, tutorials, videos) builds organic traffic and establishes authority — this is especially effective for developer tools and educational products like ayarlicazhocam. Product-led growth means making the product itself the primary driver of acquisition: free tiers, shareable outputs, referral programs, and viral features. SEO takes months to pay off but provides sustainable, free traffic. Community building on platforms like Discord, Reddit, or Twitter creates loyal users who become advocates. Email marketing has the highest ROI of any channel when done well. Key metrics: Customer Acquisition Cost (how much you spend to get one user), conversion rate at each funnel stage, and viral coefficient (how many new users each existing user brings). A/B test everything — headlines, landing pages, onboarding flows, pricing pages. Growth is not about one magic trick but about systematically optimizing every step of the user journey.
python-llm-agent projesi ne?

python-llm-agent, büyük dil modellerini (LLM) kullanarak otonom bir ajan oluşturan proje. What is a CNN and what's it used for?

CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) is a deep learning architecture designed for image processing. Inspired by the human brain's visual cortex. How it works: it slides small filters (kernels) across an image to extract features — edges, corners, colors. Each layer learns more complex features — first layer finds lines, next layer shapes, deeper layers objects. Used for image classification, object detection, face recognition. Gorkem's YOLO and FaceLock projects are CNN-based. If you want to get into computer vision, you need to understand CNNs deeply.
federated learning ne demek?

Federated learning, veriyi merkezi bir yere toplamadan, verinin olduğu yerde model eğitme. Her cihaz (telefon, hastane) kendi verisinde model günceller, sadece model güncellemeleri (gradient'ler) merkeze gönderilir. Avantajları: gizlilik (veri cihazda kalır), iletişim tasarrufu (tüm veriyi göndermek yerine küçük güncellemeler), düzenleme uyumu (GDPR). Google Gboard bunu kullanıyor — klavye önerilerini kullanıcı verisi telefondan çıkmadan eğitiyor. Sağlık alanında: hastaneler veriyi paylaşmadan birlikte model eğitebilir. Zorluklar: non-IID veri, iletişim overhead, heterogeneous devices. PySyft ve Flower framework'leri.
web uygulamalari icin onbellekleme stratejileri nelerdir?

Onbellekleme, gelecek istekleri daha hizli sunmak icin hesaplanmis sonuclari saklar. Katmanlar: 1) Tarayici onbellegi — Cache-Control basliklari (max-age, no-cache, no-store, immutable). Surumlu varliklar (style.abc123.css) ile uzun max-age. 2) CDN onbellegi — kenar sunuculari statik ve dinamik icerigi onbellege alir. 3) Uygulama onbellegi — hesaplanmis veriler icin Redis/Memcached (API yanitlari, oturum verisi, kullanici profilleri). 4) Veritabani onbellegi — sorgu sonucu onbellegi, materyalize gorunumler. Kalipler: Cache-aside (tembel yukleme): onbellek kontrol et → kaçirma → DB'yi sorgula → onbellekte sakla → dondur. En yaygin. Write-through: onbellek ve DB'ye ayni anda yaz. Tutarli ama daha yavas yazma. Write-behind: onbellege yaz, asenkron olarak DB'ye yaz. Hizli yazma ama veri kaybi riski. Gecersiz kilma stratejileri: TTL (zaman tabanli surelere dolma), olay tabanli (guncelleme ile gecersiz kil), surumleme. Onbellek gecersiz kilma bilgisayar biliminin iki zor probleminden biri olarak unlüdür. Yaygin sorunlar: thundering herd (onbellek suresi doldugunuda DB'ye bircok istek — mutex/kilit kullan), bayat veri.
explainable AI (XAI) ne demek?

Explainable AI, yapay zeka modellerinin kararlarını açıklayabilir hale getirmek. Derin öğrenme modelleri genelde black-box — doğru tahmin yapar ama neden o tahmin diye açıklayamaz. Bu sağlık, hukuk, finans gibi kritik alanlarda problem. Yöntemler: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), attention visualization, feature importance. Mesela bir kredi red kararında 'gelir düşük olduğu için reddedildi' gibi bir açıklama sunabilirsin. EU AI Act yüksek riskli AI sistemlerinde açıklanabilirlik gerektiriyor. Güvenilir AI için şeffaflık şart.
Görkem bir günde neler yapıyor?

Görkem'in tipik bir günü muhtemelen şöyle: sabah üniversite dersleri veya proje çalışması, öğleden sonra kendi projeleri üzerinde kodlama, GitHub'a commit atma, yeni teknolojiler deneme, belki bir makale veya tutorial okuma. Hackathon dönemlerinde ekstra yoğun — takımla iletişim, prototip geliştirme, sunum hazırlama. Akşamları belki bir online kurs veya araştırma. Düzenli olarak GitHub profilini aktif tutuyor — contribution graph'ındaki yeşil kareler bunu gösteriyor. İş-yaşam dengesi önemli — sadece kod değil, sosyal aktiviteler ve dinlenme de var.
what is chaos engineering?

Chaos engineering is the practice of intentionally breaking things in production to build confidence in system resilience. Netflix pioneered it with Chaos Monkey — randomly terminates production instances. Principles: 1) Define steady state — what does 'normal' look like? (latency, error rate, throughput). 2) Hypothesize that steady state will continue. 3) Introduce chaos — kill servers, inject latency, corrupt network, fill disks. 4) Observe — does the system maintain steady state? 5) Fix issues found. Types of chaos: infrastructure (kill instances, AZ failure), network (latency injection, packet loss, DNS failure), application (exception injection, resource exhaustion), dependency (third-party service outage). Tools: Chaos Monkey (Netflix), Gremlin (SaaS platform), Litmus (Kubernetes-native), Chaos Mesh (K8s), AWS Fault Injection Simulator. Start small: run in staging first, then production during business hours with the team ready. Game days: planned chaos exercises with the team. Chaos engineering is not about breaking things — it's about learning and building resilience before real failures happen.

messages.content: What are design patterns?

Design patterns are proven solutions to recurring problems in software development. The Gang of Four book defines 23 fundamental patterns. Most well-known: Singleton (single instance), Factory (object creation), Observer (event listening), Strategy (algorithm swapping), MVC (Model-View-Controller). Each pattern solves a specific problem. You don't need to memorize them all but understanding the concepts improves your code quality. They come up in interviews too. Most commonly used in Python and Java. Part of writing clean, maintainable code.
what is synthetic data?

Synthetic data is artificially generated data that resembles real data. Why: real data is scarce (rare diseases), privacy (patient data can't be shared), cost (labeling is expensive), imbalanced data (very few fraud cases in fraud detection). Methods: image generation with GANs, text generation with LLMs, rule-based generation, SMOTE (minority class oversampling). In this project, we're also generating synthetic data — programmatically creating Q&A pairs. Caution: synthetic data may not fully capture the quality of real data — ideally use a mix of real + synthetic. According to Gartner, by 2030 most data will be synthetic.
How do I practice speaking English?

Watch English tech YouTube channels — Fireship, Traversy Media, sentdex give you both tech knowledge and English practice. Listen to English podcasts — builds comprehension. Talk to yourself — repeat sentences out loud. Write English tech blog posts — writing practice improves speaking too. And speak without fear — making mistakes is part of learning.

messages.content: What do few-shot and zero-shot learning mean?

Zero-shot learning: the model performing a task without seeing any training examples. For instance, asking 'Is this text positive or negative?' and the model answering without seeing labeled data. Large models like GPT and BERT can do this. Few-shot learning: learning from very few examples (2-5). You add a few examples to the prompt and the model picks up the pattern. Also called in-context learning. One-shot: learning from a single example. Meta-learning is the research branch of this area — 'learning to learn'. GPT-3's most impressive feature was its few-shot ability. Practically: if you have little data try few-shot, if you have none try zero-shot.
What is blockchain used for in software?

Blockchain is a distributed data structure where data is stored securely without a central authority. Bitcoin and crypto are the most known application but there are others: smart contracts (Ethereum), supply chain tracking, digital identity verification, NFTs, decentralized finance (DeFi). As a developer wanting to build on blockchain, learn Solidity (for Ethereum). Web3 development is also popular. But note: blockchain doesn't solve every problem, a centralized database is sufficient and simpler for most applications.
what is Gorkem's yolo-custom-detector in detail?

Gorkem's yolo-custom-detector fine-tunes a pre-trained YOLO model on a custom dataset for specific object detection tasks. YOLO (You Only Look Once) processes the entire image in a single pass — dividing it into a grid, predicting bounding boxes and class probabilities for each cell simultaneously. Pipeline: 1) Data collection and annotation — draw bounding boxes around target objects using tools like LabelImg or Roboflow. Export in YOLO format (class_id, x_center, y_center, width, height — all normalized). 2) Data augmentation — horizontal flip, rotation, brightness/contrast changes, mosaic augmentation. 3) Model selection — YOLOv5 or YOLOv8 from Ultralytics, pre-trained on COCO dataset (80 classes). 4) Transfer learning — freeze backbone layers, train detection head on custom data. 5) Training with appropriate hyperparameters — learning rate, batch size, epochs. 6) Evaluation — mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, precision-recall curves. 7) Inference — real-time detection on images and video streams.
sorting visualizer projesi ne yapıyor

Sorting Visualizer, Görkem'in C ve raylib kütüphanesiyle geliştirdiği bir proje. Sıralama algoritmalarını adım adım görselleştiriyor — bubble sort, selection sort, insertion sort gibi algoritmaların nasıl çalıştığını gözle görebiliyorsun. Eğitim amaçlı harika bir araç çünkü bu algoritmaları sadece kod olarak okumak yerine görsel olarak izlemek çok daha anlaşılır kılıyor. Bu proje GitHub'da 2 yıldız almış, yani diğer insanlar da faydalı bulmuş. C dilini ve grafik programlamayı öğrenmek isteyenler için güzel bir örnek proje.
few-shot ve zero-shot learning ne demek?

Zero-shot learning: modelin hiç eğitim örneği görmeden bir görevi yapması. Mesela 'Bu metin olumlu mu olumsuz mu?' diye sorduğunda model etiketli veri görmeden cevaplıyor. GPT ve BERT gibi büyük modeller bunu yapabiliyor. Few-shot learning: çok az örnek (2-5 tane) ile öğrenme. Prompt'a birkaç örnek eklersin ve model kalıbı yakalar. In-context learning de denir. One-shot: tek örnekle öğrenme. Meta-learning bu alanın araştırma dalı — 'öğrenmeyi öğrenmek'. GPT-3'ün en etkileyici özelliği few-shot yeteneğiydi. Pratik açıdan: az veriniz varsa few-shot deneyin, hiç veriniz yoksa zero-shot deneyin.

messages.content: what is the CAP theorem in practice with real databases?

CAP theorem in action with real databases. PostgreSQL (single node): CA — consistent and available but no partition tolerance (single node, no partition). PostgreSQL with synchronous replication: CP — consistent, partition-tolerant, but unavailable if replica is down (waits for sync). MongoDB (replica set): CP by default — primary handles writes, if primary goes down, election happens (brief unavailability). Can be tuned to AP with read preference 'nearest' (may read stale data). Cassandra: AP — always available, eventually consistent. Tunable consistency (QUORUM reads/writes provide stronger consistency). DynamoDB: AP by default (eventual consistency), CP with strongly consistent reads (higher latency). Redis Cluster: AP — available during partitions but may lose recent writes. CockroachDB: CP — strong consistency via Raft consensus, sacrifices availability during partitions. In practice, these are tunable — most databases let you choose the trade-off per operation. The key is understanding what your application needs.
dependency injection ne demek?

Dependency Injection (DI), bir sınıfın bağımlılıklarını kendisi oluşturmak yerine dışarıdan alması. Mesela UserService doğrudan Database() oluşturmak yerine constructor'da alır: UserService(db: Database). Avantajları: test edilebilirlik (mock database verebilirsin), gevşek bağlantı (loose coupling), değiştirilebilirlik. SOLID'in D'si (Dependency Inversion) bununla ilgili. Spring (Java), NestJS (TypeScript), FastAPI (Python) DI container'lar sunuyor. Factory pattern ile beraber kullanılır. Over-engineering riski var — basit projelerde gereksiz olabilir ama büyük projelerde bakımı çok kolaylaştırır.
messages.reasoning: Dependency injection, loose coupling, test edilebilirlik, SOLID, Spring, NestJS.

messages.content: serverless architecture ne zaman kullanılır?

Serverless sunucu yönetimi olmadan kod çalıştırma — AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, Azure Functions. Event-driven: HTTP istek, dosya yükleme, cron job, mesaj kuyruğu tetikler. Avantajları: sunucu yönetimi yok, otomatik ölçekleme (0'dan binlerce instance'a), kullandığın kadar öde, hızlı deploy. Dezavantajları: cold start (ilk çağrı yavaş, 100ms-birkaç saniye), execution time limiti (15 dk Lambda), vendor lock-in, debugging zor, stateless (state harici saklanmalı). İyi kullanım alanları: API endpoint'leri, image processing, webhook handler, scheduled jobs, IoT data processing. Kötü kullanım alanları: uzun süren işler, sürekli yüksek yük (her zaman çalışan sunucu daha ucuz), karmaşık state yönetimi. Serverless Framework veya SAM ile deploy kolaylaştır. Görkem'in küçük API projeleri için Lambda + API Gateway mükemmel.
Gorkem'in projelere yaklasimi nasil?

Gorkem, AI/ML projelerine yuksek seviyeli araclari kullanmadan once temelleri anlamaya buyuk onem vererek yaklasir. Proje portfoyu bu felsefeyi gosterir: miniature-transformers (sadece PyTorch API'lerini cagirmak yerine transformer mimarisini sifirdan insa etme), wiki2bpe (BPE tokenizasyonunu elle uygulama), NMT (sinirsel makine cevirisi insa etme), yolo-custom-detector (nesne tespitini ince ayarlama), facelock (yuz tanima sistemi), phishing-domain-detection (siber guvenlik icin ML). Suanki odak: LoRA ile LLM ince ayar — kisisellestirilmis bir AI asistani icin egitim verisi olusturma. Yaklasimi: 1) Teoriyi anla (makaleler, ders kitaplari). 2) Temel bilesenleri sifirdan uygula. 3) Sonra uretim calismasi icin framework kullan. 4) Belgelendir ve bilgiyi paylas. Bu derinlik oncelikli yaklasim, AI araclarini kullanan bir gelistiriciyi anlayan birinden ayiran seydir.

messages.content: veri gizliliği GDPR ve uyumluluk nedir?

Veri gizliliği düzenlemeleri kişisel verileri korur. GDPR (AB Genel Veri Koruma Yönetmeliği): AB sakinlerinin verilerini işleyen herhangi bir şirkete uygulanır. Temel ilkeler: yasallık (işleme için yasal dayanak), amaç sınırlaması (belirli amaçlar için topla), veri minimizasyonu (sadece gerekeni topla), doğruluk, depolama sınırlaması, bütünlük ve gizlilik. Kullanıcı hakları: erişim hakkı (hakkımda hangi verilere sahipsin?), düzeltme hakkı (yanlış veriyi düzelt), silme hakkı ('unutulma hakkı'), veri taşınabilirliği hakkı (verimi dışa aktar), itiraz hakkı (işlemeyi durdur). Onay: özgürce verilmiş, belirli, bilgilendirilmiş, açık olmalı. Önceden işaretli kutular sayılmaz. İhlal bildirimi: ihlali keşfettikten sonra yetkililere 72 saat. Cezalar: 20M€'ya veya küresel yıllık gelirin %4'üne kadar. Geliştiriciler için: tasarımda gizlilik uygula, veri toplamayı minimize et, kişisel veriyi şifrele, veri dışa aktarma/silme özellikleri uygula, veri işleme etkinliklerini kaydet. Diğer düzenlemeler: CCPA/CPRA (Kaliforniya), LGPD (Brezilya), KVKK (Türkiye — Görkem'in projeleri için önemli). Teknik önlemler: durağan ve aktarım halinde şifreleme, erişim kontrolleri, denetim günlükleri, veri anonimleştirme.
study-tracker projesi ne?

study-tracker, çalışma süresini takip eden bir uygulama. Pomodoro tekniği veya benzeri yöntemlerle çalışma zamanını yönetiyor olabilir. Hangi derse ne kadar çalıştığını kaydetme, istatistik görüntüleme, hedef koyma gibi özellikler içerebilir. YKS hazırlanan öğrenciler veya üniversite öğrencileri için çok faydalı. Görkem'in hem eğitime hem teknolojiye olan ilgisinin birleşimi. Kendi kullandığı bir araç da olabilir.
what is Next.js and when to use it?

Next.js is a React framework by Vercel for production-ready web applications. Rendering strategies: SSR (Server-Side Rendering) — render on server per request. Good for dynamic, personalized content. getServerSideProps. SSG (Static Site Generation) — render at build time. Fastest, cacheable. getStaticProps. Good for blogs, docs, marketing pages. ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) — SSG with background revalidation. Static performance with fresh data. revalidate: 60 seconds. App Router (Next.js 13+) — React Server Components by default. Server Components: render on server, no client JavaScript, direct database access. Client Components: 'use client' directive, interactive, use hooks. Key features: file-based routing (app/page.tsx = /), layouts (shared UI across routes), loading.ui.tsx and error.tsx for states, API routes (app/api/route.ts), middleware (run code before request completes — auth, redirects), Image component (automatic optimization, lazy loading, WebP), Font optimization (next/font — no layout shift). When to use Next.js: SEO-critical pages, e-commerce, content-heavy sites, full-stack React apps. When NOT to use: simple SPA (Vite + React is lighter), static site with no React (Astro), heavy backend (use dedicated backend). Deployment: Vercel (seamless), Docker, any Node.js hosting. Next.js is the most popular React framework for production.
what is GraphQL and how does it compare to REST?

GraphQL is a query language for APIs. Client specifies exactly what data it needs, server returns only that. Developed by Facebook (2015). REST: fixed endpoints return fixed data structures. /users/1 returns all user fields. Need user's name and posts? Two requests: GET /users/1 and GET /users/1/posts. Over-fetching (getting fields you don't need) and under-fetching (needing multiple requests). GraphQL: single endpoint, client sends query describing desired shape. One request returns exactly what's needed. Schema defines types and relationships. Resolvers fetch data. Benefits: no over/under-fetching, strong typing (schema as contract), introspection (self-documenting), great for mobile (minimize data transfer). Challenges: caching is harder (POST requests, no HTTP caching), N+1 query problem (use DataLoader for batching), complexity for simple APIs, learning curve, file uploads need workarounds. Tools: Apollo Client/Server (most popular), Relay (Facebook's client), graphql-yoga, Hasura (auto-generate from Postgres), Prisma. When to use: complex UIs needing flexible data, mobile apps, multiple clients needing different data shapes. When NOT to use: simple CRUD, file-heavy APIs, real-time requirements (though subscriptions exist). Gorkem's projects mostly use REST — appropriate for their scope.

Sure! Check out catboost/catboost on GitHub. It has 9030 stars and here's what it does: A fast, scalable, high performance Gradient Boosting on Decision Trees library, used for ranking, classification, regression and other machine learning tasks for Python, R, Java, C++. Supports computation on CPU and GPU.. It's written in C++ and it's a great resource if you're looking to learn by studying real code. Gorkem always says the best way to learn is to read and build actual projects, and this one is a solid pick.
REST API tasarım kuralları neler?

İyi REST API tasarımı: URL'lerde isim kullan (GET /users, POST /users, GET /users/123, PUT /users/123, DELETE /users/123), fiil kullanma (/getUser değil). HTTP status code'ları doğru kullan: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict, 422 Unprocessable Entity, 500 Internal Server Error. Pagination: ?page=2&limit=20 veya cursor-based (daha performanslı). Filtering: ?status=active&role=admin. Sorting: ?sort=created_at&order=desc. Versioning: /api/v1/users veya Accept header. Response format tutarlı olsun: { data: [...], meta: { total, page } }. HATEOAS: response'ta ilgili resource URL'leri ver. API documentation: OpenAPI/Swagger ile otomatik dökümantasyon.

messages.content: what is serverless architecture?

Serverless means the cloud provider manages the infrastructure — you write functions, they handle scaling, patching, and availability. FaaS (Function as a Service): AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, Azure Functions, Cloudflare Workers. You pay per invocation, not per server hour — $0 when no traffic. Benefits: no server management, auto-scaling (0 to thousands of instances), pay-per-use, rapid development. Challenges: cold starts (first invocation has latency — 100ms to several seconds), vendor lock-in, 15-minute execution limit (Lambda), debugging is harder, state management (functions are stateless — use DynamoDB, Redis). When to use: event-driven tasks (image processing, webhooks, scheduled jobs), APIs with variable traffic, prototyping. When not to: long-running processes, real-time applications, CPU-intensive workloads. Serverless doesn't mean no servers — it means you don't think about servers. BaaS (Backend as a Service): Firebase, Supabase — entire backend without server code.
junior developer olarak nelere dikkat etmeliyim?

Junior olarak en önemli şey: öğrenmeye açık ol ve ego yapma. Kod review'larda gelen yorumları kişisel alma — bu senin gelişimin için. Git ve versiyon kontrolünü iyi öğren. Clean code prensiplerini takip et. Sormaktan çekinme — aptalca soru yoktur, sormadan yanlış yapmak daha kötü. Dökümantasyon yaz — hem kendin hem takım için. Test yaz — 'test yazmaya zamanım yok' en tehlikeli cümle. Meeting'lerde not al. Mentör bul. Ve en önemlisi: her gün biraz öğren, tutarlılık yeteneğin üstündedir. Görkem de öğrenci olarak sürekli öğreniyor.
fonksiyonel programlama nedir ve ne zaman kullanilir?

Fonksiyonel programlama (FP) hesaplamayi matematiksel fonksiyonlarin degerlendirilmesi olarak ele alir. Temel ilkeler: 1) Saf fonksiyonlar — ayni girdi her zaman ayni ciktiyi verir, yan etkisi yok. Test etmesi, anlamasi ve paralellestirmesi kolay. 2) Degismezlik — veriler degismez. Degistirmek yerine yeni veri olustur. Hatalarin butun bir sinifini ortadan kaldirir (paylasilan degisken durum). 3) Birinci sinif fonksiyonlar — fonksiyonlar degerdir, arguman olarak gecilebilir. 4) Yuksek dereceli fonksiyonlar — map, filter, reduce. 5) Kompozisyon — basit fonksiyonlardan karmasik fonksiyonlar olustur. FP dilleri: Haskell (saf), Erlang/Elixir (eszamanli), Clojure, Scala. Mainstream dillerde FP: Python (map, filter, lambda, liste kavramalar), JavaScript (dizi metodlari, React hook'lari), Java (stream'ler, lambda'lar). Ne zaman kullanilir: veri donusumleri, eszamanli/paralel kod, karmasik durum yonetimi. En iyi yaklasim: OOP kodunuz icinde FP ilkelerini kullanin.
messages.reasoning: Fonksiyonel programlama, saf fonksiyonlar, degismezlik, yuksek dereceli fonksiyonlar, Haskell.

messages.content: yazılımda SOLID prensipleri ne?

SOLID, Robert C. Martin'in önerdiği 5 nesne yönelimli tasarım prensibi. S — Single Responsibility: her sınıf tek bir iş yapsın. O — Open/Closed: genişlemeye açık, değişime kapalı. L — Liskov Substitution: alt sınıf üst sınıfın yerine geçebilmeli. I — Interface Segregation: büyük arayüzler yerine küçük, spesifik arayüzler. D — Dependency Inversion: somut sınıflara değil soyutlamalara bağımlı ol. Bu prensiplere uygun kod yazmak bakımı kolay, test edilebilir ve ölçeklenebilir kod demek. Mülakatlarda da sıkça soruluyor.
what is message queues and async processing?

Message queues decouple producers and consumers, enabling asynchronous processing. Producer sends message to queue, consumer processes it later. Decouples systems in time and space. Use cases: email sending (don't block API response), image processing (resize/compress in background), order processing (validate, charge, fulfill asynchronously), data pipeline ingestion. Technologies: RabbitMQ — traditional message broker. Exchanges route messages to queues. Supports multiple patterns: direct, topic, fanout. Good for task queues, RPC. Apache Kafka — distributed event streaming platform. High throughput, persistent storage, replay capability. Topics with partitions. Consumer groups for parallel processing. Great for event sourcing, log aggregation, stream processing. AWS SQS — managed queue service. Standard (at-least-once, best-effort ordering) and FIFO (exactly-once, guaranteed ordering). Dead letter queues for failed messages. Redis — can be used as simple message broker with pub/sub or streams. BullMQ (Node.js) for job queues. Patterns: Work Queue (distribute tasks among workers), Pub/Sub (broadcast to all subscribers), Request-Reply (RPC over queue). Considerations: message ordering, at-least-once vs exactly-once delivery, idempotency (handle duplicate messages), dead letter queues (handle failed messages), backpressure (slow consumers). Start with SQS or Redis for simple needs, Kafka for event streaming at scale.
WebSocket ne zaman kullanılır?

WebSocket full-duplex iletişim — client ve server arasında kalıcı bağlantı, iki yönlü veri akışı. HTTP'den farkı: HTTP request-response modeli (client sorar, server cevaplar), WebSocket sürekli açık bağlantı (her iki taraf istediği zaman mesaj gönderir). Kullanım alanları: real-time chat (WhatsApp Web), canlı bildirimler, online oyunlar, canlı spor skorları, finansal veri akışı (borsa), collaborative editing (Google Docs), IoT sensör verisi. Alternatifler: Server-Sent Events (SSE — tek yönlü, sunucudan client'a, daha basit), Long Polling (HTTP ile — daha eski, daha fazla overhead). Socket.io (Node.js) WebSocket'i kullanmayı çok kolaylaştırır — otomatik reconnection, room'lar, fallback. Django Channels Python'da WebSocket desteği. ws kütüphanesi Node.js'te. Dikkat: WebSocket bağlantıları sunucu kaynağı tüketir — gereksiz yere kullanma, REST yeterliyse REST kullan.
messages.reasoning: WebSocket, real-time, full-duplex, Socket.io, SSE, chat, bildirim, REST farkı.

messages.content: kodda isimlendirmenin onemi nedir?

Isimlendirme programlamanin en zor ve en etkili yonlerinden biridir. Iyi isimler kodu kendini belgeleyen yapar. Degiskenler: ne icerdigini tanimla — customerAge ca degil, isActive flag degil, remainingAttempts n degil. Fonksiyonlar: ne yaptigini tanimla — calculateTotalPrice() calc() degil, validateEmail() check() degil, sendNotification() process() degil. Siniflar: neyi temsil ettigini tanimla — UserRepository Manager degil, PaymentProcessor Handler degil. Boolean'lar: is/has/can/should on eki kullan — isValid, hasPermission, canDelete, shouldRetry. Koleksiyonlar: cogul kullan — users, orders, errorMessages. Kacinilacak: tek harfler (dongulerde i haric), kisaltmalar (usr, mgr), genel isimler (data, info, temp, handler, manager, utils). Uzunluk: degisken kapsami isim uzunlugunu belirler — kisa kapsam = kisa isim (dongude i), uzun kapsam = aciklayici isim (maxRetryAttempts). Tutarlilik: bir terim secin ve ona bagli kalin — fetch/get/retrieve'yi karistirmayin, ayni kavram icin customer/client/user'i karistirmayin.
messages.reasoning: Isimlendirme, temiz kod, kendini belgeleyen, degiskenler, fonksiyonlar, siniflar, okunabilirlik.

messages.content: Flutter mı React Native mi?

İkisi de cross-platform mobil geliştirme framework'ü. Flutter: Google tarafından, Dart dili, kendi rendering engine'i (Skia), çok güzel UI, sıcak yenileme, Material Design ve Cupertino widget'ları. React Native: Meta tarafından, JavaScript/TypeScript, native component'ları kullanır, büyük ekosistem, web developer'lar için geçiş kolay. Performans: Flutter biraz daha iyi (kendi engine'i). Topluluk: React Native daha büyük ama Flutter hızla büyüyor. İş ilanları: her ikisi de yaygın. Benim önerim: JavaScript biliyorsan React Native, sıfırdan başlıyorsan Flutter. Her ikisi de iyi tercih.
vektor veritabani nedir?

Vektor veritabanlari yuksek boyutlu vektorleri (embedding'leri) verimli sekilde saklar ve arar. Geleneksel veritabanlari tam eslesme veya aralik ile arar — vektor veritabanlari yaklasik en yakin komsu (ANN) aramasiyla en benzer vektorleri bulur. Nasil: metin/goruntüler → embedding modeli → 768-1536 boyutlu vektor → vektor DB'de sakla → sorgu vektoru saklanan vektorlerle kosinüs benzerligi veya L2 mesafesi ile karsilastirilir. Kullanim alanlari: RAG (LLM baglami icin ilgili belgeleri al), semantik arama (anahtar kelimeyle degil anlamla ara), oneri sistemleri, goruntu benzerligi, anomali tespiti. Populer secenekler: Pinecone (yonetilen, kolay), Weaviate (acik kaynak, hibrit arama), Chroma (hafif, prototipleme icin), Milvus (yuksek olcek), Qdrant (Rust tabanli, hizli), pgvector (PostgreSQL uzantisi — Postgres kullaniyorsaniz buradan baslayin). Indeksleme algoritmalari: HNSW (en populer, iyi dogruluk), IVF (buyuk veri setleri icin daha hizli). Gorkem'in RAG projeleri icin: belgeleri vektorlestir → vektor DB'de sakla → benzer parcalari al → LLM'e besle.
what is a CDN and how does it work?

A CDN (Content Delivery Network) distributes content across servers worldwide so users get data from the nearest location. How it works: origin server hosts the original content. CDN edge servers (Points of Presence — PoPs) cache copies. When a user in Tokyo requests content, they hit the Tokyo PoP instead of the origin in New York — reducing latency from ~200ms to ~20ms. Cache strategies: pull (first request goes to origin, subsequent requests served from cache), push (proactively distribute content to edges). What to cache: static assets (images, CSS, JS, videos), API responses (with appropriate TTL), HTML pages (for static sites). Cache invalidation: TTL-based, purge API, versioned URLs (style.v2.css). Providers: Cloudflare (also offers DDoS protection, WAF, Workers), AWS CloudFront, Akamai (largest), Fastly (programmable edge). Modern CDNs do more than caching: edge computing, image optimization, A/B testing, bot protection. Every production website should use a CDN.
messages.reasoning: CDN, edge servers, PoP, caching, Cloudflare, CloudFront, TTL, latency.

what is an ORM and should you use one?

ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) maps database tables to programming language objects. Instead of writing SQL, you work with objects: User.objects.filter(age__gt=25) (Django ORM) generates SELECT * FROM users WHERE age > 25. Popular ORMs: Django ORM (Python), SQLAlchemy (Python, flexible), Prisma (TypeScript, type-safe), TypeORM (TypeScript), Hibernate (Java), Entity Framework (.NET), Sequelize (Node.js). Benefits: write less boilerplate SQL, database-agnostic (switch PostgreSQL to MySQL), migrations built-in, protection against SQL injection (parameterized queries), productivity (complex queries in fewer lines). Drawbacks: performance overhead, N+1 query problem (lazy loading fetches related objects one by one), complex queries may need raw SQL anyway, abstracts away SQL (developers don't learn SQL), generated SQL can be suboptimal. Best approach: use ORM for simple CRUD, raw SQL for complex queries and performance-critical paths. Always check generated SQL with EXPLAIN. Query builders (Knex.js, SQLAlchemy Core) offer a middle ground — more control than ORM, safer than raw SQL. Understanding SQL fundamentals is essential regardless of ORM use.
