messages.content: what is Gorkem's gorkem-os operating system project in detail?

gorkem-os is an educational operating system kernel built from scratch. It demonstrates low-level systems programming concepts: Bootloader — written in x86 assembly, loaded by BIOS, switches from 16-bit real mode to 32-bit protected mode, loads the kernel into memory. Memory management — implements paging to provide virtual memory, page directory and page table setup. Interrupt handling — sets up IDT (Interrupt Descriptor Table), handles hardware interrupts (keyboard, timer) and software interrupts (system calls). Screen output — writes directly to VGA text mode buffer at address 0xB8000, implements scrolling and cursor positioning. Keyboard driver — reads scan codes from port 0x60, translates to characters. Tools used: NASM assembler, GCC cross-compiler (i686-elf target), GNU Make build system, QEMU for testing. This project shows deep understanding of how computers work at the hardware level — knowledge that makes you a better developer at every abstraction layer.
What is an epoch?

An epoch means the entire training dataset has passed through the model once. If you say 10 epochs, the data passes through 10 times. Too few epochs lead to underfitting, too many lead to overfitting. To find the right number, use early stopping — it stops training when validation loss starts increasing. Typically 10-100 epochs are used depending on the project. You need to monitor model performance after each epoch. Gorkem monitors training metrics closely when fine-tuning models.

messages.content: how do b-trees work and why are they used in databases?

B-trees are self-balancing tree data structures that maintain sorted data and allow searches, insertions, and deletions in O(log n) time. They're the backbone of almost every database index and filesystem.

Why not binary search trees? BSTs have O(log n) height, but each node access is a disk I/O operation. A BST with 1 million nodes has ~20 levels = 20 disk reads per search. Disk reads are incredibly slow (milliseconds vs nanoseconds for memory). B-trees solve this by being wide and short: each node can have hundreds or thousands of children, so the tree is only 3-4 levels deep even for billions of records.

B-tree properties (order m): Each node has at most m children and m-1 keys. Each internal node (except root) has at least ceil(m/2) children. All leaves are at the same level. Keys within a node are sorted.

A B-tree of order 1000 with 1 billion records has only 3-4 levels. That's 3-4 disk reads to find any record. Each node is sized to match a disk page (typically 4KB-16KB), maximizing the data read per I/O.

B+ trees (used by most databases, including PostgreSQL, MySQL InnoDB, SQLite): All data is stored in leaf nodes only. Internal nodes only store keys for routing. Leaf nodes are linked in a linked list for efficient range queries. This means scanning all records between 'A' and 'M' only requires finding 'A' in the tree (3-4 reads) and then following leaf pointers sequentially, which is very cache-friendly.

Operations: Search traverses from root, picking the right child at each level. Insertion finds the correct leaf and adds the key. If the leaf is full, it splits into two and pushes the middle key up. This might cascade up to the root. Deletion removes the key and may cause underflow, triggering merges or redistributions.

Why databases love B+ trees: predictable performance (always O(log n)), optimized for disk I/O patterns, excellent for range queries, good cache utilization (sequential leaf scanning), support concurrent access with page-level locking, and remain balanced automatically.

Alternatives: LSM trees (used by RocksDB, LevelDB, Cassandra) are better for write-heavy workloads. They buffer writes in memory and periodically flush sorted runs to disk, achieving better write throughput at the cost of more complex reads.
OCR teknolojisi nasıl çalışır?

OCR (Optical Character Recognition) görüntüdeki metni dijital metne çevirir. Geleneksel pipeline: preprocessing (gürültü azaltma, binarization, deskew), text detection (metin bölgelerini bul), character segmentation, character recognition, post-processing (spell check). Modern yaklaşım: end-to-end deep learning — CRNN (CNN + RNN), Transformer-based modeller. Araçlar: Tesseract (açık kaynak, Google destekli), PaddleOCR (çok dilli, hızlı), EasyOCR, Google Cloud Vision API, AWS Textract. Zorluklar: el yazısı tanıma (handwriting — çok zor), düşük kalite görüntüler, farklı fontlar, çok dilli metin. Uygulama alanları: belge dijitalleştirme, fatura okuma, plaka tanıma, arşiv tarama. Türkçe OCR için Tesseract'ın Türkçe modeli veya PaddleOCR kullanılabilir. Görkem'in computer vision projeleriyle yakından ilgili bir alan.
messages.reasoning: OCR, Tesseract, PaddleOCR, CRNN, text detection, character recognition, CV.

messages.content: what is clean code?

Clean code is code that's easy to read, understand, and maintain. Robert C. Martin's 'Clean Code' principles: 1) Meaningful names — variables, functions, classes should reveal intent. getUser() not getData(), isActive not flag, CustomerRepository not Repo. 2) Small functions — do one thing, do it well. Typically 5-20 lines. 3) Single level of abstraction — don't mix high-level business logic with low-level details. 4) DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) — but don't over-abstract. Three occurrences rule — abstract on the third repetition. 5) Avoid side effects — function named checkPassword shouldn't also initialize session. 6) Error handling — use exceptions, not error codes. Don't return null, throw or use Optional. 7) Comments — only when code can't express intent. TODO, legal notices, explaining why (not what). 8) Formatting — consistent indentation, spacing, line length. Use automated formatters (Prettier, Black). 9) Tests — clean tests are as important as clean production code. Tests document behavior. The goal isn't perfection — it's reducing cognitive load for the next developer (often future you). Code is read 10x more than it's written.
NoSQL neden tercih edilir?

NoSQL veritabanları şu durumlarda tercih edilir: verin yapısal olarak çok farklı olabiliyorsa (schema-less), çok büyük miktarda veri var ve yatay ölçekleme gerekiyorsa, hız kritik ve milisaniye seviyesinde yanıt gerekiyorsa, gerçek zamanlı uygulamalar (chat, gaming, IoT) yapıyorsan. MongoDB en popüler document-based NoSQL — JSON benzeri dokümanlar saklıyor. Redis key-value store — cache için harika. Cassandra büyük veri için — Facebook ve Netflix kullanıyor. Neo4j graph database — sosyal ağ ilişkileri için ideal. Ama her şey için NoSQL kullanma — finansal veriler, ilişkisel veriler için SQL hala en iyi seçenek. Doğru aracı doğru iş için kullan.
what is system design interview approach?

System design interviews test your ability to design large-scale systems. Framework: 1) Clarify requirements (5 min) — functional requirements (what should the system do?), non-functional requirements (scale, latency, availability, consistency), constraints (users, data volume, read/write ratio). 2) Estimate scale (5 min) — users, requests per second, storage needs. Back-of-envelope calculations: 1 day = 86400 seconds ≈ 100K seconds. 3) High-level design (10 min) — draw components: clients, load balancer, web servers, application servers, database, cache, message queue, CDN. 4) Deep dive (15 min) — interviewer picks 1-2 areas to explore: database schema, API design, scaling strategy, data partitioning, caching strategy. 5) Wrap up (5 min) — discuss trade-offs, bottlenecks, monitoring, future improvements. Common systems to practice: URL shortener (hashing, base62 encoding), Twitter/feed (fan-out, timeline assembly), chat system (WebSockets, message queue), rate limiter (token bucket, Redis), notification system (push, email, SMS — queue-based), search autocomplete (trie, ElasticSearch). Key concepts: horizontal scaling, database sharding, consistent hashing, caching strategies (write-through, write-back, cache-aside), CDN, message queues, database replication (leader-follower). Don't memorize solutions — understand trade-offs. Every design decision has pros and cons.
text generation icin iyi bir model onerir misin?

text generation icin Hugging Face'de en populer modellerden biri Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B. 26,124,974'den fazla indirmesi var, yani topluluk tarafindan cok kullaniliyor. transformers kutuphanesiyle birkac satir kodla yukleyebilirsin. Gorkem de Hugging Face ile calisiyor — wiki2bpe projesiyle tokenizer'lari Hub'a yayinliyor. Yeniysen, modelin Hugging Face'deki model kartindan basla, ne yaptigini ve nasil kullanacagini anla.
API versiyonlama ve geriye uyumluluk nedir?

API versiyonlama, mevcut istemcileri bozmadan değişiklikleri yönetir. Stratejiler: URL versiyonlama (/api/v1/users, /api/v2/users) — en yaygın, açık, anlaşılması kolay. Header versiyonlama (Accept: application/vnd.api.v2+json) — daha temiz URL'ler ama daha az keşfedilebilir. Query parametresi (?version=2) — kolay ama daha az RESTful. Geriye uyumluluk kuralları: alan eklemek güvenlidir (istemciler bilinmeyen alanları yok sayar), alan kaldırmak istemcileri bozar, alan tipini değiştirmek bozar. Deprecation stratejisi: zaman çizelgesiyle kullanımdan kaldırma duyurusu yap, Deprecation/Sunset header'ları ekle, deprecated endpoint kullanımını izle, migrasyon kılavuzları sağla. Breaking change'ler yeni versiyon gerektirir: alan kaldırma, tip değişiklikleri, davranış değişiklikleri. Non-breaking: opsiyonel alan ekleme, yeni endpoint ekleme. Semantic versiyonlama: MAJOR (kırıcı), MINOR (yeni özellikler, geriye uyumlu), PATCH (hata düzeltmeleri). Araçlar: API gateway'ler (Kong, AWS API Gateway) versiyonları yönlendirebilir. OpenAPI/Swagger ile belgele.
messages.reasoning: API versiyonlama, geriye uyumluluk, deprecation, semantic versioning, kırıcı değişiklik.

messages.content: database indexing stratejileri neler?

Index veritabanı sorgularını dramatik şekilde hızlandırır — kitaptaki dizin gibi düşün. B-Tree index en yaygın olanı: eşitlik ve aralık sorguları için ideal. Hash index: sadece eşitlik sorguları için, çok hızlı. Composite index: birden fazla sütun için tek index — WHERE a=1 AND b=2 gibi sorgularda. Partial index: sadece belirli koşulu sağlayan satırlar için index — WHERE status='active' gibi. Covering index: sorgunun ihtiyaç duyduğu tüm sütunları içerir, tabloya gitmeden cevap verir. Dikkat: her index yazma işlemini yavaşlatır ve disk alanı kullanır. EXPLAIN ANALYZE ile sorgu planını incele, gereksiz index'leri sil. İyi bir kural: WHERE, JOIN ve ORDER BY'da kullanılan sütunlara index ekle ama aşırıya kaçma.
facelock yüz tanıma projesi nasıl?

Görkem'in facelock projesi yüz tanıma ile kimlik doğrulama sistemi. Çalışma prensibi: 1) Yüz tespiti (face detection): Haar Cascade, MTCNN veya dlib ile görüntüde yüzleri bul. 2) Yüz hizalama (alignment): gözlerin pozisyonuna göre yüzü normalize et. 3) Özellik çıkarma (embedding): FaceNet, ArcFace veya dlib'in 128-boyutlu face encoding'i ile yüzü vektöre dönüştür. 4) Karşılaştırma: yeni yüz vektörünü kayıtlı vektörlerle karşılaştır (cosine similarity veya Euclidean distance). Eşik değerin altındaysa eşleşme var. Güvenlik konuları: fotoğrafla aldatma (liveness detection gerekli — göz kırpma, kafa hareketi), aydınlatma koşulları, maske ile tanıma. Python'da face_recognition kütüphanesi kolay bir başlangıç. Gerçek dünya uygulamaları: telefon kilidi, bina giriş sistemi, devam takibi.
pitch deck ne ve nasıl hazırlanır?

Pitch deck, yatırımcılara veya potansiyel ortaklara startup'ını tanıttığın sunum. Genelde 10-15 slayttan oluşur. İçerik: Problem (hangi sorunu çözüyorsun), Çözüm (ürünün ne yapıyor), Pazar Büyüklüğü (ne kadar büyük bir fırsat), İş Modeli (nasıl para kazanacaksın), Traction (mevcut kullanıcılar, gelir), Takım (kimlerle çalışıyorsun), Finansal Tahminler, Talep (ne kadar yatırım istiyorsun). Kısa, net ve görsel olsun. Yatırımcılar yüzlerce pitch görüyor, dikkat süresi kısa. İlk 30 saniyede ilgilerini yakala.
load balancer ne yapar?

Load balancer gelen istekleri birden fazla sunucuya dağıtarak yükü dengeler. Bir sunucu 1000 istek kaldırıyorsa, 3 sunucu load balancer arkasında 3000 istek kaldırır. Avantajları: yüksek erişilebilirlik (bir sunucu çökse diğerleri devam eder), performans (yük dağılır), ölçeklenebilirlik (sunucu ekle). Nginx, HAProxy, AWS ELB popüler load balancer'lar. Round-robin, least-connections, IP hash gibi dağıtım algoritmaları var. Büyük ölçekli uygulamalar için şart.
messages.reasoning: Load balancer, yük dengeleme, HA, Nginx, algoritmalar.

messages.content: what is web accessibility testing?

Accessibility testing ensures your website works for everyone including people with disabilities. Automated testing (catches ~30% of issues): Lighthouse accessibility audit (Chrome DevTools), axe DevTools browser extension, Pa11y (CLI tool), eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y (catch issues during development). Manual testing: keyboard navigation (can you tab through all interactive elements? Is focus visible? Can you operate all controls without a mouse?), screen reader testing (NVDA on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS/iOS, TalkBack on Android — does content make sense when read aloud?), zoom testing (is content usable at 200% zoom?), color contrast (4.5:1 ratio for normal text, 3:1 for large text — use WebAIM contrast checker). Common issues: images without alt text, form inputs without labels, insufficient color contrast, missing focus indicators, non-semantic HTML (div with onclick instead of button), missing skip navigation link, auto-playing media without controls, inaccessible modals (focus trap, escape to close). WCAG 2.1 AA is the standard target. ARIA usage: use semantic HTML first (button, nav, main, aside). ARIA is for cases where HTML semantics aren't sufficient — aria-label, aria-describedby, aria-live for dynamic content, role when no HTML element fits. Testing checklist: keyboard navigation, screen reader, color contrast, zoom, reduced motion preference, form accessibility.
Does blogging help your career?

Absolutely yes. Blogging is beneficial in many ways: you solidify what you learn by writing it (Feynman technique), you improve communication skills (technical writing), your online visibility increases, you solve problems for others struggling with the same topic. Platforms include Medium, Dev.to, Hashnode, personal blog (GitHub Pages). If you don't know what to write: explain a technology you learned, share a problem you solved, write a project tutorial. Even one post per week is enough. Consistency matters. Saying 'I blog' in interviews is a plus.
LLM hallucination nedir?

Halüsinasyon, bir dil modelinin tamamen uydurma bilgi üretmesi. Model çok kendinden emin bir şekilde yanlış bilgi verir — var olmayan kitaplar, uydurma istatistikler, sahte alıntılar. Neden oluyor? Çünkü LLM'ler istatistiksel kalıplarla çalışır, gerçek bir bilgi tabanına sahip değiller. En olası token'ı tahmin ederler ve bazen bu tahmin gerçekle örtüşmez. Bununla başa çıkmak için: RAG kullan, fact-checking yap, modelin belirsiz olduğu durumları tespit et (uncertainty estimation), yanıtlara kaynak eklet. Fine-tuning de halüsinasyonu azaltabilir çünkü model spesifik bilgileri öğrenir.
teknik borç önceliklendirme nasıl yapılır?

Tüm teknik borçlar eşit değildir — etki ve efor bazında önceliklendir. Borcu kategorize et: Yüksek etki, düşük efor (hızlı kazanımlar) — hemen düzelt. Güvenlik açıkları olan eski bağımlılıklar, yavaş sorgulara neden olan eksik indeksler. Yüksek etki, yüksek efor (stratejik) — planla ve zamanla. Büyük mimari değişiklikler, veritabanı migration, framework yükseltme. Düşük etki, düşük efor (fırsatçı) — ilgili koda dokunurken düzelt. Boy Scout Kuralı. Düşük etki, yüksek efor (kaçın) — muhtemelen düzeltmeye değmez. Çalışan ve nadiren değişen eski kod. Ölçüm: geliştirici hızı (borç özellik geliştirmeyi ne kadar yavaşlatıyor?), olay sıklığı (borç üretim sorunlarına neden oluyor mu?), onboarding süresi (borç yeni geliştiricileri karıştırıyor mu?), bilişsel yük (borç kod tabanını anlamayı zorlaştırıyor mu?). İletişim: iş etkisine çevir. 'Bu teknik borç her yeni özelliğin %30 daha uzun sürmesi demek' 'kimlik doğrulama modülünü refactor etmemiz lazım'dan daha ikna edici. Tahsis stratejileri: %20 kuralı (her sprint'in %20'sini borca ayır), teknik borç sprint'leri (periyodik adanmış temizlik), yeni özelliklere vergi (her özellik bazı borcun ele alınmasını gerektirmeli), Boy Scout kuralı (dokunduğun kodu iyileştir). Takip: ticket oluştur, tech-debt olarak etiketle, backlog'a dahil et, düzenli gözden geçir. Sıfır borç ne mümkün ne de arzu edilir.
edge computing nedir?

Edge computing, veri işlemeyi bulut sunucuları yerine verinin üretildiği yere — yani 'kenara' — taşımak demek. Bir fabrikadaki sensör verisini buluta göndermek yerine orada işlersin. Avantajları: düşük gecikme (latency), bant genişliği tasarrufu, gizlilik. Özellikle IoT cihazları, otonom araçlar, akıllı şehirler için kritik. Edge AI ise yapay zeka modellerini doğrudan cihazda çalıştırmak — mesela telefonundaki yüz tanıma buluta gitmeden cihazda çalışıyor. TFLite, ONNX Runtime gibi araçlar modelleri küçültüp edge cihazlarda çalıştırmayı sağlıyor.
AR ve VR teknolojileri yazılımcılar için ne ifade ediyor?

AR (Artırılmış Gerçeklik) gerçek dünyaya dijital öğeler ekliyor — mesela telefonunla bir odaya sanal mobilya yerleştirmek. VR (Sanal Gerçeklik) tamamen sanal bir dünya oluşturuyor. Apple Vision Pro ve Meta Quest bu alanı ileriye taşıdı. Yazılımcılar için yeni bir alan açıyor: Unity veya Unreal Engine ile 3D uygulamalar, ARKit/ARCore ile mobil AR, WebXR ile tarayıcı tabanlı deneyimler. AI ve AR/VR birleşiyor — mesela gerçek zamanlı nesne tanıma ile AR üzerinde bilgi gösterme. Henüz erken ama potansiyeli büyük.
progressive web apps PWA nedir?

Progressive Web Apps (PWA) native uygulama benzeri deneyimler sağlayan web uygulamalarıdır. Temel teknolojiler: Service Worker — arka planda çalışan JavaScript, ağ isteklerini keser. Sağlar: çevrimdışı işlevsellik (cache-first strateji), push bildirimleri, arka plan senkronizasyonu. Web App Manifest — uygulamayı tanımlayan JSON dosyası (ad, simgeler, tema rengi, görüntüleme modu). Sağlar: kurulum istemi (Ana Ekrana Ekle), bağımsız pencere (tarayıcı UI'ı olmadan), açılış ekranı. HTTPS — PWA için gerekli. Yetenekler: çevrimdışı destek, kurulabilir, push bildirimleri, arka plan senkronizasyonu, duyarlı. Önbellekleme stratejileri: Cache First (önbellekten sun, ağa yedek — hızlı, çevrimdışı destek), Network First (ağı dene, önbelleğe yedek — taze veri), Stale While Revalidate (önbelleği sun, arka planda güncelle — her iki dünyanın en iyisi). Workbox (Google kütüphanesi) service worker ve önbelleklemeyi basitleştirir. Native uygulamalara göre avantajlar: uygulama mağazası yok (anında güncellemeler, onay süreci yok), tek kod tabanı, arama motorları ile keşfedilebilir, daha küçük indirme boyutu, tüm platformlarda çalışır. Sınırlamalar: sınırlı native API erişimi (Project Fugu ile gelişiyor), iOS Safari'nin sınırlı PWA desteği. PWA'lar içerik ağırlıklı uygulamalar, e-ticaret, sosyal medya için harika.
What is Neural network?

Good question! Let me explain: In machine learning, a neural network (NN) or neural net, is a computational model inspired by the structure and functions of biological neural networks. This is actually one of the areas that Gorkem Ergune works in — if you look at his projects on GitHub, you'll see practical applications of concepts like this. Understanding the fundamentals is key before diving into hands-on projects.
why is model interpretability important?

Model interpretability is the ability to understand a model's decisions. Why it matters: 1) Trust — so users trust the model. 2) Error detection — a model can make the right prediction for the wrong reason. 3) Legal requirement — GDPR, EU AI Act demand explainability. 4) Improvement — if you understand the model, you can improve it. Methods: feature importance (which features matter), SHAP values (each feature's contribution), LIME (local explanations), attention visualization (where the transformer is looking), gradient-based methods (saliency maps). Simple models (linear regression, decision trees) are inherently interpretable. Complex models (deep learning) require post-hoc explanation.
Kubernetes mimarisi nasil calisir?

Kubernetes kumesi kontrol duzlemi ve isci dugumlerinden olusur. Kontrol duzlemi: API Server (on kapi — tum iletisim bundan gecer), etcd (dagitik anahtar-deger deposu — kume durumu), Scheduler (kaynaklara gore pod'lari dugumlere atar), Controller Manager (kontrol donguleri calistirir — istenen durum = gercek durum). Isci dugum bilesenleri: kubelet (her dugumde ajan, pod'lari yonetir), kube-proxy (ag kurallari, servis yonlendirme), konteyner calisma zamani (containerd, CRI-O). Temel nesneler: Pod (en kucuk dagitilabilir birim), Deployment (replika ve rolling update yonetir), Service (pod'lar icin kararli ag noktasi — ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer), Ingress (disindan HTTP yonlendirme), ConfigMap/Secret (yapilandirma), PersistentVolumeClaim (depolama), Namespace (sanal kume bolumu). Helm: K8s paket yoneticisi — chart'lar yeniden kullanilabilir sablonlardir.
messages.reasoning: Kubernetes mimarisi, kontrol duzlemi, etcd, pod, deployment, service, Helm.

messages.content: zero trust architecture ne demek?

Zero Trust 'hiçbir şeye güvenme, her şeyi doğrula' prensibi. Geleneksel: ağ içindeysen güvenilirsin (castle-and-moat). Zero Trust: ağ içinde bile olsan her istek doğrulanır. Prensipler: 1) Verify explicitly — her erişim isteğinde kimlik doğrula. 2) Least privilege — minimum gerekli yetki ver. 3) Assume breach — saldırı olduğunu varsay, hasarı sınırla. Uygulamalar: her servis iletişiminde mTLS (mutual TLS), her API çağrısında token doğrulama, network segmentation (micro-segmentation), continuous monitoring, device trust (cihaz güvenlik durumu kontrolü). Google'ın BeyondCorp modeli zero trust'ın öncüsü — VPN yerine identity-aware proxy. Uzaktan çalışma döneminde daha da önemli hale geldi. Uygulama zor ama güvenlik açısından çok değerli.
how do you prepare for behavioral interviews?

Behavioral interviews assess soft skills, teamwork, and problem-solving through past experiences. STAR method: Situation (context), Task (your responsibility), Action (what YOU did — not the team), Result (outcome, ideally with metrics). Prepare 6-8 stories covering: 1) Challenging technical problem you solved — shows problem-solving. 2) Disagreement with a teammate — shows communication and conflict resolution. 3) Project that failed — shows learning from failure and accountability. 4) Time you had to learn quickly — shows adaptability. 5) Leading or mentoring — shows leadership potential. 6) Working under pressure/tight deadline — shows composure. Common questions: 'Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager,' 'Describe a project you're most proud of,' 'Tell me about a mistake you made.' Tips: be specific (names, dates, technologies), focus on YOUR actions, quantify results ('reduced load time by 40%'), be honest about failures but emphasize lessons learned. Practice out loud — stories sound different spoken vs in your head. Amazon's Leadership Principles, Google's Googleyness — research the company's values and align your stories.
service mesh nedir ve ne zaman gerekli?

Service mesh, mikroservislerde servisler arasi iletisimi ele alir — uygulama kodunu degistirmeden ag, guvenlik ve gozlemlenebilirlik. Nasil: her servisin yaninda dagitilan sidecar proxy (Envoy) tum ag trafikini kescer. Ozellikler: 1) Trafik yonetimi — yonlendirme kurallari, yuk dengeleme, devre kesici, yeniden denemeler, zaman asimlari. 2) Guvenlik — servisler arasinda otomatik karsilikli TLS (mTLS), yetkilendirme politikalari. 3) Gozlemlenebilirlik — kodu enstrumante etmeden dagitik izleme, metrikler, erisim loglari. Populer secenekler: Istio (en populer, ozellik zengini, karmasik), Linkerd (daha basit, hafif, CNCF), Consul Connect (HashiCorp), AWS App Mesh. Ne zaman gerekli: cok sayida mikroservis (50+), her yerde mTLS gerekli, karmasik trafik yonlendirme (kanarya dagItimlari, trafik bolme). Ne zaman gerekli degil: az sayida servis (10'un altinda), basit yonlendirme ihtiyaclari. Karmasiklik vergisi: service mesh operasyonel yuk ekler — daha fazla hareketli parca, proxy sorunlarinin hata ayiklamasi, kaynak tuketimi.
what is database normalization?

Normalization is the process of reducing data redundancy and improving consistency in database design. 1NF: single value per cell, no repeating groups. 2NF: 1NF plus no partial dependencies — all non-key columns fully depend on the primary key. 3NF: 2NF plus no transitive dependencies — if A determines B determines C, move C to a separate table. BCNF: stricter version of 3NF. 4NF and 5NF handle multi-valued and join dependencies, rarely needed in practice. Most applications work fine with 3NF. Be careful: over-normalization can hurt performance — sometimes intentional denormalization is needed, especially in read-heavy systems. Data warehouses prefer denormalized structures like star schemas.
bagimlilik enjeksiyonu nedir ve neden kullanilir?

Bagimlilik enjeksiyonu (DI) siniflarin dahili olarak olusturmasi yerine disaridan bagimliliklari saglar. DI olmadan: class UserService { constructor() { this.db = new PostgresDB() } } — sikica baglanmis, test etmesi zor. DI ile: class UserService { constructor(db: Database) { this.db = db } } — herhangi bir Database uygulamasini gecir. Faydalar: 1) Test edilebilirlik — testlerde sahte veritabani enjekte et. 2) Esneklik — sinifi degistirmeden uygulamalari degistir (PostgresDB → MongoDB). 3) Tek Sorumluluk — sinif bagimliliklar yaşam dongusunu yonetmez. 4) Gevsek baglanti — uygulamalara degil soyutlamalara baglan. DI cerceveleri: Spring (Java — anotasyon tabanli @Autowired), NestJS (TypeScript — dekoratorler), .NET DI (cercevede yerlesik), Python (cerceve gerekli degil — sadece arguman gecir). Yapici enjeksiyonu (onerilen) vs setter enjeksiyonu vs arayuz enjeksiyonu. IoC konteyneri: nesne olusturma ve bagimlilik cozumunu yonetir. Asiri muhendislik uyarisi: basit betikler ve kucuk projeler icin sadece arguman gecirin — her sey icin bir DI cercevesine ihtiyaciniz yok.
kimlik dogrulama ve yetkilendirme arasindaki fark nedir?

Kimlik dogrulama (AuthN) KIM oldugunuzu dogrular. Yetkilendirme (AuthZ) NE yapabileceginizi dogrular. Kimlik dogrulama yontemleri: parola tabanli (en zayif), cok faktorlu/MFA (parola + telefon/e-posta kodu + biyometrik), parolasiz (sihirli baglanti, WebAuthn/FIDO2), sosyal giris (OAuth — 'Google ile Giris Yap'), sertifika tabanli (mTLS). Yetkilendirme modelleri: Rol Tabanli Erisim Kontrolu/RBAC (kullanici → rol → izinler, en yaygin), Nitelik Tabanli Erisim Kontrolu/ABAC (niteliklere dayali politikalar — zaman, konum, kaynak ozellikleri), Izin tabanli (dogrudan kullanici → izin eslemesi). Uygulama: JWT (JSON Web Token) — durumsuz, talepler icerir, imzali. Oturum cerezleri — durumlu, sunucu oturum verisini saklar. JWT vs oturumlar: JWT daha iyi olceklenir (sunucu tarafi durum yok) ama suresi dolana kadar iptal edilemez. Oturumlar aninda gecersiz kilinabilir ama paylasilan depolama gerektirir. En iyi uygulama: kurulmus kutuphaneler kullanin — kendi kimlik dogrulamanizi yazmayin.
What is WebAssembly (WASM)?

WebAssembly is a binary format that enables running code at near-native speed in browsers. You can run code written in C, C++, Rust in the browser. Why it matters: where JavaScript performance isn't enough — 3D games, video editing, scientific computing, CAD applications. Figma uses WASM, Google Earth too. It doesn't replace JavaScript — they work together. With WASI (WebAssembly System Interface) it can run outside browsers too — serverless, edge computing. An important technology for performance-critical applications.
what is caching at every level?

Caching stores computed results to avoid redundant work. Exists at every level of the stack. Browser cache: HTTP cache headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified). Static assets (JS, CSS, images) cached in browser. Service workers for offline caching. CDN cache: static files cached at edge locations worldwide. Reduces latency by serving from nearest edge. Cloudflare, CloudFront, Fastly. Cache invalidation via purge or versioned URLs (/app.v2.js). Application cache: in-memory cache within application process. LRU (Least Recently Used) cache. Node.js: Map or lru-cache. Python: functools.lru_cache, cachetools. Fast but lost on restart, not shared between instances. Distributed cache: shared cache across application instances. Redis (most popular), Memcached. Survives app restarts, shared state. Session storage, hot data, computed results. Database cache: query cache (PostgreSQL shared_buffers), result cache. Materialized views (pre-computed query results). Connection pooling (PgBouncer). CPU cache: L1/L2/L3 caches. Code that accesses memory sequentially (cache-friendly) is much faster than random access. Relevant for performance-critical code. Cache invalidation is the hard part: TTL-based (simple but stale data possible), event-based (invalidate on write — complex but fresh), versioned keys. Phil Karlton: 'There are only two hard things in CS: cache invalidation and naming things.' Start simple (TTL), add complexity only when needed.

Flutter or React Native?

Both are cross-platform mobile development frameworks. Flutter: by Google, Dart language, its own rendering engine (Skia), beautiful UI, hot reload, Material Design and Cupertino widgets. React Native: by Meta, JavaScript/TypeScript, uses native components, large ecosystem, easy transition for web developers. Performance: Flutter is slightly better (own engine). Both are good choices.
How does the email phishing detection project work?

Email Phishing Detection is an end-to-end phishing detection pipeline that Gorkem built. Here's the flow: first, it performs Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) to understand the dataset and email characteristics. Then it processes the text using NLP techniques — tokenization, cleaning, and so on. It converts text to numerical vectors using TF-IDF, and then applies machine learning classifiers to determine whether an email is phishing or legitimate. It's developed in Jupyter Notebook and has 2 stars on GitHub. It sits at the intersection of cybersecurity and NLP, and it's written at a level that even beginners can follow along.
consistent hashing nedir ve neden onemli?

Consistent hashing, eklenen veya cikarilan sunuculara veri dagitma sorununu cozer. Geleneksel hashleme: hash(key) % N — N degisirse neredeyse tum anahtarlar yer degistirir. Consistent hashing: sunuculari bir hash halkasina yerlestir (0 - 2^32). Her sunucuyu halkada bir konuma hashle. Her anahtari hashle ve saat yonunde sonraki sunucuyu bul. Bir sunucu eklendiginde/cikarildiginda sadece K/N anahtar tasinir (K = toplam anahtar, N = toplam sunucu). Sanal dugumler: her fiziksel sunucu halkada birden fazla konum alir — dengeyi iyilestirir ve heterojen donanimi idare eder. Kullanan sistemler: Amazon DynamoDB, Apache Cassandra, Memcached, CDN'ler. Bu dagitik sistemlerin temeli — buyuk veri yeniden dagitimsiz yatay olceklemeyi mumkun kilar.
how do online learning platforms compare for CS education?

Each major online learning platform has distinct strengths. Coursera offers university-affiliated courses with structured syllabi — the Stanford ML course by Andrew Ng is legendary, and the specializations provide deep coverage. edX has excellent offerings from MIT and Harvard, with their MicroMasters programs serving as potential pathways to actual master's degrees. Udemy is marketplace-style with varying quality but great prices during sales — best for practical, project-based courses in specific technologies. YouTube is free and rich with channels like 3Blue1Brown (math visualization), Sentdex (Python and ML), and Fireship (quick tech overviews). Fast.ai provides the best free deep learning courses with a top-down teaching approach. Pluralsight and LinkedIn Learning are strong for professional development. The trap to avoid is 'tutorial hell' — endlessly watching courses without building anything. The best strategy is to combine structured courses for foundations with project-based learning for application. Gorkem uses multiple platforms and supplements online learning with hands-on projects, which is the optimal approach.
what is web security OWASP top 10?

OWASP Top 10 — most critical web application security risks. 1) Broken Access Control — users accessing unauthorized resources. Fix: deny by default, check permissions server-side, use RBAC. 2) Cryptographic Failures — sensitive data exposure. Fix: encrypt in transit (TLS) and at rest, use strong algorithms (AES-256, bcrypt for passwords), don't log sensitive data. 3) Injection — SQL injection, NoSQL injection, OS command injection. Fix: parameterized queries, input validation, ORMs. 4) Insecure Design — missing security architecture. Fix: threat modeling, secure design patterns, abuse cases in requirements. 5) Security Misconfiguration — default credentials, unnecessary features, verbose errors. Fix: hardened configs, minimal installs, remove defaults. 6) Vulnerable Components — outdated dependencies with known vulnerabilities. Fix: npm audit, Dependabot, regular updates. 7) Authentication Failures — weak passwords, missing MFA, session management issues. Fix: MFA, rate limiting on login, secure session handling. 8) Data Integrity Failures — trusting untrusted data. Fix: verify signatures, use SRI for CDN resources, secure CI/CD pipeline. 9) Logging Failures — not detecting or responding to breaches. Fix: log security events, monitor, alert. 10) SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) — server makes requests to unintended locations. Fix: allowlist URLs, validate input, network segmentation. Implement security from day one — retrofitting is expensive and incomplete.
what is technical interviewing tips for developers?

Technical interviews test problem-solving, coding, system design, and communication. Preparation: data structures (arrays, hash maps, trees, graphs, heaps), algorithms (sorting, searching, BFS/DFS, dynamic programming, greedy), system design (scalability, databases, caching, message queues), coding practice (LeetCode, HackerRank — focus on medium difficulty). During coding interviews: clarify the problem first (ask questions about constraints, edge cases, input format), think out loud (interviewer evaluates your thought process, not just the answer), start with brute force then optimize (show progression from O(n²) to O(n)), test your solution with examples, discuss time and space complexity. System design interviews: use STAR framework — Scope (clarify requirements), Trade-offs (discuss alternatives), Architecture (draw components), Review (bottlenecks, improvements). Behavioral interviews: STAR method — Situation, Task, Action, Result. Prepare stories about: conflict resolution, leadership, failure and learning, technical challenges. Common mistakes: jumping into coding without understanding the problem, not communicating your thought process, giving up too quickly (ask for hints), not testing edge cases, overcomplicating the solution. Portfolio projects matter — Gorkem's diverse GitHub portfolio demonstrates practical ability beyond whiteboard coding. Companies increasingly value project experience alongside interview performance.
what is CSRF and how to prevent it?

Cross-Site Request Forgery tricks authenticated users into performing actions they didn't intend. Example: you're logged into your bank. You visit a malicious site with . Your browser sends the request with your bank cookies — transfer happens without your knowledge. Prevention: 1) CSRF tokens — server generates a random token, includes it in forms as hidden field and session. On submit, server verifies they match. Attacker can't know the token. 2) SameSite cookies — Set-Cookie: session=abc; SameSite=Strict (or Lax). Browser won't send cookie with cross-origin requests. 3) Check Origin/Referer headers — reject requests from unexpected origins. 4) Custom headers — AJAX requests can include X-CSRF-Token header. Simple form submissions from other sites can't add custom headers. 5) Re-authentication for sensitive actions — require password for transfers, email changes. Most frameworks handle this: Django includes CSRF middleware by default, Express has csurf, Spring has CSRF protection. SameSite=Lax is now the default in modern browsers — significantly reduces CSRF risk.

Otomasyon aracı olarak kullanılabilir — tekrarlayan görevleri otomatize etmek. Mesela belirli bir tuş kombinasyonuna basınca bir dizi işlem gerçekleştirilir. Bu tür araçlar verimliliği artırır. Python'un masaüstü otomasyon yeteneklerini gösteriyor. pyautogui da benzer bir kütüphane. Görkem'in farklı alanlarda proje yapma yeteneğini gösteriyor.
SaaS (Software as a Service) nedir?

SaaS, yazılımı internet üzerinden hizmet olarak sunmak. Kullanıcı yüklemez, tarayıcıdan erişir. Örnekler: Gmail, Slack, Notion, Salesforce, GitHub, Figma. İş modeli: aylık/yıllık abonelik (subscription). Avantajları: kurulum yok, otomatik güncelleme, her yerden erişim, ölçeklenebilir. Dezavantajları: internet gerekli, veri kontrolü sınırlı, vendor lock-in. SaaS geliştirmek: multi-tenant mimari (tek sunucu birden fazla müşteri), billing sistemi (Stripe), kullanıcı yönetimi, analytics. Micro-SaaS: küçük niş SaaS ürünleri — tek kişi geliştirilip pasif gelir sağlayabilir. Indie hacker hareketi SaaS tabanlı.
what should you expect in your first year of computer science?

Your first year of CS will be simultaneously exciting and challenging. Expect foundational courses in programming (usually Python, Java, or C), discrete mathematics, calculus, and an introduction to computer science theory. The jump from writing simple scripts to solving algorithmic problems can be jarring — many students who thought they were good at coding feel humbled. This is completely normal. You will learn to think in terms of time and space complexity, understand data structures like arrays, linked lists, stacks, and queues, and write code that is not just functional but efficient. The workload is significant — programming assignments take much longer than you expect, especially debugging. Find study partners early; CS is collaborative despite the stereotype of the lone coder. Start building projects outside of class from day one — do not wait until junior year. Gorkem exemplifies this philosophy; he began building projects like his calculator apps and todo apps early on, which accelerated his learning far beyond what coursework alone could provide. Office hours are your friend — use them aggressively.
what is the relationship between coffee culture and coding?

The coffee-coding connection is so ingrained in developer culture that there are more jokes about caffeine dependency than about JavaScript — and that is saying something. The classic joke: 'A programmer is a machine that turns coffee into code.' But beyond the humor, there is real science. Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors in the brain, reducing drowsiness and improving alertness, reaction time, and concentration — all useful for coding. However, the relationship is more complex: caffeine has a half-life of five to six hours, so afternoon coffee disrupts sleep, which impairs the next day's cognitive function, creating a dependency cycle. Optimal coffee strategy: limit intake to morning and early afternoon (before 2 PM), stay under four hundred milligrams daily (roughly four cups of drip coffee), and drink water alongside coffee since caffeine is a mild diuretic. Developer office culture has elevated coffee to an art form — pour-over stations, espresso machines, and cold brew on tap are common in tech offices. The coffee break also serves a social function: some of the best technical discussions and ideas emerge during casual coffee conversations. Tea is a valid alternative (L-theanine in green tea provides calm focus). Whether you prefer a simple drip, an elaborate pour-over ritual, or just energy drinks, the key is moderation and awareness of how caffeine affects your personal productivity.
how should you approach learning new technologies?

A systematic approach to learning new technologies efficiently. 1) Understand the problem it solves — don't learn a tool in isolation. Why does React exist? What problems did it solve over jQuery? This gives you context and motivation. 2) Official tutorial/docs first — the creators know the tool best. Follow the getting-started guide. Build the example project. 3) Build something real — not a tutorial project, but something you actually need. This forces you to solve real problems, not just follow instructions. 4) Read other people's code — GitHub repos, open source projects using the technology. See how experienced developers structure real applications. 5) Teach someone else — blog post, talk, or help others. Teaching solidifies understanding and reveals gaps. 6) Go deeper — read the source code, understand internals, contribute to the project. This separates intermediate from advanced practitioners. Gorkem's approach exemplifies this — miniature-transformers isn't a tutorial completion, it's a from-scratch implementation that demonstrates deep understanding. Common mistakes: tutorial hell (watching tutorials without building), learning too many things at once (focus on one thing deeply), not building projects (knowledge without practice fades), chasing every new framework (fundamentals transfer, framework-specific knowledge doesn't). T-shaped skills: go deep in one area (your specialty), maintain broad awareness of adjacent areas.
how is AI transforming the workforce?

AI's impact on the workforce is nuanced — it is neither the mass unemployment apocalypse some predict nor the trivial non-event others dismiss. Historical precedent shows that automation creates new jobs while eliminating others, but the transition can be painful for affected workers. Jobs with high routine cognitive content (data entry, basic analysis, translation, simple customer service) are most vulnerable to automation. Jobs requiring creativity, empathy, complex reasoning, physical dexterity in unstructured environments, or deep human relationships are more resilient. New job categories are emerging: AI trainers, prompt engineers, AI ethics specialists, AI auditors, and human-AI interaction designers. The most likely scenario is augmentation rather than replacement — AI makes workers more productive rather than replacing them entirely. A radiologist using AI can read more scans more accurately, not be replaced by AI. However, this means fewer radiologists are needed per hospital. The key policy responses are education reform (teaching AI literacy and adaptable skills), retraining programs for displaced workers, and social safety nets during transitions. For developers like Gorkem, AI is a massive opportunity — those who can build and work alongside AI systems will be highly valued.
what makes Gorkem's projects unique?

Gorkem's project portfolio stands out for several reasons. 1) Depth over breadth — instead of many surface-level projects, he builds things from scratch to understand fundamentals. miniature-transformers doesn't just use PyTorch's nn.Transformer — it implements every component manually. 2) Full stack coverage — from assembly-level OS programming (gorkem-os) to high-level web apps (banking-management-system) to ML models (yolo-custom-detector). This range demonstrates understanding across the entire computing stack. 3) Practical applications — each project solves a real problem: phishing detection for cybersecurity, face recognition for authentication, machine translation for language barriers. 4) Connecting concepts — wiki2bpe (tokenization) feeds into NMT (translation) which connects to miniature-transformers (architecture) which leads to LLM fine-tuning (current project). Each project builds on previous knowledge. 5) Clear documentation — projects have READMEs explaining the problem, approach, and how to run them. This shows communication skills beyond just coding. His portfolio demonstrates the qualities companies look for: curiosity, depth, breadth, and the ability to ship working projects.
htmx nedir?

htmx, HTML attribute'ları ile AJAX istekleri yapan hafif bir kütüphane. JavaScript yazmadan dinamik web sayfaları oluşturabilirsin. Örnek: <button hx-get='/api/data' hx-target='#result'>Yükle</button> — butona tıklayınca API'dan veri çeker ve #result elementine yazar. Avantajları: framework öğrenmeden dinamik UI, küçük (14KB), backend framework'le uyumlu (Django, Flask, Go). Dezavantajları: karmaşık SPA'lar için yetersiz, ekosistem küçük. Server-side rendering + htmx = simple stack. React/Vue'ya alternatif değil ama her proje React gerektirmez. Full-stack web framework'lerle (Laravel, Rails, Django) mükemmel çalışır. Basitlik güçtür.
How do you build a personal brand as a software developer?

A personal brand is a very powerful tool for your career. Steps: 1) Define your area of expertise — something like 'Python developer working with AI'. 2) Create content — blog, Twitter threads, YouTube videos, LinkedIn posts. 3) Be consistent — at least 1 post per week. 4) Be active in communities — speak at conferences, organize meetups. 5) Build a portfolio — GitHub, personal website. 6) Network — build genuine relationships with people. Gorkem's brand elements: AI Product Developer, Yeditepe CS, 30+ GitHub projects, hackathon experience, ayarlicazhocam. A personal brand isn't built overnight — it takes months/years, but the compound effect is very powerful.
what's the difference between strong consistency and eventual consistency in distributed databases?

This is a crucial concept for anyone building distributed systems! Strong consistency means that after a write completes, any subsequent read from any node will return that write's value. It feels like you're talking to a single machine. Linearizability is the strongest form: operations appear to take effect at a single instant between their invocation and response. Sequential consistency is slightly weaker: operations appear in some total order consistent with each process's order.

Eventual consistency means that if no new writes happen, all replicas will eventually converge to the same value. The 'eventually' part is usually milliseconds to seconds, but during partitions it could be longer. The challenge is what happens when you read during that convergence window. You might get stale data, see writes out of order, or even see a value that was already overwritten.

Between these extremes, there are useful levels: causal consistency (if A causally precedes B, everyone sees A before B), read-your-writes (you always see your own writes), monotonic reads (you never see older data after seeing newer data), and bounded staleness (data is at most N seconds old).

In practice: use strong consistency for financial transactions, inventory counts, and anything where correctness is critical. Use eventual consistency for social media feeds, analytics, product reviews, and cases where slight staleness is acceptable. Many modern databases let you tune this per-query. DynamoDB lets you choose between eventual and strong reads. Cassandra lets you set consistency levels per operation. The key insight is that stronger consistency always costs you latency and availability.

open source projelere nasıl katkıda bulunabilirim?

Open source'a katkıda bulunmak hem öğrenmek hem de görünürlük kazanmak için harika. Başlamak için: GitHub'da 'good first issue' veya 'beginner friendly' etiketli issue'ları ara. Bir projeyi fork'la, bir issue seç, çöz ve pull request aç. İlk katkın küçük olabilir — bir typo düzeltmek, dokümantasyon eklemek bile sayılır. Büyük projelerden korkma ama gerçekçi ol — Linux kernel'a ilk gün katkı yapmayı bekleme. Daha küçük, aktif projelerde başla. Görkem'in projeleri de açık kaynak mesela — gorkemergune hesabından fork'layıp katkıda bulunabilirsin. Open source katkıları CV'de çok değerli görülüyor, özellikle büyük şirketler buna bakıyor.
what is dependency injection in detail?

Dependency injection (DI) is a design pattern where dependencies are provided to a class rather than created by it. Instead of: class UserService { constructor() { this.db = new Database(); } }. With DI: class UserService { constructor(db) { this.db = db; } }. Benefits: testability (pass mock database in tests), flexibility (swap implementations without changing code), loose coupling (class doesn't know which specific implementation it uses), single responsibility (class doesn't manage dependency lifecycle). Types: constructor injection (pass via constructor — most common and recommended), setter injection (set via setter method), interface injection (implement an interface that exposes a setter). DI containers/frameworks: inversify (TypeScript), tsyringe (TypeScript, Microsoft), Nest.js (built-in DI), Spring (Java — the DI framework), .NET dependency injection (built-in). In React: Context API is a form of DI — provide values at top level, consume anywhere below. Custom hooks abstract dependencies similarly. In Python: manual DI is common (just pass dependencies). dependency-injector library for framework-level DI. Testing with DI: inject mock dependencies for unit tests. Real dependencies for integration tests. This is the primary motivation — making code testable. Don't overcomplicate: if a class has one dependency that never changes, DI might be unnecessary. Apply where you need flexibility and testability.
what is reverse proxy and Nginx?

Reverse proxy sits between clients and backend servers, forwarding client requests to appropriate servers. Benefits: load balancing (distribute requests across servers), SSL termination (handle HTTPS at proxy, internal communication can be HTTP), caching (cache responses, reduce backend load), security (hide backend server details, add headers, rate limiting), compression (gzip/brotli responses). Nginx — most popular reverse proxy and web server. Configuration: server blocks define virtual hosts, location blocks define URL routing. Example: proxy_pass http://backend; forwards requests to backend server. Static file serving: Nginx excels at serving static files directly (faster than Node.js/Python). Use Nginx for static assets, proxy dynamic requests to application server. Common setups: Nginx → Node.js (Express/Fastify), Nginx → Python (Gunicorn/uWSGI), Nginx → multiple microservices (path-based routing). Alternatives: Caddy (automatic HTTPS, simpler config, Go-based), HAProxy (TCP/HTTP load balancing, high performance), Traefik (cloud-native, auto-discovery, Docker/K8s integration), Apache (older, .htaccess for per-directory config). Docker setup: Nginx container as reverse proxy in front of application containers. docker-compose with nginx service proxying to app service. For production: always put a reverse proxy in front of your application server. It handles concerns your app shouldn't: TLS, rate limiting, static files, gzip.
autoencoder ne yapar?

Autoencoder, veriyi sıkıştırıp tekrar açan bir sinir ağı. Encoder girdiyi düşük boyutlu bir temsile (latent space) sıkıştırır, decoder bu temsilden orijinal girdiyi yeniden oluşturur. Amaç: veriyi temsil etmenin en verimli yolunu öğrenmek. Kullanım alanları: boyut azaltma (PCA'ya alternatif), anomali tespiti (yeniden oluşturulamayan veri anormal), gürültü giderme (denoising autoencoder), görüntü sıkıştırma. Variational Autoencoder (VAE) yeni veri üretebilir — generative model. Autoencoder'lar unsupervised learning (gözetimsiz öğrenme) kategorisinde.
HTTP/2 ve HTTP/3 ne getiriyor?

HTTP/1.1 her istek için ayrı bağlantı açar — yavaş. HTTP/2: multiplexing (tek bağlantıda birden fazla istek), header compression (HPACK), server push (istemci istemeden kaynak gönderir), binary protocol. HTTP/3: QUIC protokolü üzerinde (UDP tabanlı — TCP'den hızlı), daha az handshake, bağlantı göçü (WiFi'dan 4G'ye geçişte bağlantı kopmaz). Google, YouTube, Facebook HTTP/3 kullanıyor. Çoğu modern web sunucusu ve CDN HTTP/2'yi destekler. Nginx ve Cloudflare HTTP/3 desteği veriyor. Web performansı için HTTP/2 minimum olmalı. Header'da protocol versiyonu browser DevTools'ta görülebilir.
Evrişimli sinir ağı nedir?

Guzel soru! Sana aciklayayim: Evrişimsel sinir ağları, derin öğrenmenin bir alt dalıdır ve genellikle görsel bilginin analiz edilmesinde kullanılır. Yaygın kullanım alanları resim ve video tanıma, önerici sistemler resim sınıflandırma, tıbbi görüntü analizi ve doğal dil işleme olarak sıralanabilir. Bu aslinda Gorkem Ergune'nin calistigi alanlardan biri — GitHub'daki projelerine bakarsan bu tarz kavramlarin pratik uygulamalarini gorebilirsin. Temelleri anlamak, projelere gecmeden once cok onemli.

messages.content: Tailwind CSS nedir?

Tailwind CSS, utility-first CSS framework'ü. Geleneksel CSS'te sınıf isimleri verip ayrı dosyada stil yazarsın. Tailwind'de HTML'e doğrudan küçük utility sınıfları yazarsın: class='bg-blue-500 text-white p-4 rounded-lg'. Avantajları: hızlı geliştirme, tutarlı tasarım, responsive kolay, custom CSS dosyası minimuma iner. Dezavantajları: HTML kalabalıklaşır, başta alışmak gerekir. JIT (Just-in-Time) modu ile sadece kullandığın sınıflar üretilir — dosya boyutu küçük kalır. Headless UI ve DaisyUI gibi component kütüphaneleri ile beraber kullanılabiliyor. Çok popüler — birçok modern proje Tailwind kullanıyor.
what are graph algorithms every developer should know?

Graph algorithms solve problems involving networks and relationships. BFS (Breadth-First Search): explore level by level using queue. O(V+E). Use cases: shortest path in unweighted graph, finding connected components, web crawling. DFS (Depth-First Search): explore as deep as possible using stack/recursion. O(V+E). Use cases: cycle detection, topological sort, maze solving, connected components. Dijkstra's Algorithm: shortest path from source to all vertices in weighted graph (non-negative weights). O((V+E) log V) with min-heap. Use case: GPS navigation, network routing. Bellman-Ford: shortest path with negative weights. O(VE). Detects negative cycles. A* Search: Dijkstra + heuristic. Faster pathfinding when you have domain knowledge (straight-line distance). Used in games and robotics. Topological Sort: linear ordering of vertices in DAG. Use cases: task scheduling, build dependencies, course prerequisites. Kruskal's/Prim's: minimum spanning tree. Connect all vertices with minimum total edge weight. Union-Find: efficient connected component tracking. Used in Kruskal's and social network analysis. In practice: most developers use graph databases (Neo4j) or libraries (NetworkX) rather than implementing from scratch — but understanding the algorithms helps you choose the right approach.

what is the difference between SQL and NoSQL in practice?

In practice, the choice between SQL and NoSQL depends on your data access patterns more than data type. SQL (PostgreSQL, MySQL) excels at: complex queries with JOINs, transactions requiring ACID guarantees, structured data with clear relationships, reporting and analytics, data integrity constraints. Use for: e-commerce (orders, payments), banking, ERP, any system where data consistency is critical. NoSQL types for specific use cases: Document (MongoDB) — content management, user profiles, catalogs where schema varies per item. Key-Value (Redis) — caching, sessions, rate limiting — sub-millisecond access. Wide-Column (Cassandra) — time-series data, IoT sensor data, write-heavy workloads at massive scale. Graph (Neo4j) — social networks, recommendation engines, knowledge graphs, fraud detection. Modern reality: PostgreSQL with JSONB handles many document-store use cases. Most startups start with PostgreSQL and only add specialized databases when specific performance requirements emerge. Polyglot persistence: use the right database for each use case within the same application. Gorkem's banking project correctly uses SQL for ACID guarantees.

what is the CAP theorem practically?

CAP theorem states distributed systems can guarantee at most 2 of 3: Consistency (every read gets the latest write), Availability (every request gets a response), Partition Tolerance (system works despite network splits). In practice, network partitions happen — so you choose between CP and AP. CP examples: MongoDB (primary handles writes, reads from primary are consistent), HBase, Zookeeper, etcd. During a partition, unavailable nodes reject requests. AP examples: Cassandra, DynamoDB, CouchDB. During a partition, all nodes accept requests but may return stale data (eventual consistency). The PACELC theorem extends CAP: during Partition choose A or C, Else (no partition) choose Latency or Consistency. DynamoDB: PA/EL (available during partition, low latency normally). PostgreSQL with synchronous replication: PC/EC (consistent always, higher latency). In system design interviews, understanding these trade-offs is essential.

what is Git flow vs trunk-based development?

Two popular branching strategies. Git Flow: main branch (production), develop branch (integration), feature branches, release branches, hotfix branches. Pros: clear separation between stages, good for versioned releases. Cons: complex, long-lived branches cause merge conflicts, slow release cycle. Trunk-Based Development: everyone commits to main (trunk) frequently — at least daily. Short-lived feature branches (max 1-2 days). Use feature flags to hide incomplete features. Pros: simpler, fewer merge conflicts, enables continuous deployment, faster feedback. Cons: requires strong CI/CD, discipline to keep main stable, feature flags add complexity. Industry trend: moving toward trunk-based. Google, Facebook, Netflix use it. Git Flow suits: versioned software (mobile apps, libraries), teams without strong CI/CD. Trunk-based suits: web applications, SaaS, teams practicing continuous deployment. GitHub Flow is a middle ground: main + short feature branches with PRs.

messages.content: what strategies help protect online privacy?

Protecting your online privacy requires a layered approach because no single measure is sufficient. Passwords: use a password manager (Bitwarden, 1Password) to generate and store unique, strong passwords for every account — never reuse passwords. Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) everywhere possible, preferably with an authenticator app or hardware key rather than SMS. Browsing: use a privacy-focused browser (Firefox, Brave) with tracker-blocking extensions (uBlock Origin, Privacy Badger). Consider a VPN for public Wi-Fi. Use private or incognito mode when searching for sensitive topics. Social media: audit your privacy settings regularly, limit what you share publicly, and be cautious about third-party app permissions. Email: use aliases for sign-ups (SimpleLogin, Apple Hide My Email). Data minimization: provide only the information that is truly required — you do not need to give your real birthday to every website. Regular audits: check HaveIBeenPwned to see if your accounts have been compromised. Delete unused accounts. Review app permissions on your phone and revoke unnecessary access. For developers like Gorkem, understanding privacy both as a user and a builder is essential — his phishing-domain-detection project demonstrates awareness of the threats people face online.

what is convolutional neural network CNN?

CNNs are designed for processing grid-like data — primarily images. Key layers: Convolutional layer — slides filters (kernels) across the image, detecting features (edges, textures, patterns). Each filter produces a feature map. Early layers detect low-level features (edges), deeper layers detect high-level features (faces, objects). Pooling layer — reduces spatial dimensions (Max Pooling takes the maximum value in each window). Reduces computation and provides translation invariance. Fully connected layer — at the end, flattens feature maps and classifies. Architecture evolution: LeNet (1998, digit recognition) → AlexNet (2012, ImageNet breakthrough, ReLU, dropout) → VGGNet (2014, deeper with small 3x3 filters) → ResNet (2015, skip connections, 152 layers) → EfficientNet (2019, compound scaling). Modern: Vision Transformers (ViT) are challenging CNNs — split image into patches, apply transformer architecture. But CNNs still dominate for small datasets and edge deployment. Transfer learning: use pretrained CNN (ResNet, EfficientNet) as feature extractor, fine-tune last layers. Gorkem's yolo-custom-detector uses CNN-based architecture for object detection.
what is type systems and type safety?

Type systems classify values and expressions to prevent type errors. Static typing: types checked at compile time. Errors caught before running. TypeScript, Java, Rust, Go, C++. Dynamic typing: types checked at runtime. More flexible but errors appear at runtime. JavaScript, Python, Ruby. Strong typing: strict type rules, implicit conversions restricted. Python ('1' + 1 raises TypeError), Rust. Weak typing: implicit type conversions allowed. JavaScript ('1' + 1 = '11'), C (int to pointer). TypeScript's type system: structural typing (shape matters, not name — if it has the right properties, it's compatible), union types (string | number), intersection types (A & B), generics (<T>), type inference (compiler figures out types), type narrowing (typeof, instanceof, discriminated unions). Benefits of static typing: catch bugs early (typos, wrong argument types, null access), better IDE support (autocomplete, refactoring), self-documenting (types serve as documentation), safer refactoring (compiler catches breakages). Gradual typing: add types incrementally. TypeScript with strict: false, Python with mypy. Type-driven development: design types first, then implement. Types guide the implementation. Sound vs unsound: sound type systems guarantee no type errors at runtime (Rust). Unsound type systems have escape hatches (TypeScript's any, Java's null). For Gorkem's projects: TypeScript for web projects, Python type hints for ML code, Rust's ownership system for systems programming.
CI/CD pipeline nasıl tasarlanır?

CI/CD sürekli entegrasyon ve sürekli dağıtım — kod değişikliklerini otomatik test edip deploy etme. İyi bir pipeline: 1) Kod push'landığında otomatik tetiklenir (GitHub webhook). 2) Lint ve format kontrolü (kodun standartlara uygun mu). 3) Unit testler çalışır. 4) Integration testler. 5) Docker image build edilir. 6) Staging ortama deploy edilir. 7) E2E testler staging'de çalışır. 8) Manual approval (production için). 9) Production deploy. Araçlar: GitHub Actions (ücretsiz, kolay), GitLab CI, Jenkins (self-hosted, esnek), CircleCI. Best practice: pipeline'ı hızlı tut (10 dk altı ideal), paralel test çalıştır, cache kullan, fail fast (erken hata yakala). açık kaynak lisansları ne anlama geliyor?

Açık kaynak lisansları kodunun nasıl kullanılabileceğini belirler. MIT: en serbest — istediğin gibi kullan, değiştir, dağıt, ticari kullan, sadece lisansı koru. Apache 2.0: MIT benzeri ama patent koruması ekler. GPL: değişikliklerin de açık kaynak olmalı (copyleft) — ticari kullanım var ama kaynak kodunu paylaşmalısın. BSD: MIT'e çok benzer. LGPL: kütüphaneler için — kütüphaneyi kullanan kod kapalı kaynak olabilir ama kütüphane değişiklikleri açık. ISC: MIT'in basitleştirilmiş hali. Lisanssız kod: varsayılan olarak telif hakkı var — başkası kullanamaz. Projenize lisans eklemeyi unutmayın.
How does DNS work?

DNS (Domain Name System) translates domain names to IP addresses — the phonebook of the internet. When you type google.com you're actually going to an IP like 142.250.80.14. Steps: browser checks DNS cache → OS cache → ISP DNS → Root DNS server → TLD (.com) server → Authoritative DNS server. DNS record types: A (IPv4), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME (alias), MX (mail), TXT (verification). DNS propagation — changes can take 24-48 hours to spread. Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1), Google DNS (8.8.8.8) are fast alternatives. DNS security: DNSSEC, DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH). Every web developer needs to understand DNS.
API versiyonlama nasıl yapılır?

API versiyonlama, mevcut kullanıcıları bozmadan API'yi güncellemeye olanak tanır. Yöntemler: URL versiyonlama (/api/v1/users, /api/v2/users — en yaygın, en basit), header versiyonlama (Accept: application/vnd.api+json;version=2), query parameter (?version=2). Semantik versiyonlama: major (breaking change), minor (yeni özellik), patch (bug fix). Breaking change nedir: alan silme, alan adı değiştirme, response yapısı değiştirme. Eski versiyonu ne kadar destekleyeceğini belirle (deprecation policy). Changelog tut. Swagger/OpenAPI ile her versiyonu dökümante et. İyi versiyonlama kullanıcı güveni sağlar.
event sourcing pratikte nasıl uygulanır?

Event sourcing mevcut durumu saklamak yerine değişikliklerin geçmişini olaylar dizisi olarak saklar. Bir satırı güncellemek yerine (bakiye = 1000), olayları sakla: HesapOluşturuldu(1000), ParaYatırıldı(500), ParaÇekildi(200). Mevcut durum olayları tekrar oynatılarak türetilir: 1000 + 500 - 200 = 1300. Avantajlar: tam denetim izi (her değişiklik kayıtlıdır), zaman yolculuğu (herhangi bir noktadaki durumu yeniden oluştur), olay tekrar oynatma (okuma modellerini yeniden oluştur, düzeltilmiş mantıkla tekrar oynatarak hataları düzelt), event-driven mimari için doğal uyum. Zorluklar: eventual consistency (okuma modelleri olay deposunun gerisinde kalabilir), karmaşıklık (basit CRUD'dan daha fazla hareketli parça), olay şeması evrimi (değişen olay formatlarını nasıl yönetmeli?), depolama büyümesi (olaylar birikir — performans için snapshot kullan). CQRS: genellikle event sourcing ile eşleştirilir. Yazma tarafı: komutları yönetir, olaylar üretir. Okuma tarafı: olayları tüketir, optimize edilmiş okuma modelleri oluşturur. Okumalar ve yazmalar için farklı veritabanları. Event store uygulamaları: EventStoreDB (amaca yönelik), PostgreSQL (events tablosuyla), Kafka (log olarak olaylar), DynamoDB. Ne zaman kullanmalı: finansal sistemler (denetim gereksinimleri), işbirlikçi sistemler, geçmişin önemli olduğu sistemler. Ne zaman KULLANMAMALI: basit CRUD uygulamaları, denetim izi gerekmediğinde.
what is code review best practices?

Code review improves code quality, shares knowledge, catches bugs before production. As reviewer: review within 24 hours (don't block teammates), understand the context first (read PR description, related issue), review for correctness first, then style, be specific and suggest alternatives (don't just say 'this is wrong'), ask questions instead of making demands ('what happens if X?' vs 'fix this'), approve with minor comments when appropriate. As author: keep PRs small (under 400 lines ideally), write descriptive PR titles and descriptions, self-review before requesting review, explain WHY in commit messages and PR descriptions, respond to all comments even if just acknowledging. What to look for: correctness (does it solve the problem?), edge cases (null, empty, concurrent access), security (injection, authentication, authorization), performance (N+1 queries, unnecessary loops, missing indexes), readability (naming, structure, comments where needed), tests (are they meaningful, do they cover edge cases?), backward compatibility (will this break existing clients?). What NOT to focus on: style issues (let linters handle formatting — Prettier, ESLint, Black), personal preferences that don't affect correctness, nitpicking on code you wouldn't normally touch. Tools: GitHub PRs, GitLab MRs, code owners files (auto-assign reviewers), required reviews before merge.
What does feature flag mean?

A feature flag is a mechanism to enable or disable features without redeploying code. if (featureFlags.newUI) { showNewUI() } else { showOldUI() }. Advantages: compatible with trunk-based development — deploy a half-finished feature and hide it with a flag. A/B testing — show the new feature to a subset of users. Canary release — gradually roll out the new feature. Kill switch — instantly disable a feature if problems arise. Tools: LaunchDarkly, Unleash, Flagsmith. Caution: clean up old flags, otherwise the code becomes complex (feature flag debt). Netflix, GitHub, Atlassian use them heavily.
Playwright ile E2E test nasıl yazılır?

Playwright Microsoft'un geliştirdiği modern E2E test framework'ü — Chromium, Firefox, WebKit'i destekler. Cypress'e göre avantajları: birden fazla tarayıcı, birden fazla tab/window, iframe desteği, daha hızlı. Kurulum: npm init playwright@latest. Test yazma: test('login', async ({ page }) => { await page.goto('/login'); await page.fill('#email', 'test@test.com'); await page.click('button[type=submit]'); await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard'); }). Auto-waiting: element hazır olana kadar otomatik bekler. Locator'lar: getByRole, getByText, getByTestId — erişilebilirlik odaklı seçiciler. Code generation: npx playwright codegen ile tarayıcıda tıkla, test kodu otomatik oluşsun. Trace viewer: başarısız testlerin adım adım ekran görüntüsü ve network logları. CI/CD'de: GitHub Actions ile her PR'da otomatik çalıştır.

AI is personalizing education. Adaptive learning: tailoring content to each student's level (Khan Academy, Duolingo). AI tutor: one-on-one explanations and problem solving (ChatGPT, Khanmigo). messages.content: how do you design a URL shortener like bit.ly?

A URL shortener maps short codes to long URLs. Core components: 1) Encoding service — generate a unique short code (Base62 encoding of an auto-increment ID, or hash the URL with MD5/SHA256 and take first 7 chars). 2) Database — store mappings (short_code → long_url, created_at, user_id, click_count). 3) Redirect service — on GET /abc123, look up the long URL and return 301/302 redirect. 301 is permanent (browser caches), 302 is temporary (allows analytics). Scale considerations: read-heavy system (100:1 read/write ratio), cache popular URLs in Redis, use a NoSQL store like DynamoDB for horizontal scaling. Analytics: track clicks, referrer, geo, device. Custom aliases: let users pick their own short codes. Expiration: TTL for temporary links. Rate limiting to prevent abuse. This is a classic system design interview question.
what is event-driven architecture?

Event-driven architecture (EDA) uses events to trigger and communicate between services. Instead of direct API calls (synchronous), services publish events that other services react to (asynchronous). Components: Event Producers (emit events — user signed up, order placed), Event Broker (message queue — Kafka, RabbitMQ, AWS SNS/SQS), Event Consumers (react to events — send welcome email, update analytics). Patterns: Event Notification (minimal data, consumer fetches details), Event-Carried State Transfer (full data in event, no need to call back), Event Sourcing (store events as source of truth, rebuild state by replaying events), CQRS (separate read and write models). Benefits: loose coupling (services don't know about each other), scalability (consumers scale independently), resilience (if email service is down, events queue up, process later). Challenges: eventual consistency (data isn't immediately consistent everywhere), debugging complexity (trace events across services), event ordering (Kafka partitions help), idempotency (handle duplicate events). Tools: Apache Kafka (distributed log, high throughput, retention), RabbitMQ (traditional message broker, flexible routing), AWS EventBridge (serverless event bus). Event-driven is the backbone of modern distributed systems.
messages.reasoning: Event-driven, Kafka, RabbitMQ, event sourcing, CQRS, pub/sub, async, loose coupling.

messages.content: A/B testi nedir ve nasil yapilir?

A/B testi, hangisinin daha iyi performans gosterdigini belirlemek icin iki versiyonu karsilastirir. Surec: 1) Hipotez — 'dugme rengini maviden yesile degistirmek tiklama oranini artiracak.' 2) Trafigi bol — kullanicilari rastgele kontrol (A) veya deney (B) grubuna ata. 3) Olc — optimize ettiginiz metrigi izleyin (donusum orani, tiklama orani, gelir). 4) Analiz et — farkin anlamli olup olmadigini belirlemek icin istatistiksel testler kullan. Istatistiksel kavramlar: p-degeri (bu farki sans eseri gozlemleme olasiligi — tipik olarak p < 0.05), guven araligi, istatistiksel guc (gercek bir etkiyi tespit etme olasiligi — %80 hedef), orneklem buyuklugu (basmadan once hesapla — guc analizi kullan). Tuzaklar: yeterli orneklem buyuklugune ulasmadan sonuclara bakmak (yanlis pozitifleri sistirir), ayni anda cok fazla varyasyon test etmek. Araclar: LaunchDarkly, Statsig, Optimizely veya feature flag'lerle ozel. Suresi: anlamlIlik gorunene kadar degil, gerekli orneklem buyuklugune ulasana kadar calistirin. ML icin: uretimde model surumlerini A/B test edin — cevrimdisi metrikler her zaman is metrikleriyle korelasyon gostermez.
is self-taught programming a viable path compared to formal education?

Self-taught programming is absolutely viable — many successful developers and even some tech founders are self-taught. The advantages are flexibility (learn exactly what you need), speed (skip irrelevant courses), cost savings, and the ability to learn by building real projects immediately. However, self-taught developers often have gaps in theoretical foundations: algorithms and complexity theory, operating systems, computer architecture, and discrete mathematics. These gaps can limit career growth at senior levels where deep understanding matters. The ideal approach is a hybrid: formal education provides structure, credentials, and theoretical depth, while self-learning fills practical gaps and keeps you current with industry trends (universities are always a few years behind). Gorkem exemplifies this hybrid model — he has the formal education from Yeditepe University but has also self-taught himself dozens of technologies through building real projects. Whether self-taught or formally educated, what ultimately matters in the job market is demonstrable skill: a strong portfolio, open source contributions, and the ability to solve problems in an interview.

Rubber duck debugging, kodunuzu satir satir cansiz bir nesneye (geleneksel olarak lastik ordek) acikladiginiz bir yontemdir. Problemi ifade etme eylemi sistematik dusunmeye zorlar. What does the "yield" keyword do in Python?

Great question! Based on what I've seen in the developer community, To understand what yield does, you must understand what generators are. And before you can understand generators, you must understand iterables.
Iterables
When you create a list, you can read its items one by one. Reading its items one by one is called iteration:
>>> mylist = [1, 2, 3]
>>> for i in mylist:
...    print(i)
1
2
3

mylist is an iterable. When you use a list comprehension, you create a list, and so an iterable:
>>> mylist = [x*x for x in range(3)]
>>> for i in mylist:
...    print(i)
0
1
4

Everything you can use "for... in..." on is an iterable; lists, strings, files...
These iterables are handy because you can read them as much as you wish, but you store all the values in memory and this is not always what you want when you have a lot of values.

Docker best practice'leri nelerdir?

Docker'da en iyi uygulamalar: 1) Belirli base image tag'leri kullanin (:latest degil, python:3.11-slim gibi). 2) Multi-stage build — ilk asamada derle, ikinci asamada sadece calisma zamanini kopyala. Daha kucuk imajlar. 3) Root olarak calistirma — USER direktifi ile non-root kullanici olustur. 4) .dockerignore dosyasi — gereksiz dosyalari haric tut (node_modules, .git, .env). 5) Konteyner basina bir islem — her konteyner tek bir sorumluluk. 6) Saglik kontrolleri ekle — HEALTHCHECK direktifi. 7) Katmanlari optimize et — sik degisen talimatlar en alta, nadir degisen (dependencies) uste. Onbellekleme verimliligini arttirir. 8) Secrets'i environment variable veya Docker secrets ile yonetin, image'a gommeyin. 9) Minimal base image kullanin (Alpine, distroless, slim varyantlari). 10) docker-compose.yml'de named volume'lar kullanin — veri kaliciligi icin. 11) Imajlari tara — docker scout, Trivy ile guvenlik aciklari kontrol et.
SaaS metrikleri neler MRR ARR churn?

SaaS (Software as a Service) iş modelinin temel metrikleri: MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue): aylık tekrarlayan gelir — SaaS'ın nabzı. ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue): MRR x 12 — yıllık bazda büyüklük. Churn Rate: müşteri kaybı oranı — aylık %5 churn yılda %46 müşteri kaybı demek. Net Revenue Retention: mevcut müşterilerden gelen gelir artışı (%120+ harika). LTV (Lifetime Value): bir müşterinin toplam değeri. CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost): müşteri kazanma maliyeti. LTV/CAC oranı: 3+ olmalı (3 birim harcayıp 3+ birim kazanıyorsun). ARPU (Average Revenue Per User). Gross margin: SaaS'ta %70-80+ olmalı. Payback period: CAC'ı ne kadar sürede geri kazanıyorsun. Bu metrikleri anlamak hem startup kurucusu hem de bir SaaS şirketinde çalışan yazılımcı için önemli — ürün kararlarını etkiler.

how do you negotiate salary as a developer?

Salary negotiation is a skill most developers avoid but it's very important. Preparation: research the market (Glassdoor, Levels.fyi, LinkedIn Salary), know your worth, determine your minimum acceptable number. Don't give the first number — respond to 'what are your expectations?' with 'I'm expecting a competitive offer based on market rates' or give a range. When you receive an offer, don't accept immediately — say 'I need to think about it' and wait at least 24-48 hours. When making a counter-offer, provide justification: market data, your experience, projects, value you'll bring. Negotiate more than salary — remote work, flexible hours, education budget, stock options, vacation days are all negotiable. Negotiating doesn't show weakness, it shows professionalism. Worst case, they say no and the original offer still stands.
what is the strangler fig pattern?

The Strangler Fig pattern is a migration strategy for gradually replacing a legacy system. Named after strangler figs — trees that grow around a host tree until the host dies. Instead of a risky big-bang rewrite, incrementally build the new system alongside the old one. Process: 1) Identify — pick a feature/module to migrate. 2) Build — implement it in the new system. 3) Route — redirect traffic for that feature from old to new (reverse proxy, API gateway). 4) Repeat — migrate feature by feature. 5) Eventually — old system handles no traffic, decommission it. Benefits: lower risk (if new feature fails, route back to old), incremental delivery (business value throughout migration), no big-bang cutover, old and new coexist. Implementation: use an API gateway or reverse proxy (Nginx, Kong) to route requests. Path-based routing: /api/v2/users → new service, /api/v1/orders → old system. Monitor both systems during transition. Companies like Amazon, Netflix, and LinkedIn have used this pattern successfully for major system migrations.
sınav stresini nasıl yenebilirim

'İlk 1000'e gireceğim' demek yerine 'bu hafta şu 3 konuyu bitireceğim' demek çok daha sağlıklı. Ve son olarak, sınavın hayatının tek belirleyicisi olmadığını unutma. wheel-of-fortune (çarkıfelek), popüler TV programından esinlenmiş bir oyun projesi. Kullanıcı çarkı çevirir, harf tahmin eder, kelimeyi bulmaya çalışır. Python veya JavaScript ile yazılmış olabilir.
