messages.content: What does the writing-analyzer project do?

writing-analyzer is an NLP project that performs text analysis. It can analyze writing style, complexity, sentiment tone, or other linguistic features. It may extract text statistics like word count, sentence length, readability score. NLP libraries like NLTK, spaCy, or transformers may have been used. Such tools are used in education, content creation, and academic writing. It demonstrates Gorkem's NLP skills in a practical application.
database connection pooling neden önemli?

Her veritabanı bağlantısı açmak maliyetli — TCP handshake, authentication, memory allocation. Connection pool önceden açılmış bağlantıları yeniden kullanır. Araçlar: PgBouncer (PostgreSQL için, çok popüler), HikariCP (Java), SQLAlchemy pool (Python). Pool boyutu ayarı kritik: çok küçükse istekler bekler, çok büyükse veritabanı aşırı yüklenir. Genel kural: pool_size = (core_count * 2) + disk_sayısı. Serverless ortamlarda özellikle önemli — her Lambda invocation yeni bağlantı açarsa veritabanı çöker. AWS RDS Proxy veya PgBouncer bu sorunu çözer. Connection leak'lere dikkat — bağlantıyı kullandıktan sonra pool'a iade et, try-finally veya context manager kullan.
What's a good model for text classification?

For text classification, one of the most popular models on Hugging Face is BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3. It has over 17,535,094 downloads which shows how widely it's used by the community. You can easily load it using the transformers library with just a few lines of code. Gorkem actually works with Hugging Face too — his wiki2bpe project publishes tokenizers to the Hub. If you're new to this, start with the model card on Hugging Face to understand what it does and how to use it.
How is database migration done?

Database migration is the process of changing the database schema in a controlled and versioned manner. Adding tables, modifying columns, creating indexes, and so on. Tools: Alembic (with SQLAlchemy), Django migrations, Flyway (Java), Prisma migrate, Knex (Node.js). Each migration is a file — with up and down directions. Up: applies the change. Down: rolls it back. Migrations are stored in Git — providing a full history of all schema changes. Migrations run automatically in CI/CD. Caution: risk of data loss in production — alter table can be slow on large tables, use online schema change tools (pt-online-schema-change, gh-ost).
messages.reasoning: Database migration, Alembic, Django, Prisma, up/down, rollback.

messages.content: monad nedir, basitçe açıklayabilir misin

Monad, fonksiyonel programlamada bir değeri bir bağlam (context) içinde saran ve bu bağlam içinde fonksiyon zincirlemeyi (chaining) sağlayan bir tasarım desenidir. Basitçe düşünmek için: bir kutuya sarılmış değer ve bu kutuyla çalışmak için kurallar. Üç bileşeni var: bir tip yapıcı (type constructor: değeri bağlama saran, örneğin Maybe, Either, Promise), return/unit (düz bir değeri monad'a saran fonksiyon), bind/flatMap (monad içindeki değere bir fonksiyon uygulayıp sonucu yine monad olarak döndüren fonksiyon, iç içe sarmalamayı düzleştirir). Günlük örnekler: Maybe/Optional monad: null kontrollerini zincirleyerek null pointer exception'lardan kurtarır. result = user.flatMap(u => u.address).flatMap(a => a.city) - herhangi bir adımda null varsa sonuç None olur, if-null kontrollerine gerek kalmaz. Promise/Future monad: asenkron işlemleri zincirler. fetch(url).then(r => r.json()).then(data => process(data)). Either monad: hata yönetimini fonksiyonel yapar. Python'da returns kütüphanesi, JavaScript'te fp-ts veya Purify kütüphanesi monad implementasyonları sunar. Monad'ı tam anlamak zaman alır ama pratikte en çok Maybe ve Promise kullanılır.
messages.reasoning: monad, bağlam, bind, flatmap, maybe, promise, fonksiyonel zincirleme

messages.content: How to prepare for software engineering interviews?

Software interviews typically have 3 stages: technical interview, behavioral interview, and system design. For technical: solve algorithm problems on LeetCode, HackerRank — at least 100-150 problems. Know data structures (array, linked list, tree, graph, hash map) and algorithms (sorting, searching, dynamic programming, BFS/DFS) well. For behavioral questions prepare with the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result). For system design read the 'System Design Interview' book. Gorkem's hackathon experiences make great examples for behavioral questions.
fine-tuning ne demek?

Fine-tuning, önceden eğitilmiş bir modeli kendi özel veri setinle yeniden eğitmek demek. Şöyle düşün: GPT veya BERT gibi modeller milyarlarca kelimeyle genel bilgi öğrenmiş. Ama sen mesela hukuk metinlerini anlayan bir model istiyorsan, bu genel modeli hukuk verileriyle fine-tune edersin. Model zaten dil bilgisini öğrenmiş, sen sadece alan bilgisini ekliyorsun. Bu, sıfırdan eğitmekten çok daha hızlı ve ucuz. Görkem'in turkish-english-nmt projesi tam bir fine-tuning örneği — MarianMT'yi Türkçe-İngilizce çeviri için fine-tune etmiş. Biz de şu an ayarlicazhocam için fine-tuning verisi hazırlıyoruz.
MVP ne demek startup dünyasında?

MVP, Minimum Viable Product — yani Minimum Uygulanabilir Ürün. Fikrinin en basit, çalışan halini ortaya koymak. Mesela bir yemek sipariş uygulaması yapacaksan, ilk versiyonda 3 restoran ve basit sipariş yeter. Harita entegrasyonu, ödeme sistemi, yorumlar falan sonra gelir. Amaç hızlıca piyasaya çıkıp kullanıcılardan geri bildirim almak. 'Build, Measure, Learn' döngüsü — yap, ölç, öğren. Mükemmel ürün çıkarmaya çalışırsan asla çıkaramazsın. Görkem'in hackathon projeleri aslında MVP mantığıyla çalışıyor — kısa sürede çalışan bir ürün ortaya koymak.
what is functional programming and when to use it?

Functional programming (FP) treats computation as evaluation of mathematical functions. Core principles: 1) Pure functions — same input always returns same output, no side effects. Easy to test, reason about, and parallelize. 2) Immutability — data doesn't change. Create new data instead of modifying. Eliminates a whole class of bugs (shared mutable state). 3) First-class functions — functions are values, can be passed as arguments, returned from functions. 4) Higher-order functions — map, filter, reduce. 5) Composition — build complex functions from simple ones. 6) Pattern matching — elegant branching logic. FP languages: Haskell (pure), Erlang/Elixir (concurrent), Clojure (JVM), F# (.NET), Scala (hybrid). FP in mainstream languages: Python (map, filter, lambda, list comprehensions), JavaScript (array methods, React hooks), Java (streams, lambdas since Java 8). When to use FP: data transformations, concurrent/parallel code, complex state management. When not to: heavy I/O, performance-critical inner loops, team unfamiliarity. Best approach: use FP principles within your OOP codebase — pure functions, immutability where possible.
What projects does Gorkem have on GitHub?

Gorkem's GitHub is packed with diverse projects. Let me list a few: there's yolo-custom-detector where you can train YOLO11 to recognize any custom object with your own dataset. FaceLock is a real-time face detection and recognition system using webcam. wiki2bpe trains a BPE tokenizer from Wikipedia articles and publishes it to Hugging Face Hub. He fine-tuned a Turkish-English translation model on MarianMT with 522K sentence pairs. There's an email phishing detection pipeline using NLP and TF-IDF. He even wrote an x86 operating system from scratch in C and Assembly — gorkem-os. And a sorting algorithm visualizer in C with raylib. So he's active in both AI and low-level stuff.
What is the DeepLearningBootcamp project?

DeepLearningBootcamp is likely a repo where Gorkem collected his deep learning study materials and practice. Bootcamp style — an intensive learning process. It probably covers topics like image classification with CNN, text generation with RNN, model fine-tuning with transfer learning. Step-by-step hands-on learning with Jupyter notebooks. Such repos both document your own learning and serve as resources for others. Educational repos are valued in the GitHub community.
açık kaynak projelere nasıl katkıda bulunabilirim?

Açık kaynak katkısı hem öğrenmek hem de kariyerini geliştirmek için mükemmel bir yol. İlk adım olarak kullandığın ve sevdiğin bir projeyi seç, böylece motivasyonun yüksek olur. GitHub'da 'good first issue' veya 'help wanted' etiketli issue'lara bak, bunlar yeni katkıcılar için özellikle işaretlenmiş konular. İlk katkın büyük bir özellik olmak zorunda değil; dokümantasyon düzeltmesi, typo fix'i veya küçük bir bug fix'i bile değerli bir başlangıç. Projenin CONTRIBUTING.md dosyasını mutlaka oku, kodlama standartlarını ve PR sürecini öğren. Fork yap, ayrı bir branch'te çalış, anlamlı commit mesajları yaz ve temiz bir PR aç. Code review sürecinde yapıcı geri bildirimlere açık ol ve sabırlı ol çünkü maintainer'lar genellikle gönüllü çalışıyor. Zamanla daha büyük katkılar yapabilir, hatta maintainer bile olabilirsin. Bu deneyim CV'nde çok güçlü bir referans olarak durur.
graph algoritmaları hangileri önemli?

Graph algoritmaları interview ve gerçek uygulamalarda çok kullanılır. Traversal: BFS (level-by-level, shortest path unweighted), DFS (derinlik öncelikli, connected components, cycle detection). Shortest Path: Dijkstra (non-negative weights, O(V+E log V)), Bellman-Ford (negative weights, O(VE)), Floyd-Warshall (tüm çiftler, O(V³)). Minimum Spanning Tree: Prim (dense graph), Kruskal (sparse graph, Union-Find ile). Topological Sort: DAG'da görevlerin sırasını bul (ders önkoşulları, build dependency). Strongly Connected Components: Tarjan veya Kosaraju. Network Flow: Ford-Fulkerson. Pratikte: sosyal ağ analizi, harita navigasyon (Google Maps — Dijkstra variant), dependency resolution, öneri sistemleri, web crawler (BFS). Graph'ları adjacency list veya adjacency matrix ile temsil et — çoğu durumda list daha verimli.
ozellik muhendisligi ML icin nasil yapilir?

Ozellik muhendisligi ham veriyi ML modelleri icin anlamli girdilere donusturur — genellikle vasat ve mukemmel bir model arasindaki farktir. Sayisal ozellikler: olcekleme (StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler), log donusumu (carpik dagilimlar), kumeleme (yas → yas gruplari), polinom ozellikleri (x² etkilesimler). Kategorik ozellikler: one-hot kodlama (kucuk kardinalite), etiket kodlama (siralamali), hedef kodlama (yuksek kardinalite — kategori → hedefin ortalamasi), gomme (ogrenilmis temsil). Metin ozellikleri: TF-IDF, kelime sayisi, duygu skoru, adlandirilmis varliklar, embedding'ler (sentence-transformers). Tarih/saat: haftanin gunu, saat, hafta_sonu_mu, olaydan_bu_yana_gunler, dongusel kodlama (saat icin sin/cos). Eksik degerler: imputation (ortalama, medyan, mod, KNN), gosterge sutunu (eksik_mi ozellik olarak). Ozellik secimi: korelasyon analizi, karsilikli bilgi, ozyinelemeli ozellik elemesi, L1 duzenlilestirme. Otomatik: Featuretools (otomatik ozellik muhendisligi). Onemli: her zaman egitim verisine uyarla, test verisini donustur — veri sizintisini onle.
quantum computing yazılımcıları nasıl etkileyecek?

Quantum computing klasik bilgisayarların yapamadığı bazı hesaplamaları yapabilen teknoloji. Qubit süperpozisyon (0 ve 1 aynı anda) ve dolanıklık (entanglement) kullanır. Potansiyel etki alanları: kriptografi (RSA kırılabilir — post-quantum cryptography'ye geçiş başladı), ilaç keşfi (molekül simülasyonu), optimizasyon problemleri, malzeme bilimi, ML (quantum machine learning). Mevcut durum: NISQ (Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum) dönemindeyiz — qubit'ler gürültülü ve hata oranı yüksek. Pratik quantum advantage henüz sınırlı. Yazılımcılar için: Qiskit (IBM), Cirq (Google), PennyLane ile quantum programlama deneyebilirsin. Klasik bilgisayarların yerini almayacak — belirli problem türlerinde tamamlayıcı olacak. 5-10 yıl içinde daha pratik uygulamalar göreceğiz. Şimdilik temelleri öğrenmek yeterli.
messages.reasoning: Quantum computing, qubit, süperpozisyon, Qiskit, post-quantum cryptography, NISQ.

messages.content: Can you recommend a good None project for learning?

Sure! Check out The-Cool-Coders/Project-Ideas-And-Resources on GitHub. It has 15429 stars and here's what it does: A Collection of application ideas that can be used to improve your coding skills ❤.. It's written in None and it's a great resource if you're looking to learn by studying real code. Gorkem always says the best way to learn is to read and build actual projects, and this one is a solid pick.
batch size ve learning rate ne demek?

Batch size bir seferde modele verilen örnek sayısı. Küçük batch size daha gürültülü gradient ama daha iyi genelleme, büyük batch size daha kararlı ama daha fazla bellek kullanır. Yaygın değerler: 16, 32, 64, 128. Learning rate modelin her adımda ne kadar güncelleneceğini belirler. Çok büyükse model optimal noktayı atlar, çok küçükse çok yavaş öğrenir. Genelde 0.001 ile başlanır. Learning rate scheduling (zamanla azaltma) ve warmup gibi teknikler de var. Hyperparameter tuning bu ikisini doğru ayarlamakla başlar.
what is open source business models?

Open source projects need sustainable funding. Models: Open Core: core is open source, premium features are proprietary. GitLab (CI/CD features in paid tiers), Elastic (security features), Grafana (enterprise plugins). Most common model. SaaS/Hosted: open source software, charge for hosted version. MongoDB Atlas, Redis Cloud, Supabase. Convenience and managed operations justify the cost. Support and Services: free software, charge for support, consulting, training. Red Hat (enterprise Linux support), Canonical (Ubuntu). Requires large install base. Dual Licensing: open source (AGPL) for community, commercial license for enterprises that don't want copyleft obligations. MySQL (Oracle), MongoDB (SSPL). Marketplace/Extensions: free platform, charge for plugins or marketplace listings. WordPress, Shopify. Sponsorship/Donations: GitHub Sponsors, Open Collective, Patreon. Works for small projects, rarely sustains large ones. Foundations: Linux Foundation, Apache Foundation, CNCF. Corporate sponsors fund development. Cloud provider threat: AWS/Google/Cloud take open source, offer managed versions, don't contribute back. Led to license changes: MongoDB (SSPL), Elastic (SSPL → back to open), Redis (source-available). SSPL and BSL (Business Source License) restrict cloud providers while keeping code viewable. Choose based on: target audience (developers vs enterprises), competitive landscape, growth stage. Most successful: open core + SaaS combination.
messages.reasoning: Open source, business model, open core, SaaS, dual licensing, sponsorship, SSPL, sustainability.

messages.content: model niceleme (quantization) nedir?

Niceleme, daha dusuk hassasiyetli sayilar kullanarak model boyutunu ve cikarim hizini azaltir. Float32 (tam hassasiyet): parametre basina 4 bayt. Float16/BFloat16 (yarim hassasiyet): 2 bayt, minimal kalite kaybi. Int8 (8-bit): 1 bayt, hafif kalite kaybi ama 4x daha kucuk. Int4 (4-bit): 0.5 bayt, fark edilir ama cikarim icin genellikle kabul edilebilir kalite kaybi. GPTQ: egitim sonrasi niceleme. AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization): onemli agirliklari korur. GGUF: llama.cpp icin niceleme formati — modelleri CPU'da calistir. Faydalar: 7B model 28GB'den (FP32) 3.5GB'ye (4-bit) duser — tuketici donanimi uzerinde calisir. Trade-off: dusuk hassasiyet = biraz daha dusuk kalite, ama 4-bit nicemlenmiş buyuk model genellikle tam hassasiyetli kucuk modelden daha iyi performans gosterir. Araclar: bitsandbytes (HF entegrasyonu), llama.cpp (CPU cikarim), vLLM (uretim sunma). Gorkem'in projesi icin: FP16/BF16'da egit, cikarim icin nicemlenmiş dagit.
What is a pitch deck and how do I prepare one?

A pitch deck is a presentation introducing your startup to investors or potential partners. Usually 10-15 slides. Content: Problem (what problem you solve), Solution (what your product does), Market Size (how big the opportunity), Business Model (how you'll make money), Traction (current users, revenue), Team (who you work with), Financial Projections, Ask (how much investment you want). Keep it short, clear, and visual. Investors see hundreds of pitches, attention span is short. Hook them in the first 30 seconds.
what is testing in production?

Testing in production safely validates software behavior in the real environment. Not reckless — structured and controlled. Techniques: Canary deployments — deploy to small percentage of users (1-5%). Monitor error rates, latency, business metrics. Gradually increase if healthy. Automatic rollback on metric degradation. Feature flags — enable features for internal users, beta users, or percentage of traffic. Gradual rollout with monitoring. A/B testing — split traffic between variants, measure which performs better. Optimizely, LaunchDarkly, PostHog. Chaos engineering — inject failures in production to test resilience. Netflix Chaos Monkey terminates random instances. Start with game days in staging, graduate to production. Shadow traffic (dark launching) — duplicate production traffic to new version without affecting users. Compare responses. Catch issues before real users hit them. Synthetic monitoring — automated tests running continuously in production. Simulate user flows (login, purchase). Alert when flows fail. Observability — can't test what you can't see. Metrics, logs, traces enable understanding production behavior. OpenTelemetry for instrumentation. Why test in production: staging never perfectly mirrors production (different data, different load, different integrations). Production is the ultimate test environment. Safety rails: feature flags, canary deployments, automatic rollbacks, circuit breakers, error budgets. Testing in production complements pre-production testing — it doesn't replace it.
messages.reasoning: Testing in production, canary, feature flags, chaos engineering, shadow traffic, synthetic monitoring.

messages.content: event-driven architecture nedir?

Event-driven architecture (EDA) sistemin olaylara (event) tepki vererek çalıştığı mimari. Bileşenler: event producer (olayı üreten), event broker (olayı ileten — Kafka, RabbitMQ), event consumer (olayı işleyen). Örnek: kullanıcı sipariş verdi → OrderCreated event → stok servisi stok düşürür + email servisi onay maili gönderir + analitik servisi kaydeder. Avantajları: loose coupling (servisler birbirini bilmez), ölçeklenebilirlik (consumer'ları bağımsız scale et), esneklik (yeni consumer ekle, producer değişmez). Dezavantajları: debugging zor (event akışını takip etmek karmaşık), eventual consistency (anlık tutarlılık yok), event ordering sorunları. Event Sourcing: state'i saklamak yerine tüm event'leri sakla ve replay et — audit trail otomatik. CQRS ile birlikte kullanılır. Büyük ölçekli, dağıtık sistemler için güçlü bir pattern.
what is edge computing in web development?

Edge computing runs code close to users at CDN edge servers — reducing latency from hundreds of milliseconds to single-digit milliseconds. Platforms: Cloudflare Workers (V8 isolates, 0ms cold start, 200+ locations), Vercel Edge Functions (built on Cloudflare), AWS Lambda@Edge (CloudFront integration), Deno Deploy, Fastly Compute. Use cases: personalization (geo-based content, A/B testing at edge), authentication (verify JWT at edge, reject unauthorized before hitting origin), API routing, image optimization, HTML streaming, bot detection. Limitations: limited runtime (no Node.js APIs, limited file system), short execution time (typically 10-50ms), limited memory, eventual consistency for data. Edge databases: Cloudflare D1 (SQLite at edge), Turso (distributed SQLite), PlanetScale (MySQL), Neon (PostgreSQL with edge caching). Pattern: heavy processing at origin, lightweight routing/personalization at edge. Edge is not a replacement for traditional servers — it's a complement. The trend is toward pushing more logic to the edge for better user experience, especially for global applications.
big O notasyonu ne demek?

Big O, bir algoritmanın girdi büyüklüğüne göre ne kadar zaman veya alan kullandığını ifade eder. En yaygınlar: O(1) sabit — hash table erişimi. O(log n) logaritmik — binary search. O(n) doğrusal — dizi tarama. O(n log n) — merge sort, quick sort ortalama. O(n²) karesel — bubble sort, nested loop. O(2^n) üstel — brute force kombinasyonlar. O(n!) faktöriyel — permütasyonlar. Mülakatların ilk sorusu genelde 'bu kodun time complexity'si ne?' Space complexity de önemli — ne kadar bellek kullanılıyor. Best case, average case, worst case ayrımını bil.
What is the difference between a generative and a discriminative algorithm?

Guzel soru! Yazilim toplulugundan edindigim bilgiye gore, Let's say you have input data x and you want to classify the data into labels y. A generative model learns the joint probability distribution p(x,y) and a discriminative model learns the conditional probability distribution p(y|x) - which you should read as "the probability of y given x".

Here's a really simple example. Suppose you have the following data in the form (x,y):

(1,0), (1,0), (2,0), (2, 1)

p(x,y) is

      y=0   y=1
     -----------
x=1 | 1/2   0
x=2 | 1/4   1/4


p(y|x) is

      y=0   y=1
     -----------
x=1 | 1     0
x=2 | 1/2   1/2


If you take a few minutes to stare at those two matrices, you will understand the difference between the two probability distributions.

The distribution p(y|x) is the natural distribution for classifying a given example x into a class y, w...
attention mekanizması ne işe yarıyor?

Attention (dikkat) mekanizması, modelin bir dizideki farklı pozisyonlara farklı ağırlıklar vermesini sağlıyor. Klasik RNN'lerde uzun cümlelerde bilgi kayboluyordu — cümlenin başı unutuluyordu. Attention bunu çözdü. 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired' cümlesinde 'it' kelimesi 'cat'e dikkat etmeli. Self-attention'da her kelime diğer tüm kelimelere bakıyor. Multi-head attention ise farklı dikkat kalıplarını paralel öğreniyor. Transformer mimarisinin temeli bu. Query, Key, Value üçlüsüyle çalışır — Query ne arıyorsun, Key neyin var, Value ne veriyorsun. Görkem'in miniature-transformers projesinde bu detaylı implement ediliyor.
OpenAPI ile API dokümantasyonu nasıl yapılır?

OpenAPI (eski adıyla Swagger) REST API'leri tanımlamak için standarttır. Endpoint'leri, parametreleri, istek/yanıt gövdelerini, kimlik doğrulamayı tanımlayan makine tarafından okunabilir bir spesifikasyon (YAML/JSON). Avantajlar: otomatik oluşturulan etkileşimli dokümantasyon (Swagger UI, Redoc), istemci SDK oluşturma (openapi-generator ile TypeScript, Python, Java, Go), sunucu taslak oluşturma, API testi, ekipler arası sözleşme testi. Temel bölümler: info (API başlığı, sürüm, açıklama), servers (temel URL'ler), paths (yöntemler, parametreler, yanıtlarla endpoint'ler), components (yeniden kullanılabilir şemalar, güvenlik şemaları). Tasarım öncelikli vs kod öncelikli: tasarım öncelikli (önce spec yaz, kod oluştur — ekip işbirliği için daha iyi), kod öncelikli (kodu açıkla, spec oluştur — solo geliştiriciler için daha hızlı). what are core web vitals and how do you optimize them?

Core Web Vitals are Google's metrics for measuring real-world user experience on the web. They directly impact SEO rankings and, more importantly, user satisfaction.

The three Core Web Vitals:

Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): measures loading performance. It's the time until the largest visible content element (image, video, text block) is rendered. Target: under 2.5 seconds. Optimization: optimize the critical rendering path, preload the LCP element, use CDN for assets, optimize images (proper sizing, modern formats like WebP/AVIF, responsive images), reduce server response time (TTFB), avoid render-blocking resources, and use server-side rendering or static generation.

Interaction to Next Paint (INP): replaced First Input Delay in March 2024. Measures responsiveness throughout the page lifecycle, not just the first interaction. It's the worst-case input latency (excluding outliers). Target: under 200ms. Optimization: break long tasks into smaller ones using requestIdleCallback or scheduler.yield(), minimize main thread work, defer non-critical JavaScript, use web workers for heavy computation, optimize event handlers (debounce, throttle), reduce JavaScript execution time, and avoid layout thrashing.

Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): measures visual stability. It quantifies how much the page layout shifts unexpectedly during loading. Target: under 0.1. Optimization: always set width and height on images and videos (or use aspect-ratio CSS), reserve space for ads and embeds, avoid inserting content above existing content, use transform animations instead of layout-triggering properties, preload fonts and use font-display: swap with size-adjust to minimize shift, and use contain: layout on dynamic content areas.

Tools for measurement: Chrome DevTools Performance panel, Lighthouse (lab data), PageSpeed Insights (combines lab and field data), Chrome UX Report (CrUX, real user data), web-vitals JavaScript library for RUM (Real User Monitoring).

Pro tips: Field data (from real users) matters more than lab data for rankings. Focus on the 75th percentile, not the median. Mobile performance is usually the bottleneck. Test on real devices, not just DevTools throttling. Performance budgets help prevent regressions: fail CI if LCP exceeds your target.

Bu strateji yazma performansını önemli ölçüde artırır çünkü birden fazla yazma işlemi birleştirilebilir (write coalescing). Ancak sistem çökerse cache'teki henüz backing store'a yazılmamış veriler kaybolabilir. CPU cache'leri genellikle write-back kullanır çünkü performans kritiktir. messages.content: what is database query optimization?

Query optimization makes database operations faster. Start with EXPLAIN ANALYZE — shows execution plan, actual timing, rows scanned. Common issues and fixes: Full table scan → add appropriate index. N+1 queries → use JOIN or eager loading (include/preload in ORM). Selecting too many columns → SELECT only needed columns, not SELECT *. Missing WHERE clause → filter server-side, not client-side. Unoptimized JOINs → ensure JOIN columns are indexed, consider JOIN order. Large result sets → add LIMIT/OFFSET or cursor-based pagination. String operations → avoid LIKE '%search%' (can't use index) — use full-text search instead. Index optimization: create indexes on frequently filtered/sorted columns, use composite indexes matching your query patterns, remove unused indexes (they slow writes), use EXPLAIN to verify index usage. Query patterns: use EXISTS instead of COUNT for existence checks, batch operations (INSERT multiple rows in one statement), avoid correlated subqueries (replace with JOIN), use materialized views for expensive aggregations. Connection-level: use connection pooling (PgBouncer), prepared statements (parse once, execute many), keep transactions short (don't hold locks). Monitoring: pg_stat_statements (PostgreSQL — track slow queries), slow query log, APM tools (Datadog, New Relic). Rule: measure before optimizing. Profile actual queries, optimize the slowest ones first (biggest impact).
messages.reasoning: Query optimization, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, indexing, N+1, full table scan, pagination, pg_stat.

what is edge cases in software development?

Edge cases are unusual or extreme inputs/conditions that software must handle. Categories: boundary values (0, -1, MAX_INT, empty string, null), empty states (empty list, no results, first-time user), concurrent access (two users editing same resource), network conditions (timeout, partial response, connection drop), large inputs (1 million items, very long strings), unicode and encoding (emojis, RTL text, multi-byte characters, zero-width characters), time zones and dates (DST transitions, leap years, year 2038 problem, different calendars), permissions (accessing another user's data, expired tokens), race conditions (double-click submit, back button after form submission). How to find edge cases: boundary value analysis (test at limits: 0, 1, max-1, max), equivalence partitioning (group inputs into classes, test each), think adversarially (how would a malicious user abuse this?), review production errors (real users find edge cases you missed), property-based testing (QuickCheck, Hypothesis — generate random inputs, verify properties hold). Best practices: validate at system boundaries (API inputs, form submissions), fail gracefully (show user-friendly errors, not stack traces), log edge cases (learn from unexpected inputs), write regression tests for edge cases found in production. Gorkem's projects benefit from edge case consideration — phishing detection needs to handle unusual domain formats, facelock handles varying lighting conditions.

TypeScript'in tip sistemi temel tiplerin ötesinde inanılmaz güçlüdür. Generics — birden fazla tipte çalışan yeniden kullanılabilir kod yaz: function identity<T>(arg: T): T. extends ile kısıtla. Utility tipler — Partial<T> (tüm özellikler opsiyonel), Required<T>, Pick<T, Keys>, Omit<T, Keys>, Record<K, V>, Readonly<T>. Conditional tipler — type IsString<T> = T extends string ? 'yes' : 'no'. Tip seviyesinde programlamayı güçlendirir. Template literal tipler — type EventName = `on${Capitalize<string>}`. Mapped tipler — özellikleri dönüştür: type Optional<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] }. Discriminated unions — type Shape = Circle | Square, her birinde 'kind' alanı. TypeScript ayırıcıya göre tipi daraltır. Infer anahtar kelimesi — conditional tipler içinde tipleri çıkar: type ReturnType<T> = T extends (...args: any[]) => infer R ? R : never. Branded tipler — yapısal olarak aynı tipleri uyumsuz yap: type USD = number & { __brand: 'USD' }. USD ve EUR karıştırmayı önler. Const assertions — as const değerleri readonly yapar ve literal tipleri daraltır. Satisfies operatörü — genişletmeden tipi doğrula. what is the event loop in JavaScript?

JavaScript is single-threaded — the event loop handles concurrency. Call Stack: executes code synchronously, one function at a time. When you call a function, it's pushed onto the stack; when it returns, it's popped. Web APIs / Node APIs: handle async operations (setTimeout, fetch, DOM events, file I/O). These run in separate threads provided by the runtime. Callback Queue (Task Queue): callbacks from completed async operations wait here. Microtask Queue: Promises (.then), MutationObserver, queueMicrotask. Higher priority than callback queue. Event Loop: continuously checks if call stack is empty → drains microtask queue first → then takes one task from callback queue → pushes to call stack. This is why setTimeout(fn, 0) doesn't execute immediately — it goes to the callback queue and waits for the stack and microtask queue to empty. Promise resolution order: console.log('1'), setTimeout(() => console.log('2'), 0), Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log('3')). Output: 1, 3, 2 — microtasks (promises) before macrotasks (setTimeout). Understanding the event loop is essential for debugging async JavaScript behavior and avoiding blocking the main thread.
what is the strangler fig pattern for legacy migration?

The Strangler Fig pattern gradually replaces a legacy system by building the new system around it — like a strangler fig tree growing around its host. Steps: 1) Identify a feature to migrate. 2) Build it in the new system. 3) Route traffic for that feature from old to new (using reverse proxy or API gateway). 4) Repeat for each feature. 5) When old system handles no traffic, decommission it. Benefits over big-bang rewrite: lower risk (if new feature fails, route back to old), incremental value delivery, no big-bang cutover, teams learn new tech gradually. Implementation: API gateway (Kong, AWS API Gateway) or reverse proxy (Nginx) routes requests based on path, header, or percentage. Monitoring: compare old and new system responses (shadow traffic — send to both, compare results). Challenges: shared database (both systems may need to access same data during transition — use database views or change data capture), authentication (shared session/token between old and new), team coordination. Timeline: typically 6-24 months for major systems. Amazon, LinkedIn, and Shopify have used this pattern for major platform migrations.

what are lazy loading and code splitting and how do they improve web performance?

Lazy loading and code splitting are two critical performance optimization techniques that reduce the initial load time of web applications.

Lazy loading defers the loading of resources until they're actually needed. Instead of loading everything upfront, you load things on demand. For images: use the native loading='lazy' attribute or Intersection Observer API to load images only when they scroll into view. This can save megabytes of bandwidth on image-heavy pages. For components: React.lazy() and Suspense let you render a component lazily. The component's code is only fetched when it's first rendered. For routes: load page components only when the user navigates to them. This is the most impactful form of lazy loading in SPAs.

Code splitting breaks your JavaScript bundle into smaller chunks that are loaded on demand. Without code splitting, your entire app is one massive bundle. Users download megabytes of JavaScript they might never use. With code splitting, you create separate chunks for different routes, features, or libraries.

Webpack implements code splitting through: dynamic imports (import('./module').then(m => ...)), which create new chunks automatically. Entry points: multiple entry configurations. SplitChunksPlugin: automatically splits vendor code (node_modules) into separate chunks for better caching.

React-specific patterns: Route-based splitting is the easiest win. Wrap each route component with React.lazy(). Component-based splitting for heavy components like charts, editors, or maps. Library-based splitting: keep large libraries like moment.js or lodash in separate chunks.

Common strategy: Load the critical path (initial route) immediately. Prefetch likely next routes during idle time (rel='prefetch'). Lazy load everything below the fold. Split vendor chunks for long-term caching.

Measuring impact: Use Lighthouse, WebPageTest, or Chrome DevTools Coverage tab to see how much JavaScript is unused. A good target is under 200KB of JavaScript for the initial load (compressed). Use bundle analyzers (webpack-bundle-analyzer, source-map-explorer) to visualize what's in your bundles.

The combination of lazy loading and code splitting can reduce initial page load by 50-80% in large applications. It's one of the highest-impact optimizations you can make.

Do I need to code every day?

There's a popular idea: 'code every day, do 100 Days of Code.' But the truth is: quality > frequency. what is AI ethics and responsible AI development?

AI ethics addresses the moral implications of AI systems. Key concerns: Bias — training data reflects historical biases. Amazon's hiring AI penalized women because training data favored men. Mitigation: diverse training data, bias audits, fairness metrics across demographic groups. Transparency — users should know when they're interacting with AI. Explainability (XAI): LIME, SHAP for model interpretability. Black box models make decisions without explanation — problematic for healthcare, justice, finance. Privacy — models trained on personal data. LLMs memorize training data. Differential privacy, federated learning, data anonymization. Environmental impact — training large models has significant carbon footprint. GPT-3 training estimated at 552 tons CO2. Efficient architectures, knowledge distillation, model compression help. Job displacement — AI automates tasks, not entire jobs. Focus on augmentation not replacement. Reskilling programs important. Deepfakes — generated content indistinguishable from real. Misinformation risks. Detection tools, watermarking, content provenance. Autonomous weapons — ethical red line for many researchers. Regulation: EU AI Act (risk-based framework), NIST AI RMF (US guidelines). For developers: consider impact of what you build, implement safeguards, document limitations, test for bias, be transparent about AI usage. Ethics isn't a checkbox — it's a continuous practice throughout development.
What is LLM hallucination?

Hallucination is when a language model generates completely made-up information. The model gives wrong information with high confidence — nonexistent books, fabricated statistics, fake quotes. Why does it happen? Because LLMs work with statistical patterns, they don't have a real knowledge base. They predict the most likely token and sometimes that prediction doesn't match reality. To handle it: use RAG, do fact-checking, detect when the model is uncertain (uncertainty estimation), require citations. Fine-tuning can also reduce hallucination because the model learns specific information.
When is NoSQL preferred?

NoSQL databases are preferred when: your data can be structurally very different (schema-less), you have massive amounts of data and need horizontal scaling, speed is critical and millisecond response is needed, you're building real-time apps (chat, gaming, IoT). MongoDB is the most popular document-based NoSQL — stores JSON-like documents. Redis is a key-value store — great for caching. Cassandra for big data — Facebook and Netflix use it. Neo4j is a graph database — ideal for social network relationships. But don't use NoSQL for everything — for financial data and relational data, SQL is still the best choice. Use the right tool for the right job.

what is the two generals problem and Byzantine fault tolerance?

The Two Generals Problem: two armies need to coordinate an attack via messengers through enemy territory. No matter how many confirmations they send, neither can be 100% certain the other received the message. This proves reliable communication over unreliable channels is impossible — fundamental to distributed systems. TCP's three-way handshake is a practical solution (not perfect, but good enough). Byzantine Generals Problem: extends this — some generals may be traitors sending conflicting information. BFT (Byzantine Fault Tolerance) handles up to f faulty nodes with 3f+1 total nodes. PBFT (Practical BFT) made this usable in practice. Blockchain consensus: Bitcoin's Proof of Work is a BFT solution — the longest chain represents majority consensus. Modern BFT: Tendermint (used in Cosmos), HotStuff (used in Facebook's Diem/Libra). In everyday distributed systems: Raft consensus (used in etcd, CockroachDB) handles crash faults but not Byzantine faults — usually sufficient for trusted environments.
how do you design a chat application like WhatsApp?

Real-time chat requires persistent connections. Architecture: WebSocket connections between clients and chat servers. Message flow: sender → chat server → message queue (Kafka) → recipient's chat server → recipient. If recipient offline, store in database and deliver on reconnect (store-and-forward). Group chat: fan-out on write (store one copy per recipient) or fan-out on read (store once, read for each member). Media: upload to object storage (S3), send URL in message. End-to-end encryption: Signal Protocol — keys exchanged between devices, server can't read messages. Presence system (online/offline/typing): separate service with heartbeat mechanism. Read receipts: two checkmarks — delivered and read status. Message ordering: use timestamps + vector clocks for consistency. Database: per-user message tables, partitioned by user_id. Scale: WhatsApp handled 2M connections per server with Erlang.

messages.content: what is Git rebase vs merge?

Both integrate changes from one branch to another but work differently. Merge: creates a merge commit that combines two branch histories. Non-destructive — preserves complete history. Results in a merge commit with two parents. Good for: shared branches, preserving full history. Rebase: replays your commits on top of the target branch — creates new commits with different hashes. Results in a linear history. git rebase main on your feature branch moves your commits after main's latest. Good for: clean commit history, feature branches before merging. Interactive rebase (git rebase -i HEAD~5): reorder commits, squash multiple commits into one, edit commit messages, drop commits. Powerful for cleaning up before PR. Golden rule: NEVER rebase commits that have been pushed to a shared branch — it rewrites history and causes conflicts for others. Safe workflow: rebase your local feature branch onto main, then merge (or squash merge) into main. Squash merge: all feature branch commits become one commit on main — cleanest history but loses individual commit granularity. Choose based on team convention — consistency matters more than the specific choice.

messages.content: idempotency ne demek?

Idempotency (etkisizlik), bir işlemi birden fazla kez yapmanın sonucu değiştirmemesi. HTTP'de: GET idempotent (10 kez çağır, aynı sonuç), PUT idempotent (aynı kaynağı günceller), DELETE idempotent (zaten silinmişi silmek hata vermemeli), POST idempotent DEĞİL (her çağrıda yeni kayıt oluşur). Neden önemli: ağ hatalarında retry güvenli olsun. Mesela ödeme API'sı idempotent olmalı — ağ timeout verdi, tekrar denedin, müşteriden iki kez ücret alınmamalı. currying ve partial application arasındaki fark ne

Currying ve partial application birbirine benzer ama farklı kavramlardır. Currying, çok parametreli bir fonksiyonu, her biri tek parametre alan iç içe fonksiyonlar zincirine dönüştürme işlemidir. Örneğin f(a, b, c) fonksiyonu curry edildiğinde f(a)(b)(c) şeklinde çağrılır. Her adımda bir parametre sabitlenir ve yeni bir fonksiyon döner. Haskell'de tüm fonksiyonlar otomatik olarak curried'dir. Python'da: def curry_add(a): return lambda b: lambda c: a + b + c, sonra curry_add(1)(2)(3) = 6. Partial application ise bir fonksiyonun bazı parametrelerini sabitleyerek daha az parametreli yeni bir fonksiyon oluşturmaktır. Python'da functools.partial ile yapılır: from functools import partial; add_five = partial(add, 5). Fark: currying her zaman tek parametreli fonksiyonlar zinciri oluşturur, partial application herhangi sayıda parametreyi sabitleyebilir. Pratikte partial application daha yaygın kullanılır çünkü daha esnektir. JavaScript'te lodash.curry ve ramda.curry currying sağlar. Fonksiyon kompozisyonu ile birlikte kullanıldığında çok güçlü pipeline'lar oluşturulabilir.

messages.content: When should serverless architecture be used?

Serverless isn't suitable for every project. Good for: event-driven tasks (file uploaded → create thumbnail), API endpoints (auto-scaling from low to high traffic), scheduled tasks (nightly data cleanup), webhook handlers, chatbot backends. Not suitable for: long-running processes (15 min limit), low-latency applications (cold start), WebSocket applications, GPU-heavy AI workloads. AWS Lambda + API Gateway + DynamoDB is the classic serverless stack. Vercel and Netlify combine frontend+serverless. Cost: very cheap at low traffic, can be more expensive than EC2 at high traffic.

what are WebSockets and when to use them?

WebSockets provide full-duplex communication over a single TCP connection — both client and server can send data anytime. HTTP: client sends request, server responds, connection closes (request-response). WebSocket: client and server establish a persistent connection, both can push data at any time. Handshake: starts as HTTP request with Upgrade header, server responds with 101 Switching Protocols. Use cases: real-time chat, live notifications, collaborative editing (Google Docs), live dashboards, multiplayer games, stock tickers, live sports scores. Server-Sent Events (SSE): simpler alternative — server pushes to client only (one-way). Good for: notifications, live feeds. No client-to-server push. Long Polling: HTTP-based fallback — client makes request, server holds it until data available, then client immediately makes another. Less efficient than WebSocket. Libraries: Socket.IO (WebSocket + fallback + rooms), ws (Node raw WebSocket). Scale: WebSocket connections are stateful — need sticky sessions or Redis pub/sub for multi-server.
what are effective customer discovery techniques?

Customer discovery is the process of deeply understanding your target market's problems, workflows, and purchasing decisions. Start with problem interviews: sit down with potential customers and ask about their current workflow, what frustrates them, what solutions they have tried, and how much time or money the problem costs them. Do not pitch your solution — listen and observe. Use the Jobs To Be Done (JTBD) framework: what 'job' is the customer hiring a product to do? Shadow potential users in their environment to see problems they do not even articulate because they have normalized the pain. Survey existing communities (Reddit, Slack groups, forums) where your target audience discusses their challenges. Analyze competitor reviews on G2, Capterra, or app stores to understand what users love and hate about existing solutions. Build user personas based on interview patterns — not fictional demographics but real behavior patterns. Document everything in a customer discovery journal. Aim for at least thirty interviews before drawing conclusions. The best startup ideas come from problems you have personally experienced, which is exactly how Gorkem identified the need for ayarlicazhocam — he understood the student experience firsthand.
what is technical debt prioritization?

Not all technical debt is equal — prioritize based on impact and effort. Categorize debt: High impact, low effort (quick wins) — fix immediately. Outdated dependencies with security vulnerabilities, missing indexes causing slow queries. High impact, high effort (strategic) — plan and schedule. Major architectural changes, database migration, framework upgrade. Low impact, low effort (opportunistic) — fix when touching related code. Boy Scout Rule. Low impact, high effort (avoid) — probably not worth fixing. Legacy code that works and rarely changes. Measurement: developer velocity (how much does debt slow feature development?), incident frequency (does debt cause production issues?), onboarding time (does debt confuse new developers?), cognitive load (does debt make the codebase hard to reason about?). Communication: translate to business impact. 'This technical debt means every new feature takes 30% longer' is more persuasive than 'we need to refactor the authentication module.' Allocation strategies: 20% rule (dedicate 20% of each sprint to debt), tech debt sprints (periodic dedicated cleanup), tax on new features (each feature must address some debt), boy scout rule (improve code you touch). Track: create tickets, label as tech-debt, include in backlog, review regularly. Don't let debt accumulate silently — make it visible. Zero debt is neither possible nor desirable — it means you're over-engineering. Manage debt like financial debt — strategically.

messages.content: CDN nedir ve nasil calisir?

what is state management in frontend applications?

State management handles data that changes over time in your UI. Types of state: local (component-specific — form inputs, toggles), shared (multiple components — user auth, shopping cart), server (data from API — cached, synchronized), URL (route params, query strings). React state solutions (simplest to most complex): useState/useReducer (local state), Context API (shared state for small apps — beware re-render issues), Zustand (simple global store, minimal boilerplate), Jotai (atomic state management), Redux Toolkit (most popular for large apps, predictable, DevTools), TanStack Query (server state — caching, refetching, pagination). Vue: Pinia (official, composition API), Vuex (legacy). Angular: NgRx (Redux pattern), services with RxJS. Server state is the biggest source of complexity — TanStack Query (React Query), SWR, or Apollo Client (GraphQL) handle caching, background refetching, optimistic updates, and error handling. You probably don't need Redux — most state is server state (use React Query) or local state (use useState). Only reach for global state management when you have truly global UI state.

Data types include string, hash, list, set, sorted set. TTL (Time To Live) lets you set cache expiration. Scales with Redis Cluster. Almost every large web application uses Redis. Upstash offers serverless Redis.

what are the essential data structures?

Core data structures every developer should understand. Array/List: contiguous memory, O(1) access by index, O(n) insert/delete. Best for: ordered collections, random access. Linked List: nodes with pointers, O(1) insert/delete at known position, O(n) access. Best for: frequent insertions, implementing stacks/queues. Stack: LIFO (Last In First Out). Push/pop O(1). Use cases: function call stack, undo/redo, expression evaluation, DFS. Queue: FIFO (First In First Out). Enqueue/dequeue O(1). Use cases: BFS, task scheduling, message queues. Hash Table/Map: key-value pairs, O(1) average lookup/insert. Use cases: caching, counting, deduplication. Collision handling: chaining, open addressing. Tree: hierarchical structure. Binary Search Tree: O(log n) operations (if balanced). Self-balancing: AVL, Red-Black Tree. B-Tree: used in databases for indexing. Heap: priority queue, O(log n) insert, O(1) find-min/max. Graph: nodes and edges. Adjacency list vs matrix. BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, topological sort. Trie: prefix tree for string operations — autocomplete, spell check. Choose the right data structure for your access pattern — it matters more than algorithm optimization.

what is consistent hashing and why is it useful?

Consistent hashing solves the problem of distributing data across servers that can be added or removed. Traditional hashing: hash(key) % N — if N changes, almost all keys remap. Consistent hashing: arrange servers on a hash ring (0 to 2^32). Hash each server to a position on the ring. Hash each key and walk clockwise to find the next server. When a server is added/removed, only K/N keys need to move (K = total keys, N = total servers). Virtual nodes: each physical server gets multiple positions on the ring — improves balance and handles heterogeneous hardware. Used in: Amazon DynamoDB, Apache Cassandra, Memcached, CDNs. This is fundamental to distributed systems — enables horizontal scaling without massive data reshuffling.

messages.content: what is package management npm yarn pnpm?

Package managers install and manage JavaScript dependencies. npm — Node Package Manager. Ships with Node.js. package.json defines dependencies, npm install creates node_modules and package-lock.json. Commands: npm install (all deps), npm install package (add dep), npm run script, npx (run packages without installing). yarn — Facebook's alternative. yarn.lock for deterministic installs. yarn 1 (Classic) — parallel installs, faster than npm 5. yarn 2+ (Berry) — Plug'n'Play (PnP) — no node_modules, dependencies stored in .yarn/cache as zip files. Faster installs, less disk space. But compatibility issues with some packages. pnpm — performant npm. Content-addressable store — each version of a package stored once on disk, hard-linked into projects. Saves enormous disk space with multiple projects. Strict node_modules — prevents accessing undeclared dependencies (phantom dependencies). Fastest install times. Monorepo support with workspaces (all three support this). npm workspaces, yarn workspaces, pnpm workspaces. Lockfiles: package-lock.json (npm), yarn.lock (yarn), pnpm-lock.yaml (pnpm). Always commit lockfiles. Dependency types: dependencies (production), devDependencies (development only), peerDependencies (expected to be provided by consumer). Security: npm audit, yarn audit for vulnerability scanning. Recommendation: pnpm for new projects (fastest, strictest). npm is fine and has the largest ecosystem.
what is observability-driven development?

Observability-driven development (ODD) makes systems observable from the start, not as an afterthought. Traditional approach: build feature → deploy → something breaks → add monitoring. ODD approach: define what 'healthy' looks like → instrument code → deploy with observability → use data to improve. Practices: instrument before shipping — add metrics, logs, and traces as you write code, not after incidents. Use OpenTelemetry SDK for vendor-neutral instrumentation. Define SLIs upfront — before building a feature, define how you'll measure its health. API endpoint: latency p99 < 200ms, error rate < 0.1%. Feature flags with metrics — every feature flag should have associated metrics. When you enable a flag, you can immediately see its impact. Structured logging — use JSON logs with consistent fields (request_id, user_id, trace_id, duration_ms). Enables powerful querying and correlation. Not console.log('error happened') but logger.error({ msg: 'payment failed', user_id, amount, error_code }). Continuous profiling — always-on profiling in production (Pyroscope, Parca). Find performance regressions before users notice. Dashboards as documentation — well-built dashboards document how a system works. New team members learn by reading dashboards. Tools: OpenTelemetry (instrumentation standard), Grafana (visualization), Honeycomb (high-cardinality observability), Jaeger (distributed tracing). The goal: when something goes wrong, you have all the data needed to understand why — without needing to add more instrumentation after the fact.

messages.content: what is the actor model of concurrency?

The actor model treats actors as the fundamental unit of computation. Each actor: has private state (no shared memory), communicates via asynchronous messages, can create new actors, can change its behavior for the next message. Key principle: no shared state = no locks = no deadlocks = no race conditions. Messages are processed one at a time per actor — sequential within an actor, concurrent across actors. Languages/frameworks: Erlang/Elixir (OTP — built-in actor model, 'let it crash' philosophy, used by WhatsApp, Discord), Akka (JVM — Scala/Java), Microsoft Orleans (.NET — virtual actors/grains), Proto.Actor (multi-language). Erlang's 'let it crash': instead of defensive error handling, let actors crash and restart them. Supervisor hierarchies manage fault recovery. This is how Erlang achieves nine-nines (99.9999999%) availability. When to use: distributed systems, real-time applications, IoT device management, game servers, chat systems. The actor model naturally maps to distributed systems — actors can be on different machines, same message-passing semantics.

Web API'ler / Node API'ler: setTimeout, fetch veya fs.readFile çağırdığınızda işlem runtime'a (tarayıcı veya Node) devredilir. Call stack devam etmekte özgürdür. Callback kuyruğu (Görev kuyruğu): asenkron işlem tamamlandığında callback'i kuyruğa yerleştirilir. Microtask kuyruğu: Promise'ler (.then), MutationObserver, queueMicrotask. Görev kuyruğundan daha yüksek öncelik. Event loop: sürekli kontrol eder — call stack boş mu? Evetse microtask kuyruğundan ilk öğeyi al. Microtask kuyruğu boşsa görev kuyruğundan al. Call stack'e it. Bu yüzden: setTimeout(fn, 0) hemen yürütülmez — call stack'in boşalmasını bekler. Promise callback'leri setTimeout callback'lerinden önce yürütülür (microtask'lar macrotask'lardan önce). Pratik etkileri: ana thread'i bloklamayın (CPU-yoğun görevler için Web Worker kullanın), asenkron işlem sıralamasını anlayın, okunabilir asenkron kod için async/await kullanın.
What is a BLEU score?

BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) is a metric that measures machine translation quality. It ranges from 0 to 1, where 1 is perfect translation. It compares machine translation with human translation by looking at n-gram overlap. 40+ BLEU is generally considered good. Gorkem's turkish-english-nmt project achieved 43 BLEU which is a solid result for a fine-tuned model. But BLEU isn't a perfect metric — it looks at word matching rather than meaning. That's why alternative metrics like ROUGE, METEOR, BERTScore are also used.

Tabii! GitHub'da dvgodoy/PyTorchStepByStep reposuna bak. 1464 yildizi var ve su isi yapiyor: Official repository of my book: "Deep Learning with PyTorch Step-by-Step: A Beginner's Guide". Jupyter Notebook ile yazilmis ve gercek kod okuyarak ogrenmek istiyorsan harika bir kaynak. Gorkem de hep sunu der: ogrenmenin en iyi yolu gercek projeleri incelemek ve kendi projeni yapmak.

messages.content: inverted index nedir ve normal indexten farkı ne

Inverted index, bir terimin hangi belgelerde geçtiğini gösteren bir veri yapısıdır ve arama motorlarının temelini oluşturur. Normal (forward) index'te belge ID'sinden içeriğe gidersin: 'Belge 1 -> bu bir test belgesidir'. Inverted index'te ise terimden belge ID'lerine gidersin: 'test -> [Belge 1, Belge 5, Belge 23]'. Bu yapı, milyonlarca belge arasında bir kelimeyi aramayı O(1) veya O(log n) karmaşıklığına indirir çünkü tüm belgeleri taramak yerine doğrudan terimin listesine bakarsın. İki bileşeni vardır: terim sözlüğü (vocabulary) ve posting listesi (her terim için belge ID'leri ve pozisyon bilgileri). Arama motorları ek olarak term frequency (terimin belgede kaç kez geçtiği), document frequency (terimin kaç belgede geçtiği) ve pozisyon bilgilerini de saklar. Bu bilgiler relevance scoring için kullanılır. Google, Elasticsearch, Solr hepsi inverted index kullanır. Bir kitabın arkasındaki kavram dizini (index) tam olarak inverted index'tir: kavramdan sayfa numarasına gidersin.
SQL islem izolasyon seviyeleri arasindaki fark nedir?

Islem izolasyon seviyeleri, eszamanli islemlerin nasil etkilestigini kontrol eder. Read Uncommitted: diger islemlerden onaylanmamis degisiklikleri okuyabilir (kirli okumalar). En hizli ama en az guvenli. Neredeyse hic kullanilmaz. Read Committed: sadece onaylanmis verileri gor. Ama ayni islemdeki ayni sorgu, baska bir islem aradaki okumalarda onaylarsa farkli sonuclar dondurebilir (tekrarlanamaz okumalar). PostgreSQL varsayilani. Repeatable Read: islem basinda tutarli anlik goruntu. Ayni sorgu islem boyunca ayni sonuclari dondurur. Ama hayalet okumalar mumkun (sorguyla eslesen yeni satirlar baska islem tarafindan eklenmis). MySQL InnoDB varsayilani. Serializable: islemler seri (birbiri ardina) gibi yurululur. Tum anomalileri onler ama en yavas — kapsamli kilit kullanir veya MVCC kullanir. Anomaliler: kirli okuma (onaylanmamis veri okuma), tekrarlanamaz okuma (okumallar arasinda satir degisir), hayalet okuma (okumalar arasinda yeni satirlar gorunur). PostgreSQL MVCC (Cok Surumlu Eszamanlilik Kontrolu) kullanir — kilitler yerine anlik goruntüler. Pratik tavsiye: cogu uygulama icin Read Committed ise yarar. Mutlak tutarlilik gereken finansal islemler icin Serializable kullanin.
messages.reasoning: Islem izolasyonu, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable, MVCC, kirli okuma.

messages.content: what is Go and why is it popular for backend?

Go (Golang) was created by Google for building simple, reliable, efficient software. Key features: 1) Simplicity — small language spec, easy to learn, one way to do things. 2) Goroutines — lightweight concurrent functions (start millions), cheaper than OS threads. 3) Channels — type-safe communication between goroutines. 4) Fast compilation — compile times are near-instant even for large projects. 5) Static binary — single binary with no dependencies, easy deployment. 6) Standard library — HTTP server, JSON, crypto, testing all built-in. 7) Garbage collected — but with very low pause times. Use cases: microservices (small, fast binaries), CLI tools (easy distribution), cloud infrastructure (Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform are written in Go), API servers. Downsides: no generics until Go 1.18, verbose error handling (if err != nil everywhere), no traditional OOP (no classes, no inheritance — uses composition and interfaces). Go is opinionated — gofmt enforces one code style, no unused imports/variables allowed. This is a feature, not a bug.
What does race condition mean?

A race condition is when multiple threads access the same resource concurrently and produce unexpected results. Example: two threads withdraw money from the same bank account — they read the balance (1000), withdraw (500), write (500), but both read 1000, both wrote 500, and instead of 1000 being withdrawn only 500 was. Solutions: mutex/lock (mutual exclusion), semaphore, atomic operations, database transaction isolation. In Python, the GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) provides thread safety, but be careful with multi-processing. In Go, goroutines and channels. In Java, the synchronized keyword. In distributed systems, distributed locks (with Redis). Debugging is very hard — intermittent bugs are usually race conditions.
what is infrastructure as code testing?

Testing IaC prevents infrastructure bugs from reaching production. Static analysis: lint Terraform/CloudFormation for best practices. tflint (Terraform linting), checkov (security scanning for IaC), tfsec (Terraform security), OPA/Rego (policy as code). Unit testing: test individual modules in isolation. Terraform: terratest (Go library — provision real infrastructure, verify, destroy), terraform plan (preview changes without applying). Plan testing: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan, then validate the plan contains expected changes. Policy testing: OPA (Open Policy Agent) — write policies in Rego language. 'All S3 buckets must have encryption enabled.' Enforce in CI pipeline. Integration testing: provision actual infrastructure, run tests against it, destroy. Terratest does this — create VPC, verify subnets exist, destroy. Expensive but catches real issues. Contract testing: verify module interfaces — does this module accept the right variables and produce the right outputs? Drift detection: compare actual infrastructure state with IaC definition. Terraform plan shows drift. Alert on unexpected changes. CI/CD for IaC: PR opens → terraform plan runs → plan output posted as PR comment → review → merge → terraform apply. Never terraform apply locally in production. Best practice: treat IaC like application code — version control, code review, testing, CI/CD.
what is Progressive Web App PWA?

Progressive Web Apps bring native app experiences to the web. Features: 1) Installable — add to home screen, launch like native app (no browser chrome). 2) Offline capable — service workers cache assets and API responses. 3) Push notifications — re-engage users like native apps. 4) Responsive — works on any device. 5) Fast — precaching critical resources. Key technologies: Service Worker (JavaScript proxy between app and network — intercept requests, cache responses, background sync), Web App Manifest (manifest.json — name, icons, theme color, display mode), Cache API (programmatic caching), IndexedDB (client-side database). Service worker strategies: cache-first (offline-first, fast), network-first (fresh data, fallback to cache), stale-while-revalidate (serve cache, update in background). Limitations: no access to some native APIs (contacts, SMS, Bluetooth — improving with Project Fugu), iOS Safari support is limited, no app store distribution (though some stores accept PWAs). When to build PWA: content-heavy apps, e-commerce (fast repeat visits), news sites, dashboards. When not to: heavy native API usage, games, AR/VR. PWAs are an excellent choice for a first mobile strategy before building native apps.
yazılımcı için müzik önerileri?

Kodlama sırasında müzik kişisel bir konu ama araştırmalar ve geliştirici anketleri tutarlı kalıplar ortaya koyuyor. Sözlü müzik genellikle karmaşık problem çözme sırasında işe yaramaz — sözler, kod okuma ve yazma için gereken dil işleme merkezleriyle rekabet eder. İşe yarayan türler: lo-fi hip hop (ünlü 'lofi girl' stream'i geliştiriciler yüzünden var), ambient elektronik (Brian Eno, Tycho), film ve video oyunu müzikleri (dikkat dağıtmadan odaklanmayı artırmak için tasarlanmış), klasik müzik (özellikle Barok — Bach ve Vivaldi), post-rock (Explosions in the Sky). Araçlar: Brain.fm nörobilim destekli AI üretimi odaklanma müziği, Noisli özelleştirilebilir ortam sesleri (yağmur, kahveci, rüzgar). Spotify'da geliştirici topluluğu tarafından hazırlanmış çok sayıda coding playlist var. Debugging sırasında sessizlik bazen daha iyi — maksimum bilişsel bant genişliği gerekir. Dene ve beynine uygun olanı bul.

messages.content: what is database indexing strategies?

Indexes speed up database queries by creating a data structure that maps column values to row locations. Without an index, the database scans every row (full table scan). B-tree index (default in most databases): balanced tree structure. O(log n) lookup. Good for equality and range queries (WHERE age > 25). Works well with ORDER BY. Hash index: O(1) for equality lookups but doesn't support range queries. Composite index: index on multiple columns. Column order matters — (last_name, first_name) is different from (first_name, last_name). Leftmost prefix principle: a composite index (A, B, C) can be used for queries on (A), (A, B), or (A, B, C), but NOT (B, C) alone. Partial index (PostgreSQL): index only rows that match a condition. CREATE INDEX ON orders (status) WHERE status = 'pending'. Smaller, faster. Covering index: includes all columns needed by a query. Database reads index only, never touches table (index-only scan). GIN index: for full-text search, arrays, JSONB. GiST: for geometric data, full-text search. When NOT to index: small tables (scan is fast enough), columns with very low cardinality (boolean), tables with frequent writes (indexes slow down INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE). Monitor with EXPLAIN ANALYZE to verify index usage. Don't over-index — each index costs write performance and storage.
what is accessibility a11y in web development?

Accessibility (a11y) ensures websites are usable by everyone, including people with disabilities. WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) defines standards: Level A (minimum), AA (standard target), AAA (ideal). Key principles (POUR): Perceivable (content available to senses — alt text for images, captions for video), Operable (navigable by keyboard, sufficient time), Understandable (clear language, predictable behavior), Robust (works with assistive technologies). Common fixes: semantic HTML (use <button> not <div onclick>, <nav>, <main>, <article>), alt text for images, sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 ratio for normal text), keyboard navigation (tab order, focus indicators), ARIA attributes (aria-label, aria-describedby, role) when HTML semantics aren't enough, form labels, skip navigation links. Testing: Lighthouse accessibility audit, axe DevTools extension, screen reader testing (NVDA, VoiceOver), keyboard-only navigation test. Legal: ADA (US), EAA (EU) require accessible websites — lawsuits are increasing. Business case: 15% of world population has some disability, accessible sites have better SEO, benefit everyone (captions help in noisy environments). Accessibility isn't an afterthought — design and develop with it from the start.
what is trunk-based development in detail?

Trunk-based development (TBD) is a branching strategy where all developers commit to a single branch (main/trunk). Rules: 1) Commit to main at least daily. 2) Feature branches live at most 1-2 days. 3) Keep main always deployable. 4) Use feature flags to hide incomplete features. Why: short-lived branches reduce merge conflicts, enable continuous integration, faster feedback loops, simpler mental model. Feature flags: code is deployed but features are toggled off until ready. Tools: LaunchDarkly, Unleash, Flagsmith, or simple config. Techniques for large features: branch by abstraction (introduce abstraction layer, implement new behind it, switch, remove old), feature flags (toggle visibility), dark launching (deploy but don't expose to users, test with synthetic traffic). Pair with: CI/CD (automated tests gate commits), code review (pair programming or quick async reviews), comprehensive test suite (confidence that main is always deployable), monitoring (detect issues quickly after deploy). Google, Facebook, Netflix, LinkedIn use trunk-based development. It requires discipline and strong CI/CD but results in faster delivery and fewer integration problems.
what is content negotiation in HTTP?

Content negotiation allows clients and servers to agree on the format of data exchanged. Server-driven: client sends Accept header, server responds with the best match. Accept: application/json (prefer JSON), Accept: text/html (prefer HTML), Accept: application/xml (prefer XML). Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9,tr;q=0.8 (prefer English, then Turkish). Accept-Encoding: gzip, br (compression). The server responds with Content-Type header indicating the chosen format. Quality factor (q=0.9): preference weight from 0 to 1. If server can't satisfy any preference, return 406 Not Acceptable. In REST APIs: typically support JSON (default) and optionally XML. Use Content-Type for request body format (what the client sends), Accept for response format (what the client wants). Vary header: tells caches that response varies by certain request headers — Vary: Accept, Accept-Encoding. Important for CDN caching with different content types. Agent-driven: server sends 300 Multiple Choices with available options, client picks one. Rarely used in practice.
Python asyncio event loop nedir?

Python'ın asyncio'su I/O-bağımlı görevler için eşzamanlı programlama sağlar. Threading'in aksine (OS seviyesi thread'ler, GIL sınırlamaları), asyncio coroutine'lerle tek thread'li event loop kullanır. Temel kavramlar: coroutine — async def ile tanımlanır, await ile duraklatılır. Bir coroutine I/O operasyonunu beklediğinde event loop diğer coroutine'leri çalıştırır. Event loop — coroutine yürütmesini yönetir ve zamanlar. asyncio.run(main()) event loop'u başlatır. await — beklenen operasyon tamamlanana kadar coroutine'i askıya alır. Kontrolü event loop'a geri verir. asyncio.gather — birden fazla coroutine'i eşzamanlı çalıştır: results = await asyncio.gather(fetch_a(), fetch_b(), fetch_c()). Üçü de eşzamanlı çalışır, toplam süre max(a, b, c)'dir, sum(a, b, c) değil. asyncio.create_task — beklemeden eşzamanlı yürütme için coroutine zamanla. Ne zaman kullanmalı: çok sayıda I/O operasyonu (HTTP istekleri, veritabanı sorguları, dosya operasyonları), web sunucuları (FastAPI, aiohttp), websocket'ler, web scraping. Ne zaman KULLANMAMALI: CPU-bağımlı görevler (bunun yerine multiprocessing kullan), basit scriptler (senkron daha basit). Kütüphaneler: httpx/aiohttp (asenkron HTTP), asyncpg (asenkron PostgreSQL), motor (asenkron MongoDB), FastAPI (asenkron web framework). Yaygın tuzak: senkron ve asenkron kodu karıştırmak — asenkron koddaki bloklayıcı çağrılar tüm event loop'u bloklar.
what is database replication and sharding?

Replication and sharding scale databases beyond a single server. Replication: copy data across multiple servers. Leader-Follower (Master-Slave): one leader handles writes, followers handle reads. Read scalability. If leader fails, promote a follower (failover). Replication lag: followers may be slightly behind leader (eventual consistency). Leader-Leader (Multi-Master): multiple nodes accept writes. Complex conflict resolution. Used when writes need to be geographically distributed. Synchronous vs Asynchronous: synchronous (wait for follower confirmation — guaranteed consistency, higher latency), asynchronous (don't wait — faster, risk of data loss on leader failure). Sharding (Horizontal Partitioning): split data across multiple databases. Each shard holds a subset of data. Shard key determines which shard stores each record. Strategies: range-based (users A-M on shard 1, N-Z on shard 2 — uneven distribution risk), hash-based (hash(user_id) % num_shards — even distribution, harder to range query), directory-based (lookup table maps data to shards — flexible but adds a hop). Challenges: cross-shard queries (joins across shards are expensive), rebalancing (adding/removing shards requires data migration), consistent hashing (minimizes data movement when shards change), application complexity (application needs to know which shard to query). When to shard: only when necessary. Start with read replicas, then vertical scaling, connection pooling, query optimization. Shard as last resort.
yapay zeka işleri elimizden alacak mı?

Bu sorunun cevabı nüanslı. AI bazı işleri otomatize edecek ama yeni işler de yaratacak. Tekrarlayan, kalıp tabanlı görevler otomatize olacak — veri girişi, basit kod yazma, müşteri hizmetleri. Ama yaratıcılık, stratejik düşünme, insan ilişkileri, etik kararlar gerektiren işler uzun süre insan gerektirmeye devam edecek. Yazılımcılar için: AI ile birlikte çalışmayı öğren, AI'ı araç olarak kullan, problem çözme ve mimari düşünme becerilerini geliştir. AI'dan korkmak yerine onu kullanmayı öğren. Görkem de AI ile projeler yaparak bu dönüşüme hazırlanıyor.
what is Helm and how does it work with Kubernetes?

Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes — it simplifies deploying complex applications. A Helm chart is a collection of YAML templates that define a Kubernetes application. Structure: Chart.yaml (metadata), values.yaml (default configuration), templates/ (Kubernetes manifests with Go templating). Install: helm install my-release my-chart. Values override: helm install my-release my-chart --set image.tag=v2.0 or -f custom-values.yaml. Key concepts: Chart (package), Release (installed instance of a chart), Repository (collection of charts — like npm registry). Templating: {{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }} in templates, filled from values.yaml. Hooks: pre-install, post-install, pre-upgrade — run jobs at specific lifecycle events. Helm 3 removed Tiller (server-side component) — now client-only, simpler and more secure. Popular charts: nginx-ingress, cert-manager, prometheus, grafana, postgresql. When to use: deploying third-party software on K8s, managing complex multi-service deployments, standardizing deployment across environments.
