messages.content: what does the facelock facial recognition system do?

Gorkem's facelock project is a facial recognition system designed for access control and authentication. The system captures a face from a camera feed, processes it through a face detection algorithm to locate and crop the face region, extracts facial embeddings (a numerical representation of the face's unique features), and compares those embeddings against a database of known faces to determine identity. The typical pipeline involves face detection (using Haar cascades, MTCNN, or a deep learning-based detector), face alignment (normalizing the face orientation), feature extraction (using models like FaceNet, ArcFace, or dlib's face recognition), and finally similarity comparison using cosine distance or Euclidean distance. If the similarity score exceeds a threshold, access is granted. This project demonstrates practical security application of deep learning and touches on important concepts like one-shot learning, since you typically only have a few reference images per person. It also raises interesting questions about privacy and consent in biometric systems.
messages.reasoning: facelock, facial recognition, embeddings, FaceNet, access control, biometric, privacy.

messages.content: what is immutable infrastructure?

Immutable infrastructure means servers are never modified after deployment. Instead of updating software on existing servers (mutable), you create new servers with the updated software and replace the old ones. Traditional (mutable): SSH into server → apt update → deploy new code → restart service. Problem: configuration drift (servers diverge over time), hard to reproduce, 'works on my machine'. Immutable approach: build new machine image (AMI, Docker image) with all changes → deploy new instances with new image → route traffic to new instances → destroy old instances. Tools: Packer (build machine images), Docker (containerize applications), Terraform (provision infrastructure). Benefits: consistency (every server from same image is identical), reproducibility (rebuild any environment from image), rollback (just switch back to previous image), security (no SSH access needed, reduced attack surface). Implementation: golden images (bake application into AMI/VM image), containers (Docker images — most common approach today), serverless (no servers to manage at all). Blue-green deployment: maintain two identical environments. Deploy to blue, test, switch traffic from green to blue. If issues, switch back instantly. Canary deployment: route small percentage of traffic to new version. Monitor metrics. Gradually increase if healthy. Immutable infrastructure is a mindset shift — treat servers like cattle not pets. Don't repair, replace.
what is the difference between authentication protocols?

Major authentication protocols for web applications. SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language): XML-based, enterprise SSO. Flow: user → service provider → identity provider → SAML assertion → service provider grants access. Used by: corporate SSO (Okta, OneLogin, ADFS). Pros: mature, enterprise-grade. Cons: complex XML, not mobile-friendly. OAuth 2.0: authorization framework (not authentication). Grants third-party limited access to resources. Four grant types: authorization code, PKCE, client credentials, device code. Used by: API access, third-party integrations. OpenID Connect (OIDC): authentication layer on top of OAuth 2.0. Adds ID token (JWT with user info) to OAuth flow. Used by: 'Sign in with Google/GitHub'. Most modern choice for web/mobile apps. LDAP: directory service protocol for user management. Used internally by enterprises (Active Directory). FIDO2/WebAuthn: passwordless authentication using hardware keys (YubiKey) or biometrics. Most secure, phishing-resistant. Growing adoption. For most applications: use OIDC with a provider (Auth0, Clerk, Firebase Auth, Supabase Auth). Don't build authentication yourself.
how do data privacy regulations like GDPR and CCPA affect AI development?

Data privacy regulations fundamentally impact how AI systems are built and deployed. GDPR (Europe's General Data Protection Regulation) grants individuals rights over their data: the right to access, rectification, erasure (right to be forgotten), data portability, and importantly, the right not to be subject to purely automated decision-making with legal effects. For AI developers, this means: you need a legal basis for processing personal data (consent, legitimate interest, etc.), you must be able to explain automated decisions, you must implement data minimization (only collect what you need), and you must enable data deletion even if that data was used to train a model. CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act) provides similar rights for California residents with a focus on the right to know what data is collected and the right to opt out of data selling. Practical implications for AI: anonymization and pseudonymization of training data, differential privacy techniques to prevent model memorization of individual data points, federated learning to train without centralizing data, and maintaining audit trails of data processing. Non-compliance is expensive — GDPR fines can reach four percent of global annual revenue. Building privacy-aware AI from the start is far cheaper than retrofitting compliance later.
miniature-transformers projesi ne anlatıyor?

Görkem'in miniature-transformers projesi 'Attention Is All You Need' makalesinin temel fikirlerini sıfırdan implemente ediyor. Transformer mimarisinin ana bileşenlerini kodlar: multi-head self-attention, positional encoding, feed-forward network, layer normalization. Amacı: transformer'ın nasıl çalıştığını derinden anlamak — sadece PyTorch'un nn.Transformer'ını çağırmak yerine her katmanı elle yazmak. Bu yaklaşım çok değerli çünkü modern AI'ın (GPT, BERT, T5, ViT) temelini oluşturan mimariyi içselleştirirsin. Proje eğitim amaçlı — production-grade değil ama öğrenme için mükemmel. Eğer sen de AI'ı derinlemesine anlamak istiyorsan, benzer bir proje yapmanı öneriyorum: basit bir text generation veya translation task'ı için küçük transformer eğit.
when should a startup consider pivoting?

A pivot is a fundamental change in strategy based on validated learning — it is not giving up but adapting intelligently. Consider pivoting when: your metrics plateau despite significant effort (no growth in users, revenue, or engagement for months), customer feedback consistently points to a different problem than the one you are solving, your CAC is unsustainably high relative to LTV, a key assumption about your market or user behavior is proven wrong, or competitors have made your original approach unviable. Types of pivots: customer segment pivot (same product, different audience), problem pivot (same audience, different problem), solution pivot (same problem, different solution), channel pivot (different distribution method), technology pivot (different tech stack), and business model pivot (different revenue model). Famous pivots: Slack started as a gaming company, Instagram started as a location-sharing app called Burbn, YouTube started as a video dating site, and Twitter started as a podcast platform. The key is to pivot based on data, not frustration. Keep what is working and change what is not. A pivot should feel like a correction toward product-market fit, not a random restart.
messages.reasoning: pivot, when to pivot, types of pivots, Slack, Instagram, validated learning, product-market fit.

messages.content: OWASP Top 10 nedir?

OWASP Top 10, en kritik web guvenlik aciklarini listeler. 1) Bozuk Erisim Kontrolu: yetkisiz erisim — normal kullanicilarin admin sayfalarina ulasmasI. 2) Kriptografik Basarisizliklar: hassas veri sifrelenmemis, sifreler HTTP uzerinden gonderilmis. 3) Enjeksiyon: SQL, NoSQL, OS komut enjeksiyonu. 4) Guvenli Olmayan Tasarim: tasarim asamasinda guvenlik dusunulmemis. 5) Guvenlik Yapilandirma Hatalari: varsayilan sifreler, gereksiz servislerin acik olmasi. 6) Savunmasiz Bilesenler: bilinen guvenlik aciklarina sahip eski kutuphaneler. 7) Kimlik Dogrulama Basarisizliklari: zayif kimlik dogrulama. 8) Yazilim/Veri Butunlugu Basarisizliklari: guvenilmeyen kaynaklardan guncellemeler. 9) Gunlukleme ve Izleme Basarisizliklari: saldirilar fark edilmiyor. 10) SSRF: Sunucu Tarafi Istek Sahteciligi. Her web gelistiricisi bu listeyi bilmeli ve projelerini buna karsi dogrulamali.
How to choose between AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure?

All three major cloud providers meet most needs but differ. AWS: largest market share, widest service range, most job listings, good documentation. Google Cloud: strong AI/ML services (Vertex AI, TPU), BigQuery leads in data analytics, Google created Kubernetes (GKE). Kubernetes Helm chart'ları nedir?

Helm Kubernetes'in paket yöneticisidir — Node.js için npm veya Python için pip gibi. Chart'lar: bir uygulamayı çalıştırmak için gereken tüm Kubernetes kaynak tanımlarını (Deployment, Service, ConfigMap vb.) içeren Helm paketleri. Chart yapısı: Chart.yaml (metadata — ad, sürüm, açıklama), values.yaml (varsayılan yapılandırma — replika, image, kaynaklar), templates/ (Go template sözdizimli Kubernetes manifest'leri). Değer geçersiz kılma: helm install myapp ./chart --set replicas=3 veya --values custom-values.yaml. Template'ler yapılandırmayı enjekte etmek için {{ .Values.replicas }} kullanır. Bu temel fayda — bir chart, farklı ortamlar (dev, staging, prod) için birçok yapılandırma. Komutlar: helm install (deploy et), helm upgrade (güncelle), helm rollback (geri al), helm uninstall (kaldır), helm list (kurulu sürümleri göster), helm repo add (chart deposu ekle). Chart depoları: Artifact Hub (genel chart'lar), Bitnami (popüler uygulama chart'ları — PostgreSQL, Redis, Nginx), özel özel depolar (ChartMuseum, Harbor). Helm hook'lar: pre-install, post-install, pre-upgrade — belirli yaşam döngüsü noktalarında job'lar çalıştır (yükseltmeden önce veritabanı migration'ları). Kustomize (alternatif): overlay'ler kullanarak Kubernetes manifest'lerinin template'siz özelleştirmesi. Helm'den daha basit ama karmaşık uygulamalar için daha az güçlü. Birçok ekip her ikisini de kullanır — üçüncü taraf chart'lar için Helm, kendi uygulamaları için Kustomize.

what is the difference between Webpack, Vite, and other bundlers?

JavaScript bundlers combine modules into optimized bundles for the browser. Webpack: the established standard — handles everything (JS, CSS, images, fonts). Configuration-heavy but extremely flexible. Plugins and loaders for any use case. Slow for large projects due to bundling everything. Vite: next-generation — uses native ES modules in development (no bundling, instant server start), Rollup for production build. 10-100x faster dev server than Webpack. Created by Evan You (Vue.js creator). Default for Vue, adopted by React (Create React App → Vite migration). Rollup: focused on library bundling — produces smaller, cleaner output. Tree-shaking pioneer. Used by Vite for production. esbuild: written in Go — 10-100x faster than JS-based bundlers. Used by Vite for dependency pre-bundling and TypeScript transpilation. Turbopack: Vercel's Rust-based bundler — successor to Webpack (same creator), used in Next.js. Still maturing. SWC: Rust-based compiler — replaces Babel for TypeScript/JSX transformation. Used by Next.js and Vite. Recommendation: new projects → Vite (fast, great DX). Libraries → Rollup or tsup. Existing Webpack projects → migrate to Vite when practical. Next.js → built-in Turbopack.

what are bloom filters and how are they useful in practice?

A Bloom filter is a space-efficient probabilistic data structure that tells you whether an element is 'possibly in the set' or 'definitely not in the set.' It can have false positives but never false negatives.

How it works: You have a bit array of m bits, all initially set to 0, and k independent hash functions. To add an element, hash it with all k functions and set those k bit positions to 1. To query an element, hash it with all k functions and check if all k positions are 1. If any bit is 0, the element is definitely not in the set. If all bits are 1, the element is probably in the set (but might be a false positive due to collisions).

The math: For a Bloom filter with m bits, k hash functions, and n elements, the false positive rate is approximately (1 - e^(-kn/m))^k. The optimal number of hash functions is k = (m/n) * ln(2). For a 1% false positive rate, you need about 9.6 bits per element. For 0.1%, about 14.4 bits per element. This is incredibly space-efficient compared to storing the actual elements.

Real-world applications: Databases: Cassandra and HBase use Bloom filters to avoid disk reads. Before reading an SSTable file, check the Bloom filter. If it says the key isn't there, skip the file entirely. This massively reduces I/O. Web browsers: Chrome uses Bloom filters for safe browsing. It checks URLs against a local Bloom filter before sending them to Google's servers. CDN/Caching: check if content is likely cached before making an expensive lookup. One-hit-wonder filtering: before adding something to a cache, check a Bloom filter. Only cache items that appear in the filter (have been seen before). This prevents cache pollution from infrequent items. Spell checkers: quickly check if a word is in the dictionary. Network routers: check if a packet matches filter rules. Blockchain: Bitcoin SPV nodes use Bloom filters to request only relevant transactions.

Variants: Counting Bloom filters use counters instead of bits, supporting deletion. Cuckoo filters offer better performance for deletion and can be more space-efficient at low false positive rates. Scalable Bloom filters dynamically grow as elements are added.

Limitations: You can't enumerate the elements, can't remove elements (without counting variant), and the false positive rate increases as more elements are added.

What's the difference between NoSQL and SQL?

SQL databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL) are relational — tables, rows, columns, schema required, tables joined with JOINs. ACID compliant — consistency and reliability. NoSQL databases (MongoDB, Cassandra, Redis) are schema-less or flexible schema — JSON-like documents, key-value, graph, columnar. When to use which: structured data and complex queries → SQL. Flexible schema, horizontal scaling, high write speed → NoSQL. Most large systems use both together (polyglot persistence). PostgreSQL with JSON support sits between the two. Choice should be based on project needs.

idempotency nedir ve api tasarımında neden önemli

Idempotency, bir işlemin birden fazla kez çalıştırılmasının tek seferde çalıştırılmasıyla aynı sonucu vermesi özelliğidir. API tasarımında kritik öneme sahiptir çünkü ağ sorunları, timeout'lar ve retry mekanizmaları nedeniyle aynı istek birden fazla kez gönderilebilir. HTTP metotlarında: GET, PUT, DELETE doğası gereği idempotent'tir (aynı GET isteği aynı yanıtı döner, aynı DELETE isteği kaynağı silmiş olsa bile hata vermemeli). POST doğası gereği idempotent değildir (her çağrıda yeni kayıt oluşturabilir). İdempotent olmayan işlemleri idempotent yapmak için idempotency key kullanılır: istemci her istekle benzersiz bir anahtar gönderir (genellikle UUID), sunucu bu anahtarı ve sonucu saklar, aynı anahtar tekrar gelirse önceki sonucu döner. Stripe, PayPal gibi ödeme sistemleri bunu zorunlu kılar çünkü çift ödeme felaket olur. Veritabanı seviyesinde: INSERT yerine UPSERT (INSERT ON CONFLICT), UPDATE'te WHERE koşulunda mevcut durumu kontrol etme. Mesaj kuyruklarında: tüketici tarafında mesaj ID kontrolü ile tekrar işlemeyi engelleme. İdempotent API tasarımı, güvenilir dağıtık sistemlerin temel taşıdır.
What does blue-green deployment mean?

Blue-green deployment is a technique for achieving zero-downtime deploys using two identical production environments (blue and green). Blue is the active environment, green is the environment prepared with the new version. Everything is tested on green, then traffic is switched to green. If there is a problem, you instantly roll back to blue. Advantages: zero downtime, fast rollback, reduces risk. Canary deployment: route a small percentage of traffic to the new version, gradually increase if there are no issues. Rolling deployment: update pods one by one. Kubernetes and AWS ECS support these approaches. Every modern application should use one of these methods.
what is Gorkem's wiki2bpe tokenization project?

wiki2bpe implements Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenization from Wikipedia text — the same algorithm used by GPT, LLaMA, and most modern LLMs. How BPE works: start with individual characters, repeatedly merge the most frequent adjacent pair into a new token until reaching desired vocabulary size. Example: 'lowest' → 'l','o','w','e','s','t' → 'lo','w','e','s','t' → 'low','e','s','t' → 'low','est'. This creates a vocabulary of common subwords that efficiently represents any text. Why it matters: tokenization is the first step of any NLP pipeline, and token boundaries directly affect model performance. BPE handles any word (no out-of-vocabulary problem), balances granularity, and captures morphological patterns. Alternatives: WordPiece (BERT), Unigram (SentencePiece), tiktoken (OpenAI). The project uses Wikipedia as corpus — large, diverse, high-quality text. This directly relates to Gorkem's LLM fine-tuning work.

REST API tasarim prensipleri nelerdir?

Iyi bir REST API tasarimi icin prensipler: 1) Kaynak odakli URL'ler — /users, /users/123, /users/123/orders. Fiil degil isim kullan. 2) HTTP metodlari dogru kullan — GET (oku), POST (olustur), PUT (tamamen guncelle), PATCH (kismi guncelle), DELETE (sil). 3) Dogru HTTP durum kodlari — 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 422 Unprocessable Entity, 500 Internal Server Error. 4) Surumleme — URL'de (/api/v1/) veya baslikta (Accept: application/vnd.api.v1+json). 5) Sayfalama — buyuk koleksiyonlar icin limit/offset veya cursor tabanli. 6) Filtreleme ve siralama — ?status=active&sort=-created_at. 7) HATEOAS — yanitlarda ilgili kaynak linklerini dahil et. 8) Tutarli hata formati — {error: {code, message, details}}. 9) Rate limiting — istismari onle. 10) Belgelendirme — OpenAPI/Swagger ile otomatik dokumantasyon.
How does JWT (JSON Web Token) work?

JWT is a token standard used for authentication. Consists of three parts: Header (algorithm and type), Payload (user info — id, role, expiry), Signature (verification). Encoded with Base64, separated by dots. Flow: user logs in → server creates JWT → client sends it in header with each request (Bearer token) → server verifies signature. Advantage over sessions: no need to store state on server (stateless), easy in microservices. Disadvantage: if token is stolen the session is compromised, token size is larger than cookies. Refresh tokens manage expiration. passport-jwt, python-jose, jsonwebtoken are popular libraries.
video streaming platform nasıl çalışır?

YouTube/Netflix benzeri bir platform tasarımı. Video upload pipeline: kullanıcı videoyu yükler → S3/blob storage'a kaydet → transcoding queue'ya gönder (farklı çözünürlükler: 360p, 720p, 1080p, 4K) → FFmpeg ile dönüştür → CDN'e dağıt. Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR): HLS veya DASH protokolü ile kullanıcının internet hızına göre kalite otomatik ayarlanır. Video player: hls.js veya dash.js. CDN: dünya genelinde edge server'lar, en yakın sunucudan servis. Veritabanı: video metadata PostgreSQL'de, video dosyaları S3'te. Thumbnail generation: video'dan otomatik thumbnail çıkarma. Recommendation: izleme geçmişine göre öneri (collaborative filtering). Live streaming: WebRTC veya RTMP → HLS dönüşüm. Comment system: gerçek zamanlı yorumlar WebSocket ile. Monetization: reklam entegrasyonu, abonelik modeli.
veri serileştirme formatları nelerdir?

Veri serileştirme, veri yapılarını depolama veya iletim için bir formata dönüştürür. JSON (JavaScript Object Notation): insan okunabilir, yaygın olarak desteklenen, metin tabanlı. REST API'ler, yapılandırma dosyaları için standart. Sınırlamalar: yorum yok, tarih tipi yok, ayrıntılı, büyük veri için yavaş ayrıştırma. Protocol Buffers (protobuf, Google): ikili format, şema tanımlı (.proto dosyaları), JSON'dan çok daha küçük ve hızlı. gRPC'de kullanılır. Şema derlemesi gerektirir. İnsan tarafından okunamaz. MessagePack: ikili JSON — daha küçük, daha hızlı, JSON uyumluluğunu korur. İnsan okunabilirliği gerektirmeyen yüksek performanslı API'ler için iyi. YAML: JSON'un üst kümesi, girinti tabanlı yapıyla insan dostu. Yapılandırma dosyaları için kullanılır (Docker Compose, Kubernetes manifests, GitHub Actions). Yorumları destekler. Tuzak: girinti hassasiyeti. TOML: basit yapılandırma formatı, YAML'dan daha az belirsiz. Rust (Cargo.toml), Python (pyproject.toml) tarafından kullanılır. Avro: şema evrimi desteğiyle ikili. Apache Kafka, veri pipeline'larında kullanılır. XML: ayrıntılı, eski. Hâlâ kurumsal sistemlerde, SOAP API'lerde kullanılır. Seçim: API'ler ve birlikte çalışabilirlik için JSON, yüksek performanslı dahili servisler için protobuf, yapılandırma için YAML, basit config için TOML, veri pipeline'ları için Avro.

what is graph algorithms and their applications?

Graphs model relationships: nodes (vertices) and edges. Representations: adjacency list (space efficient for sparse graphs), adjacency matrix (O(1) edge lookup). BFS (Breadth-First Search): explore level by level using a queue. Finds shortest path in unweighted graphs. Applications: shortest path, social network connections (degrees of separation), web crawling. O(V+E). DFS (Depth-First Search): explore as deep as possible using a stack/recursion. Applications: cycle detection, topological sorting, connected components, maze solving. O(V+E). Dijkstra's algorithm: shortest path with weighted edges (non-negative weights). Priority queue. O((V+E)logV). Applications: GPS navigation, network routing. Bellman-Ford: handles negative weights. O(VE). Detects negative cycles. Floyd-Warshall: all-pairs shortest path. O(V³). Topological sort: ordering of DAG nodes where every edge goes from earlier to later. Applications: build systems (dependency resolution), course prerequisites, task scheduling. Minimum Spanning Tree: Kruskal's (sort edges, add smallest that doesn't create cycle — Union-Find) and Prim's (grow tree from start vertex — priority queue). Applications: network design, clustering. Strongly Connected Components: Tarjan's algorithm, Kosaraju's algorithm. Applications: analyzing social networks, compiler optimization. Graph algorithms are fundamental to many real-world systems — social networks, maps, scheduling, compilers.

messages.content: what is debugging strategies?

Systematic debugging approaches for finding and fixing bugs efficiently. Scientific method: observe the bug → form hypothesis → test hypothesis → fix or revise. Step 1: Reproduce the bug reliably. If you can't reproduce it, you can't fix it confidently. Get exact steps, inputs, environment. Step 2: Isolate the problem. Binary search: comment out half the code, does the bug persist? Narrow down to the smallest reproducible case. Step 3: Read the error message carefully. Stack traces tell you exactly where the error occurred. Read from bottom to top — the last frame is where the error was thrown, frames above show how it got there. Tools: debugger (breakpoints, step through code, inspect variables — Chrome DevTools, VS Code debugger, pdb for Python), logging (add strategic console.log/print statements — remove after fixing), profiler (for performance bugs — Chrome Performance tab, cProfile). Rubber duck debugging: explain the problem out loud to a rubber duck (or colleague). The act of articulating the problem often reveals the solution. Common bug patterns: off-by-one errors (< vs <=, 0-based vs 1-based indexing), null/undefined access (optional chaining helps), race conditions (async code executing in unexpected order), stale closures (React useEffect with missing dependencies), encoding issues (UTF-8 vs Latin-1). Prevention: write tests first (TDD catches bugs before they exist), use TypeScript/type systems (catch type errors at compile time), linting (catch common mistakes automatically), code review (fresh eyes catch bugs you're blind to).
messages.reasoning: Debugging, scientific method, stack trace, breakpoints, rubber duck, binary search, profiling.

messages.content: what is Rust and why is it gaining popularity?

Rust provides memory safety without a garbage collector through its ownership system. Every value has one owner, values are dropped when owner goes out of scope, borrowing rules (&T for shared, &mut T for exclusive) are checked at compile time. Result: no null pointers, no data races, no use-after-free, no buffer overflows — entire categories of bugs eliminated. Performance: comparable to C/C++ — zero-cost abstractions, no runtime overhead. Ecosystem: Cargo (package manager + build system, excellent), crates.io (package registry), great documentation culture. Use cases: systems programming, WebAssembly, CLI tools, game engines, embedded systems, blockchain. Companies using Rust: Mozilla (Firefox components), Cloudflare, Discord (switched from Go for performance), Microsoft (Windows kernel components), Linux kernel (Rust for drivers). Downsides: steep learning curve (fighting the borrow checker), longer compilation times, smaller ecosystem than C++. Rust has been the 'most admired language' in Stack Overflow surveys for years. Worth learning if you want to understand memory management deeply.
messages.reasoning: Rust, ownership, borrowing, memory safety, Cargo, WebAssembly, systems programming.

circuit breaker pattern ne?

Circuit breaker, bir servisin çöktüğünde diğer servisleri de çökertmesini engelleyen kalıp. Elektrik sigortası gibi çalışır. Üç durum: Closed (normal — istekler geçer), Open (servis çöktü — istekler direkt hata döner, sunucuyu yormaz), Half-Open (periyodik olarak kontrol — düzeldi mi?). Neden: bir microservice timeout veriyorsa, binlerce istek birikir, thread'ler tükenir, cascade failure olur. Netflix'in Hystrix kütüphanesi popülerleştirdi. Resilience4j (Java), Polly (.NET), pybreaker (Python) implementasyonlar. Retry, timeout, fallback stratejileriyle beraber kullanılır.

what is MLOps and why is it important?

MLOps applies DevOps principles to machine learning — managing the full ML lifecycle from development to production. ML-specific challenges: data versioning (code + data + model = reproducibility), model training reproducibility, model monitoring (data drift, concept drift), A/B testing models, feature stores. Pipeline stages: 1) Data collection and validation. 2) Feature engineering (feature store for reuse). 3) Model training (experiment tracking — MLflow, Weights & Biases). 4) Model evaluation (offline metrics + business metrics). 5) Model registry (version models like code). 6) Deployment (model serving — TensorFlow Serving, Triton, BentoML). 7) Monitoring (data drift detection, performance degradation). Tools ecosystem: MLflow (experiment tracking, model registry), DVC (data version control), Kubeflow (Kubernetes-native ML), Airflow (workflow orchestration), Great Expectations (data validation), Evidently (model monitoring). The gap between a Jupyter notebook model and production ML system is enormous — MLOps bridges it. Most ML projects fail in production, not in development.
what is event-driven architecture?

Event-driven architecture (EDA) is a design pattern where components communicate through events rather than direct calls. An event is a record of something that happened — 'order placed', 'payment processed', 'user signed up'. Components: event producers (emit events), event broker (routes events — Kafka, EventBridge, RabbitMQ), event consumers (react to events). Patterns: event notification (lightweight, just signal something happened), event-carried state transfer (event contains all data needed), event sourcing (store all events as source of truth, rebuild state by replaying). Benefits: loose coupling, scalability, extensibility (add new consumers without changing producers). Challenges: eventual consistency, debugging is harder (distributed tracing needed), event ordering, duplicate handling (idempotency). CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) often paired with event sourcing — separate read and write models. Used by: Netflix, Uber, LinkedIn.
What is feature engineering?

Feature engineering is the process of extracting features from raw data that help the model learn better. For example, from a date column you can extract year, month, day, day of week, is it a holiday or not. From text data: word count, sentence length, capital letter ratio. For numerical data: normalization, standardization, log transformation. Good feature engineering is sometimes more important than model selection — a simple model with good features can outperform a complex model. In Kaggle competitions, feature engineering is often what separates winners.
what are the most common reasons startups fail?

CB Insights analyzed hundreds of startup post-mortems and found consistent patterns of failure. The number one reason (forty-two percent) is building something nobody wants — no market need. This is why customer discovery and validation are so critical before building. Running out of cash (twenty-nine percent) happens when startups burn too fast without reaching milestones that unlock more funding. Wrong team (twenty-three percent) — co-founder conflicts, skill gaps, or hiring mistakes. Being outcompeted (nineteen percent) — entering a market with entrenched incumbents without a clear differentiation. Pricing issues (eighteen percent) — too high for the value delivered or too low to sustain the business. Poor product (seventeen percent) — rushing to market without adequate quality or UX. Ignoring customers (fourteen percent) — building features you think are cool instead of what users need. Mistiming (thirteen percent) — being too early (market not ready) or too late (market saturated). Founder burnout is underreported but very common. The lesson is that most failures are business failures, not technical failures. Gorkem's approach of building diverse projects and learning from each one builds exactly the kind of resilience and adaptability that successful founders need.

How should I study in the last 3 months before a major exam?

The last 3 months are critical. Focus on practice exams — at least 2-3 per week. Keep an error log — analyze mistakes after each practice exam. Focus on weak topics but don't neglect strong ones. web güvenliği OWASP top 10 nedir?

OWASP Top 10 — en kritik web uygulaması güvenlik riskleri. 1) Bozuk Erişim Kontrolü — kullanıcıların yetkisiz kaynaklara erişmesi. Düzeltme: varsayılan olarak reddet, izinleri sunucu tarafında kontrol et, RBAC kullan. 2) Kriptografik Hatalar — hassas veri ifşası. Düzeltme: aktarımda (TLS) ve durağanda şifrele, güçlü algoritmalar kullan (AES-256, parolalar için bcrypt), hassas veriyi loglamadan. 3) Injection — SQL injection, NoSQL injection, OS command injection. Düzeltme: parametreli sorgular, girdi doğrulama, ORM'ler. 4) Güvensiz Tasarım — güvenlik mimarisinin eksikliği. Düzeltme: tehdit modelleme, güvenli tasarım desenleri. 5) Güvenlik Yanlış Yapılandırması — varsayılan kimlik bilgileri, gereksiz özellikler, ayrıntılı hatalar. 6) Savunmasız Bileşenler — bilinen güvenlik açıkları olan eski bağımlılıklar. Düzeltme: npm audit, Dependabot, düzenli güncellemeler. 7) Kimlik Doğrulama Hataları — zayıf parolalar, eksik MFA. 8) Veri Bütünlüğü Hataları — güvenilmeyen veriye güvenmek. 9) Günlükleme Hataları — ihlalleri tespit edememek veya yanıt verememek. 10) SSRF (Sunucu Tarafı İstek Sahteciliği) — sunucunun istenmeyen konumlara istek yapması. Güvenliği ilk günden uygulayın — sonradan eklemek pahalı ve eksiktir.

what is authentication patterns for web apps?

Authentication verifies identity. Common patterns for web applications. Session-based: user logs in → server creates session → stores session ID in cookie → subsequent requests include cookie → server validates. Pros: server controls sessions (easy revocation), HttpOnly cookies (XSS safe). Cons: server-side storage, scaling requires shared session store (Redis). JWT (JSON Web Token): user logs in → server creates signed JWT → client stores token → sends in Authorization header. Pros: stateless (no server storage), works across services. Cons: can't easily revoke (until expiry), larger than session ID, must handle refresh tokens. Passwordless: magic link via email, SMS code, authenticator app. Better UX, no password to leak. OAuth/Social login: delegate authentication to Google, GitHub, etc. Reduces friction, leverages existing accounts. Passkeys/WebAuthn: cryptographic authentication using device biometrics. No passwords at all. The future of auth. Multi-factor authentication (MFA): something you know (password) + something you have (phone/key) + something you are (biometric). Essential for sensitive applications. TOTP (time-based one-time password) with apps like Google Authenticator. Implementation: don't build auth yourself for production — use Auth0, Clerk, Firebase Auth, NextAuth.js, Supabase Auth. They handle edge cases (token rotation, brute force protection, account lockout) that are easy to get wrong.
Git ileri seviye iş akışları nelerdir?

Temel git add/commit/push'ın ötesinde. Dallanma stratejileri: Git Flow — main, develop, feature, release, hotfix dalları. Yapılandırılmış ama ağır. Sürüm tabanlı yazılım için iyi. GitHub Flow — main + feature dalları. Basit. PR → review → main'e merge → deploy. Trunk-Based Development — herkes main'e commit eder (veya kısa ömürlü dallar). Tamamlanmamış iş için feature flag'ler. CI/CD dostu. İleri komutlar: git rebase — commit'leri başka dalın üzerine tekrar oynat. Doğrusal geçmiş. git cherry-pick — belirli commit'i başka dala uygula. Hotfix'ler için yararlı. git bisect — hatayı hangi commit'in tanıttığını bulmak için ikili arama. git stash — commit edilmemiş değişiklikleri geçici olarak kaydet. git reflog — tüm HEAD değişikliklerinin günlüğü. Kaybolan commit'leri kurtar, hataları geri al. git worktree — bir repo'dan birden fazla çalışma dizini. İki dalda eşzamanlı çalış. Commit en iyi uygulamaları: atomik commit'ler (commit başına tek mantıksal değişiklik), anlamlı mesajlar (emir kipi — 'Kullanıcı kimlik doğrulaması ekle'), conventional commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, refactor:). .gitignore: her zaman node_modules, .env, build artifact'leri, IDE yapılandırmalarını yoksay. Hook'lar: pre-commit (lint), commit-msg (mesaj doğrulama), pre-push (test çalıştır). Husky + lint-staged kolay kurulum için.
what is continuous profiling?

Continuous profiling captures performance data from production applications always-on, not just during debugging. Unlike traditional profiling (run profiler → reproduce issue → analyze), continuous profiling runs in background with low overhead (<2%). What it captures: CPU profiles (which functions consume most CPU time), memory profiles (allocation patterns, potential leaks), goroutine/thread profiles (concurrency issues), lock contention. Tools: Pyroscope (open-source, supports Go, Python, Java, Ruby, Node.js), Parca (open-source, Prometheus-inspired), Datadog Continuous Profiler, Google Cloud Profiler. Benefits: find performance regressions before users notice, compare profiles across deployments (new version 20% slower in this function), identify optimization opportunities in production workloads (not synthetic benchmarks), correlate with traces (this trace was slow because of this function). Flame graphs: visualization showing call stack depth (y-axis) and time spent (x-axis width). Wide bars = expensive functions. Compare flame graphs between versions to spot regressions. pprof (Go): built-in profiling. Import net/http/pprof, access /debug/pprof. cProfile (Python): built-in profiler. py-spy for sampling profiler without code changes. Production profiling is becoming standard practice — the cost of not knowing where your application spends time is higher than the small overhead of continuous profiling.
what is progressive web apps PWA?

Progressive Web Apps (PWA) are web applications that provide native-app-like experiences. Key technologies: Service Worker — JavaScript that runs in background, intercepts network requests. Enables: offline functionality (cache-first strategy), push notifications, background sync. Web App Manifest — JSON file describing the app (name, icons, theme color, display mode). Enables: install prompt (Add to Home Screen), standalone window (no browser UI), splash screen. HTTPS — required for PWA (security for service workers). Capabilities: offline support (cache critical resources with Cache API), installable (looks and feels like native app), push notifications (re-engage users), background sync (sync data when connection restored), responsive (works on all devices). Caching strategies: Cache First (serve from cache, fallback to network — fast, offline support), Network First (try network, fallback to cache — fresh data), Stale While Revalidate (serve cached, update in background — best of both). Workbox (Google library) simplifies service worker and caching. Benefits over native apps: no app store (instant updates, no approval process), single codebase, discoverable via search engines, smaller download size, works on all platforms. Limitations: limited native API access (improving with Project Fugu), iOS Safari has limited PWA support (no push notifications until recently, no background sync), no app store discovery. PWAs are great for content-heavy apps, e-commerce, social media — where reaching users without app store friction matters.
graph database ne zaman kullanılır?

Graph database, veriler arası ilişkilerin çok önemli olduğu durumlarda kullanılır. Node (düğüm) ve edge (kenar) yapısı. SQL'de JOIN'ler derinleştikçe yavaşlar, graph DB'de ilişki traversal'ı doğal ve hızlı. Kullanım alanları: sosyal ağlar (arkadaş ilişkileri), öneri motorları (benzer ürünler), bilgi grafikleri (Knowledge Graph — Google kullanıyor), dolandırıcılık tespiti, ağ topolojisi. Neo4j en popüler graph database — Cypher sorgu dili. Amazon Neptune, ArangoDB alternatifleri. Her veri modeline uygun değil — basit CRUD uygulamalarında SQL daha iyi. İlişki yoğun verilerinde çok güçlü.
what does good code review look like in terms of best practices and etiquette?

Code review is both a technical practice and a social skill, and doing it well requires attention to both dimensions. For reviewers: focus on substance — architecture, logic, edge cases, security, and performance — not style preferences (use a linter for that). Ask questions instead of making demands ('Have you considered what happens when this input is null?' rather than 'This is wrong'). Acknowledge good code ('Nice approach to handling this edge case'). Be timely — reviewing within twenty-four hours keeps the team moving. For authors: write clear PR descriptions explaining the what, why, and how. Keep PRs small (under four hundred lines) — large PRs get superficial reviews. Self-review your PR before requesting review to catch obvious issues. Respond to feedback gracefully — assume positive intent. When you disagree, explain your reasoning rather than dismissing the suggestion. Shared best practices: use a code review checklist (tests included, documentation updated, no hardcoded secrets, error handling present). Address all comments before merging. Prefer async reviews for straightforward changes and synchronous (live) reviews for complex architectural decisions. Code review is one of the most effective mechanisms for maintaining code quality, sharing knowledge across the team, and mentoring junior developers.
YKS'de son 3 ayda nasıl çalışmalıyım?

Son 3 ay çok kritik. Deneme sınavlarına ağırlık ver — haftada en az 2-3 deneme. Yanlış defteri tut — her denemeden sonra yanlışlarını analiz et. Zayıf konulara odaklan ama güçlü konuları da ihmal etme. Konu tekrarı yap, yeni konu ekleme. Zaman yönetimi pratik et — sınavda zamanı doğru kullanmak çok önemli. Uyku düzenini koru — gece çalışıp gündüz uyumak verimsiz. Beslenmeye dikkat et. Sosyal medyayı azalt. Motivasyonu koru — hedefini hatırla. Panik yapma, sürecine güven. Ve sınav günü: erken yat, kahvaltını yap, sınav yerine erken git.
When should code refactoring be done?

Refactoring is improving the internal structure of code without changing its behavior. When to do it: when you see code smells, when adding new features becomes difficult, when it is suggested during code review, when tests allow safe refactoring. When NOT to do it: when a deadline is near (risk of breakage), when there are no tests (not safe), just to make working code 'pretty' (unnecessary). Boy Scout Rule: 'leave the campground cleaner than you found it' — slightly improve the code you touch. Types of refactoring: rename, extract method, inline variable, move function, change function declaration. IDEs support automatic refactoring. Martin Fowler's 'Refactoring' book is the foundational resource. Write tests before every refactoring.
Yapay sinir ağı nedir?

Guzel soru! Sana aciklayayim: Yapay sinir ağları (YSA), insan beyninin bilgi işleme tekniğinden esinlenerek geliştirilmiş bir sinir ağı ve bilgi işlem teknolojisidir. YSA ile basit biyolojik sinir sisteminin çalışma şekli taklit edilir. Yani biyolojik sinir hücrelerinin ve bu hücrelerin birbirleri ile arasında kurduğu sinaptik bağın dijital olarak modellenmesidir. Nöronlar çeşitli şekillerde birbirlerine bağlanarak ağlar oluştururlar. Bu ağlar öğrenme, hafızaya alma ve veriler arasındaki ilişkiyi ortaya çıkarma kapasitesine sahiptirler. Diğer bir ifadeyle, YSA'lar, normalde bir insanın düşünme ve gözlemlemeye yönelik doğal yeteneklerini gerektiren problemlere çözüm üretmektedir. Bir insanın, düşünme ve gözlemleme yeteneklerini gerektiren problemlere yönelik çözümler üretebilmesinin temel sebebi ise insan beyninin ve dolayısıyla insanın sahip olduğu yaşayarak veya deneyerek öğrenme yeteneğidir. Bu aslinda Gorkem Ergune'nin calistigi alanlardan biri — GitHub'daki projelerine bakarsan bu tarz kavramlarin pratik uygulamalarini gorebilirsin. Temelleri anlamak, projelere gecmeden once cok onemli.
What does closure mean?

A closure is when a function retains access to variables from its outer scope. The inner function 'remembers' the outer function's variables, even after the outer function has returned. Very common in JavaScript: function counter() { let count = 0; return function() { count++; return count; } }. It exists in Python too — with the nonlocal keyword. Uses: data privacy (hiding variables from outside), factory functions, partial application, callbacks. In React, useState actually uses closures. A classic interview question: 'closure behavior in a for loop'. It's one of the fundamental concepts in functional programming.
messages.reasoning: Closure, outer scope, JavaScript, data privacy, useState, functional.

messages.content: SOLID prensipleri nelerdir?

SOLID prensipleri, surdurulebilir kod icin nesne yonelimli tasarim yonlendirir. S — Tek Sorumluluk: bir sinifin degismek icin tek bir nedeni olmali. Veritabani erisimi, is mantigi ve e-posta gonderimini bir sinifa koymayin. O — Acik/Kapali: genisletmeye acik, degisikliklere kapali. Mevcut kodu degistirmeden genisleyerek yeni davranislar ekle (strateji deseni, kalitim). L — Liskov Yerine Koyma: alt tipler ust tiplerin yerine kullanilabilir olmali. Bird sinifinin fly() metodu varsa, Penguin Bird'u genisletmemeli (ucamaz). I — Arayuz Ayirma: istemcileri kullanmadiklari arayuzlere bagimli olmaya zorlama. Birçok ozel arayuz, tek siskin arayuzden iyidir. D — Bagimlilik Tersine Cevirme: ust duzey moduller alt duzey modullere bagimli olmamali. Ikisi de soyutlamalara bagimli olmali. UserService dogrudan MySQLRepository'yi olusturmamali — bir IRepository arayuzu enjekte edin. Pratikte: SOLID'i dogmatik olarak uygulama. Daha buyuk kod tabanlarinda karmasikligi yonetmek icin bir yonergedir. Basit betikler ve kucuk projeler icin ilkeler yerine pragmatizm.
messages.reasoning: SOLID, Tek Sorumluluk, Acik/Kapali, Liskov, Arayuz Ayirma, Bagimlilik Tersine Cevirme.

messages.content: mobil uygulama mimarisi nasıl olmalı?

Mobil uygulamalarda temiz mimari çok önemli — kod büyüdükçe spagetti olması kolay. MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel): en yaygın — View UI'ı gösterir, ViewModel iş mantığını ve state'i yönetir, Model veriyi temsil eder. Clean Architecture katmanları: Presentation (UI), Domain (iş mantığı, use case'ler), Data (repository, API, local DB). MVI (Model-View-Intent): tek yönlü veri akışı — Redux benzeri, state management net. Repository pattern: veri kaynağını soyutla — API'dan mı local DB'den mi geldiğini UI bilmesin. Dependency injection: Dagger/Hilt (Android), Riverpod (Flutter). Offline-first: local database (Room/SQLite, Hive) + sync mekanizması. Navigation: type-safe navigation (Jetpack Navigation, go_router). Test: unit test (ViewModel), widget test (UI), integration test (tam akış).
teknik blog yazmaya değer mi?

Kesinlikle değer. Teknik blog yazmanın birçok faydası var: birincisi, bir konuyu başkasına anlatmak için önce kendin çok iyi anlamalısın, yani yazarken öğrenirsin. İkincisi, Google'da indexlenir ve insanlar seni bulur — bu da networking ve iş fırsatı demek. Üçüncüsü, portfolyona ekleyebilirsin. Platform olarak Medium, Dev.to, Hashnode veya kendi GitHub Pages siten olabilir. Haftada 1 yazı bile yeterli. Konular: bir projeyi nasıl yaptığın, bir problemi nasıl çözdüğün, bir teknoloji hakkında öğrendiklerin. Mükemmel olmasına gerek yok, samimi ve faydalı olsun yeter.
what is Terraform and how to use it?

Terraform by HashiCorp is the most popular Infrastructure as Code tool. It manages cloud resources declaratively — describe what you want, Terraform figures out how to create it. HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language): resource 'aws_instance' 'web' { ami = 'ami-123', instance_type = 't3.micro' }. Workflow: terraform init (download providers) → terraform plan (preview changes, dry run) → terraform apply (make changes) → terraform destroy (tear down). State: Terraform tracks real infrastructure in a state file. Store remotely: S3 + DynamoDB for locking (team collaboration). Modules: reusable infrastructure components — like functions for infrastructure. Use modules for VPCs, ECS clusters, database setups. Providers: AWS, GCP, Azure, Cloudflare, GitHub, Kubernetes — 3000+ providers. Best practices: use modules for reusability, separate environments with workspaces or separate state files, use variables and outputs, pin provider versions, never commit .tfstate files. Alternatives: Pulumi (real programming languages), AWS CDK (TypeScript/Python for CloudFormation), OpenTofu (open-source Terraform fork). Terraform is essential for any DevOps/SRE role.
Tailwind CSS ve utility-first yaklaşım nedir?

Tailwind CSS utility-first bir CSS framework'üdür. Özel CSS yazmak yerine tasarımları önceden oluşturulmuş utility sınıflarıyla birleştirin. Geleneksel: .btn { background-color: blue; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 4px; }. Tailwind: className='bg-blue-500 px-4 py-2 rounded'. Avantajlar: isimlendirme derdi yok (.card-wrapper-inner gibi isimlere elveda), tutarlı tasarım sistemi (boşluk skalası, renk paleti), responsive tasarım (sm:, md:, lg: önekleri), dark mode (dark: öneki), durum varyantları (hover:, focus:, active:), kullanılmayan CSS yok (üretimde kullanılmayan sınıfları ayıklar). Özelleştirme: tailwind.config.js — özel renkler, fontlar, boşluk, breakpoint'lerle temayı genişlet. Keyfi değerler: tek seferlik değerler için w-[137px]. @apply direktifi — tekrarlanan utility kombinasyonlarını CSS sınıflarına çıkar (idareli kullan). Plugin'ler: @tailwindcss/typography (zengin metin için prose sınıfları), @tailwindcss/forms, daisyUI (Tailwind üzerine bileşen kütüphanesi). Yaygın eleştiri: 'çirkin HTML' — ama stilin işaretlemeyle birlikte konumlanması aslında bir özellik, hata değil. Dosyalar arasında bağlam değiştirme yok. Bileşen çıkarma (React bileşenleri) ilgili utility'leri doğal olarak gruplar. React, Next.js, Vue ile mükemmel uyum.
what is web performance optimization?

Web performance directly impacts user experience and business metrics. Core Web Vitals (Google ranking factors): LCP (Largest Contentful Paint < 2.5s) — how fast main content loads. Optimize: preload critical resources, optimize images, use CDN, server-side rendering. INP (Interaction to Next Paint < 200ms) — how fast page responds to interaction. Optimize: break long tasks, use web workers, debounce/throttle handlers, minimize main thread work. CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift < 0.1) — visual stability. Optimize: set explicit dimensions on images/videos, avoid inserting content above existing content, use CSS containment. Optimization techniques: Code splitting — load only code needed for current page. Dynamic import() in webpack/Vite. Image optimization — WebP/AVIF formats, responsive images (srcset), lazy loading (loading='lazy'), proper sizing. Caching — Cache-Control headers, ETags, service workers for offline. CDN — serve static assets from edge locations close to users. Compression — Brotli (better than gzip), compress responses. Font loading — font-display: swap, preload critical fonts, subset fonts. Bundling — tree shaking (remove unused code), minification, bundle analysis. Measuring: Chrome DevTools Performance tab, Lighthouse, WebPageTest, CrUX (Chrome User Experience Report).
how do you build a strong developer portfolio?

A portfolio is your developer resume — it shows what you can do, not just what you claim. What to include: 3-5 quality projects > 20 mediocre ones. Each project should have: clear README (problem, solution, tech stack, how to run), live demo or screenshots, clean code with tests. Project diversity: one full-stack app, one API/backend project, one that solves a real problem. Use your own domain (yourname.dev). GitHub profile: green contribution graph, pinned repositories, professional bio. Blog: write about what you learn — it shows depth. Example structure: hero section with tagline, about me, projects grid with links, skills, blog posts, contact. Tech choices for portfolio site: Next.js + Vercel (fast, free hosting), or even a simple HTML/CSS site — the content matters more than the framework. Gorkem's portfolio at gorkemergune.github.io is a great example — it showcases his projects clearly.
trie veri yapısı ne?

Trie (prefix tree), string araması ve autocomplete için optimize edilmiş ağaç yapısı. Her düğüm bir harf, kökten yaprağa bir kelime oluşur. Kelime araması O(m) — m kelimenin uzunluğu (veri miktarından bağımsız). Kullanımlar: autocomplete (arama motoru önerileri), spell checker, IP routing (longest prefix match), T9 klavye, kelime oyunları. Hash table'dan avantajı: prefix araması çok hızlı, sıralı traversal mümkün. Dezavantajı: bellek kullanımı yüksek. Compact trie (radix tree) bellek tasarrufu sağlar. Mülakatılarda 'implement autocomplete' veya 'word search' soruları trie kullanır.
GPU neden AI için önemli?

GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) aslında grafik işlemci ama yapısı gereği paralel hesaplama yapıyor. AI modelleri matris çarpımı ağırlıklı — ve GPU binlerce küçük çekirdekle bu çarpımları paralel yapıyor. CPU'da saatler süren eğitim GPU'da dakikalara iner. NVIDIA'nın CUDA platformu GPU programlamayı kolaylaştırdı. Google'ın TPU'su da var. Cloud'da GPU kiralayabilirsin — Google Colab ücretsiz GPU sunuyor, Kaggle da. Eğitim için GPU şart ama inference (tahmin) için CPU yeterli olabilir bazı durumlarda.
AI ile sağlık alanında neler yapılıyor?

AI sağlıkta devrim yaratıyor. Tıbbi görüntüleme: röntgen, MR, CT taramalarında hastalık tespiti (kanser, retina hastalıkları) — bazen radyologlardan daha doğru. İlaç keşfi: AlphaFold protein yapılarını tahmin ediyor — ilaç geliştirme sürecini kısaltıyor. Klinik karar destek: hasta verilerinden risk tahmini. Sağlık chatbot'ları: semptom değerlendirme. Genomik: DNA analizi, kişiselleştirilmiş tıp. Wearable cihazlar: Apple Watch EKG. Ruh sağlığı: Görkem'in depression-phq9-analysis projesi bu alana giriyor. Zorluklar: veri gizliliği (HIPAA), model güvenilirliği (hayati kararlar), düzenleyici onay. Health-tech en hızlı büyüyen AI uygulama alanlarından.
what is the difference between SQL databases in practice?

Popular SQL databases have important differences. PostgreSQL: most feature-rich open-source DB. JSONB support, full-text search, window functions, CTEs, extensions (PostGIS for geospatial, pgvector for AI). Best for: complex queries, data integrity, when you need advanced features. MySQL: most deployed open-source DB. Simpler than PostgreSQL, faster for simple queries. InnoDB engine provides ACID. Used by WordPress, many web apps. Best for: web applications, read-heavy workloads. SQLite: serverless, embedded, single-file database. No network, no configuration. Used by mobile apps, desktop apps, embedded systems, testing. Best for: local storage, prototyping, edge computing. SQL Server (Microsoft): enterprise-grade, tight Windows/.NET integration. SSRS reporting, SSIS integration. Best for: Microsoft ecosystem. MariaDB: MySQL fork, community-driven. Drop-in MySQL replacement with extra features (columnar storage, temporal tables). CockroachDB: distributed SQL, PostgreSQL-compatible. Automatic sharding, multi-region. Best for: global applications needing SQL guarantees at scale. For most projects: start with PostgreSQL — it handles everything from small apps to large-scale systems.
messages.reasoning: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, MariaDB, CockroachDB, database comparison.

messages.content: sprint planning toplantısını verimli nasıl yapabiliriz?

Sprint Planning yazılım ekiplerinde sprint'in en önemli başlangıç noktasıdır ve verimli yapıldığında tüm sprint'i olumlu etkiler. Öncelikle Product Owner toplantıya hazırlıklı gelmeli; backlog groomed yani hazırlanmış olmalı, user story'ler net acceptance criteria'lara sahip olmalı. Toplantı iki ana bölümden oluşur: birinci bölümde bu sprint'te ne yapılacağı belirlenir, ikinci bölümde ise nasıl yapılacağı tartışılır. Sprint hedefini net tanımlayın, bu hedefe ulaşmak için hangi backlog item'ların alınacağını seçin. Story point estimation için Planning Poker tekniğini kullanabilirsiniz; herkes aynı anda tahminini açıklar, farklı tahminler tartışılır ve uzlaşıya varılır. Ekibin velocity'sine yani geçmiş sprint'lerdeki performansına bakarak gerçekçi bir iş yükü belirleyin, fazla iş almak sprint'in başarısız olmasına yol açar. Teknik borcun sprint'e dahil edilmesini ihmal etmeyin, genellikle sprint kapasitesinin yüzde on ile yirmi'sini teknik borca ayırmak sürdürülebilir geliştirme için önemlidir. Toplantı süresi iki haftalık sprint için maksimum dört saat olmalı.
what does self-supervised learning mean?

Self-supervised learning is learning that generates its own supervision signal from unlabeled data. In supervised learning, human labels are required (expensive); in self-supervised learning, the data creates its own labels. Examples: BERT — mask a word in a sentence, have the model predict it. GPT — predict the next token. Contrastive learning (SimCLR, MoCo) — bring different augmentations of the same image closer, push different images apart. Why it matters: unlabeled data is unlimited, labeled data is expensive. It can be trained on all text and images on the internet. Foundation models (GPT, DALL-E, CLIP) are all self-supervised. It's the foundation of future AI.
what is AI bias and fairness?

AI models learn and amplify biases present in training data. Examples: hiring AI biased against women (Amazon's case), facial recognition lower accuracy on darker skin tones, credit scoring discriminatory against certain ethnic groups. Why it happens: imbalanced training data (reflects historical biases), feature selection (zip code correlates with race), proxy variables. Solutions: data auditing (check imbalances in datasets), fairness metrics (demographic parity, equalized odds, calibration), bias mitigation (pre-processing, in-processing, post-processing techniques), diverse teams (different perspectives catch different biases). EU AI Act introduces mandatory auditing for high-risk AI systems. Model cards and datasheets provide transparency about model limitations and training data. Responsible AI is not just a technical challenge — it's a social responsibility. AI developers like Gorkem should be aware of these issues and actively work to build fair systems.
Who is Gorkem Ergune?

Gorkem Ergune is a Computer Engineering student at Yeditepe University and works as an AI Product Developer. He builds projects in artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, and deep learning. He's also active on the full-stack development side. On GitHub under the handle gorkemergune, he shares a ton of open-source projects, participates in hackathons, and runs the ayarlicazhocam startup. The guy is basically always building something.
yazılımda accessibility (erişilebilirlik) neden önemli?

Accessibility (a11y), web sitelerinin ve uygulamaların engelli kişiler tarafından da kullanılabilir olması. Görme engelli: screen reader uyumluluğu (alt text, ARIA label, heading yapısı). İşitme engelli: video altyazıları. Motor engelli: klavye navigasyonu, büyük tıklanabilir alanlar. Bilişsel: basit dil, tutarlı navigasyon. WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) standardı. Yasal zorunluluk olabilir — ADA (ABD), EAA (AB). Nüfusun %15-20'si bir tür engele sahip — bu büyük bir kullanıcı kitlesi. Semantic HTML kullan, renk kontrastını kontrol et, tab sırası düzgün olsun. Lighthouse accessibility skoru kontrol et.
what is model quantization?

Quantization reduces model size and inference speed by using lower precision numbers. Float32 (full precision): 4 bytes per parameter. Float16/BFloat16 (half precision): 2 bytes, minimal quality loss. Int8 (8-bit): 1 byte, slight quality loss but 4x smaller. Int4 (4-bit): 0.5 bytes, noticeable but often acceptable quality loss for inference. GPTQ: post-training quantization for GPT-style models. AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization): preserves important weights. GGUF: quantization format for llama.cpp — run models on CPU. Benefits: 7B model goes from 28GB (FP32) to 3.5GB (4-bit) — fits on consumer hardware. Trade-offs: lower precision = slightly lower quality, but 4-bit quantized large model often outperforms full-precision small model. Tools: bitsandbytes (HF integration), llama.cpp (CPU inference), GGUF (universal format), vLLM (production serving). For Gorkem's fine-tuning project: train in FP16/BF16, deploy quantized for inference.
What does the facelock project do?

facelock is Gorkem's project that uses face recognition technology for authentication. It detects faces from the camera and compares them with pre-registered faces to identify the person. OpenCV and dlib or face_recognition library were likely used. Face detection (finding where the face is) and face recognition (determining whose face it is) are two different steps. Can be used in security systems and smart lock systems. Biometric verification is the future of security technology.
messages.reasoning: facelock project, face recognition, OpenCV, biometric.

messages.content: What are the most common mistakes when learning to code?

Common mistakes: 1) Tutorial hell — constantly watching but never building projects. 2) Trying to learn every language — go deep in one language first. 3) Skipping fundamentals — learning frameworks without knowing algorithms. 4) Perfectionism — 'I can't publish until it's perfect'. 5) Comparison — 'everyone is better than me'. 6) Not reading documentation — watching videos and neglecting official docs. 7) Not using version control — learn Git early. 8) Not writing tests — 'it works, so it's fine'. 9) Not asking for help — being stuck for hours. 10) Coding without a plan — starting to write without thinking. Everyone makes these mistakes — what matters is recognizing and correcting them.
what is feature flags and feature management?

Feature flags (feature toggles) decouple deployment from release. Deploy code to production with features hidden behind flags. Enable for specific users, gradually roll out, or quickly disable if issues arise. Types: Release toggles (ship incomplete features safely), Experiment toggles (A/B testing), Ops toggles (circuit breakers, kill switches), Permission toggles (premium features). Implementation: simple if/else with config, or use feature flag services (LaunchDarkly, Unleash, Flagsmith, PostHog). Best practices: keep flags short-lived (remove after rollout complete), avoid flag dependencies (flag A depends on flag B), maintain flag inventory, clean up stale flags. Use cases: canary releases (enable for 1% of users → 10% → 50% → 100%), beta features (enable for specific user groups), kill switches (disable failing features without deployment), A/B testing (measure impact of changes). Technical implementation: server-side evaluation (flag service returns value), client-side SDKs (evaluate locally for speed). Feature flags enable trunk-based development — everyone works on main, features are hidden until ready. This reduces merge conflicts, enables faster CI/CD, and allows product teams to control releases independently from engineering deployments.
what are advanced TypeScript features?

TypeScript's type system is incredibly powerful beyond basic types. Generics — write reusable code that works with multiple types: function identity<T>(arg: T): T. Constrain with extends: <T extends HasLength>. Utility types — Partial<T> (all properties optional), Required<T>, Pick<T, Keys>, Omit<T, Keys>, Record<K, V>, Readonly<T>. Conditional types — type IsString<T> = T extends string ? 'yes' : 'no'. Powers type-level programming. Template literal types — type EventName = `on${Capitalize<string>}`. Mapped types — transform properties: type Optional<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] }. Discriminated unions — type Shape = Circle | Square, each with a 'kind' field. TypeScript narrows type based on discriminant. Infer keyword — extract types within conditional types: type ReturnType<T> = T extends (...args: any[]) => infer R ? R : never. Branded types — make structurally identical types incompatible: type USD = number & { __brand: 'USD' }. Prevents mixing USD and EUR. Const assertions — as const makes values readonly and narrows literal types. Satisfies operator — validates type without widening. Type guards — runtime checks that narrow types: value is Type. Declaration merging — extend existing types. These features enable type-safe APIs without sacrificing developer experience.
developer portfolyo nasil olusturulur?

Portfolyo, gelistirici ozgecimisindir — sadece ne iddia ettiginizi degil, ne yapabildiginizi gosterir. Ne dahil edilmeli: 3-5 kaliteli proje > 20 vasat. Her projede: acik README (problem, cozum, teknoloji yigini, nasil calistirilir), canli demo veya ekran goruntuleri, testlerle temiz kod. Proje cesitliligi: bir full-stack uygulama, bir API/backend projesi, gercek bir problemi cozen biri. Kendi alan adinizi kullanin (isminiz.dev). GitHub profili: yesil katki grafigi, sabitlenmis depolar, profesyonel bio. Blog: ogrendikleriniz hakkinda yazin — derinlik gosterir. Ornek yapi: slogan ile kahraman bolumu, hakkimda, proje gridi, beceriler, blog yazilari, iletisim. Portfolyo sitesi icin teknoloji secimleri: Next.js + Vercel (hizli, ucretsiz barindirma), hatta basit HTML/CSS — icerik framework'ten daha onemli. Gorkem'in gorkemergune.github.io'daki portfolyosu harika bir ornek — projelerini net bir sekilde sergiliyor.
