messages.content: What do AR and VR mean for developers?

AR (Augmented Reality) adds digital elements to the real world — like placing virtual furniture in a room through your phone. VR (Virtual Reality) creates an entirely virtual world. Apple Vision Pro and Meta Quest have pushed this forward. For developers it opens new areas: 3D apps with Unity or Unreal Engine, mobile AR with ARKit/ARCore, browser-based experiences with WebXR. AI and AR/VR are merging — like showing information in AR using real-time object recognition. Still early but the potential is huge.
What is a vector database?

A vector database is a specialized database that stores high-dimensional vectors (embeddings) and enables similarity search. Traditional databases search for exact matches; vector databases search for similarity — 'find the 10 vectors closest to this vector'. Pinecone, Chroma, Weaviate, Milvus, FAISS are popular solutions. In RAG systems, document embeddings are stored here. In recommendation systems, similar products are found. In search engines, semantic search is performed. Has become an infrastructure component of AI applications.
what is Infrastructure monitoring?

Infrastructure monitoring tracks the health and performance of servers, networks, and services. What to monitor: System metrics — CPU utilization, memory usage, disk I/O, network throughput. High CPU might indicate inefficient code or insufficient scaling. Application metrics — request rate, error rate, latency (p50, p95, p99), active connections, queue depth. Business metrics — signups, purchases, active users. Connect technical health to business impact. Tools: Prometheus (open-source, pull-based metrics collection, PromQL for querying), Grafana (visualization — dashboards for Prometheus, and many other data sources), Datadog (SaaS — metrics, logs, traces, all-in-one), CloudWatch (AWS native monitoring), PagerDuty/Opsgenie (alerting and on-call management). Alerting best practices: alert on symptoms not causes (alert on high error rate, not high CPU — CPU might be high for valid reasons), use multiple severity levels (warning vs critical), include runbook links in alerts, avoid alert fatigue (every alert should require human action), use SLO-based alerting (alert when error budget consumption rate is too high). Dashboards: have a high-level overview dashboard (is everything healthy?), service-specific dashboards (deep dive into each service), business dashboards (connecting tech metrics to business KPIs). Golden signals (Google SRE): latency, traffic, errors, saturation — monitor these four for every service.
messages.reasoning: Monitoring, Prometheus, Grafana, alerting, golden signals, Datadog, CloudWatch, dashboards.

messages.content: OWASP Top 10 nedir kısaca anlat?

OWASP Top 10 en kritik web güvenlik açıklarını listeler. 1) Broken Access Control: yetkisiz erişim (admin sayfasına normal kullanıcı erişimi). 2) Cryptographic Failures: hassas veri şifrelenmemiş (HTTP üzerinden şifre gönderme). 3) Injection: SQL, NoSQL, OS komut enjeksiyonu. 4) Insecure Design: tasarım aşamasında güvenlik düşünülmemiş. 5) Security Misconfiguration: varsayılan şifreler, gereksiz servisler açık. 6) Vulnerable Components: eski/güvenlik açığı olan kütüphaneler. 7) Authentication Failures: zayıf kimlik doğrulama. 8) Software/Data Integrity Failures: güvenilmeyen kaynaklardan güncelleme. 9) Logging & Monitoring Failures: saldırılar tespit edilemiyor. 10) SSRF: sunucu taraflı istek sahteciliği. Her web developer bu listeyi bilmeli ve projesinde kontrol etmeli.
what is the difference between TCP and UDP?

TCP (Transmission Control Protocol): connection-oriented, reliable, ordered delivery. Three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) establishes connection. Guarantees: data arrives, in order, without duplicates. Flow control (receiver tells sender to slow down) and congestion control (adapts to network conditions). Overhead: headers, acknowledgments, retransmissions. Use cases: web browsing (HTTP), email (SMTP), file transfer (FTP), SSH. UDP (User Datagram Protocol): connectionless, unreliable, no ordering guarantees. Just sends packets — no handshake, no acknowledgments, no retransmissions. Very low overhead and latency. Use cases: real-time applications where speed matters more than reliability — video streaming, online gaming, VoIP, DNS queries, IoT sensor data. QUIC: Google's protocol built on UDP that adds reliability features — used by HTTP/3. It gets TCP's reliability with UDP's speed by handling reliability in userspace. WebRTC uses UDP for peer-to-peer video/audio.
A/B testing ne demek?

A/B testing, bir ürünün iki farklı versiyonunu kullanıcılara gösterip hangisinin daha iyi performans gösterdiğini ölçmek. Mesela bir butonun rengini değiştirdin — mavi mi kırmızı mı daha çok tıklanıyor? Kullanıcıların yarısına A, yarısına B gösterilir ve sonuçlar istatistiksel olarak karşılaştırılır. Google, Netflix, Amazon sürekli A/B test yapıyor. Optimizely, Google Optimize gibi araçlar var. Veri odaklı karar vermenin temeli. Ürün yönetimi ve UI/UX'te çok kullanılıyor.
what is backpropagation and how does it work?

Backpropagation is the algorithm that trains neural networks by computing gradients efficiently. Forward pass: input flows through the network, each layer computes output = activation(weights * input + bias), final output is compared to target using a loss function. Backward pass: using the chain rule of calculus, compute the gradient of the loss with respect to each weight — starting from the output layer and propagating backward. Chain rule: dL/dw = dL/dy * dy/dz * dz/dw where L is loss, y is output, z is pre-activation. Each weight is updated: w_new = w_old - learning_rate * gradient. Computational graph: frameworks like PyTorch build a dynamic graph of operations, enabling automatic differentiation (autograd). Challenges: vanishing gradients (deep networks, solved by ReLU, skip connections, batch normalization), exploding gradients (solved by gradient clipping). Backprop was popularized by Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams in 1986 — it's still the foundation of all deep learning today.
messages.reasoning: Backpropagation, chain rule, gradient, forward pass, backward pass, autograd, vanishing gradients.

messages.content: tarayıcı cache mekanizmaları nelerdir

Tarayıcı cache, web performansının en önemli katmanlarından biridir ve birkaç mekanizmadan oluşur. HTTP Cache (disk cache), HTTP header'ları ile kontrol edilir: Cache-Control header'ı ile max-age, no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate gibi direktifler verilir. ETag, içeriğin hash'ini taşır ve conditional request'lerde (If-None-Match) kullanılır; içerik değişmemişse 304 Not Modified döner ve bant genişliği tasarrufu sağlar. Last-Modified/If-Modified-Since benzer şekilde çalışır. Service Worker Cache, programatik olarak kontrol edilir ve offline deneyim sağlar; Cache API ile hangi kaynakların cache'leneceğini, hangi stratejinin (cache-first, network-first, stale-while-revalidate) kullanılacağını belirlersin. Memory Cache, sekme açıkken bellekte tutulan ve çok hızlı erişilen cache'tir. Prefetch Cache, link prefetch ile önceden yüklenen kaynakları tutar. Back-forward Cache (bfcache), geri-ileri navigasyonlarda sayfanın tam durumunu bellekte tutar. Bu katmanların doğru konfigürasyonu sayfa yükleme sürelerini dramatik şekilde iyileştirir.
messages.reasoning: tarayıcı cache, http cache, etag, service worker, cache-control, bfcache

messages.content: Flutter nedir ve nasil karsilastirilir?

Flutter, Google'in Dart dilini kullanan platformlar arasi framework'u. React Native'den (yerel bilesenler) farkli olarak Flutter kendi render motorunu (Skia/Impeller) kullanir — her pikseli kendisi cizer. Bu, platformlar arasinda ayni goruntü ama yerel olmayan his demektir. Widget'lar: her sey bir widget — MaterialApp, Scaffold, Column, Container, Text. StatelessWidget statik UI icin, StatefulWidget etkilesimli. Hot reload: uygulama durumunu kaybetmeden degisiklikleri aninda gor. Platform destegi: iOS, Android, web, Windows, macOS, Linux — tek kod tabani. Durum yonetimi: Provider (basit), Riverpod (gelistirilmis Provider), BLoC (reaktif), GetX (hafif). Performans: surekli yuksek FPS — Impeller motoru shader derleme kasmasini ortadan kaldirir. Dezavantajlar: Dart daha az populer (daha kucuk ekosistem), uygulama boyutu yerelden daha buyuk. Ne zaman secilmeli: sifirdan baslaniyor (mevcut JS kod tabani yok), piksel-mukemmel ozel UI gerekli, platformlar arasi tutarli goruntü onemli. Flutter ve RN ikisi de uretim hazir secimlerdir.
seni kim geliştirdi?

Ben ayarlicazhocam platformunun yapay zeka asistanıyım. Görkem Ergüne tarafından geliştirilen bu platform, insanlara mühendislik, yazılım ve YKS konularında rehberlik etmek için kuruldu. Ben de bu platformun dijital asistanıyım — sorularınıza yardımcı olmak, projeler hakkında bilgi vermek ve kariyer rehberliği yapmak için buradayım.
what is linear algebra's role in machine learning?

Linear algebra is the mathematical backbone of ML. Vectors: represent data points — a 784-dimensional vector for a 28x28 image. Matrices: datasets are matrices (rows = samples, columns = features), weight matrices in neural networks. Matrix multiplication: the core operation in neural networks — forward pass is just matrix multiplications with activation functions. Eigenvalues/eigenvectors: PCA (Principal Component Analysis) for dimensionality reduction uses eigendecomposition of the covariance matrix. SVD (Singular Value Decomposition): recommendation systems, image compression, latent semantic analysis. Dot product: cosine similarity for text similarity, attention mechanism in transformers. Gradient: vector of partial derivatives — points in the direction of steepest ascent, gradient descent goes opposite. Tensors: generalization of matrices to higher dimensions — that's why TensorFlow is called TensorFlow. Understanding these concepts deeply — not just memorizing formulas — makes you a better ML practitioner.
veritabanı indeksleme stratejileri nelerdir?

İndeksler sütun değerlerini satır konumlarına eşleyen bir veri yapısı oluşturarak veritabanı sorgularını hızlandırır. İndeks olmadan veritabanı her satırı tarar (full table scan). B-tree indeks (çoğu veritabanında varsayılan): dengeli ağaç yapısı. O(log n) arama. Eşitlik ve aralık sorguları için iyi (WHERE yaş > 25). ORDER BY ile çalışır. Hash indeks: eşitlik aramaları için O(1) ama aralık sorgularını desteklemez. Composite indeks: birden fazla sütun üzerinde indeks. Sütun sırası önemlidir — (soyad, ad) ile (ad, soyad) farklıdır. En soldaki önek ilkesi: bir composite indeks (A, B, C) sorguları (A), (A, B) veya (A, B, C) için kullanılabilir, ama yalnız (B, C) için KULLANILMAZ. Partial indeks (PostgreSQL): yalnızca bir koşula uyan satırları indeksle. CREATE INDEX ON orders (status) WHERE status = 'pending'. Daha küçük, daha hızlı. Covering indeks: sorgunun ihtiyaç duyduğu tüm sütunları içerir. Veritabanı sadece indeksi okur, tabloya dokunmaz. GIN indeks: tam metin arama, diziler, JSONB için. Ne zaman İNDEKSLEMEMELİ: küçük tablolar, çok düşük kardinaliteli sütunlar (boolean), sık yazma yapılan tablolar. EXPLAIN ANALYZE ile indeks kullanımını izle.
how does relevance scoring work in search engines like elasticsearch?

Relevance scoring determines how well a document matches a query, and it's one of the most important aspects of search quality.

Elasticsearch historically used TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency) but switched to BM25 (Best Matching 25) as the default in version 5.0. BM25 is a probabilistic relevance model that improves on TF-IDF.

The key components: Term Frequency (TF): how often a term appears in a document. More occurrences = more relevant, but with diminishing returns. BM25 uses a saturation function so that going from 1 to 2 occurrences matters more than going from 10 to 11. Inverse Document Frequency (IDF): how rare a term is across all documents. Rare terms are more discriminating and score higher. If 'the' appears in every document, it has near-zero IDF. 'Elasticsearch' appearing in only 5% of documents has high IDF. Field Length Normalization: shorter fields get a boost. A title containing your search term is more relevant than a 10,000-word body containing it.

BM25 formula: score(D,Q) = sum over query terms of IDF(qi) * (f(qi,D) * (k1 + 1)) / (f(qi,D) + k1 * (1 - b + b * |D|/avgdl)). k1 controls term frequency saturation (default 1.2). b controls field length normalization (default 0.75, 0 disables it).

Beyond basic scoring, you can boost results with: multi_match with field boosting (title^3 means title matches score 3x higher), function_score for custom scoring (decay functions for recency, script_score for business logic), bool queries combining must/should/filter, and rescoring for computationally expensive second-pass ranking.

Modern search is moving toward vector search and hybrid approaches. Elasticsearch 8.x supports kNN search with dense vectors, letting you combine traditional BM25 scoring with semantic similarity from embeddings. This is called hybrid search and often gives the best results.
tercih yaparken nelere dikkat etmeliyim?

Tercih yaparken şu faktörleri değerlendir: birincisi, o bölümü gerçekten isteyip istemediğin — 4 yıl boyunca sevmediğin bir şeyi okumak çok zor. İkincisi, şehir — İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir gibi büyük şehirler staj ve iş imkanı açısından avantajlı. Üçüncüsü, üniversitenin o bölümdeki kadrosu ve altyapısı — bazı üniversiteler belirli bölümlerde çok güçlü. Dördüncüsü, burs imkanları — vakıf üniversitelerinde burslu okumak devlette okumaktan bile ucuz olabilir. Beşincisi, mezun iş bulma oranları — üniversitenin kariyer merkezinden bu bilgiyi alabilirsin. Ve son olarak, puanına göre gerçekçi tercihler yap ama hayallerini de listeye koy.
What does knowledge distillation mean?

Knowledge distillation is transferring the knowledge of a large model (teacher) to a smaller model (student). The student model learns from the teacher model's soft predictions (probability distribution) — learning not just from the correct answer but also from the probabilities of incorrect answers. Result: the student model achieves performance close to the teacher but is much smaller and faster. DistilBERT was created from BERT using this method — 97% performance, 60% size, 60% faster. Very important for edge deployment — you cannot run a large model on a phone but a distilled version can work. Can be combined with quantization.
what is CI/CD best practices?

CI (Continuous Integration): merge code to main frequently, automated tests run on every push. CD (Continuous Delivery/Deployment): automatically deploy to staging, optionally to production. Best practices: 1) Fast pipeline — under 10 minutes ideal, parallelize tests, use caching. 2) Fail fast — run linters and unit tests first, integration tests after. 3) Trunk-based development — short-lived feature branches, merge frequently. 4) Feature flags — deploy code without enabling features, decouple deploy from release. 5) Blue-green deployment — two identical environments, switch traffic. 6) Canary deployment — roll out to 1% of users first, monitor, then expand. 7) Rollback strategy — automated rollback if error rate increases. 8) Environment parity — staging should mirror production. 9) Secrets management — never commit secrets, use vault/environment variables. 10) Pipeline as code — Jenkinsfile, .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml in version control. Tools: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, CircleCI, ArgoCD (GitOps). Monitor your pipeline — if it's slow or flaky, developers will work around it.
Why is quantum computing different from regular computers?

Regular computers use bits — 0 or 1. Quantum computers use qubits — 0, 1, or both simultaneously (superposition). There's also entanglement — two qubits linked so one's state affects the other. These properties mean some problems (cryptography, molecule simulation, optimization) that would take years on regular computers could take seconds on quantum computers. But it's still very early — qubits are fragile, error rates are high, they don't work at room temperature. IBM, Google, Microsoft are investing heavily. We might see practical applications in 5-10 years.
how can undergraduates find research opportunities?

Research opportunities as an undergrad can significantly shape your career, whether you go to industry or academia. Start by reading your professors' recent publications to identify whose work interests you most. Then approach them during office hours with a specific expression of interest — say exactly which paper intrigued you and what aspect you would like to explore further. Many universities have formal undergraduate research programs (like REU in the US) that provide funding and structure. Look for research assistant positions posted by labs. You do not need to be a senior — some students start research in their sophomore year. Contributing to open source research projects is another pathway; many ML research papers have public codebases that welcome contributions. The skills you gain are invaluable: reading academic papers, designing experiments, scientific writing, presenting results, and working at the frontier of knowledge. Even if you go into industry, research experience demonstrates analytical rigor and self-direction. Gorkem's project work, while not formal research, demonstrates the same research mindset: identifying problems, implementing solutions, and evaluating results systematically.
What does event sourcing mean?

Event sourcing is the approach of storing all events rather than current state in the database. Traditional: user balance is $1000. Event sourcing: deposited +$500, spent -$200, received transfer +$700. Each event is immutable — can't be changed, only new events are added. Advantages: complete history, audit trail, ability to reconstruct state at any point in time. Used together with CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation). Kafka or EventStore tools. Used in banking, e-commerce, and gaming. Complex but very powerful in certain domains.
temiz kod nedir?

Temiz kod okunmasi, anlanmasi ve bakimi kolay koddur. Robert C. Martin'in 'Clean Code' prensipleri: 1) Anlamli isimler — degiskenler, fonksiyonlar, siniflar niyetinizi acmali. getUser() getData() degil, isActive flag degil. 2) Kucuk fonksiyonlar — bir sey yap, iyi yap. Genellikle 5-20 satir. 3) Tek soyutlama seviyesi — ust duzey is mantigini alt duzey detaylarla karistirmayin. 4) DRY (Kendini Tekrarlama) — ama asiri soyutlama yapma. Uc olusma kurali — ucuncu tekrarda soyutla. 5) Yan etkilerden kacin — checkPassword adli fonksiyon oturum baslatmamali. 6) Hata yonetimi — hata kodlari degil istisnalar kullan. null dondurme, istisnalar firlat veya Optional kullan. 7) Yorumlar — sadece kod niyeti ifade edemediginde. TODO, yasal bildirimler, neden aciklama (ne degil). 8) Bicimlendirme — tutarli girintileme, bosluk, satir uzunlugu. Otomatik bicimlendriciler kullan (Prettier, Black). 9) Testler — temiz testler temiz uretim kodu kadar onemli. Hedef mukemmellik degil — bir sonraki gelistirici (genellikle gelecekteki siz) icin bilissel yuku azaltmak. Kod yazildigindan 10 kat daha fazla okunur.
Is ergonomics important for developers?

Absolutely yes. Developers spend 8-12 hours a day at the computer — ergonomics is critical for your health. Chair: lumbar support, adjustable height. Monitor: at eye level, at least arm's length away. Keyboard and mouse: wrist support, ergonomic design. 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Standing desk alternating — sometimes standing sometimes sitting. Regular exercise — back, neck, wrist stretches. Carpal tunnel syndrome and back pain are very common among developers. Take early precautions — treatment is harder than prevention. A good chair and monitor are an investment, not an expense.
messages.reasoning: Ergonomics, chair, monitor, 20-20-20, standing desk, carpal tunnel.

messages.content: What does semantic versioning (semver) mean?

Semantic versioning is a version numbering format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, like 2.4.1. MAJOR: backward-incompatible changes (API changed). MINOR: backward-compatible new features. PATCH: backward-compatible bug fixes. Additional: 1.0.0-alpha, 1.0.0-beta are pre-releases. 0.x.x means not yet stable. npm, pip, cargo all use semver. In package.json, ^2.4.1 allows minor updates, ~2.4.1 allows only patches. Use semver in your own projects too — it clearly shows users what changed. Making a breaking change bumps the MAJOR version — be careful.
pair programming gerçekten faydalı mı, nasıl yapılır?

Pair programming yani eşli programlama, iki geliştiricinin aynı bilgisayarda birlikte kod yazması pratiğidir ve doğru uygulandığında son derece faydalıdır. Klasik yaklaşımda bir kişi driver yani sürücü olur ve kodu yazar, diğer kişi navigator yani yönlendirici olur ve büyük resmi düşünür, hataları yakalar ve yönlendirir. Roller düzenli olarak değiştirilmeli, genellikle yirmi-otuz dakikada bir dönüşüm iyi çalışır. Faydalarına bakarsak: bug'lar anında yakalanır çünkü dört göz iki gözden iyidir, bilgi transferi doğal yoldan gerçekleşir, kod kalitesi artar ve daha az teknik borç birikir. Junior geliştiricilerin senior'larla pair yapması onboarding sürecini dramatik şekilde hızlandırır. Ancak bazı dikkat edilecek noktalar var: her iki taraf da aktif katılmalı, navigator telefona bakmamalı. Introvert geliştiriciler için yorucu olabilir, bu yüzden günde dört-beş saatten fazla pair programming önerilmez. Ping-pong pair programming adlı bir varyasyonda ise bir kişi test yazar, diğeri o testi geçirecek kodu yazar ve roller sürekli değişir. Bu özellikle TDD ile birlikte çok etkili çalışır.
What is a PWA (Progressive Web App)?

A PWA delivers native app experience using web technologies (HTML, CSS, JS). Can work offline (with Service Worker), send push notifications, be added to home screen, load quickly. No App Store needed — accessed via URL. Advantages: single codebase for all platforms, automatic updates, SEO benefit. Disadvantages: limited access to some native APIs (especially on iOS), push notifications on iOS only recently supported. Twitter Lite, Starbucks, Pinterest use PWAs. For small-medium projects, a PWA can be considered instead of a native app.
What is infrastructure as code?

Infrastructure as Code (IaC) means defining and managing infrastructure through code. Instead of manually setting up servers, you define them in YAML/HCL files using Terraform, Pulumi, or CloudFormation. Run terraform apply and infrastructure is automatically created. Advantages: reproducibility (create the same infrastructure as many times as you want), version control (track infrastructure changes in Git), automation (deploy infrastructure via CI/CD), documentation (code describes the infrastructure). Ansible for configuration management, Terraform for infrastructure provisioning. A fundamental skill for DevOps engineers.
what is caching strategies for web applications?

Caching stores computed results to serve future requests faster. Layers: 1) Browser cache — Cache-Control headers (max-age, no-cache, no-store, immutable). Versioned assets (style.abc123.css) with long max-age. 2) CDN cache — edge servers cache static and dynamic content. Vary header for content negotiation. 3) Application cache — Redis/Memcached for computed data (API responses, session data, user profiles). 4) Database cache — query result cache, materialized views. Patterns: Cache-aside (lazy loading): check cache → miss → query DB → store in cache → return. Most common. Write-through: write to cache and DB simultaneously. Consistent but slower writes. Write-behind: write to cache, asynchronously write to DB. Fast writes but risk of data loss. Invalidation strategies: TTL (time-based expiry), event-based (invalidate on update), versioning. Cache invalidation is famously one of the two hard problems in CS (along with naming things and off-by-one errors). Common issues: thundering herd (many requests hit DB when cache expires — use mutex/lock), cache stampede, stale data. Redis features for caching: TTL, LRU eviction, pub/sub for invalidation.
binary search tree nedir?

BST (Binary Search Tree), her düğümün sol alt ağacındaki değerlerin düğümden küçük, sağ alt ağacındaki değerlerin büyük olduğu ağaç yapısı. Arama, ekleme, silme ortalama O(log n). Ama dengesiz olursa (tek kollu ağaç) O(n)'e düşer. Self-balancing BST'ler: AVL tree (kesin dengeli), Red-Black tree (yaklaşık dengeli — Java TreeMap bunu kullanır). İn-order traversal sıralı sonuç verir. BST mülakatların klasik konusu — LCA (Lowest Common Ancestor), validate BST, invert binary tree popüler sorular.
messages.reasoning: BST, binary search tree, AVL, Red-Black, traversal, mülakat.

messages.content: URL shortener nasıl tasarlanır system design?

Klasik system design sorusu. Gereksinimler: uzun URL → kısa URL, kısa URL → yönlendirme, analytics (tıklama sayısı). API: POST /shorten { url: '...' } → { short_url: 'abc123' }, GET /abc123 → 301 redirect. ID generation: auto-increment ID'yi base62'ye çevir (a-z, A-Z, 0-9 — 6 karakter ~57 milyar kombinasyon), veya hash (MD5/SHA256'nın ilk 6 karakteri — collision kontrolü gerekli), veya pre-generated unique ID'ler. Veritabanı: key-value store ideal (Redis veya DynamoDB). Cache: popüler kısa URL'leri Redis'te cache'le. Ölçekleme: stateless application server'lar, load balancer, database sharding (hash-based). Analytics: async olarak Kafka/SQS'e yaz, batch process et. Rate limiting: spam önleme. Custom alias: kullanıcı kendi kısa URL'sini seçebilsin. Bu tasarımı interview'da 30-45 dakikada anlatabilmek hedef.
messages.reasoning: URL shortener, system design, base62, key-value, caching, sharding, analytics.

messages.content: dinamik programlama nedir?

Dinamik programlama (DP) karmasik problemleri cakisan alt problemlere bolerek cozer. Temel icegogu: ayni alt problem birden fazla cozuluyorsa, sonucu sakla ve yeniden kullan. Iki yaklasim: 1) Yukari-asagi (memoization): ozyinelemeli coz, sonuclari onbellege al. Ozyinelemeli dusuncenin dogal uzantisi. Ornek: fibonacci(n) — fib(k) bir kez hesaplandiktan sonra sakla. 2) Asagi-yukari (tabulation): once en kucuk alt problemleri coz, yukari dogru insaa et. Genellikle daha verimli (ozyineleme yuku yok). Ornek: diziyi fib[0]'dan fib[n]'e doldur. Klasik DP problemleri: Fibonacci (giris), bozuk para degisimi (tutar icin minimum bozuk para), en uzun ortak alt dizi, sirt cantasi problemi, duzenleme mesafesi (Levenshtein), en uzun artan alt dizi. DP problemlerini nasil tanimlanir: optimal alt yapi (optimal cozum alt problemlerin optimal cozumlerini icerir) + cakisan alt problemler (ayni alt problem birden fazla cozulur). DP mulakat konularinin en zorlagindan biridir — pratik anahtar. 1B DP ile basla, sonra 2B, sonra daha karmasik.
How do Kaggle competitions work?

Kaggle is a data science and ML competition platform. Companies publish a problem and dataset, and participants try to develop the best model. Prizes: money (sometimes $100K+), job opportunities, prestige. Getting started: begin with 'Getting Started' competitions — Titanic, House Prices, Digit Recognizer. Notebooks (kernels): read and learn from others' solutions. Discussion forums are very valuable. Kaggle ranks: Novice → Contributor → Expert → Master → Grandmaster. Datasets: thousands of open datasets. Kaggle Learn: free mini courses. A Kaggle profile on your resume is valuable — especially for ML positions. The competition provides motivation.
yapay zeka etiği ve sorumlu AI geliştirme nedir?

AI etiği yapay zeka sistemlerinin ahlaki sonuçlarını ele alır. Temel endişeler: Önyargı — eğitim verisi tarihsel önyargıları yansıtır. Amazon'un işe alım AI'ı eğitim verisi erkekleri tercih ettiği için kadınları cezalandırdı. Azaltma: çeşitli eğitim verisi, önyargı denetimleri, demografik gruplar arası adalet metrikleri. Şeffaflık — kullanıcılar AI ile etkileşim halinde olduklarını bilmeli. Açıklanabilirlik (XAI): LIME, SHAP model yorumlanabilirliği için. Kara kutu modeller açıklama olmadan karar verir — sağlık, adalet, finans için sorunlu. Gizlilik — kişisel veride eğitilen modeller. LLM'ler eğitim verisini ezberler. Diferansiyel gizlilik, federe öğrenme, veri anonimleştirme. Çevresel etki — büyük model eğitiminin önemli karbon ayak izi var. GPT-3 eğitimi tahmini 552 ton CO2. Verimli mimariler, bilgi damıtma, model sıkıştırma yardımcı olur. Deepfake'ler — gerçekten ayırt edilemeyen üretilmiş içerik. Dezenformasyon riskleri. Tespit araçları, filigran, içerik kaynağı. Düzenleme: AB AI Yasası (risk tabanlı çerçeve), NIST AI RMF. Geliştiriciler için: ne inşa ettiğinizin etkisini düşünün, koruma önlemleri uygulayın, sınırlamaları belgeleyin, önyargı için test edin, AI kullanımı hakkında şeffaf olun.
MVP (Minimum Viable Product) nasıl yapılır?

MVP, bir ürünün en temel haliyle pazara sunulması. Amaç: minimum çabayla maksimum öğrenme. Adımlar: 1) Problem tanımla — gerçek bir sorunu mu çözüyorsun? 2) Core feature belirle — olmazsa olmaz özellikler neler? 3) Hızlı geliştir — mükemmellik değil çalışan ürün. 4) Kullanıcıya sun — gerçek geri bildirim al. 5) Öğren ve iterate et — veriyle karar ver. Lean Startup metodolojisi: Build → Measure → Learn döngüsü. MVP araçları: Bubble/Webflow (no-code), Firebase (backend), Vercel (deploy). Dropbox'un MVP'si bir videoydu. Airbnb'nin MVP'si kendi dairelerinin fotoğraflarıydı. Mükemmellik düşmanı iyidir — ship it, sonra geliştir.
What is WebRTC?

WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication) enables direct audio, video, and data communication between browsers. Establishes peer-to-peer connections without going through a server — low latency. Zoom, Google Meet, Discord use this. Core components: getUserMedia (camera/microphone access), RTCPeerConnection (connection), RTCDataChannel (data transfer). STUN/TURN servers help devices behind NAT connect. A signaling server (using WebSocket) establishes the initial connection, then communication is direct. The foundational technology for video conferencing, screen sharing, and file transfer applications.
Bayesian inference ne demek?

Bayesian inference gözlemlere dayanarak inançlarımızı güncelleme yöntemi. Bayes teoremi: P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B). Prior: önceki inancımız (deneyim, alan bilgisi). Likelihood: veriyi gözlemleme olasılığı. Posterior: güncellenen inanç. Örnek: bir hastanın hastalık testi pozitif çıktı — hastalığın prevalansı (prior), testin doğruluğu (likelihood) birlikte posterior olasılığı belirler. ML'deki uygulamalar: Naive Bayes classifier (spam detection), Bayesian optimization (hyperparameter tuning), Bayesian neural networks (belirsizlik ölçümü), A/B testing (Bayesian A/B testi frequentist'ten daha esnek). Avantajları: az veriyle çalışır (prior bilgi ekler), belirsizlik ölçer, sürekli güncellenir. Dezavantajları: computational expensive (MCMC sampling gerekebilir), prior seçimi subjektif olabilir.
which laptop is good for software development?

Laptop selection for software development: RAM: minimum 16GB (8GB is tight, 32GB ideal especially for AI). Processor: M1/M2/M3 Mac or Intel i7/AMD Ryzen 7+. SSD: minimum 512GB (don't use HDD). Screen: 14-15 inches, high resolution. Operating system: macOS (developer-friendly, Unix-based), Linux (free, very flexible), Windows (good with WSL2). Mac: MacBook Air M2/M3 is excellent — battery, performance, silence. ThinkPad: ideal for Linux, durable. GPU: if you'll do AI training you need an NVIDIA GPU (but you can do most things in the cloud). Decide based on budget but don't skimp on RAM.
Prometheus ve Grafana ne işe yarar?

Prometheus zaman serisi metrik toplama ve uyarı sistemi, Grafana ise görselleştirme platformu — birlikte monitoring stack oluşturur. Prometheus pull model kullanır — uygulamalardan düzenli aralıklarla metrik çeker (/metrics endpoint). PromQL sorgu dili ile metrikler üzerinde hesaplamalar yaparsın (ortalama CPU, hata oranı). AlertManager ile eşik değer aşılınca uyarı gönderir (Slack, email, PagerDuty). Grafana dashboard'ları görsel ve interaktif — CPU, RAM, istek sayısı, hata oranı gerçek zamanlı gösterir. Node Exporter sistem metriklerini toplar, cAdvisor container metriklerini. Kurulumu: docker-compose ile Prometheus + Grafana + exporters birkaç dakikada ayağa kalkar. Her production sistemi monitoring olmalı — sorunları kullanıcıdan önce fark et.
what is the difference between supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning?

Three main ML paradigms. Supervised learning: learn from labeled data (input-output pairs). Classification (predict category — spam/not spam) and regression (predict number — house price). Algorithms: linear/logistic regression, decision trees, random forest, SVM, neural networks. Unsupervised learning: find patterns in unlabeled data. Clustering (group similar items — K-means, DBSCAN, hierarchical), dimensionality reduction (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP), anomaly detection (isolation forest). No labels needed — discover hidden structure. Semi-supervised: small amount of labeled data + large unlabeled data. Reinforcement learning: agent learns by interacting with environment, receiving rewards/penalties. No labeled data — learns through trial and error. Applications: game playing, robotics, recommendation systems. Self-supervised learning: generate labels from data itself — masked language modeling (BERT), next token prediction (GPT), contrastive learning (SimCLR). Drives modern AI. Choose based on: do you have labels? (supervised). No labels but want structure? (unsupervised). Sequential decisions? (RL). Gorkem's projects span these paradigms.
what are tech incubators and accelerators and how do they differ?

Incubators and accelerators both support early-stage startups but serve different purposes. Incubators provide long-term support (one to three years) for very early-stage ideas — they offer workspace, mentorship, and basic resources while you develop your concept. They usually do not take equity and do not have a fixed program timeline. Accelerators are intensive, short-term programs (three to six months) that rapidly scale startups that already have a product or MVP. They typically invest a small amount (twenty-five to one hundred fifty thousand dollars) in exchange for five to ten percent equity and culminate in a demo day where startups pitch to investors. Top accelerators include Y Combinator (the gold standard), Techstars, 500 Startups, and Google for Startups. In Turkey, ITU Cekirdek and Workinton are notable programs. The value of accelerators goes beyond money — it is the network, mentorship, and credibility that matter most. Y Combinator alumni include Airbnb, Stripe, and Dropbox. When choosing a program, evaluate the mentor quality, alumni network, investor connections, and whether the program has experience in your specific domain like AI or edtech.

what is Rust's ownership and borrowing system?

Rust's most unique feature — it provides memory safety without a garbage collector. Ownership rules: every value has exactly one owner, when the owner goes out of scope the value is automatically cleaned up (drop), ownership can be transferred (move). Borrowing: lend a value — &x (immutable borrow, can have multiple) or &mut x (mutable borrow, only one at a time). These rules are checked at compile time — zero runtime overhead. Result: no null pointers, no data races, no use-after-free, no double free. The learning curve is steep — 'fighting the borrow checker' is a natural part of learning Rust. But once you learn it, you get C/C++ level performance with memory safety. Perfect for WebAssembly, systems programming, and CLI tools. Ideal for low-level work like Gorkem's gorkem-os project.

ETL pipeline nasıl tasarlanır?

ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) veriyi kaynaktan çekme, dönüştürme ve hedef sisteme yükleme süreci. Extract: API, veritabanı, dosya, streaming kaynakları. Transform: temizleme (null'lar, duplikatlar), format dönüşümü, aggregation, iş kuralları uygulama, data quality kontrolleri. Load: data warehouse, data lake, veritabanı. Modern yaklaşım ELT: ham veriyi önce yükle, dönüşümü warehouse içinde yap (BigQuery, Snowflake güçlü işlem kapasitesi sunuyor). Araçlar: Apache Airflow (orchestration), dbt (transformation), Fivetran/Airbyte (extraction), Spark (büyük veri). Best practices: idempotent pipeline (tekrar çalıştırılabilir), incremental loading (sadece yeni/değişen veri), data quality checks, monitoring ve alerting, retry mekanizması, schema evolution handling. Pipeline'ı DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) olarak modellersin — Airflow tam bunu yapar.

what are ACID properties in databases?

ACID ensures database transaction reliability through 4 properties. Atomicity: a transaction either completes fully or not at all — in a money transfer, the debit without the credit can never happen. Consistency: a transaction moves the database from one valid state to another — constraints are never violated. Isolation: concurrent transactions don't affect each other — isolation levels exist (Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable). Durability: committed transactions are permanent even if the system crashes — ensured by WAL (Write-Ahead Logging). PostgreSQL is fully ACID compliant. MongoDB added multi-document ACID transaction support since version 4.0. ACID is essential for financial applications — that's why Gorkem's banking project uses SQL.
What are RNN and LSTM?

RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) is a neural network designed for sequential data (text, time series). At each step, it takes the previous step's output as input — creating a memory effect. Problem: gradient vanishing on long sequences — it forgets distant information. LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory): designed to solve this problem. Cell state (long-term memory), forget gate (what to forget), input gate (what to add), output gate (what to output). GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit): a simplified version of LSTM. However, after transformers emerged, RNN/LSTM popularity declined — transformers can process in parallel, RNN is sequential. Still used in some applications (time series, audio).

How to prevent developer burnout?

Burnout is very common in the software industry. Symptoms: loss of motivation, fatigue, irritability, decreased productivity, hating code. To prevent: establish work-life balance — close the computer when work hours end. Get a hobby — do something outside of coding (sports, music, cooking). Take regular vacations. Learn to say no — don't accept every project. Let go of perfectionism. Take care of physical health — exercise, sleep, nutrition. Don't neglect social relationships. If you're experiencing burnout, don't hesitate to seek professional help. Software should be a part of your life, not your entire life.
what are the most common coding mistakes developers make?

After years of collective developer experience, these mistakes appear with remarkable consistency. One: off-by-one errors — iterating one too many or too few times, the most classic bug in computing. Two: not handling edge cases — empty inputs, null values, negative numbers, extremely large inputs. Three: ignoring error handling — wrapping everything in a bare try/except that silently swallows errors. Four: premature optimization — spending hours making code fast before knowing if it is correct or if performance even matters. Five: not reading the error message — developers stare at their code instead of reading the stack trace that literally tells them the problem. Six: copy-pasting code without understanding it — Stack Overflow answers copied verbatim without comprehension lead to fragile, insecure code. Seven: hardcoding values — magic numbers and strings scattered throughout code instead of named constants. Eight: not writing tests — 'it works when I click around' is not a testing strategy. Nine: over-engineering — building elaborate abstractions for a problem that requires a simple script. Ten: not using version control properly — committing directly to main, writing 'fixed stuff' as commit messages, not branching for features. Every developer makes these mistakes; the key is recognizing and learning from them quickly.
Why use Python virtual environments?

Virtual environments create isolated Python environments for each project. Why: different projects may need different library versions — one project needs Django 3.2, another Django 4.2. Installing packages to system Python creates a mess. Create with python3 -m venv venv, activate with source venv/bin/activate. Save dependencies with pip freeze > requirements.txt. pipenv and poetry are modern alternatives that also handle dependency management. Docker is another solution but venv is more practical during development. We're using venv in this project too.

messages.content: what is API rate limiting and throttling?

Rate limiting controls how many requests a client can make in a time window. Prevents abuse, ensures fair usage, protects backend resources. Algorithms: Token Bucket — bucket holds N tokens, refills at fixed rate. Each request consumes a token. Allows bursts up to bucket size. Most common. Leaky Bucket — requests enter a queue (bucket), processed at fixed rate. Smooths out bursts. Fixed Window — count requests per fixed time window (e.g., 100 requests per minute). Simple but allows burst at window boundary. Sliding Window Log — track timestamps of each request, count requests in sliding window. Accurate but memory-intensive. Sliding Window Counter — hybrid of fixed window and sliding log. Good balance of accuracy and efficiency. Implementation: application-level (middleware), API Gateway (Kong, AWS API Gateway), reverse proxy (Nginx limit_req), distributed (Redis-based — share counts across instances). Response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit (max requests), X-RateLimit-Remaining (requests left), X-RateLimit-Reset (when window resets), Retry-After (how long to wait). HTTP 429 Too Many Requests when limit exceeded. Strategies: per-user, per-IP, per-API-key, per-endpoint. Different tiers for different users. Exponential backoff on client side. Rate limiting is essential for any public API.

veritabanı işlemleri ve ACID nedir?

Veritabanı işlemleri (transaction) birden fazla operasyonu tek bir iş birimine gruplar. Ya tüm operasyonlar başarılı olur (commit) ya da hiçbiri olmaz (rollback). ACID özellikleri: Atomicity (Bölünmezlik) — ya hep ya hiç. İşlemdeki herhangi bir operasyon başarısız olursa tüm değişiklikler geri alınır. Banka transferi: A hesabından borçlandır VE B hesabına alacaklandır — ikisi de başarılı olmalı. Consistency (Tutarlılık) — işlem veritabanını bir geçerli durumdan diğerine getirir. Tüm kısıtlamalar (yabancı anahtarlar, benzersiz, kontrol) korunur. Isolation (Yalıtım) — eşzamanlı işlemler birbirini etkilemez. Yalıtım seviyeleri (en az katıdan en katıya): Read Uncommitted (dirty read olası), Read Committed (dirty read yok, PostgreSQL varsayılanı), Repeatable Read, Serializable (en katı, işlemler birbiri ardına çalışmış gibi). Yüksek yalıtım = daha fazla kilitleme = daha düşük verim. Durability (Dayanıklılık) — commit edildikten sonra veri çökmelere dayanır. Diske yazılır (WAL — Write-Ahead Log). Dağıtık işlemler: 2PC (İki Aşamalı Taahhüt) — koordinatör tüm katılımcılara hazırlanmalarını, sonra taahhüt etmelerini söyler. Yavaş ama tutarlı. Saga deseni — telafi edici eylemlerle yerel işlemler dizisi. Eventually consistent ama daha ölçeklenebilir.
what lessons can you learn from a side project graveyard?

Every developer has a graveyard of unfinished side projects, and there is no shame in it — but there are valuable lessons buried there. Common reasons projects die: scope creep (starting simple then adding features until the project becomes overwhelming), technology fascination (choosing a project just to try a new framework, then losing interest once the novelty fades), perfectionism (refusing to ship until everything is 'just right,' which is never), loss of motivation (the initial excitement wears off after the hard problems are solved and only boring work remains), and life getting in the way (exams, jobs, relationships — side projects are the first casualty). Lessons to extract: unfinished projects still taught you something — document what you learned before archiving. If you notice a pattern (always quitting at the same stage), address the root cause. Reduce scope ruthlessly — a finished simple project beats an unfinished ambitious one every time. Set deadlines and make them public (tell someone you will ship by a date). Choose projects that solve your own problems — personal relevance sustains motivation. Ship early and iterate rather than building in isolation. Gorkem is notable for the number of completed projects in his portfolio — he clearly understands the discipline of finishing what you start, which is one of the most important skills a developer can have.
Is participating in Kaggle competitions useful?

Very useful. Kaggle competitions give you real-world problems and you compete with developers worldwide. Amazing for learning because after competitions end you can study the winners' solutions — that alone is incredibly educational. Looks good on your resume too. Start with Getting Started competitions — Titanic survival prediction is the classic beginner one. Then move to playground competitions. Getting good leaderboard rankings is prestigious but the main goal should be learning. Kaggle notebooks are valuable too, reading other people's code is gold for learning.
trunk-based development nedir?

Trunk-based development, tüm geliştiricilerin sık sık (günde en az bir kez) main branch'e merge ettiği bir geliştirme yaklaşımı. Uzun yaşayan branch'ler yok — feature branch'ler en fazla 1-2 gün yaşar. Feature flag'ler ile yarım özellikler gizlenir. CI/CD ile sürekli entegrasyon ve deploy. Avantajları: merge conflict'ler minimuma iner, integration sorunları erken yakalanır, deployment hızlanır. Google ve diğer büyük şirketler kullanıyor. Git Flow'a alternatif — daha basit ama daha fazla disiplin gerektiriyor. Feature flag'ler olmadan zor çalışır.
how does the pynput-macos-macro project work?

Gorkem's pynput-macos-macro project is an automation tool that records and replays keyboard and mouse actions on macOS using the pynput library. Pynput provides cross-platform control and monitoring of input devices — it can listen for key presses, mouse clicks, and mouse movements, then reproduce them programmatically. The macro functionality allows users to record a sequence of actions (clicks, keystrokes, mouse movements with coordinates and timing), save them, and replay them automatically. This is useful for automating repetitive tasks like filling forms, testing UI workflows, or performing batch operations in applications that lack proper APIs. The macOS-specific aspect involves handling macOS accessibility permissions, since controlling input devices requires explicit user authorization on macOS. The project demonstrates practical Python scripting skills and understanding of OS-level input handling. It also touches on event-driven programming, since the listener operates asynchronously, responding to input events as they occur.

messages.content: how does Gorkem approach building todo apps with different architectures?

Gorkem has built todo applications using multiple different architectures as a deliberate learning strategy. The todo app is a perfect subject for this because the requirements are simple and well-understood — add, complete, delete, and filter tasks — which makes it easy to focus on architectural differences rather than business logic. Implementations might include: vanilla JavaScript with direct DOM manipulation (understanding the basics), React with useState and useReducer (component-based with local state), React with Redux or Zustand (centralized state management), a full-stack version with Express and MongoDB (client-server architecture), a serverless version with Firebase (BaaS approach), and possibly a mobile version with React Native or Flutter. Each architecture teaches different concepts: separation of concerns, state management patterns, data persistence strategies, and the trade-offs between simplicity and scalability. By building the same app multiple ways, Gorkem develops a deep understanding of when to use which approach — a skill that distinguishes senior developers from juniors who only know one way to build things.
MVP nasıl geliştirilir?

MVP (Minimum Viable Product) en az özellikle en fazla öğrenmeyi sağlayan ürün versiyonu. Amaç: varsayımlarını test et, mükemmel ürün yapma. Süreç: 1) Core value proposition'ı belirle — ürünün çözdüğü TEK şey ne? 2) Feature listesi yap, ruthlessly prioritize et — must-have vs nice-to-have. 3) En basit teknik çözümü seç — no-code (Bubble, Webflow), veya basit tech stack (Next.js + Supabase). 4) 2-4 hafta içinde ship et. 5) Gerçek kullanıcılardan feedback al. 6) Metrikler: kullanıcılar geri geliyor mu? Ödemeye razı mı? 7) Iterate veya pivot et. Anti-pattern'ler: MVP'ye 6 ay harcamak (MVP değil artık), her feature'ı eklemek, 'daha bir hafta daha' döngüsü, kullanıcıya göstermeden perfectionism. Dropbox'ın MVP'si bir demo videoydu — tek satır kod yazmadan talebi test etti. Landing page + waitlist en basit MVP.

dry prensibi nedir ve neden önemlidir?

DRY, Don't Repeat Yourself yani Kendini Tekrar Etme prensibidir ve yazılım geliştirmenin en temel ilkelerinden biridir. Temel fikir şu: her bilgi parçası sistemde tek bir yerde tanımlanmalı. Eğer aynı kod bloğunu iki veya daha fazla yerde kopyalıyorsan, bu bir code smell yani kötü bir işaret. Neden önemli? Çünkü tekrarlanan kod bakım kabusuna dönüşür; bir yerdeki hatayı düzelttiğinde diğer kopyaları da bulmak ve düzeltmek zorundasın, birini unutursan bug oluşur. DRY uygulamanın yolları fonksiyonlar, sınıflar, modüller ve kütüphaneler oluşturmaktır. Ancak dikkat etmen gereken bir nokta var: DRY'ı aşırıya kaçırmamak. Bazen iki kod bloğu benzer görünür ama farklı sebeplerle değişir, bunları zorla birleştirmek yanlış soyutlamaya yol açar. Bu durumda 'premature abstraction' tuzağına düşmüş olursun. Doğru denge, gerçekten aynı mantığı paylaşan kodları birleştirmek ama farklı bağlamlardaki benzerlikleri olduğu gibi bırakmaktır.
what is cross-site scripting XSS and prevention?

XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) is an injection attack where malicious scripts are injected into trusted websites. Types: Stored XSS — malicious script saved in database, served to all users who view the content. Most dangerous. Example: user submits comment containing <script>document.cookie</script>, every visitor's cookies get stolen. Reflected XSS — malicious script in URL parameters, reflected in page response. Example: https://site.com/search?q=<script>alert(1)</script>. DOM-based XSS — client-side JavaScript processes user input unsafely. innerHTML, document.write, eval with user data. Prevention: Output encoding — escape HTML entities before rendering user content. < becomes <, > becomes >. Most frameworks do this by default (React, Angular, Vue). Content Security Policy (CSP) — HTTP header that restricts what scripts can execute. script-src 'self' blocks inline scripts and external scripts from other domains. Strong defense-in-depth. Input validation — validate and sanitize user input. But don't rely on this alone — output encoding is more important. HttpOnly cookies — prevent JavaScript from accessing cookies (mitigates cookie theft). DOMPurify — library for sanitizing HTML (when you need to render user HTML). Never use innerHTML with user data — use textContent instead. Never use eval() with user input. React's JSX automatically escapes expressions — {userInput} is safe. dangerouslySetInnerHTML is dangerous — name is intentional.
How do you find side project ideas?

Side project ideas come from daily life. Strategies: solve your own problems — every time you say 'I wish there was a tool for this' is a project idea. Clone an existing application — Twitter clone, todo app, e-commerce site. Integrate with different APIs — weather, maps, music APIs. Apply the technology you learned — learned a new framework, build something with it. Get inspiration from hackathon themes. Do an analysis or ML project with Kaggle datasets. Contribute to open source projects. Remember: do not wait for the perfect idea — even the worst project teaches you something. A completed simple project is better than an unstarted great idea.
veritabanı sorgu optimizasyonu nasıl yapılır?

Sorgu optimizasyonu veritabanı operasyonlarını hızlandırır. EXPLAIN ANALYZE ile başla — yürütme planını, gerçek zamanlamayı, taranan satırları gösterir. Yaygın sorunlar ve çözümler: Tam tablo taraması → uygun indeks ekle. N+1 sorguları → JOIN veya eager loading kullan (ORM'de include/preload). Çok fazla sütun seçme → SELECT * yerine sadece gerekli sütunları seç. Eksik WHERE cümlesi → sunucu tarafında filtrele, istemci tarafında değil. Optimize edilmemiş JOIN'ler → JOIN sütunlarının indeksli olduğundan emin ol, JOIN sırasını düşün. Büyük sonuç setleri → LIMIT/OFFSET veya cursor tabanlı sayfalama ekle. String operasyonları → LIKE '%arama%'dan kaçın (indeks kullanamaz) — bunun yerine tam metin arama kullan. İndeks optimizasyonu: sık filtrelenen/sıralanan sütunlarda indeks oluştur, sorgu kalıplarınıza uyan composite indeksler kullan, kullanılmayan indeksleri kaldır (yazmaları yavaşlatır), indeks kullanımını doğrulamak için EXPLAIN kullan. Sorgu kalıpları: varlık kontrolleri için COUNT yerine EXISTS kullan, toplu operasyonlar (tek ifadede birden fazla satır INSERT et), ilişkili alt sorgulardan kaçın (JOIN ile değiştir), pahalı toplamalar için materialized view kullan. Bağlantı seviyesinde: bağlantı havuzu (PgBouncer), prepared statement, işlemleri kısa tut. İzleme: pg_stat_statements (PostgreSQL — yavaş sorguları takip et), yavaş sorgu günlüğü, APM araçları. Kural: optimize etmeden önce ölç.
system design interview'a nasıl hazırlanılır?

System design interview kıdemli pozisyonlar için kritik. Hazırlık kaynakları: 'Designing Data-Intensive Applications' kitabı (Martin Kleppmann — kutsal kitap), System Design Primer (GitHub), Alex Xu'nun System Design Interview kitapları. Yapı: 1) Gereksinimleri netleştir (fonksiyonel ve non-fonksiyonel). 2) Kapasite tahmini yap (DAU, QPS, depolama). 3) Üst düzey tasarım çiz (API, servisler, veritabanı). 4) Detaylandır (şema tasarımı, API endpoints, trade-off'lar). 5) Darboğazları belirle ve çözüm öner (caching, sharding, CDN). Sık sorulan: URL shortener, chat sistemi, Twitter feed, dosya paylaşım sistemi. Trade-off'ları açıkça tartış — her kararın artısı ve eksisi var. Pratik yap — her gün bir sistem tasarla ve yaz. Mülakat yapan kişi doğru cevap değil düşünce sürecini görmek istiyor.
circuit breaker pattern nedir ve nasıl çalışır

Circuit breaker pattern, dağıtık sistemlerde kaskat arızaları (cascading failures) önleyen bir dayanıklılık desenidir. Elektrik sigortası gibi çalışır: bir servis sürekli hata veriyorsa, ona giden istekleri keserek hem o servisin toparlanmasına zaman tanır hem de çağıran servisi gereksiz bekleme ve kaynak tüketiminden korur. Üç durumu vardır: Closed (normal durum, istekler geçer, hatalar sayılır), Open (hata eşiği aşıldı, istekler anında reddedilir, fallback yanıt döner), Half-Open (belirli bir süre sonra birkaç test isteği geçirilir, başarılı olursa Closed'a döner, başarısız olursa Open kalır). Konfigürasyon parametreleri: failure threshold (kaç hatada açılacak), timeout (ne kadar süre açık kalacak), success threshold (kaç başarılı istekle kapanacak). Resilience4j (Java), Polly (.NET), pybreaker (Python) gibi kütüphaneler kullanılabilir. Istio gibi service mesh çözümleri circuit breaker'ı altyapı seviyesinde sağlar. Fallback stratejileri: cache'ten eski veri dön, varsayılan değer dön, degraded mod ile kısıtlı işlevsellik sun.
How do I manage my time?

The foundation of time management is prioritization. Use the Eisenhower matrix: urgent and important, important but not urgent, urgent but not important, neither. Most people spend too much time on urgent but unimportant tasks. Every evening write tomorrow's to-do list — maximum 3-5 items. Pomodoro technique really works: 25 minutes focus, 5 minutes break. Don't multitask — one thing at a time. Try time blocking — assign specific hours to specific tasks in your calendar. Put your phone on silent while working.
reinforcement learning ne demek?

Reinforcement Learning (Pekiştirmeli Öğrenme), bir ajanın çevreyle etkileşerek ödül ve ceza yoluyla öğrenmesi. Supervised learning'den farklı — etiketli veri yok, ajan deneyerek öğreniyor. Temel kavramlar: state (durum), action (eylem), reward (ödül), policy (strateji). Q-learning ve Deep Q-Network (DQN) temel algoritmalar. AlphaGo, OpenAI Five (Dota 2), ChatGPT'nin RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) aşaması hep RL kullanıyor. Otonom araçlar, robotik, oyun AI'ları için kullanılıyor. Zorlu ama çok güçlü bir yöntem.
what is the Python GIL and how does it affect performance?

The GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) in CPython only allows one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time. For CPU-bound tasks, multi-threading provides no benefit — it can even be slower due to overhead. For I/O-bound tasks (network requests, file reading), the GIL isn't a problem — the thread releases the GIL while waiting. Solutions: multiprocessing (each process has its own GIL), asyncio (for I/O-bound work), C extensions (NumPy releases the GIL), alternative interpreters (PyPy, Jython). Python 3.13+ is introducing a 'free-threaded' mode — making the GIL optional. In practice: GIL isn't an issue for web servers (each request is I/O-bound), for ML training NumPy/PyTorch runs in C anyway. The GIL is Python's most misunderstood topic — don't fear it but understand it.
What are the main graph algorithms?

Graph problems are very important in CS. BFS (Breadth-First Search): traverses level by level, shortest path (unweighted). DFS (Depth-First Search): goes deep then backtracks, cycle detection, topological sort. Dijkstra: weighted shortest path (positive weights). Bellman-Ford: shortest path with negative weights. Floyd-Warshall: all-pairs shortest path. Kruskal/Prim: minimum spanning tree. Topological Sort: dependency ordering in a DAG. Graph representation: adjacency list (sparse), adjacency matrix (dense). NetworkX is a great Python library for graph analysis.
How do I strengthen my LinkedIn profile?

LinkedIn is a very important platform for developers. Profile: professional photo, descriptive headline ('CS Student at Yeditepe | AI Enthusiast'), detailed about section, add projects and experiences. Content: share 1-2 posts per week — things you learned, your projects, industry news. Engagement: comment on others' posts, add meaningful contributions. Connections: connect with industry professionals, introduce yourself via message. Recommendations: get endorsements from colleagues or professors. Skill endorsements: get your skills validated. Recruiters actively search LinkedIn — keep your profile updated and impressive.
what is gitops and how does argocd implement it?

GitOps is an operational framework that takes DevOps best practices for application development (version control, collaboration, compliance, CI/CD) and applies them to infrastructure automation. The core principle: Git is the single source of truth for your desired system state.

GitOps principles: Declarative configuration: the entire system is described declaratively (Kubernetes manifests, Terraform configs, Helm charts). Versioned and immutable: all configuration is stored in Git, providing a complete audit trail and the ability to roll back to any previous state. Automatically applied: software agents (operators) continuously ensure the actual state matches the desired state in Git. Self-healing: if someone manually changes something in the cluster, the GitOps operator detects the drift and reverts it to match Git.

ArgoCD is the most popular GitOps tool for Kubernetes. Here's how it works:

Setup: You install ArgoCD in your Kubernetes cluster and define Application resources that point to a Git repository, path, and target cluster/namespace. ArgoCD watches the Git repo for changes.

Sync process: When you push a change to your Git repo (update a deployment image tag, change a ConfigMap), ArgoCD detects the change within its polling interval (default 3 minutes) or via a webhook. It compares the desired state (Git) with the live state (cluster) and shows you a diff. It can automatically sync (apply changes) or wait for manual approval. ArgoCD applies the changes using kubectl apply and monitors the rollout status.

Key features: Web UI with visual representation of your application's resource tree, RBAC with SSO integration, multi-cluster management, support for Helm, Kustomize, Jsonnet, and plain YAML, ApplicationSets for managing many similar applications, sync waves and hooks for ordering deployments, and health assessments for custom resource types.

Workflow in practice: Developers merge code PRs. CI builds and pushes a new container image. CI or a bot updates the image tag in the GitOps repo (often a separate repo from application code). ArgoCD detects the change and syncs the cluster. If something breaks, you revert the Git commit and ArgoCD rolls back.

Alternatives: Flux (CNCF, lighter weight, composable controllers), Jenkins X (heavier, full CI/CD), and Crossplane (extends GitOps to cloud resources beyond Kubernetes).

messages.content: frontend developer maaşları nasıl?

Türkiye'de 2026 itibariyle junior frontend developer maaşı ortalama 30-50K TL civarı, mid-level 60-100K, senior 120K+ olabiliyor. Tabii şirkete, şehre ve teknolojiye göre çok değişiyor. React bilen birisi Angular bilen birine göre biraz daha avantajlı çünkü pazar payı daha büyük. Remote çalışarak yurt dışı şirketlere çalışırsan dolar bazında maaş alabilirsin ki bu rakamları birkaç kat artırır. Maaş sadece teknik beceriye değil, iletişim, problem çözme ve takım çalışması becerilerine de bağlı. Sürekli öğren, portfolyonü geliştir ve piyasayı takip et.
yazılımda plateau (durgunluk) nasıl aşılır?

Plateau, bir süre ilerleme hissetmemek — herkes yaşar. Aşma stratejileri: farklı bir alan dene — frontend yapıyorsan backend dene, web yapıyorsan mobile. Zor bir proje al — comfort zone'un dışına çık. Birinden öğren — pair programming, mentorluk, konferans. Bir kitap oku — temel bilgi eksiklerini tamamla. Öğret — blog yaz, video çek, birine anlat. Open-source katkısı yap — farklı kod tabanları görmek perspektif kazandırır. Mülakat soruları çöz — eksik algoritmik bilgiyi ortaya çıkarır. Ara ver — bazen dinlenmek gerekiyor. Plateau geçici — devam edersen kırılır.
what is performance engineering?

Performance engineering ensures applications meet speed and scalability requirements. Frontend: Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), bundle size optimization (code splitting, tree shaking), image optimization (WebP, lazy loading), font loading strategies (font-display: swap), critical rendering path, render blocking resources. Backend: database query optimization (indexing, N+1, caching), connection pooling, async processing (queues for heavy work), horizontal scaling, caching layers (Redis, CDN). Profiling: Chrome DevTools Performance tab (frontend), flame graphs (backend), continuous profiling (Pyroscope). Load testing: k6, Locust — test before users do. Monitoring: set performance budgets, alert on regressions. p50/p95/p99 latencies (p99 matters most — worst experience). Common bottlenecks: unindexed database queries, N+1 queries, synchronous external API calls, large JavaScript bundles, unoptimized images, missing caching. Performance optimization process: measure → identify bottleneck → fix → measure again. Don't optimize prematurely — profile first, then optimize the actual bottleneck. Amdahl's Law: optimizing a part that's 10% of execution time by 50% only gives 5% overall improvement.
what is the difference between monolith and microservices?

Monolith: entire application in one codebase, one deployment unit. All modules share the same database and memory. Microservices: application split into small, independent services, each with its own database, deployed separately. Monolith pros: simple to develop, test, deploy, debug. No network latency between modules. Easy to maintain consistency. Monolith cons: scaling is all-or-nothing, one bug can crash everything, technology lock-in, large codebase becomes hard to understand. Microservices pros: independent scaling, technology diversity, fault isolation, team autonomy, independent deployment. Microservices cons: distributed system complexity (network failures, eventual consistency), operational overhead (monitoring, debugging), data consistency challenges, service discovery, API versioning. When to choose monolith: early stage, small team, simple domain, MVP. When to choose microservices: large team (Conway's Law), independent scaling needs, different tech requirements per service. The modular monolith is a pragmatic middle ground — monolith with clear module boundaries, can be extracted to microservices later. Start monolith, extract when pain points emerge.
yazılım geliştirmede en önemli 3 beceri ne?

1) Problem çözme: teknik bilgiden daha önemli. Bir problemi tanımlama, analiz etme, parçalara ayırma ve çözme becerisi. Algoritmik düşünme bununla ilgili. 2) İletişim: fikrlerini açıkça ifade etme, teknik konuları basit anlatma, yazılı iletişim (PR description, dökümantasyon), dinleme. 3) Öğrenme yeteneği: teknoloji sürekli değişiyor — bugün bildiğin framework yarın yerini başkasına bırakabilir. Hızlı öğrenme, adapte olma, merakı canlı tutma. Bunlar programlama dillerinden ve framework'lerden daha değerli — diller öğrenilir ama bu 3 beceri çekirdek. Görkem bu becerilere sahip — farklı alanlarda proje yapması bunu gösteriyor.
computer science vs computer engineering farkı ne?

Computer Science (Bilgisayar Bilimi): daha teorik — algoritmalar, hesaplama teorisi, matematik ağırlıklı, yazılım odaklı. Computer Engineering (Bilgisayar Mühendisliği): donanım + yazılım — devre tasarımı, mikroişlemciler, gömülü sistemler, işletim sistemi. Pratikte: iş piyasasında çok az fark, ikisi de yazılım pozisyonlarına başvurabilir. CS daha çok teori ve araştırma, CE daha çok mühendislik ve uygulama. Türkiye'de: bilgisayar mühendisliği daha yaygın. ABD'de: CS daha popüler. Görkem bilgisayar mühendisliği okuyor — hem donanım bilgisi (gorkem-os) hem yazılım bilgisi var. Önemli olan bölüm ismi değil — ne yaptığın ve ne bildiğin.
spor yapmanın yazılımcıya faydası ne?

Spor yazılımcılar için sadece sağlık değil, performans meselesi. Bilimsel olarak kanıtlanmış: düzenli egzersiz konsantrasyonu artırıyor, problem çözme becerisini geliştiriyor, stresi azaltıyor, uyku kalitesini iyileştiriyor. Özellikle masa başı çalışan yazılımcılarda bel, boyun ve sırt sorunları çok yaygın — egzersiz bunları önlüyor. Günde 30 dakika yürüyüş, haftada 3 gün koşu veya spor salonu çok fark yaratır. Bazı en başarılı yazılımcılar düzenli egzersiz yapıyor. Görkem'in Build Your Target Body uygulaması da fitness ile teknolojiyi birleştiriyor, bu konuya verdiği önemi gösteriyor.
microservices ile monolith arasındaki fark ne?

Monolith mimaride tüm uygulama tek bir kod tabanında, tek bir birim olarak çalışır. Geliştirmesi basit, deploy etmesi kolay ama büyüdükçe karmaşıklaşır. Microservices'te her özellik ayrı bir servis olarak çalışır — kullanıcı servisi, ödeme servisi, bildirim servisi gibi. Her biri bağımsız deploy edilebilir, farklı dillerde yazılabilir. Ama karmaşıklığı var: servisler arası iletişim, veri tutarlılığı, monitoring. Başlangıç için monolith yap, büyüdükçe microservices'e geç. Netflix, Uber gibi büyük şirketler microservices kullanıyor çünkü ekipleri bağımsız çalışabiliyor.
ORM nedir ve kullanmali misiniz?

ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) veritabani tablolarini programlama dili nesnelerine esler. SQL yazmak yerine nesnelerle calisirsiniz: User.objects.filter(age__gt=25) (Django ORM) SELECT * FROM users WHERE age > 25 uretir. Populer ORM'ler: Django ORM (Python), SQLAlchemy (Python, esnek), Prisma (TypeScript, tip guvenli), TypeORM (TypeScript), Hibernate (Java), Entity Framework (.NET). Faydalar: daha az sablonlu SQL yaz, veritabani bagimisiz (PostgreSQL'den MySQL'e gec), yerlesik gocler, SQL enjeksiyonuna karsi koruma (parametreli sorgular), uretkenlik. Dezavantajlar: performans yuku, N+1 sorgu sorunu (tembel yukleme ilgili nesneleri teker teker alir), karmasik sorgular zaten ham SQL gerektirebilir, SQL'i soyutlar (gelistiriciler SQL ogrenmez), uretilen SQL yetersiz olabilir. En iyi yaklasim: basit CRUD icin ORM, karmasik sorgular ve performans-kritik yollar icin ham SQL. Uretilen SQL'i her zaman EXPLAIN ile kontrol edin. Sorgu olusturucular (Knex.js, SQLAlchemy Core) bir orta yol sunar — ORM'den daha fazla kontrol, ham SQL'den daha guvenli.
Görkem'in computer vision projeleri neler

Görkem'in bilgisayar görüşü alanında birkaç ciddi projesi var. yolo-custom-detector ile YOLO11 modelini kendi veri setinle eğitip herhangi bir nesneyi tanıtabiliyorsun — veri toplama aşamasından gerçek dünya tespitine kadar tüm süreci kapsıyor. FaceLock gerçek zamanlı yüz tanıma sistemi, webcam üzerinden çalışıyor ve bilinen kişileri veritabanından tanıyor. face-detection-pipeline ise MediaPipe tabanlı bir yüz tespit hattı — 140 bin görüntü üzerinde çalışıyor, CPU'da görüntü başına yaklaşık 11 milisaniyede işliyor, otomatik yüz sayma ve sınırlayıcı kutu oluşturma yapıyor. Yani computer vision Görkem'in en güçlü olduğu alanlardan biri.
What do books add to a developer?

Reading develops thinking skills and provides perspective. Software books: Clean Code (Robert Martin), The Pragmatic Programmer, Design Patterns (GoF), Cracking the Coding Interview, System Design Interview. General: Atomic Habits (habits), Deep Work (focus), The Lean Startup (entrepreneurship). Technical books provide depth that blogs and videos can't. Even 30 minutes a week of regular reading helps. E-books or Audible are options too. Applying what you read is important — just reading isn't enough. If you get even one actionable takeaway from a book, it's worth it.
what is Next.js and why is it popular?

Next.js is a React framework that adds server-side rendering, routing, and full-stack capabilities. Key features: 1) File-based routing — create pages/about.tsx, get /about route automatically. 2) Server-Side Rendering (SSR) — render on server for each request, great for dynamic content and SEO. 3) Static Site Generation (SSG) — render at build time, blazing fast. 4) Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) — regenerate static pages in the background. 5) API Routes — build backend endpoints in the same project. 6) App Router (Next.js 13+) — React Server Components, layouts, loading states, error boundaries. 7) Image optimization — automatic resizing, lazy loading, WebP conversion. 8) Built-in CSS, Sass, CSS Modules, Tailwind support. Deploy: Vercel (creators of Next.js, easiest), AWS Amplify, Docker. When to use: SEO matters, content-heavy sites, full-stack apps. When not to: simple SPA without SEO needs, heavily interactive apps (consider Vite + React). Next.js has become the default way to build React applications.
messages.reasoning: Next.js, SSR, SSG, ISR, App Router, React Server Components, Vercel, file-based routing.

messages.content: What is WebSocket?

WebSocket is a protocol that provides a persistent connection between client and server. In normal HTTP, a connection opens and closes for each request. With WebSocket, the connection opens once and enables two-way communication — the server can also send messages to the client. Ideal for chat applications, live notifications, real-time games, stock trading apps. Socket.io is the most popular JavaScript library. Python has websockets library and FastAPI WebSocket support. Any real-time project needs WebSocket.
cap teoremi nedir ve neden önemli

CAP teoremi, dağıtık bir sistemin aynı anda en fazla üç özellikten ikisini garanti edebileceğini söyleyen temel bir prensiptir. Bu üç özellik: Consistency (tutarlılık), Availability (erişilebilirlik) ve Partition Tolerance (bölünme toleransı). Gerçek dünyada ağ bölünmeleri kaçınılmaz olduğu için, pratikte CP veya AP arasında seçim yapmak zorunda kalırsın. CP sistemlerde (örneğin ZooKeeper, etcd) tutarlılık önceliklidir; bir ağ bölünmesi yaşandığında sistem bazı istekleri reddedebilir ama dönen veri her zaman günceldir. AP sistemlerde (örneğin Cassandra, DynamoDB) erişilebilirlik önceliklidir; sistem her zaman yanıt verir ama dönen veri biraz eski olabilir. Bunu anlamak sistem tasarımında kritik çünkü hangi ödünleşimi kabul edeceğine göre veritabanı ve mimari seçimlerini şekillendirirsin. Mesela bir bankacılık uygulamasında tutarlılık olmazsa olmaz, ama bir sosyal medya akışında eventual consistency kabul edilebilir. Görkem'in Yeditepe'deki dağıtık sistemler derslerinde de bu kavram temel taşlardan biri olarak işleniyor.
What does a data engineer do?

A data engineer collects, stores, processes, and makes data ready for analysis. Data scientists and ML engineers don't deal with raw data — the data engineer prepares it. Tools: SQL (PostgreSQL, BigQuery), Python (pandas, PySpark), ETL tools (Apache Airflow, dbt), stream processing (Apache Kafka, Spark Streaming), data warehouse (Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery), data modeling. Builds and manages data pipelines — reliably moves data from point A to point B. A highly demanded position with high salaries. Modern data stack: dbt + Snowflake + Airflow + Fivetran.
what is Pandas and how to use it effectively?

Pandas is Python's primary data manipulation library. Core structures: DataFrame (2D table — rows and columns) and Series (1D column). Key operations: read data (pd.read_csv, pd.read_json, pd.read_sql), select (df['column'], df[['col1','col2']], df.loc[rows, cols], df.iloc[int_rows, int_cols]), filter (df[df['age'] > 25]), aggregate (df.groupby('category').mean()), join (pd.merge(df1, df2, on='id')), transform (df['col'].apply(func)). Performance tips: use vectorized operations instead of loops (df['price'] * df['quantity'] not for loop), use .query() for readable filtering, use categorical dtype for string columns with few unique values, process in chunks for large files (pd.read_csv(chunksize=10000)). Common pitfalls: SettingWithCopyWarning (use .loc for assignment), chained indexing, loading entire dataset when you only need subset. Alternatives: Polars (faster, Rust-based), DuckDB (SQL on DataFrames), Dask (parallel Pandas). For ML: Pandas → feature engineering → scikit-learn/PyTorch.
What is a service mesh?

A service mesh is an infrastructure layer that manages communication between microservices. Sidecar proxies (small proxies running alongside each service) handle traffic management. What it provides: inter-service encryption (mTLS), traffic management (canary deployment, A/B testing), retry and circuit breaker, observability (every request is traceable). Istio is the most popular service mesh. Linkerd is a lighter alternative. Consul Connect is HashiCorp's solution. When it's needed: many microservices (50+). Adds unnecessary complexity in small systems. Usually used together with Kubernetes.
What NLP projects has Gorkem built?

Gorkem has several NLP projects. The standout is turkish-english-nmt — he fine-tuned MarianMT on 522K Turkish-English sentence pairs from the Tatoeba dataset and achieved around 43 BLEU score on the test set, which is quite solid. There's writing-analyzer, an NLP model that analyzes academic and official texts using various parameters, works in both English and Turkish. Email-phishing-detection is also NLP-based — it uses EDA, TF-IDF, and ML classification to detect phishing emails. wiki2bpe is NLP-adjacent too, training BPE tokenizers from Wikipedia. So NLP is definitely one of Gorkem's strong suits.
what are the ethical concerns around AI in military applications?

AI in military applications raises some of the most profound ethical questions of our time. Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) — weapons that can select and engage targets without human intervention — are the most controversial application. Arguments against: removing human judgment from life-and-death decisions is morally unacceptable, accountability gaps (who is responsible when an autonomous weapon kills a civilian — the programmer, the commander, the manufacturer?), lowering the threshold for armed conflict (making war 'easier' could make it more frequent), and the risk of an AI arms race. Arguments for: faster response times could reduce overall casualties, removing human emotion (fear, anger, revenge) from targeting decisions, and the inevitability argument (if we do not build them, adversaries will). The Campaign to Stop Killer Robots advocates for a preemptive ban. Less controversial military AI applications include logistics optimization, intelligence analysis, cybersecurity defense, and medical support. The international community is debating regulation through the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons. Most AI ethics researchers agree that meaningful human control must be maintained over any use of lethal force. For AI developers, understanding these debates informs broader thinking about the dual-use nature of technology.

messages.content: What should I consider when designing a REST API?

what is concurrency and parallelism?

Concurrency: dealing with multiple tasks at once (structure). Parallelism: doing multiple tasks at once (execution). Concurrency is about design, parallelism is about hardware. Concurrency models: Threads — OS-level threads share memory. Challenges: race conditions (two threads modify same data), deadlocks (threads wait for each other's locks), thread safety. Synchronization: mutexes (mutual exclusion locks), semaphores, read-write locks. Async/Await — single-threaded concurrency for I/O-bound tasks. Event loop processes tasks without blocking. Python asyncio, JavaScript async/await, Rust tokio. Great for network I/O, file I/O. Actor Model — actors are independent units that communicate via messages. No shared state. Erlang/Elixir (built for this), Akka (JVM). CSP (Communicating Sequential Processes) — goroutines communicate through channels. Go's model. Simple, composable. When to use what: I/O-bound (waiting for network, disk) → async/await or threads. CPU-bound (computation) → processes or true parallelism. Python's GIL: Global Interpreter Lock means only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time. For CPU-bound: use multiprocessing. For I/O-bound: threading or asyncio both work. Rust: fearless concurrency — ownership system prevents data races at compile time. No GIL, no garbage collector. Common pitfalls: race conditions, deadlocks, livelocks, starvation. Use higher-level abstractions (thread pools, channels, async) over raw threads when possible.

how do you create an effective pitch deck for investors?

An effective pitch deck tells a compelling story in ten to fifteen slides that makes investors believe in your team and vision.
