what are React design patterns?

Common React patterns for scalable applications. Compound Components — components that work together sharing implicit state. Like <Select><Option>...</Option></Select>. Uses React.Children or Context internally. Render Props — pass a function as prop that returns JSX. Gives parent control over rendering while child manages logic. Replaced mostly by hooks. Custom Hooks — extract reusable logic into functions starting with 'use'. useLocalStorage, useFetch, useDebounce. The most important pattern in modern React. Higher-Order Components (HOC) — function that takes a component, returns enhanced component. withAuth(Component). Less common now, hooks are preferred. Controlled vs Uncontrolled — controlled: React manages form state (value + onChange). Uncontrolled: DOM manages state (ref). Controlled gives more control, uncontrolled is simpler. Provider Pattern — Context Provider at top of tree, consumers access shared state. Good for themes, auth, locale. Don't use for frequently changing state (causes re-renders). Container/Presentation — separate data logic from UI. Container fetches data, presentation renders it. Still useful conceptually even with hooks. State Reducer Pattern — give consumers control over state transitions: useReducer with an overridable reducer. Composition over inheritance — always in React. Never extend components. Use children prop, render props, or hooks. Gorkem builds React applications — these patterns improve code quality.

what should everyone know about cyberbullying?

Cyberbullying is the use of digital platforms to harass, threaten, or humiliate others, and it has become a serious societal issue, particularly among young people. Unlike traditional bullying, cyberbullying follows victims everywhere through their devices, can be anonymous (emboldening aggressors), spreads rapidly to large audiences, and creates permanent digital records that are nearly impossible to fully delete. Forms include harassment (repeated hostile messages), doxing (revealing private information), impersonation (creating fake accounts to damage reputation), exclusion (deliberately excluding someone from online groups), and image-based abuse (sharing intimate images without consent). The psychological impact is severe: anxiety, depression, social withdrawal, academic decline, and in extreme cases, self-harm. For developers, there is a professional responsibility — if you build platforms where people interact, you must design moderation systems, reporting mechanisms, and safety features. AI can help detect cyberbullying through sentiment analysis and pattern recognition, but human moderators remain essential for nuanced judgments. If you witness cyberbullying, document it, report it, and support the victim. Creating a culture of digital respect starts with individual behavior.

messages.content: how does HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 improve web performance?

HTTP/1.1 limitations: one request per TCP connection (head-of-line blocking), text-based headers (verbose), no server push. HTTP/2 improvements: multiplexing (multiple requests over one connection — no head-of-line blocking at HTTP level), header compression (HPACK — reduces header size by 85-90%), server push (server sends resources before client requests them), binary framing (more efficient parsing). HTTP/2 problem: head-of-line blocking at TCP level — one lost packet blocks all streams. HTTP/3 improvements: built on QUIC (UDP-based) — eliminates TCP head-of-line blocking (streams are independent), faster connection establishment (0-RTT), built-in encryption (TLS 1.3 integrated), better mobile performance (connection migration — survives network changes). Adoption: most major websites support HTTP/2, HTTP/3 adoption growing (Cloudflare, Google). As a developer: use HTTPS (required for HTTP/2+), minimize number of domains (multiplexing makes domain sharding unnecessary), keep resources small (compression matters more than concatenation).
messages.reasoning: HTTP/2, HTTP/3, QUIC, multiplexing, head-of-line blocking, HPACK, server push.

what is the CAP theorem and distributed database trade-offs?

CAP theorem: distributed systems can guarantee at most two of three properties. Consistency — every read returns the most recent write. All nodes see the same data at the same time. Availability — every request gets a response (success or failure). No request is rejected. Partition tolerance — system continues operating despite network partitions (messages lost/delayed between nodes). In distributed systems, network partitions WILL happen. So the real choice is: CP (Consistency + Partition tolerance) — during a partition, system rejects requests to maintain consistency. Examples: HBase, MongoDB (with strong read concern), Zookeeper. AP (Availability + Partition tolerance) — during a partition, system accepts requests but may return stale data. Examples: Cassandra, DynamoDB, CouchDB. PACELC extension: if Partition → choose A or C, Else (normal operation) → choose Latency or Consistency. Most systems choose latency over consistency in normal operation (eventual consistency). Consistency models: Strong consistency (linearizable — most expensive), Sequential consistency, Causal consistency, Eventual consistency (cheapest — all replicas eventually converge). Real-world: most applications use eventual consistency with conflict resolution. Banking needs strong consistency for transfers. Social media feeds tolerate eventual consistency. Choose based on business requirements, not technical preference.
messages.reasoning: CAP theorem, consistency, availability, partition tolerance, PACELC, eventual consistency.

messages.content: veritabanı bağlantı havuzu nedir?

Bağlantı havuzu her istek için yeni bağlantı oluşturmak yerine veritabanı bağlantılarını yeniden kullanır. Her sorgu için TCP bağlantısı + TLS el sıkışma + kimlik doğrulama oluşturmak pahalıdır (~50-100ms). Havuz önceden oluşturulmuş bağlantı setini korur. Bir istek veritabanına ihtiyaç duyduğunda havuzdan bağlantı ödünç alır, kullanır ve geri döner. Havuz yapılandırması: min bağlantılar (boşta bile canlı tut), max bağlantılar (veritabanını bunaltmayı önle), boşta zaman aşımı (çok uzun süre kullanılmayan bağlantıları kapat), bağlantı ömrü (bağlantıları periyodik olarak döndür). PostgreSQL: max_connections varsayılan 100. Her bağlantı ~5-10MB RAM kullanır. 100 uygulama sunucusu her biri 10 bağlantı isterse = 1000 bağlantı — limiti aşar. Çözüm: PgBouncer (harici bağlantı havuzlayıcı) — uygulama ve veritabanı arasında oturur, binlerce uygulama bağlantısını düzinelerce veritabanı bağlantısına çoğaltır. Modlar: transaction (işlemden sonra serbest bırak — en yaygın), session (oturumdan sonra serbest bırak), statement (her ifadeden sonra serbest bırak). Bulut veritabanları: AWS RDS Proxy (yönetilen havuzlama), Supabase dahili olarak PgBouncer kullanır. Üretimde her zaman bağlantı havuzu kullan — en kolay performans kazanımlarından biridir.
what is a message queue and when should you use one?

Message queues decouple producers from consumers — the producer sends a message and doesn't wait for the consumer to process it. Use cases: 1) Async processing — user uploads image, queue a resize job, respond immediately. 2) Load leveling — absorb traffic spikes, process at steady rate. 3) Microservice communication — services communicate without direct coupling. 4) Reliability — if consumer is down, messages wait in queue. Options: RabbitMQ (traditional message broker, routing, exchanges), Apache Kafka (distributed log, high throughput, replay capability), Amazon SQS (managed, simple), Redis Streams (lightweight). Patterns: point-to-point (one consumer per message), pub/sub (multiple consumers get each message). Dead letter queue: store messages that fail processing repeatedly. Ordering: Kafka guarantees order within partitions, SQS FIFO queues. Choose based on: throughput needs, ordering requirements, message size, replay capability.
transfer learning nedir ve neden onemli?

Transfer learning, bir gorevden edinilen bilgiyi baska bir gorevde performansi artirmak icin kullanir. Sifirdan egitmek yerine (milyonlarca goruntu, haftalarca hesaplama), ImageNet uzerinde on-egitilmis bir modelle (ResNet, EfficientNet) basla ve kendi gorevine ince ayar yap. Surec: 1) On-egitilmis modeli yukle. 2) Son siniflandirma katmanini kendi sinif sayina gore degistir. 3) Erken katmanlari dondur (genel ozellikler ogrenmislerdir — kenarlar, dokular). 4) Sadece son birkac katmani kendi veri setinle egit. 5) Istege bagli olarak tum katmanlari ac ve cok dusuk ogrenme orani ile ince ayar yap. Bu ise yarar cunku erken katmanlar gorevler arasi aktarilabilir evrensel ozellikler ogreniyor. NLP'de: BERT, GPT buyuk metin kuplari uzerinde on-egitilir, sonra duygu analizi, NER, soru cevaplama icin ince ayar yapilir. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) parametre verimli bir ince ayar yontemidir — Gorkem bunu LLM fine-tuning projesi icin kullaniyor.
ElasticSearch ne işe yarar?

ElasticSearch, tam metin arama (full-text search) motoru. Büyük miktarda veriyi çok hızlı arayabilirsin — milisaniyeler içinde. Kullanım alanları: site içi arama, log analizi (ELK Stack), gerçek zamanlı analitik, öneri sistemleri. Lucene tabanlı, Java ile yazılmış. JSON formatında veri depolar. Inverted index yapısı ile metin aramayı hızlandırır. Kibana ile görselleştirme yapılır. Logstash ile veri akışı sağlanır. E-ticaret sitelerinde ürün arama, Wikipedia'nın arama özelliği, GitHub'ın kod arama özelliği ElasticSearch benzeri teknolojiler kullanıyor. Büyük veri araması için standart araç.
what is load balancing strategies?

Load balancing distributes traffic across multiple servers to ensure reliability and performance. Algorithms: Round Robin — requests go to servers in order. Simple but doesn't account for server capacity or current load. Weighted Round Robin — assign weights based on server capacity. More powerful servers get more traffic. Least Connections — route to server with fewest active connections. Good when request processing time varies. IP Hash — hash client IP to determine server. Ensures same client always hits same server (sticky sessions). Useful for session-based applications. Least Response Time — route to server with fastest response + fewest connections. Random — simple, surprisingly effective at scale with many servers. Types: Layer 4 (Transport) — routes based on IP and port. Fast, doesn't inspect content. TCP/UDP level. Layer 7 (Application) — routes based on HTTP headers, URL path, cookies. Can make intelligent routing decisions. Slower but more flexible. Tools: Nginx (L7, most popular reverse proxy/LB), HAProxy (L4/L7, high performance), AWS ALB (L7, managed), AWS NLB (L4, managed), Traefik (cloud-native, auto-discovery). Health checks: periodically verify backend servers are healthy. Remove unhealthy servers from rotation, re-add when recovered. Session persistence: sticky sessions (always route to same server), or store sessions externally (Redis) for true stateless load balancing.
messages.reasoning: Load balancing, round robin, least connections, Layer 4, Layer 7, Nginx, HAProxy, ALB.

messages.content: performans muhendisligi nasil yapilir?

Performans muhendisligi uygulamalarin hiz ve olceklenebilirlik gereksinimlerini karsilamasini saglar. Frontend: Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), paket boyutu optimizasyonu (kod bolme, agac sallama), goruntu optimizasyonu (WebP, tembel yukleme), font yukleme stratejileri (font-display: swap), kritik render yolu. Backend: veritabani sorgu optimizasyonu (indeksleme, N+1, onbellekleme), baglanti havuzu, asenkron isleme (agir is icin kuyruklar), yatay olcekleme, onbellekleme katmanlari (Redis, CDN). Profilleme: Chrome DevTools Performance sekmesi (frontend), alev grafikleri (backend), surekli profilleme (Pyroscope). Yuk testi: k6, Locust — kullanicilardan once test edin. Izleme: performans butceleri belirleyin, gerilemeler konusunda uyarin. p50/p95/p99 gecikmeleri (p99 en cok onemli — en kotu deneyim). Yaygin darbogazlar: indekslenmemis veritabani sorgulari, N+1 sorgulari, senkron dis API cagrilari, buyuk JavaScript paketleri, optimize edilmemis goruntüler, eksik onbellekleme. Performans optimizasyonu sureci: olc → darbogazI belirle → duzelt → tekrar olc. Erken optimize etmeyin — once profil cikarin, sonra gercek darbogazI optimize edin.
Is web scraping legal?

The legality of web scraping is a complex topic. Generally: scraping publicly accessible data is usually legal, but respecting a site's robots.txt file and terms of service is important. Things to watch out for: apply rate limiting (be kind to the server), do not collect personal data (GDPR), commercial use may have additional restrictions, some sites prohibit scraping in their terms of service. If an API is available, use the API — it is more reliable and legal. Sites like LinkedIn and Facebook are aggressive against scraping. Academic research and personal use are generally less problematic. In this project, we used APIs — the safest approach.
canary release ve feature flag arasındaki fark ne

Canary release ve feature flag, kontrollü dağıtım stratejileridir ama farklı seviyede çalışır. Canary release, altyapı seviyesinde çalışır: yeni sürümü trafğin küçük bir yüzdesine (örneğin yüzde 5) yönlendirirsin, metrikleri izlersin (hata oranı, latency, iş metrikleri), sorun yoksa kademeli olarak trafik yüzdesini artırırsın (yüzde 5 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100). Sorun varsa trafığı eski sürüme geri yönlendirirsin. Uygulanması: Istio, Nginx, AWS ALB weighted target groups, Argo Rollouts. Feature flag ise uygulama seviyesinde çalışır: kodda bir koşul ile yeni özelliği açıp kapatırsın. Dağıtım ve release ayrılır: kodu deploy edersin ama özellik kapalıdır, hazır olduğunda belirli kullanıcılara veya gruplara açarsın. LaunchDarkly, Unleash, Flagsmith gibi araçlar kullanılabilir. A/B testing için de kullanılır: farklı kullanıcı segmentlerine farklı deneyimler sunarsın. İkisi birlikte kullanılabilir: canary release ile altyapıyı kademeli dağıtırsın, feature flag ile yeni özellikleri kontrollü açarsın. Kill switch olarak: production'da sorun çıkarsa flag'ı kapatarak anında geri alırsın.
messages.reasoning: canary release, feature flag, kademeli dağıtım, a/b testing, launchdarkly

messages.content: how should you communicate with investors effectively?

Communicating with investors is a distinct skill from communicating with engineers or users. Speak in terms of business outcomes, not technical features — instead of 'we use a transformer-based architecture with LoRA fine-tuning,' say 'our technology enables personalized AI tutoring at one-tenth the cost of human tutors.' Be honest about risks and challenges; sophisticated investors see through hype and respect founders who acknowledge uncertainty while presenting clear mitigation strategies. Send concise, regular investor updates (monthly) even before fundraising — this builds relationships and demonstrates accountability. When pitching, control the narrative by anticipating tough questions and preparing data-driven answers. Key metrics investors care about: growth rate, retention, unit economics (LTV/CAC ratio), burn rate, and runway. Follow up promptly after meetings. If an investor passes, ask why — the feedback is valuable. Build relationships before you need money; the best time to meet investors is when you are not fundraising. Get warm introductions whenever possible — cold emails have very low response rates. Gorkem's ability to clearly document and present his technical projects demonstrates the communication skills that translate directly to investor relations.
what is data lake vs data warehouse?

Data warehouse: structured, processed data optimized for analytics queries. Schema-on-write — define schema before loading data. Star/snowflake schema. SQL-based querying. Examples: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks SQL. Use for: business intelligence, reporting, dashboards, SQL analytics. Data lake: raw, unprocessed data in any format (structured, semi-structured, unstructured). Schema-on-read — interpret data when querying. Store everything — logs, images, JSON, CSV, Parquet. Examples: S3, Azure Data Lake, Google Cloud Storage. Use for: machine learning (need raw data), data exploration, archive/compliance. Data lakehouse (modern approach): combines benefits of both. Structured tables on top of data lake storage. Delta Lake (Databricks), Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi. ACID transactions on data lake files. Query with SQL and ML tools. Modern data architecture: sources → ingestion (Fivetran, Airbyte) → data lake (S3, raw storage) → transformation (Spark, dbt) → data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) → BI (Looker, Metabase). Or with lakehouse: sources → ingestion → lakehouse (Delta Lake on S3) → both SQL analytics and ML. Key formats: Parquet (columnar, compressed — standard for analytics), ORC (Hadoop ecosystem), Avro (row-based, schema evolution), Delta (Parquet + transaction log). For most companies: start with a data warehouse (Snowflake/BigQuery). Add data lake when you have ML needs or need to store raw data economically.
miniature-transformers-from-scratch projesi hakkında bilgi ver

miniature-transformers-from-scratch, transformer mimarisini sıfırdan implemente eden bir proje. 'Attention Is All You Need' makalesindeki mimariyi Python ve PyTorch ile kodlamak. Multi-head attention, positional encoding, feed-forward layers, layer normalization — tüm bileşenler sıfırdan yazılıyor. Bu projeyi yapmak transformer'ları gerçekten anlamak demek. ChatGPT, BERT, T5 hepsi transformer tabanlı — bu mimariyi anlamak modern AI'ı anlamak demek. Görkem'in teorik bilgiyi pratiğe dökmesinin en güzel örneği.
exception handling neden önemli?

Exception handling (hata yönetimi) programınızın beklenmeyen durumlarda çökmesini önler. Python'da try-except blokları kullanılır. Mesela dosya okuyorsun ama dosya yok — FileNotFoundError. API'ye istek atıyorsun ama internet yok — ConnectionError. Kullanıcı sayı yerine harf girdi — ValueError. Bu hataları yakalamaz isen program çöker ve kullanıcı kötü bir deneyim yaşar. Ama her yere try-except koymak da doğru değil — sadece gerçekten oluşabilecek hataları yakala. Genel Exception yakalamak kötü pratik çünkü gerçek hataları gizler.
how is AI model bias detected and reduced?

Model bias is when a model discriminates against certain groups. Examples: a credit model discriminating against women, facial recognition having lower accuracy on darker-skinned people. Detection: measure performance separately for different demographic groups, confusion matrix for each group. Fairness metrics: demographic parity, equalized odds, calibration. Reduction: Pre-processing — data balancing, increasing representation. In-processing — training with fairness constraints. Post-processing — adjusting prediction thresholds by group. Tools: AI Fairness 360 (IBM), Fairlearn (Microsoft). Bias can't be completely eliminated but can be reduced. It should be considered from the data collection stage onward. This is a fundamental topic of ethical AI development.
what is site reliability best practices?

SRE best practices for production systems. Runbooks: step-by-step guides for common incidents. 'Database CPU high' → check slow queries → identify N+1 → optimize or restart. Reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR). On-call: rotation schedule, escalation policies, incident response procedures. Avoid alert fatigue — every alert should be actionable. PagerDuty, Opsgenie for alert management. Postmortem culture: after every incident, write a blameless postmortem. What happened? Timeline of events. Root cause analysis (5 Whys). Action items to prevent recurrence. Share learnings across the organization. Capacity planning: monitor growth trends, provision ahead of demand. Load test regularly to know your limits. Game days: practice failure scenarios. Simulate database failover, region outage, dependency failure. Build muscle memory for incident response. Chaos engineering: intentionally inject failures to find weaknesses. Chaos Monkey (random instance termination), Gremlin (controlled chaos experiments). Start small (kill one instance) and gradually increase blast radius. SLO-based alerting: alert when error budget is being consumed too fast, not on individual metrics. This reduces noise and focuses on user impact. Progressive rollouts: deploy to canary → small percentage → full rollout with automatic rollback on metric degradation.
saga pattern ne?

Saga pattern, microservice'lerde dağıtık transaction yönetimi. Monolith'te tek veritabanı transaction'ı var ama microservice'lerde her servisin kendi DB'si var — tek transaction olmaz. Saga: her servis kendi transaction'ını yapar ve başarısızlıkta compensating transaction (geri alma) çalıştırır. İki tür: Choreography (her servis event yayınlar, diğerleri dinler — basit ama takibi zor) ve Orchestration (merkezi bir orkestratör koordine eder — daha kontrollü). Örnek: sipariş → stok azalt → ödeme al. Ödeme başarısız → stok geri artır → sipariş iptal. Temporal, Camunda orkestrasyon araçları.
knowledge distillation ne demek?

Knowledge distillation, büyük bir modelin (teacher) bilgisini küçük bir modele (student) aktarma. Teacher modelin soft predictions'larını (olasılık dağılımı) student model öğrenir — sadece doğru cevaptan değil, yanlış cevapların olasılıklarından da öğreniyor. Sonuç: student model teacher'a yakın performans gösterir ama çok daha küçük ve hızlı. BERT'ten DistilBERT bu yöntemle oluşturuldu — %97 performans, %60 boyut, %60 daha hızlı. Edge deployment için çok önemli — büyük modeli telefonda çalıştıramazsın ama distilled versiyonu çalışabilir. Quantization ile birlikte kullanılabilir.
messages.reasoning: Knowledge distillation, teacher-student, soft predictions, DistilBERT, edge.

messages.content: what is event sourcing?

Event sourcing stores all changes as a sequence of events rather than just current state. Instead of UPDATE account SET balance=90, you store Event: {type: 'MoneyWithdrawn', amount: 10, timestamp: '...'}. Current state is derived by replaying all events. Benefits: complete audit trail (every change recorded), temporal queries (what was the state at any point in time?), debugging (replay events to reproduce bugs), event-driven integration (other services react to events). Challenges: event store grows forever (use snapshots for performance), eventual consistency, schema evolution (events are immutable — how to handle format changes?), steep learning curve. Implementation: event store (EventStoreDB, or PostgreSQL with events table), projections (materialize current state from events for queries), snapshots (periodically save current state to avoid replaying all events). When to use: financial systems (audit trail critical), complex domains where understanding history matters, systems requiring undo/replay. When not to: simple CRUD applications, when eventual consistency is unacceptable. Often combined with CQRS — separate read and write models.
what is data structures for interviews?

Essential data structures for technical interviews. Array — contiguous memory, O(1) access by index, O(n) insert/delete. Use for: sequential data, when you need fast random access. Linked List — nodes with pointers. O(1) insert/delete at known position, O(n) search. Use for: frequent insertions/deletions, implementing stacks/queues. Stack — LIFO. push/pop O(1). Use for: undo operations, parsing expressions, DFS, call stack. Queue — FIFO. enqueue/dequeue O(1). Use for: BFS, task scheduling, buffering. Hash Table — key-value pairs, O(1) average lookup/insert/delete. Use for: counting, caching, deduplication. Collisions: chaining or open addressing. Tree — hierarchical data. Binary Search Tree: O(log n) search/insert/delete (balanced). Use for: sorted data, range queries. AVL/Red-Black for guaranteed balance. Heap — complete binary tree, O(1) find min/max, O(log n) insert/extract. Use for: priority queues, top-K problems, scheduling. Graph — nodes and edges. Represented as adjacency list or matrix. BFS (shortest path unweighted), DFS (cycle detection, topological sort). Use for: networks, shortest path, dependency resolution. Trie — prefix tree. O(m) lookup where m is key length. Use for: autocomplete, spell checking, IP routing. Know the time complexity, use cases, and trade-offs for each. Practice implementing them from scratch.
fine-tuning ile prompt engineering arasındaki fark ne?

İkisi de LLM'i belirli bir göreve uyarlamak için kullanılır ama çok farklı yaklaşımlar. Prompt engineering: modeli değiştirmezsin, sadece iyi yazılmış talimatlarla yönlendirirsin. Hızlı, ucuz, ama sınırlı. Few-shot, chain-of-thought prompting teknikleri var. Fine-tuning: modelin ağırlıklarını kendi verinle güncellersin. Daha güçlü, kalıcı ama veri ve hesaplama gerektirir. LoRA gibi verimli fine-tuning yöntemleri var. Genelde önce prompt engineering dene, yetmezse fine-tuning yap. Bu projede de fine-tuning yapıyoruz — kendi verilerimizle modeli eğitiyoruz.
what is documentation-driven development?

Documentation-driven development writes documentation before or alongside code, not after. Approaches: README-driven development — write the README first. Describe what the project does, how to use it, API examples. This forces you to think about the user experience before implementation. Design docs — write a design document before starting significant features. Problem statement, proposed solution, alternatives considered, trade-offs. Get feedback before writing code. API documentation first — design the API contract (OpenAPI spec) before implementation. Frontend and backend teams can work in parallel. Architecture Decision Records (ADR) — document why specific technical decisions were made. Template: title, status, context (why), decision (what), consequences (trade-offs). Create an ADR for every significant technical decision. Benefits: forces clear thinking (writing reveals unclear thinking), enables parallel work (teams agree on interfaces), creates institutional knowledge (why was this designed this way?), reduces misunderstanding (everyone reads the same spec). Tools: Docusaurus, Mintlify, GitBook for docs sites. Mermaid for diagrams in Markdown. Draw.io for architecture diagrams. RFC process for larger changes. Common mistake: writing docs after code — docs become stale because updating is tedious. Write docs as you code. Treat docs as part of the deliverable, not an afterthought.
merhaba nasılsın
Merhaba! Ben bir yapay zeka olduğum için tam olarak 'nasılım' diyemem ama hazırım ve enerjiyim yerinde diyelim. Sen nasılsın, bugün sana nasıl yardımcı olabilirim?
what's the difference between metrics, logs, and traces and how do they complement each other?

These are the three pillars of observability, and understanding how they work together is key to building debuggable systems.

Metrics are numerical values measured over time. They tell you WHAT is happening. Examples: request rate (requests/second), error rate (5xx responses/total), latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99), CPU and memory usage, queue depth, active connections. Metrics are cheap to collect and store (a counter takes the same space regardless of traffic), great for alerting and dashboards, and ideal for understanding trends and anomalies. Tools: Prometheus, Datadog, CloudWatch, InfluxDB. Metric types: counters (only go up), gauges (go up and down), histograms (distribution of values), summaries (pre-calculated quantiles).

Logs are timestamped, immutable records of discrete events. They tell you WHY something happened. Examples: 'User 123 failed login: invalid password', 'Order 456 payment declined: insufficient funds', stack traces, audit records. Logs provide rich context but are expensive at scale (can be gigabytes per hour). Structured logging (JSON format) makes them queryable. Tools: ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana), Loki, Splunk, Datadog Logs.

Traces are the end-to-end journey of a request across services. They tell you WHERE time is spent. A trace shows you that a request took 2 seconds total: 50ms in the API gateway, 1.5s in the payment service (which spent 1.4s calling a third-party API), and 200ms in the notification service. Traces are essential for microservices debugging. Tools: Jaeger, Zipkin, Tempo, Datadog APM.

How they complement each other: Metrics alert you that p99 latency spiked to 5 seconds. You look at traces to find which service is slow. You find the payment service is taking 4 seconds. You look at logs from the payment service and discover the third-party payment API is timing out. This metrics -> traces -> logs flow is the standard debugging workflow.

The modern approach is correlation: embed trace IDs in logs so you can jump from a log line to its full trace, use exemplars to link metrics to specific traces, and derive metrics from traces (called RED metrics: Rate, Errors, Duration).

messages.content: When should you use microservices vs monolith?

Monolith: a single large application. Advantages: simple to develop, simple to deploy, simple to debug, ideal for starting out. Disadvantages: grows more complex over time, a single error can crash everything, hard to scale. Microservices: small independent services. Advantages: independent deployment, technology diversity, scalability, fault isolation. Disadvantages: distributed system complexity, network latency, data consistency challenges, operational overhead (requires Kubernetes, monitoring). Rule: start with a monolith, transition to microservices as needed. 'Premature microservices' is one of the most common architectural mistakes. Netflix and Amazon moved to micro, but they started small.
what is Git bisect and how to use it?

Git bisect uses binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug. Process: 1) git bisect start. 2) git bisect bad (current commit has the bug). 3) git bisect good v1.0 (this commit was working). 4) Git checks out a middle commit — you test it. 5) git bisect good or git bisect bad based on your test. 6) Repeat until Git identifies the exact commit. 7) git bisect reset when done. With N commits, it finds the bug in log2(N) steps — 1000 commits needs only ~10 tests. Automated bisect: git bisect run ./test.sh — provide a script that exits 0 for good, non-zero for bad. Git runs it automatically. Example: git bisect run pytest tests/test_login.py — automatically finds which commit broke login tests. Tips: write regression tests for bugs — then bisect can be fully automated. Works best with small, atomic commits (another reason for clean commit history). This is one of Git's most underused but powerful features. Every developer should know about it.
Why are women underrepresented in tech?

There are many historical and cultural factors. Computer science was actually female-dominated early on — Ada Lovelace, Grace Hopper were pioneers. But from the 1980s, personal computers were marketed as 'boy toys' and the balance shifted. Societal pressures, lack of role models, workplace culture issues all contribute. But things are changing — communities like Women Who Code, Django Girls, She Codes are growing. Tech companies run diversity programs. If you're in this field or want to enter it, know that technology is for everyone and diverse teams build better products.
kaggle yarışmaları nasıl çalışır?

Kaggle, veri bilimi ve ML yarışma platformu. Şirketler problem ve veri seti yayınlar, katılımcılar en iyi modeli geliştirmeye çalışır. Ödüller: para (bazen $100K+), iş fırsatı, prestij. Başlangıç: 'Getting Started' yarışmalarıyla — Titanic, House Prices, Digit Recognizer. Notebook'lar (kernel): diğerlerinin çözümlerini oku ve öğren. Discussion forumları çok değerli. Kaggle rank: Novice → Contributor → Expert → Master → Grandmaster. Dataset'ler: binlerce açık veri seti. Kaggle Learn: ücretsiz mini kurslar. CV'de Kaggle profili değerli — özellikle ML pozisyonları için. Rekabet motivasyon sağlıyor.

messages.content: 12-Factor App metodolojisi nedir?

12-Factor App, modern, olceklenebilir web uygulamalari insaa etmek icin bir metodolojidir. 1) Kod tabani — surüm kontrolunde izlenen tek kod tabani, bircok dagitim. 2) Bagimliliklar — acikca beyan et ve izole et (requirements.txt, package.json). 3) Yapilandirma — ortam degiskenlerinde sakla, kodda degil. 4) Yedekleme servisleri — veritabanlari, kuyruklar, onbellekleri ekli kaynaklar olarak ele al (yapilandirma ile degistir). 5) Insaa, surum, calisma — asamalari kesinlikle ayir. 6) Islemler — durumsuz islemler olarak yurut (durumu veritabaninda/onbellekte sakla). 7) Port baglama — servisleri port baglama ile dis dunya paylas (bagimsiz). 8) Eszamanlilik — islem modeli araciligiyla olcekle (yatay olcekleme). 9) Elden cikarilabilirlik — hizli baslatma, zarifce kapatma (SIGTERM ele al). 10) Gelistirme/uretim esitligi — ortamlari mumkun oldugunca benzer tut. 11) Loglar — olay akimlari olarak ele al (stdout'a yaz, platformun toplamasina izin ver). 12) Yonetici islemleri — tek seferlik islemler olarak calistir (gocler, betikler). Bu ilkeler konteynerlestirilmis, bulut yerel dagitimlarla mukemmel uyum saglar.

how does the trolley problem apply to autonomous vehicles?

The trolley problem — a thought experiment about sacrificing one person to save many — becomes practically relevant with autonomous vehicles that must make split-second decisions in unavoidable accident scenarios. Should a self-driving car swerve to avoid hitting five pedestrians if it means hitting one? Should it prioritize the safety of its passengers over pedestrians? Should it consider the age, number, or social status of potential victims? The MIT Moral Machine experiment surveyed millions of people across cultures and found significant cultural variation in these preferences — undermining the idea of a universal ethical framework for programming these decisions. In practice, several important nuances emerge: these dilemmatic scenarios are extremely rare compared to the everyday safety benefits of autonomous driving (which could prevent most of the 1.35 million annual global traffic deaths caused by human error), engineering solutions (better braking, sensing, and avoidance) can reduce the frequency of unavoidable situations, and the real ethical question may not be 'how should the car choose?' but 'is it ethical NOT to deploy safer autonomous vehicles because of rare edge cases?' The legal and regulatory frameworks for these decisions are still being developed worldwide.

consistent hashing nedir ve neden dağıtık sistemlerde kullanılır

Consistent hashing, dağıtık sistemlerde verilerin düğümler arasında dağıtımını ve düğüm eklenip çıkarıldığında minimum veri taşınmasını sağlayan bir hash tekniğidir. Normal hash ile mod alarak dağıtım yapsan (hash(key) % N), bir düğüm eklenip N değiştiğinde neredeyse tüm anahtarların yeri değişir. Consistent hashing'de düğümler ve anahtarlar bir hash ring üzerinde konumlandırılır. Bir anahtar, ring üzerinde saat yönünde kendisinden sonraki ilk düğüme atanır. Bir düğüm eklendiğinde sadece komşu düğümün anahtarlarının bir kısmı taşınır, diğer düğümler etkilenmez. Bir düğüm çıktığında sadece o düğümün anahtarları saat yönündeki sonraki düğüme taşınır. Virtual nodes (vnodes) ile düğümlerin ring üzerinde birden fazla noktada temsil edilmesi sağlanır, böylece yük daha dengeli dağıtılır. Kullanım alanları: Amazon DynamoDB (key dağıtımı), Apache Cassandra (partition dağıtımı), Memcached ve Redis cluster (key routing), CDN'lerde (içerik dağıtımı), load balancer'larda (session affinity). Consistent hashing, ölçeklenebilir dağıtık sistemlerin temel yapı taşlarından biridir.

one epoch = one forward pass and one backward pass of all the training examples
batch size = the number of training examples in one forward/backward pass. The higher the batch size, the more memory space you'll need.
number of iterations =  number of passes, each pass using [batch size] number of examples. To be clear, one pass = one forward pass + one backward pass (we do not count the forward pass and backward pass as two different passes).

For example: if you have 1000 training examples, and your batch size is 500, then it will take 2 iterations to complete 1 epoch.

can you compare write-through and write-back caching and when to use each?

Sure! These are two fundamental caching strategies with very different tradeoffs.

Write-through caching writes data to both the cache and the backing store synchronously. When a write comes in, the cache updates itself and immediately writes to the database before returning success. Pros: the cache and database are always consistent, data durability is guaranteed since it's persisted immediately, and reads are fast since the cache is always warm after writes. Cons: write latency is higher because you wait for the database write, and every write hits the database even if the data is overwritten again quickly.

Write-back (write-behind) caching writes data to the cache first and returns success immediately. The data is asynchronously flushed to the database later, often in batches. Pros: write latency is very low since you only write to memory, batching reduces database load significantly, and it absorbs write spikes gracefully. Cons: risk of data loss if the cache node crashes before flushing, complexity in handling flush failures, potential consistency issues, and harder to debug.

When to use write-through: financial systems where data loss is unacceptable, systems with moderate write loads, scenarios where read-after-write consistency is required, and when you have fast database writes (like SSDs).

When to use write-back: high-write-throughput systems like gaming leaderboards or analytics, systems where some data loss is tolerable, write-heavy workloads that would overwhelm the database, and CPU/GPU caches (hardware actually uses write-back by default).

There's also write-around: writes go directly to the database, bypassing the cache. The cache is only populated on reads. This prevents cache pollution from data that's written but rarely read. Many real systems combine strategies. For instance, you might use write-through for critical data and write-back for metrics.

messages.content: what is the NMT neural machine translation project?

Gorkem's NMT project implements neural machine translation — translating text between languages using deep learning. Architecture: typically encoder-decoder with attention. Encoder: processes source language sentence into a context representation. Decoder: generates target language sentence word by word using the context. Attention mechanism: allows the decoder to focus on relevant parts of the source sentence for each output word — critical breakthrough (Bahdanau attention, then self-attention in Transformers). Training: parallel corpus (sentence pairs in both languages), teacher forcing (feed correct previous word during training), beam search (explore multiple translation candidates during inference). Evaluation: BLEU score (compare generated translation against human references). Challenges: rare words (subword tokenization — BPE, SentencePiece), long sentences, domain-specific vocabulary. Modern NMT uses Transformer architecture exclusively — pre-trained multilingual models (mBART, NLLB) achieve remarkable quality. This project connects with Gorkem's wiki2bpe tokenization work and his interest in NLP.

Recommendation: try free resources first (freeCodeCamp, The Odin Project, CS50). If you can't progress on your own, consider a bootcamp. When choosing a bootcamp: research graduate outcomes, check the curriculum, see if there's a free trial. In Turkey: Patika.dev and Kodluyoruz are free alternatives.

messages.content: Kubernetes nedir?

Kubernetes (kısaca K8s), container'ları yöneten bir orkestrasyon platformu. Docker container'lar oluşturur, Kubernetes bu container'ları büyük ölçekte yönetir — otomatik ölçekleme, yük dengeleme, kendini iyileştirme, rolling update yapıyor. Bir container çökerse otomatik yenisini başlatır. 100-1000 container'ı yönetmen gerektiğinde Docker tek başına yetmez, K8s devreye girer. Google tarafından geliştirildi, şimdi açık kaynak. Cloud native uygulamaların standart altyapısı haline geldi. AWS EKS, Google GKE, Azure AKS yönetilen K8s hizmetleri sunuyor. Karmaşık ama öğrenmeye değer.
REST API ile GraphQL arasındaki fark ne?

REST API'de her kaynak için ayrı endpoint var — /users, /posts, /comments gibi. Her istekte sabit bir veri yapısı döner, fazla veya eksik veri alabilirsin. GraphQL'de tek bir endpoint var ve tam olarak istediğin veriyi sorarsın — ne fazla ne eksik. REST daha basit ve yaygın, GraphQL daha esnek ama öğrenme eğrisi var. Küçük projeler için REST yeterli, büyük ve karmaşık veri yapılarında GraphQL avantajlı. Facebook GraphQL'i icat etti çünkü mobil uygulamalarında veri transferini optimize etmek istedi. İkisini de bilmek iyi ama önce REST'i öğren.
What are the most useful habits for a developer?

Daily habits: 1) Write code for at least 30 minutes every day — consistency is key. 2) Read technical articles — Hacker News, Dev.to, Medium. 3) Commit to GitHub — the contribution graph is motivating. 4) Learn something new — even something small. Weekly: 5) Solve one LeetCode problem. 6) Make progress on your own project. 7) Write or read a blog post. Monthly: 8) Try a new technology. 9) Read a chapter from a book. 10) Contribute to the community. Do not start all these habits at once — add them one by one. Habit stacking — attach a new habit to an existing one. Gorkem probably produces so many projects through similar habits.
what does Jamstack mean?

Jamstack: JavaScript, APIs, Markup. A modern web development approach — static pages + API calls. Traditional: the server generates the page on every request. Jamstack: pages are generated at build time (static), dynamic data is fetched via APIs. Advantages: very fast (served from CDN), secure (no server, small attack surface), scalable, cheap hosting. Tools: Next.js, Gatsby, Astro, Hugo, 11ty. Headless CMS: Strapi, Contentful, Sanity — content management through APIs. Hosting: Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages. Ideal for blogs, portfolios, landing pages, e-commerce. Gorkem's portfolio was likely built with the Jamstack approach.
veritabanı türleri nelerdir?

İki ana kategori var: SQL (ilişkisel) ve NoSQL (ilişkisel olmayan). SQL veritabanları tablolar halinde veri saklar, satırlar ve sütunlar var. Örneğin PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite. Yapılandırılmış veri için ideal — kullanıcı bilgileri, siparişler gibi. NoSQL ise farklı modeller sunuyor: document-based (MongoDB), key-value (Redis), graph (Neo4j), column-family (Cassandra). Yapılandırılmamış veya hızlı değişen veriler için iyi. Hangisini seçeceğin projeye bağlı. Görkem'in study-tracker uygulaması SQLite kullanıyor mesela — lokal, hafif ve offline çalışıyor. Başlangıç için SQL öğren, sonra ihtiyacına göre NoSQL'e geç.
git branching stratejileri neler?

Git'te birçok branching stratejisi var. Git Flow: main, develop, feature, release, hotfix branch'leri — büyük ekipler için yapılandırılmış. GitHub Flow: main + feature branch'ler, PR ile merge — basit ve etkili. Trunk-based development: herkes main branch'e kısa yaşayan branch'lerle sık sık merge eder — CI/CD ile uyumlu. GitLab Flow: GitHub Flow + environment branch'ler (staging, production). Başlangıçta GitHub Flow önerilir — basit ama etkili. Feature branch oluştur, PR aç, code review al, merge et. Commit mesajları anlamlı olsun. Branch isimlerinde convention kullan: feature/login, bugfix/auth-error.

messages.content: are deepfakes dangerous and how to detect them?

Deepfakes use AI to generate realistic fake video and audio. Dangers: disinformation (fake videos of politicians), fraud (imitating a CEO's voice to authorize wire transfers — real cases exist), reputation damage, privacy violations. Detection methods: facial detail inconsistencies (eye blinking patterns, teeth, hairline), lighting and shadow mismatches, metadata analysis, frequency analysis (GANs leave specific frequency patterns). Tools: Microsoft Video Authenticator, Deepware Scanner, Intel FakeCatcher. Prevention: media literacy (don't believe everything you see), source verification, digital signatures and watermark technologies (C2PA standard). Positive uses also exist: film industry (aging/de-aging effects), education, voice synthesis for disabled individuals. This is a dual-use technology — it can be used for good or bad. The important thing is awareness and critical thinking. As AI becomes more capable, the ability to verify authenticity becomes increasingly important.
What does the attention mechanism do?

The attention mechanism lets the model assign different weights to different positions in a sequence. In classic RNNs, information was lost in long sentences — the beginning was forgotten. Attention solved this. In 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired,' the word 'it' should attend to 'cat.' In self-attention, every word looks at all other words. Multi-head attention learns different attention patterns in parallel. This is the foundation of the transformer architecture. Works with the Query, Key, Value trio — Query is what you're looking for, Key is what you have, Value is what you give. Gorkem's miniature-transformers project implements this in detail.
what is TDD test-driven development?

TDD follows a strict cycle: Red → Green → Refactor. 1) Red: write a failing test first — it should describe the desired behavior. 2) Green: write the minimum code to make the test pass — no more. 3) Refactor: clean up the code while keeping tests green. Benefits: forces you to think about requirements before coding, produces testable code by design, serves as documentation, gives confidence to refactor, catches regressions immediately. Critics say: slower initial development, some tests are trivial, can lead to testing implementation details, not practical for all situations (UI, exploratory coding). Pragmatic TDD: use it for complex logic, algorithms, and critical paths. Skip it for simple getters/setters and UI prototyping. BDD (Behavior-Driven Development) extends TDD: write tests in natural language — 'Given a logged-in user, When they click delete, Then the item is removed.' Tools: Cucumber, Behave. TDD is a discipline — it gets easier with practice.
What is the sorting-visualizer project?

sorting-visualizer is an application that visualizes sorting algorithms. It shows step-by-step animations of how bubble sort, quick sort, merge sort, insertion sort work. A great educational tool — understanding algorithms visually is much more effective. Likely built with JavaScript and canvas or React. Such projects demonstrate both programming ability and skill in creating educational materials. Algorithms are a cornerstone of the CS curriculum.

Gorkem Ergüne approaches projects with a learn-by-building philosophy. His GitHub portfolio (gorkemergune.github.io) shows diverse, real-world projects spanning AI/ML, systems programming, and web development. Each project targets a specific skill gap — miniature-transformers implements transformer architecture from scratch to understand attention mechanisms, not just use them. wiki2bpe builds tokenization from ground up rather than depending on libraries. gorkem-os tackles operating system fundamentals — process management, memory allocation, file systems. The phishing-domain-detection project combines ML with practical security. yolo-custom-detector applies computer vision to real-world object detection. banking-management-system covers full-stack development with proper architecture. facelock brings together computer vision and security. How do I save a trained model in PyTorch?

Guzel soru! Yazilim toplulugundan edindigim bilgiye gore, Found this page on their github repo:

Recommended approach for saving a model
There are two main approaches for serializing and restoring a model.
The first (recommended) saves and loads only the model parameters:
torch.save(the_model.state_dict(), PATH)

Then later:
the_model = TheModelClass(*args, **kwargs)
the_model.load_state_dict(torch.load(PATH))


The second saves and loads the entire model:
torch.save(the_model, PATH)

Then later:
the_model = torch.load(PATH)

However in this case, the serialized data is bound to the specific classes and the exact directory structure used, so it can break in various ways when used in other projects, or after some serious refactors.


See also: Save and Load the Model section from the official PyTorch tutorials.

messages.content: What is the worldcup-bpe-tokenizer project?

worldcup-bpe-tokenizer trains a BPE tokenizer on World Cup data. An interesting dataset choice — NLP work with football data. This project provides both sports data analysis and tokenization practice. Similar logic to Gorkem's wiki2bpe project — tokenizer training from different data sources. Training domain-specific tokenizers can yield better results than general tokenizers in certain applications. A creative project idea — combining interests with technology.
what is the difference between monorepo tools?

Monorepo tools manage multiple packages/projects in a single repository. Turborepo: fast builds with intelligent caching (local + remote). Understands task dependencies. Minimal config. Best for: TypeScript/JavaScript projects, teams wanting simplicity. Nx: full-featured monorepo toolkit. Computation caching, affected detection (only test what changed), dependency graph visualization, code generators, plugins for React, Angular, Node. Best for: large teams, enterprise. Lerna: original JS monorepo tool. Manages versioning and publishing of npm packages. Now maintained by Nx team. Best for: npm package publishing. Bazel: Google's build system. Supports any language. Hermetic builds (reproducible), distributed caching, remote execution. Steep learning curve. Best for: large polyglot monorepos (Google has everything in one repo). Rush: Microsoft's monorepo tool. Phantom dependency detection, incremental builds. Best for: large npm monorepos. pnpm workspaces: simple monorepo support with pnpm's efficient node_modules structure (symlinks, not copies). Best for: lightweight monorepo without extra tools. Start with Turborepo (simplest) or Nx (most features) for JavaScript projects.
distributed cache nasıl tasarlanır?

Distributed cache veriye hızlı erişim için bellekte saklama — veritabanı yükünü azaltır. Redis ve Memcached en popüler seçenekler. Redis: veri yapıları (string, hash, list, set, sorted set), persistence, pub/sub, Lua scripting. Memcached: basit key-value, multi-threaded, daha az özellik ama basit kullanım. Cache stratejileri: Cache-Aside (lazy loading — önce cache'e bak, yoksa DB'den çek ve cache'e yaz), Write-Through (her yazma hem cache'e hem DB'ye), Write-Behind (cache'e yaz, async olarak DB'ye yaz), Read-Through (cache otomatik DB'den doldurur). Eviction policies: LRU (en az kullanılan), LFU (en az sıklıkta kullanılan), TTL (süre dolunca sil). Cache invalidation: 'bilgisayar biliminde en zor iki şey: cache invalidation ve isimlendirme.' Thundering herd problemi: aynı anda çok sayıda istek cache miss yaşarsa DB'ye hücum eder — mutex ile önle.
how do you validate a startup idea before building anything?

Idea validation is the single most important step before writing any code. The goal is to determine whether real people have the problem you want to solve and whether they would pay for a solution. Start with the 'mom test' — ask potential customers about their existing problems and behaviors, not whether they would use your hypothetical product (people lie to be polite, but they cannot fake past behavior). Conduct at least twenty customer interviews to identify patterns. Look for existing solutions and understand why they fall short — if nobody else is trying to solve this problem, ask yourself whether the problem even exists. Create a landing page describing your solution and measure sign-up conversions to gauge interest quantitatively. Test willingness to pay by offering pre-orders or letters of intent. Search for the problem in communities like Reddit, Twitter, and Stack Overflow to see if people are actively complaining about it. Only after validating demand should you start building. Many startups fail not because of bad execution but because they build something nobody wants. Gorkem's ayarlicazhocam project started from a validated need — students genuinely need accessible AI-powered guidance.
What's the difference between data science and AI?

Data science and AI are related but different fields. Data science focuses on extracting meaning from data — statistics, data analysis, visualization, business intelligence. A data scientist says 'analyze last year's sales data and predict next quarter.' AI focuses on developing machines' ability to think and make decisions like humans — image recognition, NLP, autonomous systems. ML is a subset of AI. In practice they overlap a lot — a data scientist uses ML models, an AI engineer does data analysis. Gorkem's projects lean more toward AI but he has data science skills too.
what are Python metaclasses and when to use them?

A metaclass is a class of a class — it controls how classes are created. Normal classes create objects, metaclasses create classes. type is the default metaclass in Python. Use cases: ORM frameworks (Django Model Field definitions work through metaclasses), API validation, singleton pattern, enforcing abstract base classes. Write your own with class Meta(type) and override __new__ or __init_subclass__. In practice, most projects don't need metaclasses — decorators and class decorators are usually sufficient. 'If you don't know whether you need metaclasses, you don't need them' — Tim Peters. But if you're building a framework or creating a DSL, they're a very powerful tool.
What is the difference between compiled and interpreted languages?

Compiled languages: source code is compiled into machine code, then executed. Fast execution but platform-dependent. C, C++, Rust, Go. Interpreted languages: source code is executed line by line through an interpreter. Slower but portable and flexible. Python, JavaScript, Ruby. JIT (Just-In-Time) compilation: compiles at runtime — combines the advantages of both. Java (JVM), JavaScript (V8), Python (PyPy). Bytecode: an intermediate format — source code → bytecode → runs on a VM. Python .pyc files are bytecode. In practice: if speed is critical, go compiled (C, Rust); if you want rapid development, go interpreted (Python, JS). Modern trend: JIT is closing the gap between the two.
how do you prepare a pitch deck?

A pitch deck is a presentation explaining your startup to investors — typically 10-15 slides. Structure (Guy Kawasaki 10/20/30 rule — 10 slides, 20 minutes, 30 point font): 1) Problem — a real, significant pain point. 2) Solution — your approach. 3) Market size — TAM (Total Addressable Market), SAM (Serviceable), SOM (Obtainable). 4) Business model — how will you make money? 5) Traction — user count, revenue, growth rate. 6) Team — why you? Show relevant experience. 7) Competition — your advantage over competitors (don't say 'no competition'). 8) Financial projections — 3-5 year outlook. 9) The ask — how much investment, what will you use it for? 10) Contact information. Design: clean, minimal text, lots of visuals, consistent colors. Storytelling: problem → solution → why now → why us flow. The best pitch decks tell a compelling story that makes investors feel the urgency and opportunity.
state management karşılaştırması: Redux vs Zustand vs Jotai?

State management React'te en tartışmalı konulardan biri. Redux: en eski ve en kapsamlı — büyük ekipler ve karmaşık state için. Redux Toolkit boilerplate'i azalttı ama yine de öğrenmesi zor. Zustand: minimal, hook-based — create ile store oluştur, component'te useStore ile kullan. Boilerplate yok, öğrenmesi kolay, küçük-orta projeler için ideal. Jotai: atom-based (Recoil benzeri) — her state parçası bağımsız atom, bottom-up yaklaşım. Fine-grained re-render — sadece değişen atom'u kullanan component yeniden render olur. React Query/TanStack Query: server state için — API verisi cache'leme, senkronizasyon, invalidation. Tavsiye: çoğu proje için Zustand + React Query yeterli. Redux sadece çok karmaşık client state varsa. Context API basit global state için (tema, dil) ama sık değişen state için performans sorunu yaratır.
messages.reasoning: State management, Redux, Zustand, Jotai, React Query, atom, boilerplate.

messages.content: event-driven architecture nedir?

Event-driven architecture (EDA) bilesenlerin dogrudan cagri yerine olaylar araciligiyla iletisim kurdugu bir tasarim kalipsidir. Olay, olan bir seyin kaydidir — 'siparis verildi', 'odeme islendi', 'kullanici kaydoldu'. Bilesenler: olay ureticileri, olay aracisi (Kafka, EventBridge, RabbitMQ), olay tuketicileri. Kalipler: olay bildirimi (hafif, sadece bir sey oldugunu isaret eder), olay tasimali durum aktarimi (olay gereken tum verileri icerir), event sourcing (tum olaylari gercek kaynak olarak sakla, yeniden oynayarak durumu yeniden olustur). Faydalar: gevsek baglanti, olceklenebilirlik, genisletilebilirlik (ureticileri degistirmeden yeni tuketiciler ekle). Zorluklar: nihai tutarlilik, hata ayiklama zor (dagitik izleme gerekli), olay siralama, yinelenen islem (idempotency). CQRS genellikle event sourcing ile eslestirilir — ayri okuma ve yazma modelleri. Netflix, Uber, LinkedIn kullanir.
What should be on a developer's CV?

A software CV should be short and concise — 1-2 pages. Must have: contact info (email, GitHub, LinkedIn, portfolio URL), education, technical skills (languages, frameworks, tools), projects (what you did, what tech you used, what was the outcome), work experience (if any), certifications, hackathons, open-source contributions. Must not have: photo (debatable), irrelevant work experience, subjective skill levels ('5/5 Python'), long paragraphs. Make it ATS (Applicant Tracking System) friendly — simple format, PDF, keywords. Overleaf has LaTeX CV templates. Customize your CV for each position.
Gorkem'in facelock projesi nasil calisir detayli?

Gorkem'in facelock projesi yuz tanima ile kimlik dogrulama sistemi. Calisma prensibi: 1) Yuz tespiti (face detection): Haar Cascade, MTCNN veya dlib ile goruntude yuzleri bul. 2) Yuz hizalama (alignment): gozlerin pozisyonuna gore yuzu normalize et. 3) Ozellik cikarma (embedding): FaceNet, ArcFace veya dlib'in 128-boyutlu face encoding'i ile yuzu vektore donustur. 4) Karsilastirma: yeni yuz vektorunu kayitli vektorlerle karsilastir (kosinüs benzerligi veya Oklid mesafesi). Esik degerin altindaysa eslesme var. Guvenlik konulari: fotograf ile aldatma (canlilik tespiti gerekli — goz kirpma, kafa hareketi), aydinlatma kosullari, maske ile tanima. Python'da face_recognition kutuphanesi kolay bir baslangic. Gercek dunya uygulamalari: telefon kilidi, bina giris sistemi, devam takibi. Bu proje bilgisayarli gorme ve guvenlik kesisiminde Gorkem'in becerilerini sergilemektedir.
ACID properties ne demek veritabanında?

ACID veritabanı transaction'larının güvenilirliğini sağlayan 4 özellik. Atomicity: transaction ya tamamen tamamlanır ya hiç — para transferinde bir hesaptan düştü ama diğerine eklenmedi olmaz. Consistency: transaction veritabanını geçerli bir durumdan başka geçerli bir duruma taşır — kurallar (constraints) ihlal edilmez. Isolation: eş zamanlı transaction'lar birbirini etkilemez — isolation levels var (Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable). Durability: commit edilen transaction kalıcıdır, sistem çökse bile — WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) ile sağlanır. PostgreSQL tam ACID uyumlu. MongoDB 4.0'dan itibaren multi-document ACID transaction desteği ekledi. Finansal uygulamalarda ACID olmazsa olmaz — Görkem'in banking projesinde bu yüzden SQL kullanılıyor.
messages.reasoning: ACID, Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability, transaction, WAL.

messages.content: imposter syndrome nasıl aşılır?

Imposter syndrome — kendini yeterli görmeme, 'bir gün beni yakalayacaklar' hissi — yazılımcılarda çok yaygın (%70'e kadar). Nedenleri: sürekli yeni teknoloji (hep geride hissedersin), sosyal medyada herkes uzman görünür, alan çok geniş (her şeyi bilmek imkansız). Çözümler: 'brag document' tut — başarılarını, çözdüğün problemleri, öğrendiklerini yaz, kötü hissettiğinde oku. 6 ay önceki halinle kıyasla, başkalarıyla değil. Bilmemek normal — kıdemli geliştiriciler de her gün Google'lıyor. Başkalarına mentor ol — öğretince ne kadar bildiğini fark edersin. Topluluğa katıl — herkesin benzer zorluklar yaşadığını gör. 'Fake it till you make it' yerine 'learn it as you do it'. Görkem'in 30+ projesi bile imposter syndrome hissettirmeyebilir — ama o projeler onun yetkinliğinin kanıtı.
what is data pipelines and ETL?

Data pipelines move and transform data from source to destination. ETL (Extract, Transform, Load): traditional approach. Extract data from sources (databases, APIs, files) → Transform (clean, normalize, aggregate, join) → Load into data warehouse. Transformation happens before loading. ELT (Extract, Load, Transform): modern approach. Extract → Load raw data into warehouse → Transform using warehouse compute power (SQL with dbt). Warehouses are powerful enough — let them handle transformation. Batch vs Streaming: batch (process data in scheduled intervals — hourly, daily), streaming (process data in real-time as it arrives). Tools: Batch: Apache Airflow (workflow orchestration, DAGs in Python), Luigi (simpler, LinkedIn), dbt (SQL transformations in warehouse), Apache Spark (distributed data processing). Streaming: Apache Kafka (event streaming platform), Apache Flink (stream processing), Kafka Streams (library, no separate cluster), AWS Kinesis (managed streaming). Orchestration: Airflow (most popular, Python DAGs), Prefect (modern, Pythonic), Dagster (software-defined assets, great testing), Temporal (workflow engine, code-first). Modern data stack: Fivetran/Airbyte (extract & load) → Snowflake/BigQuery (warehouse) → dbt (transform) → Looker/Metabase (BI). Data quality: Great Expectations (data validation framework), dbt tests, monitoring data freshness and completeness. Start simple — a Python script on a cron job is a valid data pipeline for small scale.
What are the tokenization methods in NLP?

Tokenization is the process of breaking text into pieces. Methods: Word-level — split by spaces, simple but large vocabulary, unknown words are a problem. Character-level — each letter is a token, small vocabulary but creates long sequences. Subword — most popular: BPE (Byte Pair Encoding) merges frequently occurring character pairs, WordPiece (used by BERT), SentencePiece (language-independent, used by T5), Unigram (probability-based). Hugging Face tokenizers library is very fast — written in Rust. Gorkem's wiki2bpe project trains a BPE tokenizer. Tokenization choice directly affects model performance.
messages.reasoning: Tokenization, BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece, Unigram, wiki2bpe.

messages.content: what is design patterns in software engineering?

Design patterns are reusable solutions to common software design problems. Creational patterns — how objects are created: Singleton (one instance, global access — use sparingly, hard to test), Factory Method (create objects without specifying exact class — useful for plugins), Builder (construct complex objects step by step — good for objects with many optional parameters), Dependency Injection (pass dependencies instead of creating them — testability, loose coupling). Structural patterns — how objects compose: Adapter (convert interface to match what client expects — wrap old API), Decorator (add behavior without modifying class — middleware in Express), Proxy (control access to object — caching proxy, auth proxy), Facade (simplify complex subsystem — provide simple interface). Behavioral patterns — how objects interact: Observer (pub/sub — event emitters, React state updates), Strategy (swap algorithms at runtime — different sorting or payment methods), Command (encapsulate action as object — undo/redo), Iterator (traverse collection without exposing structure — for...of loops). Most important for modern development: Dependency Injection, Observer, Strategy, Factory, Decorator. Anti-pattern: overusing patterns. Don't force patterns where simple code works. Patterns should emerge from need, not be applied preemptively. Gorkem's projects use patterns naturally — MVC in web apps, Observer in event systems.
What's a good model for translation?

For translation, one of the most popular models on Hugging Face is google-t5/t5-small. It has over 27,245,112 downloads which shows how widely it's used by the community. You can easily load it using the transformers library with just a few lines of code. Gorkem actually works with Hugging Face too — his wiki2bpe project publishes tokenizers to the Hub. If you're new to this, start with the model card on Hugging Face to understand what it does and how to use it.

messages.content: how do you handle secrets in applications?

Secrets management is critical — leaked credentials cause data breaches. Never do: hardcode secrets in code, commit to git, store in plaintext config files, log secrets, share via chat/email. Environment variables: basic approach — store in .env (never committed), inject at deployment. Better than hardcoding but still plaintext on disk. Secret managers: AWS Secrets Manager, Google Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault — encrypted storage, access control, rotation, audit logs. Best approach. Kubernetes: Secrets resource (base64 encoded, not encrypted by default — use Sealed Secrets, external-secrets-operator, or SOPS for encryption). CI/CD: GitHub Actions Secrets, GitLab CI Variables — encrypted, injected at runtime. Rotation: regularly rotate secrets, automate with secret manager. If compromised: revoke immediately, rotate, audit access logs. Git history: if secret was ever committed, it's in history forever. Use git-secrets (pre-commit hook to prevent), BFG Repo-Cleaner or git filter-branch to remove from history. .env.example: commit a template with dummy values for documentation. Gorkem's projects should always use environment variables at minimum, secret managers for production.
what is compiler design basics?

Compilers translate source code into machine code. Phases: Lexical analysis (tokenization) — convert character stream into tokens. 'int x = 5;' → [INT, IDENTIFIER(x), EQUALS, NUMBER(5), SEMICOLON]. Tools: regex patterns, finite automata. Lex/Flex. Syntax analysis (parsing) — convert tokens into Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) based on grammar rules. Context-free grammars (BNF notation). Parser types: recursive descent (LL, top-down, easy to write by hand), shift-reduce (LR, bottom-up, handles more grammars). Tools: Yacc/Bison. Semantic analysis — type checking, scope resolution, symbol table management. Is this variable declared? Do types match? Intermediate representation — transform AST into IR (three-address code, SSA form). Platform-independent. Optimization — dead code elimination, constant folding, loop unrolling, inlining, register allocation. NP-hard in general. Code generation — emit target code (machine code, bytecode, LLVM IR). Register allocation, instruction selection. Runtime: compiled (C, Go, Rust — ahead-of-time), interpreted (Python, Ruby — line by line), JIT (Java, JavaScript V8 — compile at runtime based on hot paths). LLVM: modular compiler infrastructure. Frontend (Clang for C/C++, Rustc) → LLVM IR → optimization passes → backend (x86, ARM). Understanding compilers helps with: writing better code, building DSLs, understanding performance characteristics. Gorkem's gorkem-os project involves low-level code generation concepts.

messages.content: How do microservices communicate?

Microservice communication happens in two ways: synchronous and asynchronous. Synchronous: direct calls via REST API or gRPC — simple but couples services together. Asynchronous: message queues (RabbitMQ, Apache Kafka) — services don't wait for each other, messages are placed in a queue and the other service picks them up when ready. Event-driven architecture works on this principle. gRPC is faster than REST because it uses Protocol Buffers. Large systems prefer async because one service crashing doesn't affect others.

messages.content: what are tries and when would you use them over hash maps?

A trie (pronounced 'tree' or 'try', from reTRIEval) is a tree data structure where each node represents a character in a string. The path from root to a node spells out a prefix, and nodes can be marked as end-of-word.

Structure: The root is empty. Each edge represents a character. Each node has up to alphabet_size children (26 for lowercase English). A boolean flag marks which nodes represent complete words. For example, storing 'cat', 'car', 'card': root -> c -> a -> t (end), and a -> r (end) -> d (end).

Time complexity: Insert and search are O(L) where L is the word length, regardless of how many words are stored. This is the key advantage. A hash map also has O(L) for hashing the string, but a trie gives you much more.

When tries beat hash maps:

Prefix search: 'Find all words starting with pre-' is trivial in a trie (navigate to the prefix node, then enumerate all descendants). Hash maps can't do this without checking every key.

Autocomplete: Given a partial input, you can efficiently find all completions. This is how search engines, IDEs, and phone keyboards work. You traverse to the prefix node and perform BFS/DFS to find completions, optionally ranked by frequency.

Spell checking: Find words within edit distance K of a query. Tries can prune large portions of the search space during traversal.

Longest prefix matching: Used in IP routing tables (longest prefix match for routing decisions) and URL routing. Tries find the longest matching prefix in O(L) time.

Sorted iteration: Tries naturally iterate in lexicographic order. Hash maps have no inherent ordering.

When hash maps are better: Simple exact lookups where you don't need prefix operations. When memory is constrained and the alphabet is large (each trie node can use significant memory). When strings are long and varied (the trie becomes very deep with little sharing).

Optimizations: Compressed tries (radix trees/Patricia trees) merge nodes with single children, dramatically reducing memory usage. For the string 'romane', 'romanus', 'romulus', instead of one node per character, you get 'rom' -> 'an' -> 'e'/'us' and 'ulus'. Ternary search tries use three children per node (less, equal, greater) for better memory usage with large alphabets. Array-mapped tries (used in Clojure and Scala's persistent data structures) provide efficient immutable collections.

how to start a tech startup as a student?

How does the attention mechanism work?

The attention mechanism allows a model to learn which parts of the input sequence to focus on. Three key components: Query (what you're looking for), Key (what you're looking at), Value (what you return). Attention score = softmax(Q * K^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V. Multi-head attention runs multiple attention computations in parallel to capture different relationships. Self-attention learns relationships between words in a sentence. Attention is the heart of the transformer architecture — the paper 'Attention Is All You Need' is named for this reason. Gorkem's miniature-transformers project implements this from scratch.

SQL JOIN turleri nelerdir?

JOIN'ler birden fazla tablodan satirlari bir kosula gore birlestirir. INNER JOIN: her iki tablodan sadece eslesen satirlari dondurur. Kullanicinin siparisi yoksa gorunmez. LEFT JOIN: sol tablodan tum satirlar + sagdan eslesen satirlar. Eslemeyen sag taraf NULL olur. Kullanim: tum kullanicilari siparisleriyle listele (siparissiz kullanicilar dahil). RIGHT JOIN: sag tablodan tum satirlar + soldan eslesen. Daha az yaygin — tablolari degistirip LEFT JOIN kullanabilirsiniz. FULL OUTER JOIN: her iki tablodan tum satirlar. Eslesme olmayan yerlerde NULL. CROSS JOIN: A tablosundaki her satir B'deki her satirla birlestirilir (Kartezyen carpim). N * M satir. Nadiren gerekli. SELF JOIN: tablo kendisiyle birlestirilir. Kullanim: calisan-yonetici iliskileri. Performans: indeksli sutunlarda JOIN'ler hizlidir. N+1 sorgu problemi: ORM tembel yukleme — tek JOIN yerine N+1 sorgu ile N ilgili nesneyi alma.

messages.content: what is web performance optimization?

Web performance directly impacts user experience and business metrics. Core Web Vitals: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint — main content visible, target < 2.5s), FID/INP (interaction responsiveness, target < 200ms), CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift — visual stability, target < 0.1). Optimization strategies: 1) Reduce bundle size — code splitting, tree shaking, lazy loading, dynamic imports. 2) Optimize images — WebP/AVIF format, responsive images (srcset), lazy loading, CDN. 3) Minimize network requests — HTTP/2 multiplexing, preload critical resources, prefetch next pages. 4) Caching — Cache-Control headers, service workers, CDN edge caching. 5) CSS — remove unused CSS (PurgeCSS), critical CSS inline in head, avoid render-blocking CSS. 6) JavaScript — defer non-critical JS, use web workers for heavy computation, avoid long tasks blocking main thread. 7) Server — use CDN, enable compression (Brotli > gzip), edge rendering (SSR at CDN level). Tools: Lighthouse (Chrome DevTools), WebPageTest, Chrome DevTools Performance tab. Every 100ms of improvement in load time increases conversion by 1% (Amazon study).
attention mekanizması nasıl çalışır?

Attention mekanizması, bir modelin girdi dizisinin hangi kısımlarına odaklanması gerektiğini öğrenmesini sağlar. Üç temel bileşen var: Query (ne arıyorsun), Key (neye bakıyorsun), Value (ne döndürüyorsun). Attention score = softmax(Q * K^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V formülüyle hesaplanır. Multi-head attention birden fazla attention hesaplamasını paralel yaparak farklı ilişkileri yakalar. Self-attention bir cümledeki kelimelerin birbirleriyle ilişkisini öğrenir. Transformer mimarisinin kalbi attention — 'Attention Is All You Need' makalesi bunun için bu ismi aldı. Görkem'in miniature-transformers projesi bunu sıfırdan implemente ediyor.
rate limiting ve throttling nasıl uygulanır

Rate limiting, bir kaynağa belirli bir sürede yapılabilecek istek sayısını sınırlamaktır ve API'leri kötüye kullanımdan korur, kaynak tüketimini kontrol eder. Yaygın algoritmalar: Token Bucket'ta belirli oranda token eklenir, her istek bir token harcar, token bitince istekler reddedilir (burst'e izin verir). Leaky Bucket'ta istekler sabit oranda işlenir, fazlalıklar kuyrukta bekler veya reddedilir (düzgün çıkış oranı). Fixed Window'da sabit zaman penceresinde (1 dakika) istek sayısı sayılır ama pencere sınırlarında burst sorunu olabilir. Sliding Window Log'da her isteğin timestamp'i tutulur, pencere kayarak hesaplanır (doğru ama bellek yoğun). Sliding Window Counter, fixed window ve sliding log'un hibrit yaklaşımıdır. Redis ile rate limiting çok yaygındır: INCR ve EXPIRE komutları ile basit fixed window uygulanır, Lua script ile atomik sliding window yapılabilir. HTTP yanıtlarında X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After header'ları ile istemciye bilgi verilir. API Gateway seviyesinde (Kong, AWS API Gateway) veya uygulama seviyesinde uygulanabilir.

messages.content: what is technical writing for developers?

Technical writing communicates technical concepts clearly. Essential skill for developers. Documentation types: README (project overview, setup instructions, usage examples — first thing people see), API docs (endpoints, parameters, responses, examples — OpenAPI/Swagger), architecture docs (system overview, component interactions, decision records), tutorials (step-by-step learning — beginner-friendly), how-to guides (solve specific problems — task-oriented), reference (complete API reference — comprehensive), ADRs (Architecture Decision Records — why specific technical decisions were made). Writing principles: know your audience (beginner vs experienced developer), use active voice ('Run the command' not 'The command should be run'), include code examples (worth more than paragraphs of explanation), keep it concise (remove unnecessary words), structure with headers (scannable), version your docs with your code. Tools: Markdown (universal, simple), Docusaurus (documentation website), Mintlify (modern docs), GitBook, Notion. README template: project name, description, features, installation, usage, configuration, contributing, license. Architecture Decision Records (ADR): title, status, context (why), decision (what), consequences (trade-offs). Write docs as you code — not after. Good documentation multiplies the impact of your code. Gorkem's GitHub projects benefit from clear READMEs that explain purpose and setup.
