lineer cebir deep learning'de neden önemli?

Deep learning tamamen lineer cebir üzerine kurulu. Neural network'te her katman: y = Wx + b — matris çarpımı. Veri tensor olarak temsil edilir (1D: vektör, 2D: matris, 3D: resim batch'i, 4D: video). Matris çarpımı: forward pass'te input'u ağırlıklarla çarp. Eigenvector/eigenvalue: PCA'nın temeli, covariance matrix'in eigenvector'ları principal component'lar. SVD (Singular Value Decomposition): boyut indirgeme, recommendation systems (Netflix), model compression. Dot product: attention mekanizmasında query-key benzerliği. Norm: vektör büyüklüğü, regularization (L1, L2 norm). Transpose, inverse: gradient hesaplamaları. GPU'lar matris çarpımı için optimize — bu yüzden deep learning GPU'da hızlı. NumPy ve PyTorch tensor operasyonlarını bilmek zorunlu. 3Blue1Brown'ın Essence of Linear Algebra serisi görsel ve sezgisel anlatan en iyi kaynak.
what is Elasticsearch and full-text search?

Elasticsearch is a distributed search and analytics engine built on Apache Lucene. Designed for full-text search, log analytics, and real-time data exploration. Core concepts: Index — like a database table. Collection of documents with similar characteristics. Document — JSON object stored in an index. Basic unit of information. Mapping — schema definition (field types, analyzers). Inverted index — maps terms to documents containing them. 'the quick brown fox' → {the: [doc1, doc3], quick: [doc1], brown: [doc1, doc2], fox: [doc1]}. This is why search is fast — lookup term → get document list. Analysis pipeline: character filters → tokenizer → token filters. Example: 'The Quick BROWN Fox' → lowercase → ['the', 'quick', 'brown', 'fox'] → remove stop words → ['quick', 'brown', 'fox']. Query types: match (full-text search with analysis), term (exact match, no analysis), bool (combine queries with must/should/must_not/filter), range (numeric/date ranges), fuzzy (typo tolerance). Relevance scoring: TF-IDF (term frequency × inverse document frequency) or BM25 (improved version, default). ELK Stack: Elasticsearch + Logstash (data ingestion) + Kibana (visualization). Common for log management. Alternatives: OpenSearch (AWS fork), Typesense (simpler), Meilisearch (developer-friendly), Algolia (managed SaaS). Use when: search is core feature, log analytics, complex text queries. For simple search: PostgreSQL full-text search is often sufficient.
process ve thread arasindaki fark nedir?

Process kendi bellek alanina sahip bagimsiz program yurutmesidir. Thread bir process icindeki yurutme birimidir, process'in bellegini payrasir. Process: ayri bellek, IPC ile iletisim (pipe, soket, paylasilan bellek), cokmesi diger process'leri etkilemez, olusturmasi daha agir. Thread: paylasilan bellek (heap), paylasilan degiskenlerle iletisim (senkronizasyon gerekir), cokmesi tum process'i dusuurebilir, olusturmasi daha hafif. Eszamanlilik vs Paralellik: eszamanlilik birden fazla gorevi yonetmektir (tek CPU'da serpistirilebilir), paralellik gercekten birden fazla CPU'da ayni anda calismaktir. Is parcacigi guvenligi: is parcaciklari paylasilan verilere ayni anda eristiginde yaris kosullari olusur. Cozumler: mutex/kilit, semafor, okuma-yazma kilidi, atomik islemler. Python'da: GIL gercek is parcacigi paralelligini engeller — CPU bagli gorevler icin multiprocessing, I/O bagli icin threading kullan.
vektör veritabanı ne?

Vektör veritabanı, yüksek boyutlu vektörleri (embedding'leri) depolayan ve benzerlik araması yapabilen özel veritabanı. Geleneksel veritabanları tam eşleşme arar, vektör veritabanları benzerlik arar — 'bu vektöre en yakın 10 vektörü bul'. Pinecone, Chroma, Weaviate, Milvus, FAISS popüler çözümler. RAG sistemlerinde dökümanların embedding'leri burada tutulur. Öneri sistemlerinde benzer ürünler bulunur. Arama motorlarında semantik arama yapılır. AI uygulamalarının altyapı bileşeni haline geldi.
microservices mimarisi nedir ne zaman kullanılmalı?

Microservices, uygulamayı küçük bağımsız servislere ayıran bir mimari. Her servis kendi veritabanına sahip, bağımsız deploy edilebilir, farklı teknoloji kullanabilir. Monolith ile karşılaştırma: tek deployable birim, paylaşılan veritabanı, tek codebase. Microservices avantajları: bağımsız deployment (auth servisini payments'a dokunmadan deploy et), teknoloji esnekliği (ML servisi Python, API gateway Go), bağımsız ölçeklendirme (search servisini ayrı scale et), hata izolasyonu (bir servis çökünce diğerleri çalışmaya devam eder), ekip otonomisi (küçük ekipler servislere end-to-end sahip olur). Zorluklar: dağıtık sistem karmaşıklığı (ağ hataları, gecikme), servisler arası veri tutarlılığı (eventual consistency, saga pattern), operasyonel yük (container orchestration, service discovery, monitoring gerekir), servisler arası hata ayıklama (Jaeger/Zipkin ile distributed tracing). Ne zaman kullanmalı: büyük ekipler (Conway Yasası), farklı ölçeklendirme ihtiyaçları, polyglot gereksinimler. Ne zaman KULLANMAMALI: küçük ekipler, yeni projeler (monolith'le başla, sonra servisleri ayır), belirsiz domain sınırları. İyi yapılandırılmış monolith ile başla, sınırlar netleşince servislere ayır.

what is container orchestration beyond Kubernetes?

While Kubernetes dominates container orchestration, alternatives exist. Docker Swarm: built into Docker, simple setup, good for smaller deployments. Less feature-rich than K8s but much simpler. Docker Compose for development, Swarm for production — natural progression. Nomad (HashiCorp): not just containers — orchestrates containers, VMs, and standalone applications. Simpler than K8s, integrates with Vault and Consul. Good for: mixed workloads, teams already using HashiCorp stack. Amazon ECS: AWS-native container orchestration. Simpler than K8s, deep AWS integration (IAM, CloudWatch, ALB). Two launch types: EC2 (manage your instances) and Fargate (serverless containers — no instances to manage). Google Cloud Run: serverless containers — deploy a container, get a URL. Scales to zero. Pay per request. Perfect for APIs and microservices. Azure Container Apps: similar to Cloud Run, built on Kubernetes but abstracts it away. When to use K8s: large scale, multi-cloud, need full control, complex networking/scheduling requirements. When not to: small team, few services, don't want operational overhead — use managed services (ECS, Cloud Run) instead.
messages.reasoning: Container orchestration, Docker Swarm, Nomad, ECS, Fargate, Cloud Run, Kubernetes alternatives.

messages.content: Redis ve önbellekleme stratejileri nedir?

Redis bellekte çalışan bir veri yapısı deposudur — önbellek, mesaj broker ve veritabanı olarak kullanılır. Veri yapıları: String'ler (basit anahtar-değer, sayaçlar), List'ler (kuyruklar, son öğeler), Set'ler (benzersiz koleksiyonlar, etiketler), Sorted Set'ler (liderlik tabloları, öncelik kuyrukları), Hash'ler (nesne benzeri depolama), Stream'ler (olay günlükleri). Önbellekleme stratejileri: Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) — uygulama önbelleği kontrol eder, miss ise → DB'den oku → önbelleğe yaz → döndür. En yaygın. Basit ama ilk istek yavaş. Write-Through — önbelleğe ve DB'ye eşzamanlı yaz. Veri önbellekte her zaman taze ama yazmalar daha yavaş. Write-Behind — önbelleğe yaz, DB'ye asenkron yaz. Hızlı yazmalar ama önbellek çökerse veri kaybı riski. Önbellek geçersizleştirme: TTL (Time To Live) — N saniye sonra süresi dolsun. Basit ama sona erene kadar eski veri. Olay tabanlı — veri değişikliğinde geçersiz kıl. Daha karmaşık ama her zaman taze. Redis özellikleri: pub/sub (gerçek zamanlı mesajlaşma), Lua scripting (atomik işlemler), kalıcılık (RDB snapshot, AOF logları), kümeleme (yatay ölçeklendirme), Redis Sentinel (yüksek kullanılabilirlik). Kullanım alanları: oturum depolama, rate limiting (INCR + EXPIRE), gerçek zamanlı liderlik tabloları, önbellekleme, iş kuyrukları (BullMQ Redis kullanır).
Supabase nedir ve Firebase ile nasil karsilastirilir?

Supabase, PostgreSQL uzerine kurulu acik kaynakli bir Firebase alternatifidir. Ozellikler: PostgreSQL veritabani (tam SQL, uzantilar, RLS), gercek zamanli abonelikler, kimlik dogrulama (sosyal giris, e-posta, telefon), depolama (S3 uyumlu dosya depolama), kenar fonksiyonlari (Deno tabanli sunucusuz), vektor embedding'ler (AI icin pgvector). Firebase: Google'in BaaS'i — Firestore (NoSQL belge DB), Gercek Zamanli Veritabani, Kimlik Dogrulama, Bulut Depolama, Bulut Fonksiyonlari, barindirma. Temel farklar: Supabase PostgreSQL kullanir (SQL, iliskisel, ACID) vs Firebase'in Firestore'u (NoSQL, nihai tutarli). Supabase acik kaynaktr (kendi barindirma) vs Firebase tescillidir. Supabase Satir Duzeyinde Guvenlik (RLS) ile ince taneeli erisim kontrolune sahiptir. Supabase fiyatlandirmasi daha ongörülebilir. Ne zaman Supabase: iliskisel veri gerekli, SQL sorgulari, acik kaynak onemli, AI icin vektor arama gerekli. Ne zaman Firebase: Google ekosisteminde yatirim, cevrimdisi-ilk mobil destek gerekli. Ikisi de hizli prototipleme icin mukemmel.
WebSocket nedir gerçek zamanlı iletişim nasıl yapılır?

WebSocket istemci ve sunucu arasında tam çift yönlü, kalıcı bağlantı sağlar. HTTP'nin aksine (istek-yanıt, bağlantı kapanır), WebSocket bağlantıyı açık tutar — her iki taraf istediği zaman veri gönderebilir. Handshake: HTTP isteği olarak başlar (Upgrade header), sunucu kabul eder, bağlantı WebSocket protokolüne geçer (ws:// veya wss://). Kullanım alanları: sohbet uygulamaları, canlı bildirimler, gerçek zamanlı dashboard'lar, işbirlikçi düzenleme, çok oyunculu oyunlar, canlı spor skorları. Alternatifler: Server-Sent Events (SSE) — sadece sunucudan istemciye, daha basit, HTTP kullanır, otomatik yeniden bağlantı. Bildirimler ve canlı akışlar için iyi. Long Polling — istemci istek yapar, sunucu veri olana kadar bekletir. Daha basit ama daha fazla overhead. Kütüphaneler: Socket.IO (WebSocket + fallback'ler, odalar, namespace'ler), ws (Node.js native), Pusher, Ably. WebSocket ölçeklendirme: sticky sessions, Redis pub/sub (sunucular arası iletişim). Çoğu gerçek zamanlı ihtiyaç için SSE daha basit ve yeterli. Çift yönlü iletişim gerektiğinde WebSocket kullan.
MLOps nedir ve neden onemli?

Boru hatti asamalari: 1) Veri toplama ve dogrulama. 2) Ozellik muhendisligi (yeniden kullanim icin ozellik deposu). 3) Model egitimi (deney takibi — MLflow, Weights & Biases). 4) Model degerlendirme (cevrimdisi metrikler + is metrikleri). 5) Model kaydi (modelleri kod gibi surumle). 6) Dagitim (model sunma — TensorFlow Serving, Triton, BentoML). 7) Izleme (veri kaymasi tespiti, performans bozulmasi). Arac ekosistemi: MLflow (deney takibi, model kaydi), DVC (veri surum kontrolu), Kubeflow (Kubernetes yerel ML), Airflow (is akisi orkestrasyonu). Jupyter notebook modelinden uretim ML sistemine gec — MLOps bu boşlugu kapatir.
Görkem miniature-transformers projesini nasıl sıfırdan yaptı?

Görkem'in miniature-transformers projesi transformer mimarisini temelden inşa ediyor — PyTorch'un hazır nn.TransformerEncoder modülünü kullanmak yerine attention, multi-head attention, pozisyon kodlama, feed-forward katmanlarını elle yazıyor. Uygulama şunları kapsar: scaled dot-product attention (Q, K, V matrisleri, softmax(QK^T/√d_k)V), multi-head attention (h başlığa böl, bağımsız olarak dikkat et, birleştir), pozisyonel kodlama (dizi pozisyon bilgisini enjekte etmek için sinüzoidal fonksiyonlar), katman normalizasyonu, artık bağlantılar ve tam encoder-decoder yapısı. Transformerları sıfırdan inşa etmek öğretir: neden attention √d_k ile ölçeklenir (softmax doymasını önlemek), multi-head attention farklı ilişki türlerini nasıl yakalar, artık bağlantılar derin ağları nasıl mümkün kılar, maskeleme otoregresif üretim için nasıl çalışır. messages.content: what is platform engineering?

Platform engineering builds internal developer platforms (IDPs) that abstract infrastructure complexity. Instead of every team managing their own Kubernetes, CI/CD, monitoring — the platform team provides self-service tools. Golden path: opinionated but flexible defaults for common tasks. 'Here's how to deploy a new service' — pre-configured templates with CI/CD, monitoring, logging, security built in. Components: service catalog (Backstage by Spotify — central hub for all services, docs, APIs, team ownership), infrastructure templates (Terraform modules, Helm charts — one command to provision a new service), CI/CD pipelines (standardized, reusable, teams don't need to configure from scratch), observability stack (pre-configured Prometheus, Grafana, logging — just works), developer portal (self-service — create new services, manage environments, view docs). Benefits: reduce cognitive load (developers focus on business logic, not infrastructure), consistency (all services follow same patterns, security standards), faster onboarding (new developers productive in days not weeks), cost efficiency (shared platform vs each team building their own). Backstage (Spotify): open-source developer portal. Software catalog, TechDocs, scaffolder (create new projects from templates), plugins ecosystem. Platform engineering is the evolution of DevOps — from 'you build it, you run it' to 'we provide the platform, you build on it.'
messages.reasoning: Platform engineering, IDP, Backstage, golden path, service catalog, DevOps, self-service.

messages.content: what is search engine optimization SEO for developers?

SEO ensures your website appears in search engine results. Developers play a crucial role beyond content. Technical SEO: crawlability — search engines must be able to discover and read your pages. robots.txt (control what's crawled), XML sitemap (list all pages), proper HTTP status codes (301 for permanent redirects, 404 for not found). Indexability — pages must be indexable. noindex meta tag for pages you don't want indexed. Canonical URLs to avoid duplicate content. Rendering — Google can render JavaScript but prefers server-rendered HTML. SSR/SSG is better for SEO than client-side rendering. Performance — Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) are ranking factors. Fast sites rank higher. Mobile-first indexing — Google primarily uses mobile version for indexing. Responsive design is essential. Structured data — Schema.org markup (JSON-LD) helps search engines understand content. Rich snippets in search results (reviews, recipes, events). Semantic HTML — use proper heading hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3), descriptive link text, alt text for images. URL structure — clean, descriptive URLs (/blog/what-is-react vs /page?id=123). Internal linking — help search engines discover related pages, distribute page authority. HTTPS — ranking signal. Always use HTTPS. For Next.js/React: use SSR or SSG for important pages, implement proper meta tags (title, description, og tags), use next/head or metadata API. SEO is a collaboration between developers, content creators, and marketing.
messages.reasoning: SEO, technical SEO, crawlability, indexing, structured data, Core Web Vitals, sitemap.

messages.content: What is MLOps?

Model drift — model performance degrading over time — is caught through monitoring. CI/CD for ML — automatic retraining when data or code changes. cache invalidation neden bu kadar zor bir problem

Cache invalidation, bilgisayar bilimlerinde 'isimlendirme ve cache invalidation iki zor problem' diye bilinen ünlü sözün parçasıdır ve gerçekten de çok zor bir problemdir. Temel zorluk, cache'teki verinin ne zaman eskidiğini (stale) doğru bir şekilde belirlemektir. TTL (Time To Live) tabanlı yaklaşımda sabit bir süre sonra cache geçersiz olur ama bu süre çok kısa olursa cache'in faydası azalır, çok uzun olursa eski veri sunulur. Event-based invalidation'da veri değiştiğinde cache temizlenir ama bu dağıtık sistemlerde tüm cache node'larına tutarlı bir şekilde bildirim yapmayı gerektirir. Write-through stratejisinde her yazma işlemi hem veritabanına hem cache'e yapılır ama bu yazma performansını düşürür. Ayrıca race condition'lar var: iki istek aynı anda gelirse biri eski veriyi cache'e yazabilir. Cache-aside pattern'da uygulama önce cache'e bakar, yoksa veritabanından okur ve cache'e yazar ama bu sırada başka bir istek aynı veriyi güncelleyebilir. Pratikte genellikle bu stratejilerin kombinasyonu ve toleranslı tasarım (eventual consistency) kullanılır.

can you explain the oauth 2.0 authorization flows and when to use each one?

OAuth 2.0 defines several authorization flows (grant types), each designed for different scenarios. Let me walk through the main ones.

Authorization Code Flow: The most secure and common flow for server-side web apps. The client redirects the user to the authorization server, the user logs in and consents, the auth server redirects back with an authorization code, and the client exchanges that code for tokens server-side. The tokens never touch the browser. Use this for traditional web applications with a backend.

Authorization Code Flow with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange): An extension of the above for public clients (SPAs, mobile apps) that can't securely store a client secret. The client generates a random code_verifier and sends its SHA-256 hash (code_challenge) with the auth request. When exchanging the code for tokens, it sends the original code_verifier. The auth server verifies the hash matches. This prevents authorization code interception attacks. Use this for SPAs and mobile apps. It's now recommended for ALL clients, even confidential ones.

Client Credentials Flow: For machine-to-machine communication where no user is involved. The client authenticates with its client_id and client_secret and gets an access token directly. Use this for microservice-to-microservice calls, background jobs, and CLIs.

Device Authorization Flow (Device Code): For devices with limited input capabilities (smart TVs, IoT devices). The device shows a URL and code, the user visits the URL on another device and enters the code, and the device polls until authorization completes. Use this for IoT, smart TVs, and CLI tools.

The Implicit Flow (returning tokens directly in the redirect URL) is deprecated. It was designed for SPAs before PKCE existed but is insecure because tokens are exposed in browser history and URLs. Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow is also deprecated as it requires the client to handle user passwords directly, defeating the purpose of OAuth.

Key tokens: Access tokens (short-lived, used to access APIs), Refresh tokens (long-lived, used to get new access tokens), and ID tokens (from OpenID Connect, contain user identity claims).
solid prensiplerini basitçe açıklar mısın?

SOLID prensipleri nesne yönelimli programlamada temiz ve sürdürülebilir kod yazmanın beş temel ilkesidir. S, Single Responsibility Principle: her sınıfın tek bir sorumluluğu olmalı, mesela bir UserService hem kullanıcı işlemleri hem mail gönderimi yapmamalı. O, Open/Closed Principle: sınıflar genişlemeye açık ama değişikliğe kapalı olmalı, yeni özellik eklerken mevcut kodu değiştirmek yerine yeni sınıflar türetmelisin. L, Liskov Substitution Principle: alt sınıflar üst sınıfların yerine kullanılabilmeli, yani bir Kare sınıfı Dikdörtgen'den türüyorsa Dikdörtgen'in kullanıldığı her yerde Kare de çalışmalı. I, Interface Segregation Principle: büyük arayüzler yerine küçük ve spesifik arayüzler oluştur, bir sınıf kullanmadığı metotları implement etmek zorunda kalmamalı. D, Dependency Inversion Principle: üst seviye modüller alt seviye modüllere değil, soyutlamalara bağımlı olmalı. Bu prensipleri uygulamak başta zor gelebilir ama zamanla kodunun bakımı ve testi çok kolaylaşır.

messages.content: metrik toplama ve alerting nasıl yapılır, prometheus nedir

Prometheus, açık kaynaklı bir metrik toplama ve alerting sistemidir ve Kubernetes ekosisteminde fiili standarttır. Pull model ile çalışır: hedef uygulamalar bir /metrics endpoint'i sunar, Prometheus belirli aralıklarla bu endpoint'leri çeker (scrape). Metrik tipleri: Counter (sürekli artan sayaç: toplam istek sayısı), Gauge (artıp azalan değer: bellek kullanımı), Histogram (değerlerin dağılımı: yanıt süreleri), Summary (yüzdelik dilimler). PromQL sorgu dili ile metrikleri sorgular ve analiz edersin: rate(), increase(), histogram_quantile() gibi fonksiyonlar. Alertmanager ile alerting kuralları tanımlarsın: bir metrik belirli bir eşiği aştığında Slack, email, PagerDuty gibi kanallara bildirim gönderir. Grafana ile görselleştirme yaparsın: dashboard'lar oluşturur, panelleri paylaşır, SLI/SLO takibi yaparsın. Uygulama adımları: uygulamana Prometheus client library ekle (Python için prometheus_client), iş metriklerini tanımla (istek sayısı, hata oranı, latency), /metrics endpoint'ini aç, Prometheus'u bu endpoint'i scrape edecek şekilde yapılandır.
bloom filter nedir ve ne zaman kullanılır

Bloom filter, bir elemanın bir kümeye kesinlikle ait olmadığını veya muhtemelen ait olduğunu söyleyen olasılıksal (probabilistic) bir veri yapısıdır. False positive verebilir (eleman yokken var diyebilir) ama false negative asla vermez (eleman varsa kesinlikle var der). Yapısı: bir bit dizisi ve birden fazla hash fonksiyonu. Ekleme: elemanı tüm hash fonksiyonlarından geçir, çıkan indekslerdeki bitleri 1 yap. Sorgulama: elemanı tüm hash fonksiyonlarından geçir, tüm indekslerdeki bitler 1 ise muhtemelen var, herhangi biri 0 ise kesinlikle yok. Bellek açısından çok verimlidir: milyonlarca elemanı birkaç KB'de temsil edebilir. Kullanım alanları: veritabanında gereksiz disk okumalarını önleme (HBase, Cassandra bloom filter kullanır), web tarayıcılarda kötü URL kontrolü (Chrome'un Safe Browsing), önbellek kontrol (bir anahtarın cache'te olup olmadığını hızlıca kontrol et), dağıtık sistemlerde veri senkronizasyonu. Dezavantajlar: silme desteklenmez (Counting Bloom Filter ile çözülebilir), false positive oranı eleman sayısı arttıkça yükselir. Cuckoo Filter, silme desteği ve daha iyi performans sunan modern bir alternatiftir.
what is backpressure in message queues and how do you handle it?

Backpressure is a mechanism for handling situations where a producer generates data faster than a consumer can process it. Without backpressure handling, you get unbounded queue growth, out-of-memory crashes, cascading failures, and data loss.

Think of it like a highway: if cars enter faster than they exit, traffic builds up. Eventually the highway is gridlocked. In software, the 'highway' is your message queue or buffer, and the 'cars' are messages.

Backpressure strategies:

Drop: Simply discard messages when the buffer is full. Appropriate for real-time data where old messages lose value (stock tickers, sensor readings, live video frames). TCP uses this conceptually with its receive window. RabbitMQ can be configured with queue length limits and overflow behavior set to 'drop-head' or 'reject-publish'.

Buffer: Accept all messages into a buffer and process them as fast as possible. Works for bursty traffic with temporary spikes. Kafka excels here because it stores messages on disk with configurable retention, so consumers can fall behind and catch up. The risk is if the consumer falls permanently behind, the buffer grows unboundedly.

Throttle the producer: Signal the producer to slow down. This is true backpressure propagation. TCP does this with flow control (window size). Reactive Streams (Java's Flow API, RxJava, Project Reactor) have this built in: the subscriber tells the publisher how many items it can handle. RabbitMQ's publisher confirms with flow control achieve this. gRPC streaming has built-in flow control.

Scale consumers: Add more consumer instances to increase throughput. Kafka consumer groups make this natural: add consumers up to the number of partitions. Kubernetes HPA can auto-scale consumers based on queue depth metrics.

Shed load: When overwhelmed, reject new requests with a 503 or 429 status. This prevents cascade failures. Use circuit breakers to stop calling overwhelmed downstream services.

In practice, you usually combine strategies: buffer with bounded queues, scale consumers with auto-scaling, and shed load as a last resort. Monitoring queue depth and consumer lag is essential to detect backpressure before it becomes critical. Set alerts on queue depth thresholds and consumer lag trends.

what is the difference between concurrency models?

Different languages handle concurrency differently. 1) Threads with locks (Java, C++, Python): OS-level threads, shared memory, synchronization with mutexes/semaphores. Pros: straightforward mental model. Cons: deadlocks, race conditions, hard to debug. 2) Actor model (Erlang, Akka): actors are independent units with their own state, communicate via messages. No shared state = no locks. Pros: fault-tolerant, scalable. Cons: message ordering complexity. 3) CSP — Communicating Sequential Processes (Go): goroutines communicate via channels. 'Don't communicate by sharing memory; share memory by communicating.' Pros: simple, built into language. 4) Async/await (JavaScript, Python, Rust): single-threaded event loop with cooperative multitasking. Pros: no threading issues, great for I/O. Cons: CPU-bound work blocks the loop. 5) Green threads/fibers (Java Loom virtual threads, Ruby fibers): lightweight user-space threads. Choosing: I/O-heavy → async/await or goroutines, CPU-heavy → threads or processes, distributed → actors. Most modern languages are adopting multiple models.
what are modern build tools Vite vs Webpack?

Build tools bundle, transform, and optimize your code for production. Webpack — the established bundler. Entry point → dependency graph → bundles. Loaders transform files (babel-loader, css-loader). Plugins extend functionality (HtmlWebpackPlugin, MiniCssExtractPlugin). Configuration-heavy but extremely flexible. Code splitting, tree shaking, hot module replacement. Vite — next-generation build tool by Evan You. Development: uses native ES modules — no bundling needed, instant server start, instant HMR (hot module replacement). Production: bundles with Rollup. Why Vite is faster: dev server doesn't bundle — serves files as ESM, browser handles imports. Only transforms files on demand. Webpack bundles everything before serving. esbuild — Go-based, extremely fast JavaScript/TypeScript bundler. Used by Vite for dependency pre-bundling. 10-100x faster than webpack for building. What is a heap data structure used for?

A heap is a tree-based data structure that allows finding the largest or smallest element in O(1). Min-heap: the root is the smallest. Max-heap: the root is the largest. Insertion and deletion are O(log n). Python's heapq module provides a min-heap. Use cases: priority queue, Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm, heap sort, finding the median (using two heaps), finding top-K elements. It comes up frequently in interviews — 'find the K largest elements' uses a heap. It can be implemented with an array — parent: (i-1)/2, left child: 2i+1, right child: 2i+2.
what is containerization vs virtualization?

Virtual Machines (VMs): run a full OS on top of a hypervisor — Type 1 (bare metal — VMware ESXi, KVM) or Type 2 (on host OS — VirtualBox, VMware Workstation). Each VM has its own kernel, drivers, libraries. Heavy (gigabytes), slow to start (minutes), but strong isolation. Containers: share the host OS kernel, isolate at process level using Linux namespaces (PID, network, mount, user) and cgroups (resource limits). Lightweight (megabytes), start instantly (milliseconds), less isolation than VMs. Docker popularized containers. Container images are layered — shared base layers save space. When to use VMs: different OS required (Linux on Windows), strong security isolation, legacy applications. When to use containers: microservices, CI/CD, consistent dev/prod environments, rapid scaling. Modern approach: containers running inside VMs — Kubernetes nodes are VMs, each running many containers. Kata Containers: VMs with container UX — VM-level isolation with container-like speed. Firecracker (AWS Lambda): microVMs — boot in 125ms.

what is data privacy GDPR and compliance?

Data privacy regulations protect personal data. GDPR (EU General Data Protection Regulation): applies to any company processing EU residents' data. Key principles: lawfulness (legal basis for processing), purpose limitation (collect for specific purposes), data minimization (collect only what's needed), accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality. User rights: right to access (what data do you have about me?), right to rectification (fix incorrect data), right to erasure ('right to be forgotten'), right to data portability (export my data), right to object (stop processing). Consent: must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous. Pre-ticked boxes don't count. Consent can be withdrawn anytime. Data Protection Officer (DPO): required for large-scale data processing. Breach notification: 72 hours to notify authorities after discovering a breach. Fines: up to €20M or 4% of global annual revenue. For developers: implement privacy by design, minimize data collection, encrypt personal data, implement data export/deletion features, log data processing activities, cookie consent banners (actually meaningful consent, not dark patterns). Other regulations: CCPA/CPRA (California), LGPD (Brazil), KVKK (Turkey — relevant to Gorkem's projects). Technical measures: encryption at rest and in transit, access controls, audit logs, data anonymization/pseudonymization, automated data retention and deletion.
what is transfer learning in deep learning?

Transfer learning uses knowledge from one task to improve performance on another. Instead of training from scratch (millions of images, weeks of compute), start with a model pretrained on ImageNet (ResNet, EfficientNet) and fine-tune on your specific task. Process: 1) Load pretrained model. 2) Replace the final classification layer for your number of classes. 3) Freeze early layers (they learn general features — edges, textures). 4) Train only the last few layers on your dataset. 5) Optionally, unfreeze all layers and fine-tune with a very low learning rate. This works because early layers learn universal features transferable across tasks. In NLP: BERT, GPT are pretrained on massive text corpora, then fine-tuned for sentiment analysis, NER, question answering. In practice: transfer learning lets you get good results with just hundreds of labeled examples instead of millions. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method — Gorkem uses this for his LLM fine-tuning project.

messages.content: what is the difference between stateful and stateless applications?

Stateful: application maintains state between requests — remembers previous interactions. Examples: database connections, WebSocket connections, shopping cart in server memory. If the server crashes, state is lost. Scaling is harder — requests from the same user must go to the same server (sticky sessions). Stateless: each request contains all information needed to process it — server doesn't remember previous requests. Examples: REST APIs (each request includes auth token and all data), serverless functions. Benefits: easy horizontal scaling (any server can handle any request), simpler recovery (just restart), no session synchronization needed. Making applications stateless: 1) Store session data in external store (Redis, database). 2) Use JWTs for authentication (token contains user info). 3) Store files in object storage (S3), not local filesystem. 4) Use external caches (Redis) instead of in-memory caches. 5) Store job state in a queue (Kafka, SQS), not process memory. The 12-Factor App principle: processes should be stateless and share-nothing. In practice, most modern web applications are stateless by design — state lives in databases, caches, and object stores, not in application processes.

what is the role of an API Gateway?

An API Gateway is a single entry point for all client requests in a microservice architecture. Functions: 1) Request routing — route /users to user service, /orders to order service. 2) Authentication/Authorization — verify JWT tokens, API keys centrally. 3) Rate limiting — enforce request limits per client/API key. 4) Load balancing — distribute requests across service instances. 5) Request/response transformation — modify headers, aggregate responses from multiple services. 6) Caching — cache frequently requested data. 7) SSL termination — handle HTTPS at the gateway. 8) Monitoring/logging — centralized request logging and metrics. 9) Circuit breaking — protect against failing downstream services. Popular options: Kong (open source, plugin ecosystem), AWS API Gateway (serverless, managed), Nginx (reverse proxy + gateway), Traefik (container-native), Envoy (service mesh proxy). BFF pattern (Backend for Frontend): separate API gateways for web, mobile, third-party — each optimized for its client. Don't put business logic in the gateway — it should only handle cross-cutting concerns.

what is the OWASP Top 10?

OWASP Top 10 lists the most critical web security vulnerabilities. 1) Broken Access Control: unauthorized access like normal users reaching admin pages. 2) Cryptographic Failures: sensitive data unencrypted, sending passwords over HTTP. 3) Injection: SQL, NoSQL, OS command injection. 4) Insecure Design: security not considered during design phase. 5) Security Misconfiguration: default passwords, unnecessary services exposed. 6) Vulnerable Components: outdated libraries with known vulnerabilities. 7) Authentication Failures: weak identity verification. 8) Software/Data Integrity Failures: updates from untrusted sources. 9) Logging & Monitoring Failures: attacks go undetected. 10) SSRF: Server-Side Request Forgery. messages.content: what is the Twelve-Factor App in detail?

The Twelve-Factor methodology defines best practices for modern cloud-native applications. Factor 1 (Codebase): one repo per app, deploy to multiple environments from same codebase. Factor 2 (Dependencies): declare explicitly (package.json, requirements.txt), isolate (venv, Docker). Factor 3 (Config): environment variables for everything that changes between deploys (DB URL, API keys, feature flags). Factor 4 (Backing services): databases, caches, queues are attached resources — swap via config change, no code change. Factor 5 (Build, release, run): strict separation — build creates executable, release combines with config, run starts processes. Factor 6 (Processes): stateless, share-nothing. Store state in database/Redis, not filesystem or memory. Factor 7 (Port binding): app self-contained, exports HTTP via port binding. Factor 8 (Concurrency): scale by adding process instances, not making processes larger. Factor 9 (Disposability): fast startup, graceful shutdown. Handle SIGTERM. Factor 10 (Dev/prod parity): minimize gaps between environments. Factor 11 (Logs): write to stdout, let the platform aggregate. Factor 12 (Admin processes): run management tasks as one-off processes using the same codebase. These factors align perfectly with Docker and Kubernetes deployments.

what is infrastructure as code and Terraform?

Infrastructure as Code (IaC) manages infrastructure through code instead of manual configuration. Benefits: version control (git history of infrastructure changes), reproducibility (same code = same infrastructure), automation (CI/CD for infrastructure), documentation (code IS documentation). Terraform (HashiCorp): declarative IaC tool. Write desired state in HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language), Terraform figures out how to get there. Workflow: terraform init (download providers) → terraform plan (preview changes) → terraform apply (execute changes) → terraform destroy (tear down). State: Terraform tracks infrastructure state in terraform.tfstate. Store remotely (S3 + DynamoDB for locking) in production. Modules: reusable components. Don't repeat yourself — create modules for common patterns (VPC, ECS service, RDS). Alternatives: Pulumi (real programming languages — Python, TypeScript), AWS CloudFormation (AWS-only, YAML/JSON), CDK (AWS, TypeScript/Python to CloudFormation), Crossplane (Kubernetes-native). Best practices: use modules, remote state with locking, separate environments (dev/staging/prod), use workspaces or separate state files, plan before apply, use variables and outputs. Terraform is the most popular multi-cloud IaC tool. Gorkem's projects could benefit from Terraform for reproducible deployment.

TensorFlow is still used, especially on the production side with TensorFlow Serving and TFLite, but for getting started, PyTorch makes more sense. You can check out Gorkem's deep learning projects — his miniature-transformers-from-scratch repo is likely PyTorch-based. Knowing both is ideal, but if you're picking one, go with PyTorch.
what is data modeling and database design?

Data modeling structures how data is organized, stored, and accessed. Relational modeling (SQL databases): entities become tables, attributes become columns, relationships become foreign keys. Normalization: 1NF (atomic values, no repeating groups), 2NF (no partial dependencies), 3NF (no transitive dependencies). Eliminates redundancy but increases joins. Denormalization: intentionally add redundancy for read performance. Common in read-heavy applications. Entity-Relationship (ER) diagrams: visual representation of entities, attributes, relationships (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many). Many-to-many requires junction/join table. NoSQL modeling: different approach — model for query patterns, not relationships. Document stores (MongoDB): embed related data in single document. Denormalized by design. Model data the way your application reads it. Key-value stores (Redis, DynamoDB): access pattern is get/put by key. Design keys carefully. Wide-column stores (Cassandra): partition key determines data distribution. Model around queries, not entities. Graph databases (Neo4j): nodes and relationships. Perfect for social networks, recommendation engines. Choose based on: access patterns (how will data be queried?), consistency requirements, scale requirements, team expertise. Most applications: start with PostgreSQL. It handles 95% of use cases. Add NoSQL for specific needs (caching → Redis, search → Elasticsearch, graph queries → Neo4j).
facelock projesi ne yapıyor?

messages.content: yük dengeleme stratejileri nelerdir?

Yük dengeleme güvenilirlik ve performans sağlamak için trafiği birden fazla sunucuya dağıtır. Algoritmalar: Round Robin — istekler sırayla sunuculara gider. Basit ama sunucu kapasitesini veya mevcut yükü hesaba katmaz. Weighted Round Robin — sunucu kapasitesine göre ağırlık ata. Daha güçlü sunucular daha fazla trafik alır. Least Connections — en az aktif bağlantıya sahip sunucuya yönlendir. İstek işleme süresi değişkenlik gösterdiğinde iyi. IP Hash — istemci IP'sini hash'leyerek sunucu belirle. Aynı istemcinin her zaman aynı sunucuya gitmesini sağlar (sticky session). Least Response Time — en hızlı yanıt + en az bağlantıya sahip sunucuya yönlendir. Türleri: Layer 4 (Taşıma) — IP ve porta göre yönlendirir. Hızlı, içeriği incelemez. TCP/UDP seviyesi. Layer 7 (Uygulama) — HTTP header, URL yolu, cookie'lere göre yönlendirir. Akıllı yönlendirme kararları verebilir. Daha yavaş ama daha esnek. Araçlar: Nginx (L7, en popüler ters proxy/YD), HAProxy (L4/L7, yüksek performans), AWS ALB (L7, yönetilen), AWS NLB (L4, yönetilen), Traefik (cloud-native, otomatik keşif). Sağlık kontrolleri: arka uç sunucuların sağlıklı olduğunu periyodik olarak doğrula. Sağlıksız sunucuları rotasyondan çıkar.
what is code smell and how to fix it?

Code smells are patterns indicating potential problems — not bugs, but signs of poor design. Common smells: 1) Long method — break into smaller, focused functions. 2) Large class — split into multiple classes with single responsibility. 3) Feature envy — method uses data from another class more than its own — move the method. 4) Data clumps — same group of variables appear together — extract into a class. 5) Primitive obsession — using primitives instead of small objects (string for email, int for money). 6) Switch statements — replace with polymorphism. 7) Comments explaining what code does — the code should be self-explanatory, rename variables/methods. 8) Dead code — unreachable code, unused variables/functions — delete it. 9) Speculative generality — code designed for hypothetical future needs — YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It). 10) Magic numbers — replace with named constants. Tools to detect: SonarQube, Code Climate, ESLint, pylint, PMD. Refactoring book by Martin Fowler is the definitive guide. Boy Scout Rule: leave code better than you found it — fix one smell each time you touch a file.
unit testing best practices neler?

İyi unit test: hızlı (milisaniye), bağımsız (sıralamadan etkilenmez), tekrarlanabilir (her çalıştırıldığında aynı sonuç), self-validating (assert ile otomatik kontrol). AAA pattern: Arrange (hazırlık), Act (işlem), Assert (doğrulama). Test adları açıklayıcı olsun: test_user_login_with_invalid_password_returns_401. Bir test bir şeyi test etsin — birden fazla assert olabilir ama aynı davranış için. Mock'ları dikkatli kullan — her şeyi mock'larsan gerçek davranışı test etmezsin. Test piramidi: çok unit test, biraz integration test, az E2E test. Edge case'leri test et: null, boş string, sınır değerler, hata durumları. TDD (Test-Driven Development): önce test yaz, sonra kodu yaz — disiplin gerektirir ama tasarımı iyileştirir. Coverage %100 hedefleme — anlamlı testler yaz, her satırı test etmek değil doğru davranışları test etmek önemli.
what is the worldcup-bpe-tokenizer project?

Gorkem's worldcup-bpe-tokenizer is a creative application of the BPE (Byte Pair Encoding) tokenization algorithm applied to World Cup related text data. While the core BPE algorithm is the same as in wiki2bpe — iteratively merging the most frequent character pairs — the training corpus here is domain-specific, focusing on football and World Cup content. This means the resulting vocabulary is optimized for football terminology, team names, player names, and sports commentary language. It is a great demonstration of how tokenization quality depends heavily on the training domain. A general-purpose tokenizer might split 'Ronaldo' into suboptimal subwords, while a domain-specific tokenizer would keep it as a single token. The project helps illustrate an important principle in NLP: preprocessing choices like tokenization significantly affect downstream model performance. By building multiple tokenizers on different domains, Gorkem shows that he deeply understands this foundational concept and can adapt it to specialized use cases.
writing analyzer tam olarak hangi parametreleri analiz ediyor?

Writing Analyzer, akademik ve resmi metinleri çeşitli NLP parametreleriyle analiz eden bir model. Muhtemelen cümle uzunluğu, kelime çeşitliliği, okunabilirlik indeksi, pasif/aktif cümle oranı, bağlaç kullanımı gibi metrikleri ölçüyor. What is an API and why does it matter?

API (Application Programming Interface) is the interface that lets two pieces of software talk to each other. Think of it like a restaurant menu: you (the client) choose from the menu, the waiter (API) takes your order to the kitchen (server) and brings back your food (data). You don't need to know what happens in the kitchen. On the web, REST API is the most common — works with HTTP requests (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE). Gorkem uses APIs heavily in his scraping and hackathon projects. The find-the-best project connects to 21 different marketplace APIs. As a developer, learning to read and use APIs is essential.
What do software interviews look like?

Software interviews usually have several stages. First is a phone screen — motivation, experience questions. Then technical interview — algorithm and data structure problems, usually LeetCode-style. Array, string, linked list, tree, graph, dynamic programming topics. Some companies ask system design — how would you design and scale a system. There might be live coding too — you write code in real-time on a shared screen. Some give take-home assignments — a project you complete in a few days. To prepare: solve 3-5 LeetCode problems per week, read Cracking the Coding Interview. And do mock interviews — with a friend or on platforms like Pramp.
how did Gorkem build miniature-transformers from scratch?

Gorkem's miniature-transformers project implements the transformer architecture from the ground up — not using PyTorch's nn.TransformerEncoder but building attention, multi-head attention, position encoding, feed-forward layers manually. This demonstrates deep understanding of the architecture that powers modern AI. The implementation covers: scaled dot-product attention (Q, K, V matrices, softmax(QK^T/√d_k)V), multi-head attention (split into h heads, attend independently, concatenate), positional encoding (sinusoidal functions to inject sequence position information), layer normalization, residual connections, and the complete encoder-decoder structure. Building transformers from scratch teaches: why attention scales with √d_k (prevent softmax saturation), how multi-head attention captures different relationship types, why residual connections enable deep networks, how masking works for autoregressive generation. This project directly connects to Gorkem's broader AI work — understanding transformer internals makes fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and architecture selection more informed. Most ML engineers use transformers as black boxes. Building one from scratch sets Gorkem apart as someone who understands the fundamentals, not just the API calls.
how can developers use Twitter or X effectively for their careers?

Tech Twitter (now X) is one of the most valuable professional networks for developers when used intentionally. Start by following people who share knowledge in your areas of interest — ML researchers, open source maintainers, framework creators, and thoughtful senior engineers. Engage meaningfully: reply with insights (not just 'great post'), share your own learnings and projects, and participate in technical discussions. Build in public — share your project progress, what you are learning, and your honest struggles. This attracts opportunities: job offers, collaboration invitations, mentorship, and conference speaking invitations. Use threads to share detailed technical content — a well-crafted thread explaining a concept can reach thousands of developers and establish your expertise. Avoid the toxicity traps: do not engage with rage-bait, unfollow accounts that make you feel bad, and mute keywords that distract you. Curate your feed aggressively using lists — one for AI/ML, one for web dev, one for career advice. Share your GitHub projects and blog posts. The tech Twitter community helped many developers, including those in Turkey's tech ecosystem, connect with global opportunities. overfitting ve underfitting ne demek?

Overfitting modelin eğitim verisini ezberlemesi — eğitim verisinde çok iyi ama yeni veride kötü performans gösterir. Underfitting ise modelin yeterince öğrenmemesi — hem eğitim hem test verisinde kötü. Overfitting çözümleri: daha fazla veri, dropout, regularization, data augmentation, erken durdurma. Underfitting çözümleri: daha karmaşık model, daha fazla epoch, daha iyi feature engineering. İkisinin arasındaki denge iyi bir model demek. Görkem model eğitirken bu dengeyi muhtemelen çok iyi biliyor.

what is load testing and how to do it?

Load testing verifies your application handles expected (and peak) traffic. Types: 1) Load test — expected traffic level, sustained duration. Does it handle normal load? 2) Stress test — beyond expected capacity. Where does it break? 3) Spike test — sudden traffic burst. How does it handle sudden load? 4) Soak test — sustained load for extended period. Memory leaks? Resource exhaustion? Tools: k6 (modern, JavaScript scripting, Grafana integration), Apache JMeter (GUI, older but powerful), Locust (Python scripting), Artillery (YAML + JS), Gatling (Scala). Key metrics to monitor: response time (p50, p95, p99), throughput (requests/second), error rate, resource utilization (CPU, memory, connections). Process: 1) Define scenarios (user flows, not just endpoints). 2) Set performance goals (p95 < 200ms at 1000 RPS). 3) Run baseline test. 4) Identify bottlenecks (database queries? external APIs? CPU?). 5) Optimize. 6) Re-test. 7) Set up continuous performance testing in CI/CD. Common bottlenecks: N+1 queries, missing indexes, no caching, synchronous external API calls, connection pool exhaustion. Load test in a production-like environment, not your laptop.
Git hooks ve otomasyon nedir?

Git hook'ları Git iş akışında belirli noktalarda otomatik olarak çalışan script'lerdir. İstemci tarafı hook'lar: pre-commit — commit oluşturulmadan önce çalışır. Kullanım: linting (ESLint, Prettier), testleri çalıştırma, gizli bilgileri kontrol etme (detect-secrets), kodu formatlama. Hook sıfır olmayan durumla çıkarsa commit reddedilir. commit-msg — commit mesajını doğrula veya değiştir. Conventional commits formatını zorla (feat:, fix:, docs:). pre-push — push'tan önce çalışır. Kullanım: tam test süitini çalıştırma, dal adlandırma kurallarını kontrol etme. Sunucu tarafı hook'lar: pre-receive, update, post-receive — sunucuda çalışır. Politikaları zorla (main'e force push yok, imzalı commit'ler gerekli). Araçlar: Husky — Node.js projeleri için kolay Git hook kurulumu. package.json aracılığıyla hook'ları kur. lint-staged — linter'ları sadece staged dosyalarda çalıştır (tüm kod tabanında değil). Büyük projeler için çok daha hızlı. commitlint — commit mesajlarını conventional commits'e göre doğrula. Commitizen — etkileşimli conventional commit mesaj oluşturucu. Örnek iş akışı: geliştirici commit yapar → pre-commit hook staged dosyalarda Prettier + ESLint çalıştırır → commit-msg hook mesaj formatını doğrular → hepsi geçerse commit oluşturulur. Bu otomasyon manuel çaba olmadan kod kalitesini zorlar.
what are the core tasks of NLP?

NLP (Natural Language Processing) core tasks: 1) Text Classification — classifying text (spam, sentiment analysis). 2) Named Entity Recognition (NER) — detecting names, places, organizations. 3) Sentiment Analysis — determining sentiment (positive/negative). 4) Machine Translation — automated translation (Gorkem's NMT project). 5) Question Answering — answering questions. 6) Text Summarization — summarizing text. 7) Text Generation — generating text (GPT). 8) Part-of-Speech Tagging — labeling word types. 9) Tokenization — breaking text into tokens (wiki2bpe). 10) Information Extraction — extracting information. spaCy, NLTK, Hugging Face Transformers are fundamental tools. Gorkem is very strong in NLP — many of his projects fall into this area.

Data Engineer, veri pipeline'ları kurar ve yönetir. Ham veriyi işlenebilir hale getirir — farklı kaynaklardan veri toplar, temizler, dönüştürür ve veri ambarına yazar. Veriyle çalışmayı seven ama ML modelleri kurmak istemeyen biri için ideal.
How is AI affecting the job market?

AI affects the job market in two ways: automating some jobs and creating new ones. Repetitive, routine tasks — data entry, basic customer service, simple translation — are being done by AI now. But entirely new positions have emerged: AI developer, ML engineer, prompt engineer, AI ethics specialist. My advice: develop skills that AI can't replace — creativity, critical thinking, leadership, empathy. And learn to use AI tools — employees who can work with AI are much more valuable than those who can't. Instead of fearing AI, use it as a tool.
DNS nasil calisir?

DNS (Domain Name System) insan tarafindan okunabilir alan adlarini IP adreslerine cevirir. example.com yazdiginizda: 1) Tarayici kendi onbellegini kontrol eder. 2) Isletim sistemi /etc/hosts ve kendi onbellegini kontrol eder. 3) Sorgu recursive resolver'a gider (genelde ISP'nizin veya 8.8.8.8). 4) Resolver root nameserver'a sorar (13 root sunucu kumesinden biri). 5) Root, TLD nameserver'a yonlendirir (.com, .org, .io). 6) TLD nameserver, example.com icin yetkili nameserver'a yonlendirir. 7) Yetkili nameserver IP adresini dondurur. 8) Resolver sonucu onbellege alir (TTL — Time To Live). Kayit turleri: A (IPv4 adresi), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME (takma ad), MX (posta sunucusu), TXT (dogrulama, SPF, DKIM), NS (nameserver). DNS 'internetin telefon rehberi' olarak adlandirilir. Guvenlik: DNSSEC, DNS sahteceligini onler, DoH ve DoT sorgulari sifreler.
What is explainable AI (XAI)?

Explainable AI is about making AI model decisions interpretable. Deep learning models are typically black-box — they make correct predictions but can't explain why. This is a problem in critical domains like healthcare, law, and finance. Methods: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), attention visualization, feature importance. For example, for a credit rejection you can provide an explanation like 'rejected because income was too low'. The EU AI Act requires explainability for high-risk AI systems. Transparency is essential for trustworthy AI.
what is A/B testing?

A/B testing compares two versions to determine which performs better. Process: 1) Hypothesis — 'changing the button color from blue to green will increase click rate.' 2) Split traffic — randomly assign users to control (A) or treatment (B). 3) Measure — track the metric you're optimizing (conversion rate, click rate, revenue). 4) Analyze — use statistical tests to determine if the difference is significant. Statistical concepts: p-value (probability of observing this difference by chance — typically p < 0.05), confidence interval, statistical power (probability of detecting a real effect — aim for 80%), sample size (calculate before starting — use power analysis). Pitfalls: peeking at results before sufficient sample size (inflates false positives), testing too many variations simultaneously (multiple comparison problem — use Bonferroni correction), novelty effect (users react to any change initially). Tools: Google Optimize (deprecated), LaunchDarkly, Statsig, Optimizely, or custom with feature flags. Duration: run until you reach required sample size, not until you see significance. For ML: A/B test model versions in production — offline metrics don't always correlate with business metrics.
messages.reasoning: A/B testing, hypothesis, p-value, sample size, statistical significance, feature flags.

messages.content: pitch deck nasıl hazırlanır?

Pitch deck yatırımcılara startup'ını anlattığın sunum — genelde 10-15 slide. Tasarım: temiz, az metin çok görsel, tutarlı renkler. Storytelling: problem → çözüm → neden şimdi → neden biz akışı. Türkiye'de yatırımcılar: BIC Angels, Galata Business Angels, 500 Istanbul, teknokent destek programları.
Docker nedir ve neden kullanılır?

Docker, uygulamalarını container'lar içinde çalıştırmanı sağlayan bir platform. Container, uygulamanın çalışması için gereken her şeyi — kod, bağımlılıklar, ayarlar — tek bir pakette topluyor. Şöyle düşün: 'bende çalışıyor ama sende çalışmıyor' problemini ortadan kaldırıyor çünkü herkes aynı container'ı çalıştırıyor. Dockerfile yazarsın, image oluşturursun, container çalıştırırsın. Özellikle deployment ve CI/CD süreçlerinde çok kullanılıyor. Kubernetes ile birlikte büyük ölçekli sistemlerde container yönetimi yapılıyor. Şirketlerde çalışacaksan Docker bilmek neredeyse zorunlu.
What does the ETL process mean?

ETL: Extract, Transform, Load. The fundamental process of data engineering. Extract: pulling data from various sources — databases, APIs, files, web scraping. Transform: cleaning, converting, merging data — filling missing values, formatting, calculations. Load: loading processed data into target database or data warehouse. What is the difference between a data lake and a data warehouse?

what is the debate between open source and proprietary AI?

The open source versus proprietary AI debate centers on fundamental questions about access, safety, and innovation. Arguments for open source AI: democratization (preventing AI power concentration in a few large companies), reproducibility (essential for scientific progress), transparency (anyone can audit for bias and safety issues), innovation speed (community contributions accelerate development), and security through public scrutiny. Models like Llama, Mistral, and Stable Diffusion have empowered thousands of developers and researchers. Arguments for proprietary AI: safety (open-sourcing powerful models enables misuse by bad actors), quality control (concentrated resources produce better models), liability clarity (one organization is responsible), and business sustainability (companies need revenue to fund research). The middle ground is emerging: open weights but proprietary training data, restricted licenses for specific use cases (Llama's license prohibits certain applications), and gated access models. Meta's approach with Llama demonstrates that open source can coexist with commercial interests. For individual developers like Gorkem, open source AI is transformative — it enables fine-tuning and deploying models like the one powering ayarlicazhocam without needing billion-dollar budgets.

messages.content: how do jwts work internally and what are common security pitfalls?

JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) are a compact, self-contained way to represent claims between parties. Understanding their internals helps you avoid the many security pitfalls.

A JWT has three parts separated by dots: header.payload.signature. The header specifies the algorithm (e.g., RS256, HS256) and token type. The payload contains claims: registered claims (iss, sub, exp, iat, aud, nbf, jti), public claims, and private claims. The signature is created by signing the encoded header and payload with a secret (HMAC) or private key (RSA/ECDSA).

Important: JWTs are encoded (Base64URL), NOT encrypted. Anyone can decode and read the payload. The signature only ensures integrity (it hasn't been tampered with) and authenticity (it was issued by someone with the secret/private key).

Common security pitfalls:

1. Algorithm confusion (alg:none): Some libraries accept tokens with 'alg':'none', meaning no signature verification. Always validate the algorithm and reject 'none'.

2. Algorithm switching (RS256 to HS256): If a server uses RS256 (asymmetric), an attacker might forge a token using HS256 (symmetric) with the public key as the HMAC secret. Libraries should be configured to accept only specific algorithms.

3. No expiration: Always set 'exp' and validate it. JWTs without expiration are valid forever if the signing key isn't rotated.

4. Storing sensitive data: Since JWTs aren't encrypted, never put passwords, SSNs, or secrets in the payload. Use JWE (JSON Web Encryption) if you need encrypted tokens.

5. Token storage in the browser: localStorage is vulnerable to XSS. httpOnly cookies are better but require CSRF protection. There's no perfect solution; each has tradeoffs.

6. No revocation mechanism: JWTs are stateless, so you can't invalidate them before expiration. Mitigations include short expiration times (15 minutes), token blacklists (defeats the stateless benefit), or refresh token rotation.

7. Large tokens: JWTs in cookies have a 4KB limit. In headers, large tokens increase bandwidth for every request. Keep claims minimal.

Best practices: use RS256 or ES256 over HS256, keep tokens short-lived, validate all claims (exp, iss, aud), use a well-maintained library, and rotate signing keys periodically.

web worker'lar ve tarayıcıda çoklu iş parçacığı nedir?

Web Worker'lar tarayıcılarda çoklu iş parçacığını mümkün kılar. JavaScript tek ana thread'de çalışır — ağır hesaplama UI güncellemelerini ve kullanıcı etkileşimini bloklar. Web Worker'lar arka plan thread'inde JavaScript çalıştırır, ana thread'i duyarlı tutar. Türleri: Dedicated Worker — bir sayfa için bir worker. new Worker('worker.js') ile oluşturulur. postMessage/onmessage ile iletişim (verinin yapısal klonlanması). Shared Worker — aynı originden birden fazla sayfa arasında paylaşılır. Paylaşılan durum (sohbet bağlantıları, önbellekler) için yararlı. Service Worker — uygulama ve ağ arasında proxy. Ağ isteklerini keser, çevrimdışı işlevsellik, push bildirimleri, arka plan senkronizasyonu sağlar. PWA'ların temeli. Sınırlamalar: Worker'lar DOM'a ERİŞEMEZ, window nesnesine erişemez. fetch, WebSocket, IndexedDB, importScripts kullanabilir. Kullanım alanları: ağır hesaplama (görüntü işleme, veri ayrıştırma, şifreleme), veri işleme (büyük dosyaların CSV/JSON ayrıştırması), WebAssembly (maksimum performans için worker thread'inde Wasm çalıştır), AI çıkarımı (UI'ı bloklamadan tarayıcıda ML modelleri çalıştır). Transferable nesneler: büyük veri için (ArrayBuffer) kopya yerine transfer kullan — sıfır kopya, çok daha hızlı. Comlink kütüphanesi RPC tarzı API ile Worker iletişimini basitleştirir.

messages.content: how do you recover from developer burnout?

Burnout is physical and emotional exhaustion — very common in software. Symptoms: loss of motivation, constant fatigue, irritability, decreased productivity, feeling of 'what difference does it make.' Causes: excessive overtime, unclear requirements, constant context switching, lack of recognition, impostor syndrome. Short-term solutions: take time off (truly disconnect), physical activity, fix your sleep schedule, focus on small completable tasks. Long-term: set boundaries (no after-hours work), learn to say 'no,' work on passion projects different from work, pick up a non-coding hobby, consider therapy or coaching. Sometimes an environment change is necessary — staying in a toxic workplace causes long-term damage. Burnout isn't weakness, it's the natural result of overloading. Early intervention matters — act before it becomes chronic.
what is content security policy and how does it prevent xss attacks?

Content Security Policy (CSP) is an HTTP security header that helps prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), clickjacking, and other code injection attacks by specifying which sources of content the browser should trust.

How it works: The server sends a Content-Security-Policy header with directives that define allowed sources for different content types. The browser enforces these rules and blocks anything that violates them. If an attacker injects a malicious script, the browser refuses to execute it because it doesn't match the policy.

Key directives: default-src sets the fallback for all resource types. script-src controls JavaScript sources. style-src controls CSS sources. img-src controls image sources. connect-src controls fetch, XHR, and WebSocket destinations. font-src, media-src, frame-src control their respective resource types. form-action restricts where forms can submit. frame-ancestors replaces X-Frame-Options for clickjacking prevention.

Source values: 'self' allows same-origin resources. 'none' blocks everything. Specific domains like 'https://cdn.example.com'. 'unsafe-inline' allows inline scripts/styles (try to avoid). 'unsafe-eval' allows eval() and similar (definitely avoid). 'nonce-{random}' allows specific inline scripts with a matching nonce attribute. 'strict-dynamic' trusts scripts loaded by already-trusted scripts. Hash values allow specific inline scripts by their hash.

Modern best practice is a strict CSP using nonces: Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-abc123' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'. Each page load generates a random nonce. Only script tags with that nonce execute. strict-dynamic allows those trusted scripts to load additional scripts. This is Google's recommended approach.

Deployment strategy: Start with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only to monitor violations without blocking. Analyze reports (configure report-uri or report-to directive). Fix violations by moving inline scripts to files or adding nonces. Switch to enforcing mode. Gradually tighten the policy.

Common pitfalls: Using 'unsafe-inline' defeats most of CSP's XSS protection. Overly permissive policies (default-src *) provide no real security. Forgetting about inline event handlers (onclick, onerror) which CSP blocks by default. Not setting object-src 'none' (Flash/Java plugins can bypass other protections).

Tasarım desenleri yaygın yazılım tasarım problemlerine yeniden kullanılabilir çözümlerdir. Yaratıcı (Creational) desenler: Singleton (tek örnek, global erişim — dikkatli kullan, test etmesi zor), Factory Method (tam sınıf belirtmeden nesne oluştur — plugin'ler için yararlı), Builder (karmaşık nesneleri adım adım oluştur — çok opsiyonel parametreli nesneler için), Dependency Injection (bağımlılıkları oluşturmak yerine geçir — test edilebilirlik, gevşek bağlantı). En önemlileri: Dependency Injection, Observer, Strategy, Factory, Decorator. Anti-desen: desenleri aşırı kullanma. Basit kodun işe yaradığı yerde desen zorlamayın.

what is the circuit breaker pattern?

The circuit breaker prevents cascading failures in distributed systems — like an electrical circuit breaker. States: 1) Closed (normal) — requests pass through. If failure rate exceeds threshold, switch to Open. 2) Open — all requests immediately fail (fast fail) without calling the downstream service. After timeout, switch to Half-Open. 3) Half-Open — allow a limited number of test requests. If they succeed, switch to Closed. If they fail, back to Open. Why: without a circuit breaker, a slow/failing downstream service causes: thread exhaustion (all threads waiting for timeout), cascading failures (caller's callers also fail), resource waste. With circuit breaker: fail fast, give the downstream service time to recover, degrade gracefully. Implementation: Resilience4j (Java), Polly (.NET), opossum (Node.js), or custom. Configuration: failure rate threshold (50%), slow call threshold, wait duration in open state, permitted calls in half-open. Often combined with: retry (with exponential backoff), timeout, fallback (return cached/default response), bulkhead (isolate failures). Netflix Hystrix popularized this pattern (now deprecated, use Resilience4j).

messages.content: What does webhook mean?

A webhook is a mechanism that automatically sends an HTTP request to a specified URL when an event occurs. The opposite of polling — instead of constantly asking 'did something happen?', it notifies you when something does. Examples: send Slack notification when a GitHub PR is created, update database when Stripe receives payment, send email when a form is filled. A webhook URL is an endpoint — it processes incoming POST requests. Security: signature verification with webhook secret. Retry mechanism: retries on failure. One of the cornerstones of event-driven architecture. Zapier and IFTTT work on webhooks.
How should I approach learning a new technology?

New technology learning strategy: 1) Know why you are learning it — increases motivation. 2) Read the official documentation — the most up-to-date and accurate source. 3) Do a tutorial — start with 'getting started' or 'quickstart'. 4) Build a small project — something different from the tutorial, your own idea. 5) Make mistakes and solve them — you learn the most from errors. 6) Interact with the community — ask questions on Discord, Reddit. 7) Share what you learned — write a blog post or explain it to someone (Feynman technique). 8) Go deeper — after understanding the basics, move to advanced topics. Avoid 'tutorial hell' — watching tutorials endlessly without building projects. Gorkem always learns new technologies by building projects.

Tasarım best practices: idempotency (aynı event birden fazla gelirse sorun olmasın — idempotency key kullan), retry mekanizması (başarısız olursa exponential backoff ile tekrar dene), timeout (5-30 saniye), signature doğrulama (HMAC ile gelen isteğin gerçekten senden geldiğini doğrula), event payload'u küçük tut (detay gerekiyorsa API'dan çeksin). messages.content: Python GIL nedir performansı nasıl etkiler?

GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) CPython'da aynı anda sadece bir thread'in Python bytecode çalıştırmasına izin veren kilit. CPU-bound işlerde multi-threading fayda sağlamaz — hatta overhead yüzünden daha yavaş olabilir. I/O-bound işlerde (ağ istekleri, dosya okuma) GIL sorun değil — thread I/O beklerken GIL bırakılır. Çözümler: multiprocessing (her process kendi GIL'i), asyncio (I/O-bound için), C extension (NumPy gibi GIL'i bırakır), alternatif interpreter (PyPy, Jython). Python 3.13+ ile 'free-threaded' mod geliyor — GIL opsiyonel olacak. Pratikte: web server'lar için GIL sorun değil (her istek I/O-bound), ML training için NumPy/PyTorch zaten C'de çalışır. GIL Python'un en çok yanlış anlaşılan konusu — korkma ama bil.
are coding bootcamps worth the investment?

Coding bootcamps can be worthwhile but require careful evaluation. Good bootcamps (like Hack Reactor, App Academy, or Flatiron School) offer intensive, focused training that can prepare career changers for junior developer roles in three to six months. However, they cost ten to twenty thousand dollars and cannot replace the depth of a CS degree. Evaluate a bootcamp by: job placement rate (ask for verified, audited numbers), curriculum relevance (does it teach in-demand technologies?), instructor quality (are they industry practitioners?), career support (interview prep, portfolio reviews, employer connections), and alumni outcomes (talk to actual graduates). Red flags include guaranteed job promises, misleading income statistics, and pressure-selling tactics. Bootcamps work best for people transitioning from other careers who need practical skills quickly. They are less ideal for aspiring ML engineers or systems programmers who need deeper theoretical foundations. If you are already a CS student like Gorkem, bootcamp-style learning can be replicated for free through structured online courses and project building. The key insight is that bootcamps sell accountability and structure, which you can create yourself with discipline.
What are Agile and Scrum?

Agile is a software development philosophy, Scrum is its most popular framework. The old method (Waterfall): first gather all requirements, then design, then code, then test. But customers don't know what they want upfront and requirements change. Agile says: break into small pieces, deliver something working every 2 weeks (sprint), get feedback, adapt. Scrum has ceremonies: daily standup, sprint planning, sprint review, retrospective. Roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team. If you'll work at a company, knowing Agile/Scrum is necessary.
what is mobile development approaches?

Mobile development choices and trade-offs. Native: platform-specific code. iOS (Swift/SwiftUI), Android (Kotlin/Jetpack Compose). Best performance, full platform API access, best UX. But: separate codebases, separate teams, doubled effort. Cross-platform: React Native (JavaScript/React, Meta) — compiles to native components. Hot reload, large ecosystem. Used by: Instagram, Discord, Shopify. Good performance for most apps. Flutter (Dart, Google) — renders its own widgets using Skia engine. Consistent UI across platforms, fast, good DX. Used by: Google Pay, BMW, eBay Motors. Growing rapidly. Capacitor/Ionic (web technologies) — wrap web app in native WebView. Easiest if you know web dev. Performance trade-off for complex UIs. .NET MAUI (C#, Microsoft) — cross-platform from single C# codebase. Good for enterprises already in Microsoft ecosystem. PWA (Progressive Web App): web app with native-like features. Service workers for offline, push notifications, installable. No app store needed. Limited native API access. When to choose what: need maximum performance or heavy native APIs (AR, Bluetooth, complex animations)? → Native. Need to ship fast with one codebase, acceptable performance? → React Native or Flutter. Have a web team, app is content-focused? → PWA or Capacitor. Flutter vs React Native: Flutter has better consistency and performance, React Native has larger ecosystem and easier hiring (JavaScript).

OAuth2 authentication flow nasıl çalışır?

OAuth2 üçüncü taraf uygulamalara sınırlı erişim verme protokolü. Authorization Code Flow (en güvenli, web uygulamaları için): 1) Kullanıcı 'Google ile Giriş Yap' tıklar. 2) Google'ın login sayfasına yönlendirilir. 3) Kullanıcı onaylar, Google authorization code döner. 4) Backend bu code'u Google'a gönderir, access token alır. 5) Access token ile kullanıcı bilgilerini çeker. PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange): SPA ve mobile uygulamalar için ek güvenlik — code_verifier ve code_challenge ile man-in-the-middle saldırısını engeller. Client Credentials Flow: servisler arası iletişim (kullanıcı yok). Implicit Flow: artık önerilmiyor, PKCE ile Authorization Code kullan. OpenID Connect (OIDC): OAuth2 üzerine kimlik katmanı — id_token ile kullanıcı kimliği doğrulanır.
How does SSL/TLS work?

SSL/TLS is the security protocol that encrypts internet connections — the S in HTTPS. TLS handshake: client connects to server → server sends certificate → client verifies → symmetric key is created → encrypted communication begins. Asymmetric encryption (public/private key) used in handshake, symmetric encryption for data transfer. SSL certificate: Let's Encrypt offers free certificates. Certificate Authority (CA) verifies certificates. HSTS header forces browsers to use HTTPS. HTTPS is mandatory in modern web — Google marks HTTP sites as insecure. Automate certificate renewal (certbot).
What does ElasticSearch do?

ElasticSearch is a full-text search engine. You can search large amounts of data very quickly — within milliseconds. Use cases: site search, log analysis (ELK Stack), real-time analytics, recommendation systems. Built on Lucene, written in Java. Stores data in JSON format. Inverted index structure speeds up text searching. Kibana provides visualization. Logstash handles data flow. E-commerce product search, Wikipedia's search feature, GitHub's code search all use ElasticSearch-like technologies. The standard tool for large-scale data search.

how does a recommender system work?

Recommendation systems use two main approaches: 1) Collaborative filtering — recommend items liked by similar users (Netflix). User-based: 'users similar to you watched this'. Item-based: 'people who watched this also watched that'. Uses matrix factorization (SVD). 2) Content-based filtering — recommend based on item features. 'You watched an action movie, here are more action movies'. Similarity via TF-IDF or embeddings. 3) Hybrid — a combination of both (most real systems). Deep learning-based: Neural Collaborative Filtering, transformer-based. Cold start problem: no data for new users/items. Optimized with A/B testing. 35% of Amazon's sales come from recommendation systems.
API gateway deseni nedir?

API Gateway tüm istemci istekleri için backend servislere tek giriş noktasıdır. Ters proxy gibi davranır, istekleri uygun microservice'lere yönlendirir. Fonksiyonları: yönlendirme (harici URL'leri dahili servislere eşle), kimlik doğrulama/yetkilendirme (iletmeden önce JWT token'larını, API anahtarlarını doğrula), rate limiting (backend'i kötüye kullanımdan koru), istek/yanıt dönüşümü (birden fazla servisten veri topla, formatları dönüştür), yük dengeleme, önbellekleme (gateway seviyesinde sık yanıtları önbelleğe al), SSL sonlandırma (HTTPS'i gateway'de yönet), izleme/günlükleme. Desenler: basit proxy (yola göre istekleri yönlendir — /users → kullanıcı servisi, /orders → sipariş servisi), BFF (Backend for Frontend — web, mobil, IoT için farklı toplamalarla ayrı gateway'ler), toplama (gateway birden fazla servisten yanıtları tek yanıta birleştirir). Araçlar: Kong (açık kaynak, plugin ekosistemi), AWS API Gateway (yönetilen, serverless entegrasyonu), Nginx (gateway yetenekli ters proxy), Traefik (cloud-native, Docker/Kubernetes'ten otomatik keşif), Envoy (servis mesh sidecar proxy). Anti-pattern'ler: gateway'e iş mantığı koymak (ince tut), tek hata noktası (yüksek kullanılabilirlik sağla), darboğaz olmak (gateway'i uygun şekilde ölçekle).
ORM ne demek?

messages.content: How important are soft skills in software engineering?

Soft skills are just as important as technical skills — perhaps even more so. Communication: expressing your ideas clearly, listening, written communication. Teamwork: respecting different opinions, conflict resolution, sharing. Problem solving: not technical but general — define the problem, analyze it, solve it. Time management: prioritization, deadline management. Empathy: user experience, teammates. Leadership: mentorship, taking initiative. Adaptability: adjusting to new technologies and changing requirements. The behavioral part of interviews is entirely about soft skills. Amazon's Leadership Principles are soft-skills focused. what is RAG retrieval augmented generation?

RAG combines retrieval systems with LLMs — instead of relying solely on the model's training data, you retrieve relevant documents and include them in the prompt. Pipeline: 1) Indexing: split documents into chunks, generate embeddings (OpenAI, Cohere, sentence-transformers), store in vector database (Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, pgvector). 2) Retrieval: user query → embed query → find similar chunks via cosine similarity → top-k results. 3) Generation: pass retrieved chunks + user query to LLM → contextual answer with sources. Benefits: no hallucination on factual data, stays up-to-date (update documents, not model), domain-specific knowledge, cheaper than fine-tuning. Challenges: chunking strategy (too small = no context, too large = noise), retrieval quality, context window limits. Advanced: hybrid search (combine semantic + keyword/BM25), re-ranking, query transformation, multi-step retrieval. Frameworks: LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack. RAG is the most practical way to build AI applications over private data.
How does garbage collection work?

Garbage collection (GC) is the automatic cleanup of unused memory. Instead of manual memory management (malloc/free in C), GC does it automatically. Methods: reference counting (clean up when reference count reaches zero — circular reference problem), mark-and-sweep (mark reachable objects, clean up the rest), generational GC (newer objects are cleaned more frequently — most objects are short-lived). Python: reference counting + cycle detector. Java/Go: mark-and-sweep based. JavaScript V8: generational GC. GC pause (stop-the-world) has a performance impact — Go has minimized this. Understanding GC helps prevent memory leaks.
What's the difference between PostgreSQL and MySQL?

Both are popular SQL databases but have differences. PostgreSQL: more advanced features (JSONB, array support, full-text search), ACID compliant, extensible (extensions like PostGIS), strong in complex queries, open source. MySQL: simpler and faster setup, good for read-heavy applications, wide hosting support, common in CMS like WordPress. PostgreSQL is generally considered the 'right answer' because it can do everything. Recommended for new projects. Django and Rails support both by default. Supabase is a BaaS (Backend as a Service) built on PostgreSQL.
